codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.text.2: Obtain eight blocks and test a small construct. Gaining height requires additional force, and levitite strongly resists low-speed movement. Do not substitute an expectation of “negative mass” for testing: cargo balance and actual thrust determine behavior. Store blend away from accidental heat sources.
codex.quest.aero_basics.levitite.title: Levitite
A navigation table outputs redstone toward a destination provided by a supported navigation item. It is not a complete aircraft schedule and does not control every propeller itself. Prepare the table and test it on a stationary platform first.

Insert a suitable navigation item and compare outputs on different sides. The signal weakens when a side is not facing directly toward the target; different supported items supply different destinations. Compare the selected location with actual coordinates before connecting steering.

Automatic travel still needs signal processing, thrust, stability, altitude limits and stopping. Begin with directional lamps, then a short controlled turn. Do not send the first craft far away unattended under the assumption that the table is a complete autopilot. Reliable navigation builds on tested manual flight and return.
codex.quest.aero_basics.navigation.title: Navigation Table
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.0: A propeller produces thrust when rotated and moves a physical construct. A complete wooden propeller and a bearing for a built-up propeller are different propulsion arrangements. Prepare both and review their separate scenes rather than assuming identical mounting.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.1: For a constructed propeller, attach a connected structure with at least two suitable sail blocks in front of the bearing. Supply rotation and observe thrust direction. Reverse it through rotation direction or the supported wrench setting.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.text.2: Check drive attachments and propeller clearance before moving the hull. Actual thrust changes with altitude and motion through air, so a ground test does not promise identical speed everywhere. Begin with brief acceleration and stopping near the pad. Control lift and horizontal movement separately.
codex.quest.aero_basics.propeller.title: Propellers
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.0: Sensors provide signals for your logic rather than assembling an autopilot automatically. An altitude sensor responds to elevation, a gimbal sensor to orientation, and a laser sensor to a suitable visible beam. Prepare all three and begin with a separate ground rig and lamps.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.1: Set altitude boundaries and check signal direction. Configure the gimbal angle and test each axis. A laser sensor needs a separate beam source; blocks can obstruct it and a filter can restrict color.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.text.2: Compare outputs with actual positions before connecting burners or steering. Reversed feedback may amplify roll instead of correcting it. Retain manual control and limit initial corrections near the ground. After verification, sensors can support altitude control and docking, but their signals still need the correct actuators.
codex.quest.aero_basics.sensors.title: Sensors
codex.quest.ca_electric.accumulator.text: A modular accumulator stores FE between generation and consumers. Its recipe uses a brass casing, capacitors, a copper rod and electrum wire. Prepare one module and separate input and output connections so both behaviors are visible.

Connect the alternator to input and watch charge rise. After storing a little energy, stop generation and run a motor: the reserve should fall while supporting operation. Modules combine only in valid arrangements, so check expansion against Ponder.

Storage smooths interruptions but cannot compensate for a persistent generation deficit. If charge falls with every cycle, reduce demand or add supply. Do not confuse the modern module with the deprecated standalone accumulator. The item objective confirms a block; observe actual readings to verify charging and discharge.
An alternator converts Create rotation into FE electricity for connected devices. Prepare it and a mechanical source with spare capacity. This version requires at least 32 RPM, so a slow directly connected water wheel may need speed-increasing gearing.

Supply a shaft, check speed and connect a suitable electrical receiver. Watch generation and total stress: increasing alternator speed demands more mechanical capacity. Begin with one load or a small accumulator.

If no energy arrives, check RPM, electrical connection direction and receiving space. A rotating model does not guarantee output under every condition. Do not loop an alternator into a motor expecting perpetual generation; conversion creates no extra energy. A steady source supports later storage networks and electrical equipment.
codex.quest.ca_electric.alternator.title: Alternator
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.task.3: Manually: the burner with a straw accepts bioethanol and heats the basin
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.0: A straw lets an ordinary filled blaze burner accept suitable liquid fuel. Rolling paper or bamboo produces the straw. Prepare a filled burner, straw and bioethanol bucket; no separate liquid-burner crafting item is required.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.1: Apply the straw to the installed burner, then supply bioethanol by bucket or pipes. The fuel itself comes from mixing sugar, cinder flour and two biomass, yielding 125 mB per cycle. A bucket requires several cycles.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.text.2: Check heat in the basin above and actual fluid acceptance. Inventory items do not prove that the block was modified. Confirm the manual objective only when the straw-equipped burner accepts bioethanol and heats its basin. If it does not work, inspect straw application, fuel and fluid delivery separately.
codex.quest.ca_electric.burner.title: Liquid Blaze Burner
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.0: Connectors transfer FE between wires and compatible blocks. Prepare four ordinary connectors, suitable spools and a redstone relay. Start with a short alternator-to-motor or accumulator connection instead of wiring the whole base.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.1: Mount connectors on devices and set their modes with a wrench: the source side must extract energy and the consumer side deliver it. Join them with compatible wire. Large connectors and high-current spools follow their own restrictions.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.text.2: The relay permits transfer while receiving redstone, so missing signal can explain an empty receiver. Test with the lever on and off. If generation exists but the consumer is stopped, inspect endpoint modes and relay state. A visible wire alone does not verify correct energy direction.
codex.quest.ca_electric.connector.title: Connectors and Cables
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.0: A digital adapter lets ComputerCraft interact with supported Create devices. It is not a standalone universal display that shows arbitrary numbers immediately after placement. Prepare the adapter and choose an actual measurable block such as a speedometer or stressometer.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.1: Check for a compatible computer and connect the adapter as a peripheral according to the installed integration documentation. Supported devices include specific instruments, bearings, piston, pulleys and speed controller; an arbitrary nearby chest is not automatically supported.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.text.2: Begin by reading one value before commanding a moving machine. Compare it with the ordinary goggles tooltip. If no computer setup exists yet, retain the item and use a native Create display for now. The objective checks the adapter, not a program or automatic control of the entire factory.
codex.quest.ca_electric.digital.title: Digital Adapter
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.0: Electrum is used in electrical components and higher-current wire links. The installed Create Addition recipe mixes one gold and one silver ingot in a heated basin to produce two alloy ingots. Gold and zinc do not replace this recipe.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.1: Prepare silver from available pack metalworking, gold and an operating heated mixer. Test one pair of ingots, then make eight electrum ingots. If the recipe is unavailable, check whether JEI accepts the chosen silver ingot under its required tag.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.text.2: Some alloy is later rolled and pressed for components, so keep a separate reserve. Electrum spools serve compatible connector types rather than simply acting as faster copper everywhere. The add-on’s amulet concerns item charging; do not treat it as experience storage based on an older description.
codex.quest.ca_electric.electrum.title: Electrum
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_conversion: Manually compare two modes by RPM, generation, demand and charge change, then select a sustainable mode

Two steady operating modes make conversion between Create and FE easier to understand. Prepare an alternator at sufficient speed, a small accumulator and a motor driving one consumer. Keep stress and electrical readings accessible.

Record alternator input RPM and generation, then motor demand at a modest speed. Change only one setting and compare after the system settles. Watch whether stored energy rises or gradually disappears.

Confirm manually after comparing two modes and selecting one the source can sustain. If demand exceeds generation, storage only delays shutdown. Do not drive the alternator from the motor expecting a surplus. This trial helps choose a remote machine’s transmission without adding unnecessary infrastructure instead of fixing the energy balance.
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.ta: Manually verify a machine runs from storage during generator shutdown and charge rises again after generation resumes
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.te: An accumulator is useful when its reserve actually covers an ordinary source interruption. Prepare a working alternator on a shaft, a partly charged accumulator module and one controlled consumer. Do not test on an important factory’s only supply.

Stop the alternator’s shaft for a brief known interval and observe falling charge while the machine continues operating. Restore generation and check that the reserve recovers. If charge does not rise, inspect connection directions and generation balance.

Confirm manually after both observations. Record the tested interruption length: “accumulator” does not mean enough energy for an entire night. Reassess when adding consumers, since previous capacity may no longer suffice. For a moving craft, also account for time between docking and energy required for safe return.
codex.quest.ca_electric.guide_reserve.ti: A Reserve for a Brief Outage
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.0: An electric motor converts FE into rotation and conveniently powers an individual machine. Prepare the motor and a network with enough generation or stored energy. It suits a remote consumer where a long shaft is awkward.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.1: Connect electricity and set speed on the rear panel. Begin at modest RPM, run a shaft to one machine and observe energy use. Speed settings affect consumption; increase them only after stable operation.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.text.2: A motor is not a required engine for an ordinary Create train, which moves under its own rules. This objective concerns obtaining rotation from electricity. If the machine stops, separately check FE supply, connection, chosen speed and output-network stress. Another cogwheel cannot repair a fully discharged accumulator.
codex.quest.ca_electric.motor.title: Electric Motor
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.0: A portable energy interface transfers FE between contraption accumulators and a stationary network. A direct wire to a moving accumulator does not replace the contact. The objective requests one interface, but operation needs a pair, moving and stationary.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.1: Place working faces opposite each other with a valid one- or two-block gap and bring the contraption to the connection point. Set energy direction using stationary connector modes. Docking exposes the accumulators belonging to the moving construct.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.text.2: Check charge changes during a small transfer, then separation and continued movement. Redstone on the stationary interface prevents engagement, so account for nearby wiring. It suits onboard consumers; do not regard a battery as mandatory fuel for an ordinary Create train. Owning the device proves neither alignment nor charging.
codex.quest.ca_electric.pei.title: Portable Energy Interface
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.0: A rolling mill turns suitable metals into rods and wires. Input form matters: ingots generally become rods, while sheets become wires. Older advice to roll a rod again does not replace the specific material’s recipe.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.1: Prepare the mill, rotation and small stocks of copper ingots and sheets. Drop the chosen input on top, wait for processing and interact to retrieve output. Use one material for the first trial and compare the resulting item with JEI.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.text.2: If work stops, check power, recipe and free output. A belt and two funnels can automate the mill, but observe a manual cycle first. Rods and wire feed electrical components and spools; store them separately so similar metal intermediates do not complicate the next crafting steps.
codex.quest.ca_electric.rolling.title: Rolling Mill
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.0: A Tesla coil charges compatible energy items beneath it. It also has a dangerous mode that damages nearby entities when activated by redstone. Prepare the coil, FE supply and a dedicated place away from the workshop entrance.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.1: Connect power and place a supported discharged item beneath the working area according to Ponder. First verify that its charge increases without enabling the harmful mode. Keep retrieval access clear.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.text.2: Do not assume the coil processes sand into glass without an installed recipe; its verified role here is charging. If using entity-damage mode, enclose the area and prevent accidental signals from nearby levers. The item objective confirms the device; determine compatibility of an actual tool by comparing its energy before and after testing.
codex.quest.ca_electric.tesla.title: Tesla Coil
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.0: Copper wire is used for spools and electrical components, while a filled spool creates a link between connectors. Prepare eight wires by rolling copper sheets and craft a copper spool. Retain its empty spool after wiring.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.1: Place two compatible connectors, then interact with the first and second using the filled spool. Copper serves the corresponding low-current network. A more expensive spool does not make arbitrary connector types compatible.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.text.2: Inspect the line and verify actual energy transfer once a source exists. If a link cannot be created, check connector type and permitted distance. Eight crafting wires do not mean eight installed connections. Use the intended empty-spool interaction for removal rather than dismantling every machine to move one wire.
codex.quest.ca_electric.wire.title: Wire and Spools
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.0: The block armor inspection tool displays block properties in Big Cannons’ damage system. It helps select protection using data rather than appearance alone. Prepare the tool and several different building samples on the range.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.1: Inspect each block and compare its displayed properties. They are not a universal promise to withstand every charge: results also depend on projectile, speed and barrier construction. Test a small sample instead of the working base’s wall.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.text.2: A gas mask protects against relevant gas effects and does not replace armor, cover or distance from explosions. Equip it in a supported slot and read its hints before hazardous testing. Both items aid preparation, but assess protection under the selected in-game ammunition conditions rather than treating one successful test as a guarantee.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.armor.title: Armor and Protection
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.0: Autocannon ammunition combines a projectile, case and propellant into a completed feeding item. Prepare armor-piercing and flak variants using their own recipes, plus a tracer tip. A separate projectile component is not always a finished loaded round.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.1: Trace JEI steps from casing to completed ammunition and apply extra parts where required. Load a small uniform batch into the container. Tracers make trajectories visible; configure their placement and spacing separately from ordinary rounds.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.text.2: Test types individually on the range rather than mixing the first load. Flak effects and penetration serve different purposes, so identical impacts need not produce identical outcomes. Check consumption and case ejection after a short burst. Obtaining items confirms supplies; selecting ammunition for the installation requires observation.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autoammo.title: Autocannon Rounds
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.autocannon.text: An autocannon uses completed ammunition items, unlike a big cannon with separate propellant loads. Prepare a steel barrel, a finished breech and an ammunition container. Check required breech internals and connections against the installed type’s recipes.
Assemble compatible sections and place them on a suitable base. Load only a small amount of ammunition and provide space for ejected cases. Test aiming while empty, then issue a brief firing command.

Signal strength on the mount’s firing face affects rate, so do not begin at maximum. A recoil spring adds barrel movement as part of customization; one component does not establish a complete mechanism. Limit the firing sector and watch remaining ammunition so a short trial does not become an unintended long burst.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.0: A breech permits loading from the rear and must close completely before firing. Prepare a steel sliding breech and a quick-firing version. The latter is made by applying a quick-firing mechanism to a suitable sliding breech; finish the base component first.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.1: Rotation opens a sliding breech so ammunition can enter the exposed bore. For the quick-firing version, interact with its side: load the projectile first, then propellant, and close it. This differs from muzzle ramming.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.text.2: Remove the loader from the opening before firing. A sliding breech affects permitted gun strength, so a charge used with another closure may no longer be suitable. Configure an automatic arm only after manual testing, providing spent-case output and checking closed state.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.breech.title: Breeches
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.0: Bronze sections provide a different property set from cast iron. An installed recipe mixes copper, zinc and cinder flour under ordinary heat; a tin-based alternative depends on available pack materials. Copper and zinc without the addition make brass, so ingredients matter.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.1: Produce bronze, melt it under a foundry lid and cast the required sections. Bore the cooled workpieces with water and rotation as in the training foundry. Obtain three finished bronze barrels.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.text.2: Do not attach them casually to a cast iron chamber and regard the whole gun as bronze. Weak sections and breech properties still matter. Compare length and charge again before the new installation’s first shot. The objective confirms sections; range or reliability improvements require testing the assembled gun.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.bronze.title: Bronze
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.0: A drop mortar shell is intended for a special gun that fires when suitable ammunition is dropped into its bore. The requested item does not turn any upright barrel into a mortar. Prepare the shell and check a permitted configuration through its documentation and Ponder.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.1: Install and inspect the empty gun on a separate site first. Confirm the specific mortar-mode loading method and intended trajectory. Keep your head away from the bore during ammunition feeding.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.text.2: A high-arcing shot may land beyond the nearby visible backdrop, so inspect the landing area and limit the trial to one shot. This explosive shell differs from a mortar stone and ordinary grapeshot. The item objective confirms ammunition preparation; verify installation compatibility before loading and record the result in the range log.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.mortar.title: Mortar
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.nethersteel.tex: Nethersteel is an expensive cannon material with its own production chain. The installed mixing recipe combines a netherite scrap with four steel ingots or eight cast iron ingots, requires superheating and produces eight nethersteel ingots. Ordinary coal heating is insufficient.

Prepare superheating, make the alloy and perform the required casting, processing and component-finishing recipes. The objective needs three completed barrels and a screw breech, not merely alloy stock.

A screw breech is unlocked by rotation, then moved aside by machinery for loading. Return and close it before firing. Expensive material does not promise risk-free shooting: bore obstructions, incorrect assembly and unsuitable loads remain dangerous. Test the empty breech movement before using a verified ammunition combination.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.0: HE and AP shells have explosive behavior governed by a compatible fuze. Do not confuse an AP Shell with the non-explosive AP Shot. Prepare both shells and impact and timed fuzes, keeping them separate until configuration.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.1: Read the specific ammunition recipe and hints, then fit its fuze on the intended face. Configure timed delay before loading and test an impact fuze against a suitable isolated target. A shell without its intended detonation mechanism need not behave like a finished explosive round.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.text.2: Conduct the first trial away from structures with clearance behind and around the target. Avoid changing propellant and fuze simultaneously. Item objectives check components rather than assembled ammunition. Record configuration and outcome so repeated loading does not rely on memory.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.shells.title: Shells
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.0: Steel guns involve ordinary and built-up sections. Prepare steel from an available metalworking line and check recipes for the required castings. The objective needs three ordinary barrels and one built-up barrel, so a stock of ingots alone will not complete it.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.1: Ordinary workpieces undergo casting and boring. For a built-up section, manufacture the required layers, combine them with a cannon builder and finish by heating with fan airflow through lava. Transformation requires the correct layer set and takes time.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.text.2: A stack of nested layers is not necessarily a finished built-up block. Check the resulting item name and inspect connections. A reinforced section does not make a weak chamber or breech invulnerable. Preserve inspection access after moving it and test a permissible charge on a separate target.
codex.quest.cbc_advanced.steel.title: Steel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.0: A big cannon consists of compatible sections of one material and type. The objective requests three cast iron barrels, a chamber and a closed end. That end closes the breech side rather than plugging the muzzle: the projectile needs an open exit ahead.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.1: Lay components along one axis and inspect each orientation. The chamber holds propellant, while barrel sections define projectile travel. Owning three sections does not require using all of them in the first test gun.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.text.2: Compare length and minimum projectile speed with material strength. A long cast iron bore can require propellant exceeding its permitted limit, so keep the first gun short. Correct connections and mounting are still needed before firing. Inventory parts prove neither a continuous bore nor safe loading.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.barrel.title: First Barrel
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.0: A cast mould defines the cross-section of the cast component. A small mould is made by mechanically cutting a suitable log; select the saw result so you do not make ordinary planks. Prepare the mould, casting sand and a modest supply of molten cast iron.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.1: Use the mould to form a layer on the worksite, checking orientation against Ponder. Join layers as needed, then fill through suitable fluid delivery. Solidification begins after sufficient filling and takes time.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.text.2: A comparator distinguishes filling from completion: a finished cast outputs level 15. Remove the outer shell with the supported interaction afterward. The resulting bore is not finished and must be drilled. Avoid breaking valuable cast blocks with an ordinary pickaxe without checking harvesting rules; some become scrap.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.cast.title: Barrel Mold
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.0: A cast workpiece must be bored before a projectile can pass through it. Prepare a cannon drill, two extension poles, steady water and a rotating setup for the workpiece. The boring head is part of the installed mechanism; no separate head item is needed.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.1: Align drill and workpiece axes, mounting the casting on a rotating base as shown in Ponder. Supply water and begin a slow feed. Drill speed must be at least the workpiece’s rotational speed; faster operation also increases water demand.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.text.2: Read the failure tooltip if work stops: dry boring and insufficient speed need different corrections. Collect scrap separately and obtain the finished cast iron barrel without breaking it with an unsuitable tool. One successful trial matters more than a long queue of untested castings.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.drill.title: Boring
Manually move a finished cast section intact to a new location and check its orientation

A finished cast section can be lost through incorrect harvesting. Many such blocks return scrap to an ordinary pickaxe; a suitable Silk Touch pickaxe or contraption movement preserves them according to mod rules. Choose one small already bored training component.

Read the cannon-moving Ponder scene and prepare its destination before removal. With a tool, verify the required enchantment; with machinery, confirm that the section belongs to the assembly and has a clear route.

Confirm manually when the same finished section stands at the destination rather than a newly crafted replacement. Inspect orientation and future joints. This trial matters before expensive steel casts: foundry and range are usually separate, and intact transport should be part of production rather than luck.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.guide_cast_signa: A cannon cast can report filling and completion through redstone. Prepare a comparator and a small cast with a known metal requirement. Position observation so you do not approach molten metal for every inspection.

Connect the comparator and compare empty, partly filled and completed states. Values zero through fourteen indicate filling; fifteen means completion after solidification. Full volume and a finished component are therefore not the same moment.

Keep a clear indicator beside the walkway and wait for completion before removing the shell. The item objective only checks a comparator; observing three states explains its value. This arrangement supports later automatic cast removal once safe component extraction without turning it into scrap is understood.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.guide_load_limit: Manually record material, breech, projectile travel length and a load meeting minimum velocity without exceeding strength

A safe load is chosen from both maximum strength and minimum velocity for bore length. Cast iron makes this particularly apparent: an overly long first gun may lack a convenient permissible load. Prepare goggles and an empty short cannon on the range.

Read material, breech and propellant properties. Record projectile travel length and compare required initial speed with allowed stress. Include the projectile’s starting section when mod rules count it as part of the traveled bore.

Confirm manually only after selecting a compatible combination, not after a lucky shot. If required propellant exceeds strength, shorten or redesign the gun instead of hoping it survives. The record becomes a reference for new materials and distinguishes stored charges from the quantity permitted in one shot.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.0: A cannon loader moves ammunition along an axis like a specialized piston. The requested ram rod and worm are separate manual loading and extraction tools, not necessarily the loader block’s installed heads. An automatic rig also needs extension poles and a suitable fitted head.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.1: Align loader, ammunition and bore on one axis. Use a ram head for loading and a worm head to clear a jam. Ordinary mechanical loading requires returning the gun from its assembled state to blocks first.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.text.2: Begin with an empty stroke and verify complete withdrawal before gun assembly and firing. Automatic loading does not mean safe continuous fire without stage control. Keep a hand tool for maintenance: after a failed shot, never add another projectile on top of one left in the bore.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.loader.title: Autoloading
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.0: A basin foundry lid turns a Create basin into metal-melting equipment. For cast iron, first prepare an iron ingot and coal: heated basin compacting with a press produces a cast iron ingot. This is a separate step before melting, not an arbitrary mixture beneath the lid.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.1: Install the lid over a suitably heated basin and insert cast iron. Melting one ingot yields 90 mB of molten metal. A bucket needs at least 1000 mB, so one ingot is insufficient. Route fluid into a separate reservoir.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.text.2: If processing stops, inspect heat and available fluid output. Keep different molten metals in separate tanks and enclose the foundry area. The lid and bucket confirm preparation; later quests use the metal in an actual world-placed cast.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.melting.title: Melting Metal
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.0: A Cannon Mount assembles a gun and controls aiming, while a wheeled Cannon Carriage serves manual transport and operation. They are different bases. Prepare both items, but test one stationary mount without ammunition first.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.1: Position the gun relative to the mount as shown in Ponder. A signal to the hammer-marked face controls assembly, while kinetic inputs change aiming angles. The separate firing face must not accidentally receive power from the assembly lever.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.text.2: Test empty-gun aiming and its return to assembly position during disassembly. Learn the wheeled carriage controls separately: it cannot be automated like the mount. Leave ample clearance and stay outside a long cannon’s abrupt return path. Proceed to loading only after its base is verified.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.mount.title: Mount and Carriage
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.0: Propellant gives a projectile initial speed while stressing the gun. Register four packed gunpowder first, then use them to craft four charges: both objectives can be completed sequentially without duplicate supplies. This is not a mandatory single gun load. Compact three suitable gunpowder items with a basin press; combine packed gunpowder with an empty casing to make a charge.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.1: Store ammunition away from test-mount controls. Before loading, compare total propellant stress with chamber and breech strength, and velocity with bore length. Goggles-enhanced tooltips show these properties.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.text.2: Excess propellant can destroy the cannon; insufficient propellant can leave a projectile inside. Therefore “always use one” is unreliable too. Match a short first gun with a permissible charge. Avoid changing material, length and ammunition simultaneously, which makes failure difficult to diagnose.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.powder.title: Powder Charge
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_ba: The paper objective serves as a reminder to keep a test log; it does not prove manufacturing or firing. Prepare a sheet and choose a recording method beside the range, such as a book, sign or personal note. Preserving data matters more than carrying paper.
Before firing, record gun material, projectile travel length, ammunition type and propellant quantity. Note the aiming point and mount position. Add the outcome and any faults afterward.

Avoid changing several parameters between control shots. If a projectile fails to leave, unload and inspect the gun first; a new entry does not replace clearing a jam. The objective neither consumes paper nor reads its contents. Confirm an actual repeatable cycle manually in the next quest after safe inspection.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_ru: Manually fire a control shot, repeat loading, record the charge and verify the mechanism returns to its starting position

Acceptance ends with a repeatable-cycle trial, not one lucky hit. Prepare the checked range, a record of the chosen charge and two identical loads compatible with the gun. All observers must remain outside the firing line.

Fire a control shot, then repeat the loading cycle. Record the chosen charge and verify that the mechanism returns to its starting position. Between shots, confirm a clear bore and fully withdrawn loader; if a jam is suspected, extract the remaining object first.

Confirm manually after a successful in-world trial. The Codex does not automatically measure firing or establish safety with a checkbox. If the second cycle differs, examine breech, assembly and feeding states in order. Do not compensate for faulty loading with stronger propellant, which can damage the installation and surroundings.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.range_service_se: A separate range lets you test a cannon without endangering the working base. The target block is a visible aiming marker, not armor capable of stopping any projectile. Choose a remote site and inspect the area beyond the impact point.

Place the marker against a suitable safe background, designate the operator’s position and keep villagers, animals and players out of the firing direction. Check charge, projectile, breech and loading sequence for your specific gun.

Test assembly and aiming without ammunition first. Keep assembly and firing commands separate, and ensure disassembly does not sweep the barrel through anyone. The item objective confirms a prepared target; inspection establishes actual range readiness. The next objective prepares a record so repeated firing conditions can be compared.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.0: Casting sand forms the shell that holds molten metal until it solidifies. The installed recipe for one portion uses two ordinary sand blocks, dirt and a clay ball. Gather enough for sixteen portions, collecting clay near water beforehand.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.1: Combine the ingredients in a crafting grid and separate casting sand from ordinary construction sand. Keep it beside moulds and a clear area where vertical layers can be built.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.text.2: Do not substitute only sand and clay: dirt is required too. Future cast width and height determine consumption, so the objective’s stock does not guarantee any large gun. Make one training layer before spending everything. This lets you check cast construction and molten-metal delivery without rebuilding a tall casting column.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.sand.title: Casting Sand
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.0: Solid shot and grapeshot let you compare different firing results. Solid shot penetrates targets, while grapeshot separates on firing; these are not identical rounds with different appearances. Prepare both but test one first on a separate range.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.1: For muzzle loading, put propellant near the closed breech, with the projectile ahead toward the open muzzle, and ram it correctly. Before assembly, inspect the bore for extra objects. A mount receives its firing command on the designated face after loading, assembly and aiming.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.text.2: Do not ignite an arbitrary section based on advice for another mechanism. Verify the allowed combination of length, projectile and charge, then fire once. The item objective does not measure shooting; later trials check repeatability and loader return.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.shot.title: First Shot
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.0: Separately placed cannon blocks in Survival do not necessarily connect automatically. A cannon welder joins adjacent compatible sections but has restrictions on materials and cannon types. Prepare the tool and an aligned pair of cast iron components.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.1: Interact with the welder on two neighboring sections in sequence. They must share an axis, compatible connecting faces, material and cannon type. Check every joint instead of attempting to weld an arbitrary mixture of autocannon and big-cannon parts.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.text.2: Some components cannot be welded or are weakened by welding; manufacturing and moving a complete section may be preferable. The welder does not remove material-strength limits. Before mounting, inspect continuity again and remove foreign blocks from the bore. Owning the tool does not mean every joint has been processed.
codex.quest.cbc_foundry.welder.title: Welding Sections
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_batch: Now produce sixteen bread through the prepared operations. Begin with a small wheat supply and an empty output chest so the trial results do not mix with previously cooked food. Check that the millstone receives rotation.

Mill the grain, wash its flour into dough, then bake the dough in a separate hot processing area. Watch the first item at each transition. If an intermediate item does not change, inspect the airflow medium and allow enough processing time.

Collect sixteen bread into your normal inventory for credit; they do not need to be surrendered or consumed. Inventory tracking cannot distinguish production methods, so completion alone does not prove automation. Keep the bread for travel and use the remaining wheat to test interruptions and a full output chest.
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_run.t: Manually verify separate flour, dough and bread routes; a full output chest must not eject bread or return it to hot airflow

This bread-line trial checks behavior after normal operation and during a blockage. Prepare some wheat, clear access to the depots and temporarily disconnect other consumers if they make observation difficult. Manual confirmation becomes available after obtaining the trial bread.

Feed wheat and follow the route to ensure flour, dough and bread do not mix on the return path. Then fill the output chest and confirm that finished bread is neither thrown outside nor returned to the hot airflow. Free some space and verify that extraction resumes.

Confirm completion only after these observations in the world. The Codex does not measure item routes or know whether you tested a blockage. If bread is lost, fix the output or limit input first; increasing fan speed does not solve a full warehouse.
codex.quest.create_andesite.bakery_setup: A bread line makes good use of wheat by connecting milling, washing and baking. Prepare the millstone, fan and two depots listed in the objectives. These begin a test rig, but continuous operation also needs power, water, a heated processing area and transfers between stages.

First mill wheat. Put the first depot in airflow passing through water to turn flour into dough. Reserve the second for baking dough with a valid recipe, such as smoking airflow through a campfire; craft another fan for independent air streams.

Do not combine the wet and hot stages in one undivided area. Label the inputs and leave room to remove intermediate items manually. This quest checks equipment ownership; the next batch demonstrates a product, and a separate trial checks the entire line’s reliability.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.0: A mechanical belt transports items and also transmits rotation between its ends. Belt connectors are crafted from dried kelp, so harvest and dry kelp beforehand. Both objectives check the same item; they represent a stock of placement connectors, not individual belt segments.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.1: Place two compatible parallel shafts and use the connector on one, then the other. Begin with a short horizontal belt. Supply rotation and drop one inexpensive item onto it to see the travel direction.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.text.2: Connect the beginning to an input and the end to an output chest through funnels. Without extraction, items accumulate and stop the flow. Keep the belt’s working section clear above a press; internal belt segment items are not needed for construction.
codex.quest.create_andesite.belt.title: Mechanical Belts
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.0: A filled blaze burner provides controlled heat for a basin. Craft an empty burner first and let the quest register it before traveling to blazes in the Nether. Bring armor, food and fire protection, since capturing one requires approaching a dangerous creature.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.1: Use the empty burner on a living blaze to obtain a filled burner. Place it directly beneath the basin and supply suitable fuel, such as coal, for ordinary heat. Brass requires a heated basin with a mixer.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.text.2: Capturing a blaze does not automatically provide enough heat for every recipe. Special superheating uses blaze cakes, which are unnecessary for your first brass. Check the flame state and recipe before loading expensive materials, and add automatic fuel feeding after a reliable manual cycle.
codex.quest.create_andesite.blaze.title: Blaze Burner
Andesite casing forms the base of early machines. Gather logs, an axe and andesite alloy; eight casings need eight wooden bases. Avoid turning all your timber into planks, since this process requires stripped wood.

Place a log, strip its bark with the axe, then apply andesite alloy to the stripped block. Remove the resulting casing and use it in crafting. Repeat eight times, keeping some alloy for the machines themselves.

If nothing happens, make sure the log is stripped and you are holding alloy. A press does not make casings from ordinary planks. A deployer can automate this application later, but preparing casings manually beside the crafting table is quicker for your first press and millstone.
codex.quest.create_andesite.casing.title: Andesite Casing
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.0: Chutes move items between levels without long sloping belts. Prepare four and begin with a vertical run between an upper chest and a lower receiver. Keep access to both ends so you can inspect their contents.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.1: An ordinary chute transfers items downward. Upward movement uses airflow from an encased fan above or below; the chute itself does not take rotational input like a pump. If a fan blocks one end, arrange insertion or extraction from the side.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.text.2: A smart chute adds filtering, extracted stack size and redstone shutoff, but does not replace the fan. Test upward movement with one item and read the direction using goggles. This vertical route suits millstones, overhead storage and factory floors with little room for belts.
codex.quest.create_andesite.chute.title: Chutes
codex.quest.create_andesite.crafter_basi: Mechanical crafters assemble recipes from individual crafting cells placed in the world. Crafting them already requires brass, so this branch returns to the andesite workshop after heated metal processing. Five crafters make a small training rig, but cannot accommodate every large recipe layout.

Place the cells in one plane, supply rotation and use the wrench to direct their arrows toward a shared output. Load a simple suitable recipe and leave a receiver available for the result. Larger patterns require more crafters.

If assembly does not start, check occupied cells, arrow directions and power connections. Precision mechanisms are not assembled here; they require deployers and sequenced processing. The crafters’ next major role is the oversized crushing wheel recipe, which cannot fit a normal crafting table.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.0: A depot holds one stack of items at a convenient processing point. A press or deployer can work above it, while treated fan airflow can reach it from the side. Craft a depot and four andesite funnels, then place input and output chests nearby.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.1: First place material on the depot manually and confirm that the chosen machine processes it. Add funnels one at a time, checking direction: one supplies items and the other extracts them. The wrench helps change supported connection orientations.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.text.2: An andesite funnel lacks the full filtering features of a brass funnel. Extraction that happens too early may remove raw material before processing, so initially collect output manually. When finished sheets must be distinguished from ingots, use an appropriate belt arrangement or wait for brass filters.
codex.quest.create_andesite.depot.title: Depot and Funnels
codex.quest.create_andesite.ejector.text: A weighted ejector sends items through the air between points where a belt would be awkward. Crafting it requires a precision mechanism. Prepare a clear launching area and a generous receiving zone without lava, drops or exposed walkways.

Configure its target before placement, following the item’s hints and Ponder scene, then provide rotation to charge it. Begin with one inexpensive item and watch the entire trajectory. Make sure no wall or low ceiling obstructs the route.

The ejector can launch entities too, so stay off its platform while commissioning it. Prepare a separate safe landing if transporting players. After testing, arrange a receiving chest and suitable collection: an item landing on the ground has not yet reached secure storage.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.0: A fan creates airflow, while a medium in that airflow determines item processing. Water enables washing, lava enables blasting, ordinary fire or a campfire enables smoking, and soul fire enables special haunting recipes. For your first trial, wash flour because its result is easy to recognize.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.1: Place water between the fan and a depot holding flour, supply rotation and check airflow direction. Water must intersect the airflow, and the item must remain in the treated portion long enough. Ordinary ice does not provide universal freezing.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.text.2: Build a separate enclosed area with nonflammable walls for hot processing. Unsuitable items can be lost in dangerous media. Before connecting storage, test one JEI recipe and confirm that finished products leave instead of remaining in the shared airflow.
codex.quest.create_andesite.fan.title: Encased Fan
codex.quest.create_andesite.guide_washin: Washing is useful for more than flour: gravel has a recipe with useful random outputs. Prepare gravel, a water-fed fan stream and a separate depot. Keep this rig away from the bakery output so metallic products do not mix with food.

Place gravel in the water-treated airflow and wait for processing. Collect iron nuggets separately from other results. Output is probabilistic, so nine gravel do not promise nine nuggets; the installed recipe shows exact chances.

Accumulate nine nuggets and take them into your normal inventory. They are not surrendered and remain available for alloy or assembly. Nugget possession does not prove their origin, so actually follow at least one gravel batch through washing before expanding the line.
Manually separate nuggets and byproducts, fill an output, and verify item retention and recovery after freeing space

Mixed washing outputs make assembly supplies awkward: those machines need specific parts rather than everything on the depot. Prepare brass funnels, a filter and separate receivers. Bring a small gravel batch and clear space for byproducts.

Assign one output to iron nuggets and another to remaining results. Wash the batch and inspect both containers. Temporarily fill the nugget receiver; the line should retain items instead of spilling them into water or onto the floor.

Confirm manually only after correct sorting and the full-output trial. Stopping is acceptable if material remains safe; flow should resume when space is freed. Nuggets can now feed alloy or sequenced assembly while random byproducts retain a controlled route.
codex.quest.create_andesite.millstone.te: A millstone processes grain and other materials that have milling recipes. Craft the machine, collect wheat from a farm and leave room above it for feeding. Supply rotation through an appropriate gear connection; Ponder provides a useful placement reference.

Insert wheat, wait for milling to finish and extract the flour. This objective needs eight portions. Start small: the machine is easier to inspect before adjacent funnels immediately remove its output.

Do not insert arbitrary ore expecting guaranteed doubling. The specific JEI recipe determines output and byproducts. Flour opens the bread line, since washing can turn it into dough. Later you can connect the millstone’s input and output to storage; keeping access clear makes blockages easier to find.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.0: A mixer combines ingredients in a basin to make alloys, food mixtures and other products. Prepare the machine and basin, leaving space below the basin for a future burner. Position the mixer above it as shown in Ponder and connect its cogwheel to a transmission.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.1: For the first trial, use the unheated andesite alloy recipe: add andesite and a suitable nugget to the basin. The mixer needs sufficient speed; if its head will not descend, check rotation speed, ingredients and available capacity.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.text.2: Heated recipes need a separate heat source under the basin. Remove finished contents manually or through a configured output; a nearby depot alone does not guarantee extraction. After a successful test, prepare a brass line with separate arrangements for metal ingredients and burner fuel.
codex.quest.create_andesite.mixer.title: Mechanical Mixer
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.0: A mechanical press turns ingots into sheets for fans, pipes and other components. Prepare a press, depot, eight iron ingots and a working transmission. Mount the press above the depot as shown in its Ponder scene, so the working head can reach the item.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.1: Connect rotation to the press’s side shaft and place ingots on the depot. Wait for the stroke, then collect the iron sheets. Process one ingot first to check height and power before feeding the rest.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.text.2: A rotating shaft does not prove that the press is positioned correctly. If processing does not occur, check the depot spacing, available capacity and input recipe. Eight sheets let you craft further equipment; continuous belt feeding is easier to build after a successful manual trial.
codex.quest.create_andesite.press.title: Mechanical Press
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.0: A mechanical saw performs two distinct jobs: processing items on its work surface and cutting blocks in front of its blade. Craft one and begin with timber processing on a stable platform. Supply rotation and face the blade upward for cutting recipes.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.1: Place a suitable input on the work surface or feed it by belt. Some materials have several possible results; set the saw’s output filter to avoid receiving unwanted slabs or stairs. Compare the first recipe with JEI.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.text.2: Tree cutting uses a different orientation, and a saw on a moving contraption works when it encounters a tree. Keep these modes separate and stay clear of the blade. A stationary saw saves timber and alloy when producing parts; build a logging contraption after learning about moving structures.
codex.quest.create_andesite.saw.title: Mechanical Saw
codex.quest.create_andesite.sheets_line_: Prepare thirty-two iron ingots and an empty receiver for this trial batch. Before feeding, confirm that the press and belt rotate and that the output funnel leads to the correct chest. A small verified batch is more useful than an arbitrary warehouse full of inputs.

Load the ingots into the input chest and wait for processing. Watch items pause beneath the head and finished sheets move onward. If the line stops, check the output first: a full receiver can look like a broken press.

Take thirty-two iron sheets into your normal inventory. The objective checks possession without consuming metal, leaving the sheets available for pipes and later equipment. Items do not record how they were made; observe operation without manual feeding, then perform the separate restart trial.
Manually stop and restart rotation after a trial batch; processing must resume without manually repositioning items

Stopping the drive should not force you to rearrange materials on the production line. Prepare a few ingots and room in the output chest. A clutch or a safely disconnectable shaft section accessible from a walkway is useful for this trial.

Run a trial batch, then interrupt rotational power. After switching it back on, the line must resume processing without manually repositioning items. Watch the press, the section beneath it and the extraction point, rather than just belt movement.

If an ingot remains after restarting, check whether the press drive was disconnected separately from the belt and whether output is blocked. Confirm manually after a successful in-world trial. The Codex does not automatically record machine interruptions; the checkbox is your confirmation of the described result.

A sheet line removes the need to place every ingot under the press by hand. Gather a press, two belt connectors and two funnels, then prepare input and output chests. Leave enough space between them for the press head and transmission maintenance.

Join shafts with a belt and mount the press above its working section. Aim one funnel to feed ingots and the other to extract into the output chest. Place an ingot manually first and confirm that it passes under the press before unloading.

If an unprocessed ingot leaves, check press height and output-funnel position. The route must not bypass the machine on a neighboring belt. Owning the components completes preparation; a trial batch and a stop-and-restart test will establish how the automatic line behaves.
Andesite alloy is needed for shafts, cogwheels and your first machines. Mine ordinary andesite underground and collect iron; smelt the ore and turn some ingots into nuggets. Zinc nuggets also work, but there is no need to search specifically for zinc to start your workshop.

In a crafting grid, place two andesite blocks and two nuggets diagonally opposite one another in a 2×2 square to make one alloy. Prepare sixteen alloys and keep some stone in reserve. Polished andesite does not replace ordinary andesite in this recipe.

A mixer will later make alloy more economically. Manual crafting currently supplies everything needed to start rotation; avoid spending the entire batch on one component, or the next machine will send you back to the mine.
codex.quest.create_basics.andesite.title: Andesite Alloy
A large water wheel expands an early workshop without using fuel. It needs more clearance around its axis, so mark out the channel and maintenance area first. Install it near the existing transmission and leave a way to disconnect the new branch temporarily.

Supply flowing water and check rotation before joining the main network. A large wheel has its own speed; sources working together must deliver compatible rotation. Adding more water cannot correct an incompatible connection.

Measure the resulting capacity with a stressometer before attaching more machines. The large wheel adds capacity, while gearing determines the required working shaft speed. Keeping the old wheel as a separate source for an auxiliary line is useful when a shared connection becomes cramped.
codex.quest.create_basics.bigwheel.title: Large Water Wheel
Cogwheels connect rotating axes and let you choose a machine speed. Prepare four small and two large cogwheels: enough to compare a direct transmission with a speed change. Check their crafting ingredients in JEI, then leave space in front of the machine to rearrange the gears.

Meshing gears reverse rotation. Driving a small gear from a large one doubles speed; driving a large gear from a small one halves it. Not every neighboring position meshes correctly, so use the Ponder scene as a placement reference.

Speeding up a consumer increases stress without increasing source capacity. If everything stops after changing the transmission, restore the lower speed and compare instrument readings. This gear pair will help with mixers, presses and awkwardly positioned machine inputs.
codex.quest.create_basics.cogwheel.title: Cogwheels
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.0: Engineer’s goggles reveal extra information about the machine you are looking at. Craft and equip them in a suitable equipment slot; use the helmet slot for a reliable initial check. Carrying them in a bag is not enough.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.1: Look at a source, an operating consumer and a fluid tank. The information depends on the block: some show stress and speed, others contents or boiler status. Read the units so that capacity is not mistaken for rotational speed.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.text.2: If an expected line is missing, check your equipment and aim at the actual relevant block. Goggles help locate bottlenecks without extra instruments, but do not replace observing items leaving the machine. Remember that replacing combat headgear matters during dangerous expeditions; workshop diagnosis is best done somewhere safe.
codex.quest.create_basics.goggles.title: Engineer's Goggles
A dedicated production branch lets you stop machines while the source and auxiliary equipment keep rotating. Prepare a clutch and lever, then find a transmission section before the press or millstone. Choose somewhere accessible without entering moving parts.

Insert the clutch into a shaft gap and power it with the lever. Confirm that the source continues while the selected consumer stops. Remove the signal and check that rotation resumes in its original direction.

Do not place the switch after a branch you also intended to service, since that branch would remain powered. Label the lever and keep it visible. The item objective checks two components; the described installation supports the next experiment in diagnosing stops through instruments.
codex.quest.create_basics.guide_stress_r: Manually identify the stop using instruments and restore rotation by disconnecting load, reducing speed or correcting direction

A stopped network does not always need another generator. Prepare instruments, an isolated-branch switch and a consumer with adjustable gearing. Use an inexpensive test rig without interrupting water to an operating boiler.

Compare speed and stress with the machine connected and disconnected. If the rig is overloaded, remove excess load with the clutch or reduce consumer speed. For conflicting directions, correct the transmission rather than adding capacity. You need not overload a large factory deliberately; reproducing a safe case on a separate network is enough.

Confirm manually once you can explain the stop and restore rotation with one chosen correction. Restore the working setting and verify that the machine produces output. This trial turns goggles and instrument readings into an understandable repair sequence.
codex.quest.create_basics.handcrank.text: A hand crank lets you test a small machine before building a permanent power source. Craft it and place it on a free shaft end. A short transmission and one consumer are enough for the experiment; a crank cannot replace power for an entire factory.

Hold interaction on the crank to rotate the network. Sneaking reverses its direction, which is useful for moving a piston a short distance or checking which way a belt travels. Watch your food supply because manual operation uses hunger.

If the crank does not move the machine, check its connection and stress. During testing, do not make a moving platform your only escape route. Replace the crank with a water wheel afterward, and keep it for commissioning isolated machines away from the workshop.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.task.0: Open the cogwheel Ponder scene by holding W over the item
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.0: Ponder demonstrates a mechanism in a small interactive scene, showing placement, connections and startup order. Start with a cogwheel, because meshing gears are easier to understand in motion than in a static crafting recipe. Open your inventory or JEI and hover over the item.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.1: Hold W unless its binding has changed. Watch the cogwheel scene, move between steps and rotate the camera to see the axes. If no key hint appears, check the Ponder control binding and whether the selected item has scenes.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.text.2: After watching, reproduce one gear pair beside the workshop. Ponder explains block behavior, while JEI shows recipes in this installed pack. Use both: an illustrated setup does not mean its materials are already in your inventory.
codex.quest.create_basics.ponder.title: Ponder Scenes
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.0: Sails let you finish and expand an operating windmill. A white sail and an empty sail frame both count as suitable sail blocks: fabric changes appearance rather than making one block provide several units of capacity. Prepare eight white sails using the JEI recipe.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.1: Stop the bearing and wait for the structure to become ordinary blocks. Add sails to the connected wings, check symmetry to keep walkways convenient, and assemble the windmill again. Symmetry looks pleasant, but the source primarily cares about the number of counted sail blocks.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.text.2: Compare speed before and after expansion. The bearing evaluates its assembled structure, so extra sails in a nearby chest do nothing. If there is no increase, check whether the added blocks joined the assembly and whether the windmill has reached its effective limit.
codex.quest.create_basics.sail.title: Sails
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.0: A shaft carries rotation along its axis and connects a source to a machine. Craft eight shafts from andesite alloy using the JEI recipe; a crafting table is enough for now. A mechanical saw will later produce six shafts from one alloy.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.1: Place several shafts end to end. Their axis must continue the source output and the machine input: touching side surfaces does not create a connection. Use cogwheels or a gearbox to turn the transmission around a corner.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.text.2: Check movement at both ends before building a long main line. Shafts neither increase speed nor add capacity. If the network stops after a machine is connected, look for excessive stress or conflicting directions instead of trying to fix it with more shafts.
codex.quest.create_basics.shaft.title: Shaft
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.0: A speedometer measures its shaft speed, while a stressometer shows how much network capacity is being used. Craft both instruments and connect them to the same network as the working machine. An instrument on an isolated shaft says nothing about the neighboring line.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.1: Read them without a consumer, then connect a press or millstone. Read speed and stress again after changing the gearing. This reveals why faster processing can stop the entire workshop: the consumer needs more available capacity.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.text.2: During an overload, temporarily disconnect the new machine to restore rotation. Then reduce its speed or add a source. Avoid joining opposing outputs at random: conflicting directions are different from insufficient capacity. Leave instruments visible from a walkway so the next fault can be diagnosed without removing the floor.
codex.quest.create_basics.stress.title: Stressometer and Speedometer
codex.quest.create_basics.waterwheel.tex: A water wheel supplies continuous rotation without fuel. Prepare the wheel, a water bucket and solid blocks for a small channel. Arrange the spillway so flowing water touches the paddles; placing the wheel beside still water is not enough.

First confirm that the wheel itself rotates, then run a shaft to the workspace. Add channel walls, since spilled water can wash away redstone dust and carry loose items off the floor. Ponder illustrates the arrangement of flow and shaft.

Connect one machine and compare its behavior with the disconnected network. If capacity is insufficient, add compatible sources or reduce consumer speed. A wheel suits your first press and millstone, but owning the item does not verify that an installed source works.
A windmill generates rotation from an assembled moving structure with sails. Place a windmill bearing with its output toward the planned transmission, then build a connected frame in front of its working face. At least eight suitable sail blocks are needed to start; this quest asks for sixteen frames.

Sail frames count too. Attach the wings to the block in front of the bearing, using sail connections and glue where other frame blocks need joining. Leave clearance around the structure and interact with the bearing to assemble it.

If it will not start, check the sail count and their connection to the bearing. Once assembled, connect a shaft at the back. Stop and disassemble the windmill before extending its wings; a large moving structure is awkward to repair.
codex.quest.create_basics.windmill.title: Windmill
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.0: The wrench helps position Create components precisely and rebuild the workshop neatly. Craft it using JEI and keep it near your shafts on the hotbar. A pickaxe breaks blocks, but does not replace orientation controls.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.1: Interact with an installed component using the wrench to rotate it or change an available variant. Sneak-interacting removes supported blocks. Practice on a single shaft first, since targeting different faces can produce different results.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.text.2: Before dismantling an operating line, stop rotation and collect items from exposed sections. Do not assume that every inventory and every neighboring machine state will survive removal. The wrench is especially useful for funnel direction, transmission axes and train assembly; it saves materials when one rotation can correct a placement mistake.
codex.quest.create_basics.wrench.title: Wrench
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.0: A mechanical arm transfers items between preselected points. It is not required for the first precision mechanism; instead, a mechanism is part of its own recipe. Prepare the arm after sequenced assembly is running and leave clear space beside several depots.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.1: Before placing the arm, use it to select supported inputs and outputs. Repeated interaction changes a point’s role; check the selection colors, then place the arm and supply rotation. Use an intermediate depot or funnel for an unsupported inventory.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.text.2: Try transferring one stack, then fill one output. The distribution mode determines whether the arm skips a blocked destination or waits. It has no universal filter of its own; brass funnels can provide restrictions. An arm is useful for supplying burners and several nearby operations.
codex.quest.create_brass.arm.title: Mechanical Arm
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_b: Produce eight precision mechanisms using the prepared loop. Refill all three component supplies beforehand and empty the outputs. Random outcomes mean more golden workpieces are needed than completed products, so do not budget inputs solely around eight.

Feed sheets gradually and watch unfinished mechanisms return. Each passes through five trios of operations; completed mechanisms and byproducts must leave the line. If one hand stops, check its material before increasing the speed of the entire installation.

Collect eight mechanisms into your normal inventory for credit. You keep the items; the Codex checks possession rather than production history. Reserve some output for spare arms and speed control. After this batch, test a temporary nugget shortage so routine supply exhaustion does not require rebuilding the queue manually.
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_r: Manually remove and restore iron nuggets; the queue must resume and completed mechanisms must not enter a sixth lap

Sequenced assembly should survive a missing component without losing workpieces. Prepare several unfinished mechanisms on the line and make sure output chests have space. This trial concerns correct recovery rather than record speed.

Temporarily remove the iron nuggets, then restore them. Verify that the workpiece queue resumes and completed mechanisms are not sent around for a sixth lap. Follow at least one workpiece through the final stage and output, including any byproduct it produces.

After a successful trial, confirm manually; the Codex does not automatically watch deployer state. If the queue stays stopped, inspect the hand’s filter and return routes. Do not push workpieces past the missing operation: repaired feeding should let them continue their own sequence without losing a stage.
codex.quest.create_brass.assembly_line_s: A return loop removes manual repetition of fifteen operations per workpiece. Prepare the three deployers, brass funnels and belts listed, plus separate component stocks. The loop entrance must accept golden sheets and returning unfinished mechanisms.

Arrange operations in this order: small cogwheel, large cogwheel, iron nugget. Give each hand a filter and its own feed. After the third stage, extract completed products and return only the unfinished mechanism to the first stage.

Provide a separate byproduct outlet: byproducts appear when the recipe finishes and must not block the return route. Run one workpiece first and follow every lap. Item objectives confirm equipment, not filters or routing; the batch and supply-interruption trial will demonstrate those.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.0: Brass is needed for filtering funnels, deployers and more advanced automation. Prepare copper and zinc ingots, a mixer with a basin, and a fueled blaze burner. Zinc is mined as an ore resource and smelted, so reserve storage for it beforehand.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.1: Put one copper and one zinc ingot into the heated basin: the recipe produces two brass ingots. Ordinary heat is enough; blaze cakes are unnecessary. Check mixer rotation and wait for its head to descend.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.text.2: Repeat enough times to obtain sixteen ingots, replenishing burner fuel as needed. If mixing stops, inspect heat, speed and basin contents. Divide the first brass between casings and feeding equipment; spending it all on decoration would delay the next branch, which needs several different mechanisms.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass.title: Brass
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_casing.te: Brass casing connects your new metalworking capability with precision machinery. Prepare eight stripped logs and brass ingots. Making casings beside the crafting table is convenient when deployer and funnel components are already stored there.

Place a log, strip its bark and apply a brass ingot to the stripped surface. Collect the casing and repeat until you have eight. The method resembles andesite casing production, but uses a different covering material.

Do not substitute copper for brass or press planks: that produces another result or fails the recipe. Keep part of the stock for later equipment. The casing itself neither filters items nor receives commands; those features belong to machines crafted from it. You can now move on to deployers for the first sequenced assembly operations.
codex.quest.create_brass.brass_funnel.te: Brass funnels select transferred items and extraction amounts, while tunnels distribute belt traffic. Prepare four funnels, two tunnels and an ordinary filter. Mix two easily distinguished materials in a small chest for testing.

Assign one funnel a specific item and direct it to a separate receiver. Then configure an item-list filter and check its allow or deny mode. Choose the distribution behavior between available outputs separately on the tunnel.

An ordinary filter is not an attribute filter: property-based rules belong to another item. Test sorting with a small mixed batch, especially funnel direction. These devices are needed in assembly loops, where only unfinished intermediates should return while completed mechanisms and random byproducts must leave the cycle.
Chromatic compound appears among Create’s items, but this pack’s installed recipes provide no confirmed survival method to obtain it. Older advice about light, shadow and special casings does not describe an active production branch. This quest instead teaches practical sorting by item properties.

Craft an attribute filter and open its settings with a sample item. Select an available property from the displayed list, then place the filter in a brass funnel on a separate chest. Use an inexpensive mixture for testing.

Confirm that the rule passes the expected items and retains the others. Choose conditions offered by the installed interface rather than assumptions based on names. Such a filter helps a mixed tool or food store without requiring an invented rare-material chain.
codex.quest.create_brass.chromatic.title: Sorting by Attributes
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.0: Crushing wheels process materials with crushing recipes, including certain ores and obsidian. Their oversized recipe uses mechanical crafters; prepare enough cells for the entire JEI pattern. A working pair needs two wheels.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.1: Place the wheels at the correct spacing and drive them in opposing directions so items are drawn into the gap. Provide collection underneath and controlled feeding above. Test with one inexpensive material that has a known recipe.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.text.2: Fence off the dangerous gap: wheels damage entities. Stop the drive before maintenance and never retrieve items from inside an operating crusher. Product quantities and byproducts depend on the recipe, so do not assume identical doubling for every ore. Washing may provide a useful separate processing stage afterward.
codex.quest.create_brass.crushing.title: Crushing Wheels
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.0: A deployer repeats individual player actions: using an item, placing a block or attacking in its selected mode. Prepare two devices and an accessible rotational drive for the first assembly operation. Leave space in front as shown in Ponder: it acts at the position two blocks ahead.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.1: Give the hand its required item and test on a simple target. The wrench switches use and attack modes, while the filter restricts its held contents. For belt processing, face the deployer down toward the intermediate item.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.text.2: If the hand moves without a result, check mode, held item and target position. Redstone stops new actions after the current cycle finishes. Sequenced assembly consumes components, so provide separate feeds for small cogwheels, large cogwheels and nuggets instead of one unfiltered mixed input.
codex.quest.create_brass.deployer.title: Deployer
A precision mechanism comes from sequenced assembly of a golden sheet, rather than ordinary crafting. Prepare golden sheets, small and large cogwheels and iron nuggets. For the first trial, move the intermediate item manually between deployers or change the item held by one hand.

Apply a small cogwheel, then a large cogwheel, then an iron nugget. The installed recipe repeats that trio five times. Watch the unfinished mechanism’s state so the next operation is not attempted out of order.

The outcome is probabilistic, so four sheets do not guarantee four mechanisms. Keep spare components and collect byproducts separately. Obtain four completed mechanisms in your normal inventory to access mechanical arms and speed controllers. A full return loop is easier to build once the sequence is understood with one workpiece.
codex.quest.create_brass.precision.title: Precision Mechanism
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.0: An item vault combines several blocks into a large machine-accessible inventory. Prepare four blocks and insertion and extraction equipment: its contents cannot be opened manually like a normal chest. Build an output before loading valuable materials.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.1: Construct a valid elongated shape and attach a funnel to a wall. Its square cross-section can be up to three blocks wide, and length is limited by that width. Verify formation, then insert a small stack of stone.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.text.2: Arrange extraction into an accessible chest and confirm that all test items return. The vault does not sort its contents; connected logistics need filters. This buffer suits the gap between crushing and further processing, or a freight contraption. Leave readable external indication so a large closed inventory does not conceal an overflow.
codex.quest.create_brass.vault.title: Item Vault
A mechanical bearing rotates an attached structure using an external drive. Unlike a windmill bearing, it consumes rotation rather than creating a source from sails. Prepare a bearing and a small glued crossbar for testing.
