Place the structure in front of its working face and supply rotation from behind. Inspect clearance for a full turn, including corners and projecting tools. Begin at low speed to see which blocks joined the assembly.

If some remain behind, stop and check their connection to the block in front of the bearing. Account for stop and disassembly settings when returning it to blocks. This drive suits a circular farm or rotating bridge; use a windmill bearing and suitable sails when the purpose is power generation.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.cart.tex: A cart assembler turns a structure above rails into a moving contraption. This is separate from Create’s large train system. Prepare an assembler, minecart, ordinary rails and a small glued platform with an empty chest.

Place the assembler on a rail section and position the platform in its assembly area. Bring in the minecart and control assembly as shown in Ponder, first testing a short straight route. A coupling connects suitable minecarts; it does not convert Create railway bogeys into ordinary carts.

Stop at a disassembly point after traveling and inspect the cargo and platform membership. Keep the first route away from dangerous bends and drops. Cart contraptions support early mining and transport, but their mounting, control and rails differ from a later station-built locomotive.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.clockwor: A clockwork bearing builds moving hands tied to world time. It is a specialized clock mechanism, not an ordinary bearing with one fixed speed. Prepare it and short, easily distinguished hands made from inexpensive blocks.

Assemble the hands and connections according to Ponder, providing the separate hour and minute attachments. Supply the required rotation and check dial orientation. Leave space between the hands and wall so the clock remains readable from outside. Do not glue the hands together: the minute hand is a separate structure in front of the hour hand.

Observe their positions at different times of the game day. If both parts behave identically, inspect their attachments rather than only their lengths. A clock suits a central square or station; keep critical production control on signals and sensors, since a visible clock hand is not itself an electrical timer.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.controls: Contraption controls expose supported functions on an assembled machine. A seat holds a passenger on a moving structure, but does not make it a steerable train. Prepare the controls and green seat requested.

Glue both blocks to a test platform and assemble it using your familiar drive. Check seating and panel interaction. Available controls depend on the structure: an elevator selects floors, while other contraptions expose their relevant toggles.

Do not confuse this block with separate train controls. Before boarding, retain an external stop and ensure you can dismount safely after stopping. A slow, short journey is enough for the first trial. Once the seat and panel are checked, move them to a working drill or passenger cabin without assuming a seat replaces a brake.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.elevator: An elevator pulley moves a cabin between marked floors. Prepare the pulley and ordinary redstone contacts first: stationary contacts become elevator contacts during assembly. A cabin and two landings need three contacts, so this objective uses the obtainable starting components.

Build a glued cabin with a contact facing a stationary one. Mark the second floor with another contact in the same vertical column. Supply rotation and assemble the elevator by interacting with the pulley. Configure floor names and pulse-driven calls.

Test the empty cabin at both floors first. Fence the shaft, retain an emergency exit and ensure doors do not expose a drop when the cabin is absent. Contraption controls inside allow floor selection; having the parts in inventory does not verify correct stops.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.gantry.t: A gantry carriage travels along a special gantry shaft and carries an attached structure. The single carriage requested is not a complete system: you also need gantry shafts, power and glue. Begin with a short horizontal guide above a clear area.

Build a continuous guide, mount the carriage in the correct orientation and attach a small platform. Supply rotation to the shaft and test travel in both directions. Review Ponder’s movement and rotational-transfer modes before connecting working tools.

Do not leave a guide end over a drop, and define the useful travel range beforehand. If the structure will not move, check shaft type and carriage connection; ordinary shafts cannot replace gantry shafts. After a short trial, the system can carry a drill or freight attachment along a fixed line.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.glue.tex: Super glue connects blocks that must move together. Chassis helps assemble larger structures with configurable attachment ranges. Prepare glue, four linear chassis and a few inexpensive blocks for a first platform.

Select the future assembly area with glue according to the item hints. Keep the floor, warehouse wall and rotational source outside the selection. Configure chassis attachment direction and range, and prepare the required faces as shown in Ponder.

Inspect the highlighted attached blocks before starting. A touching chest or tool does not always join automatically. Move the structure a short distance and confirm that everything intended travels with it. Once connections are understood, you can build piston gates, rotating farms or lifting platforms without accidentally attaching half the workshop.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.guide_ha: Open the mechanical harvester Ponder scene and review its contraption operation

A rotating harvester teaches a useful contraption without a large drilling rig. Prepare a mechanical bearing, a few frame blocks, a harvester, a chest and glue. Choose a small mature wheat plot with a surrounding walkway.

Open the harvester’s Ponder scene and study the working-edge orientation on a moving structure. Build a short bearing arm so the harvester passes over the intended crops and the chest belongs to the same glued assembly. Begin with one slow turn.

Watch that the arm does not include a fence or neighboring base and that mature crops are actually processed. Viewing the scene confirms familiarization; farm operation remains a separate observation. Before expansion, learn how the chosen crop behaves after harvesting and whether your arrangement needs additional planting.
Manually verify crops enter onboard storage and transfer through docked interfaces to a stationary chest without disassembly

Crops inside a moving chest have not yet reached bakery storage. Prepare a pair of portable storage interfaces, a funnel or another extraction method, and an empty stationary chest. Use the small harvester already tested.

Attach one interface to the contraption and place its counterpart opposite the passing position at a valid distance. Connect extraction on the stationary side. Harvest a little crop and wait for docking while watching items reach the final chest.

Confirm manually when crops complete the route without disassembling the machine or carrying items out of onboard storage. If docking occurs but items remain, check extraction direction and free space. This unloading turns the farm into a bakery input and avoids stopping the bearing after every harvest.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.piston.t: A mechanical piston moves a structure in a straight line, while extension poles determine available travel. Prepare the piston and four poles. For the first trial, choose a short horizontal workspace and a small glued panel instead of a complete wall.

Install poles along the piston axis and supply rotation from the side. Reversing the drive changes movement. If the panel must return with the head, use suitable sticky attachment and test it before the first full extension.

Watch travel limits and clearance for the entire structure, including protruding parts. An ordinary piston does not make every separate block an attached load. Stop rotation before correcting connections. A successful test opens sliding gates and bridges; a sequenced gearshift can later program precise travel.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.pulley.t: A rope pulley raises and lowers an attached structure. It suits a small freight platform or vertical drill, but does not choose floors like a dedicated elevator mechanism. Craft the pulley and prepare a solid support over a shallow testing area.

Supply rotation, lower the rope to the platform and check its glued attachments. Reversing rotation changes travel direction. Begin without a passenger or cargo, watching the lower limit and the return upward.

Stay out from beneath the moving platform and leave a ladder out of the shaft. If only part of the structure moves, stop and fix its connections. Add containers and tools after testing. For a passenger elevator with floor calls, use the next branch with landing contacts and cabin controls.
codex.quest.create_contraptions.tools_co: Tools give a moving structure a job: drills break blocks ahead, harvesters collect suitable mature crops, ploughs work soil, and rollers alter surfaces according to their mode. Prepare the four listed tools and a small testing area.

Attach tools facing their intended route and connect storage to the same assembly. Start with one tool and a few dirt blocks. Placement operations need material in an accessible contraption inventory.

Do not assume all these blocks work exclusively while moving: some also have stationary powered uses. Check the specific mode you intend to use. Fence the drill route and never aim it at the base. Before building a large farm or road machine, verify that results and dropped items are actually collected.
A copper backtank stores compressed air for a diving helmet and certain tools. Craft it, then reserve an accessible rotating transmission section in the workshop. A freshly crafted item should not be assumed charged.

Place the backtank as a block and connect rotation. Wait for it to fill while watching its air reserve, then remove and equip it in the chest slot. Higher speed helps charging, but the source and connection must work correctly.

Check the charge again before traveling. Compatible equipment consumes air, which does not automatically refill merely because you stand on land wearing the tank. It occupies an armor slot, so account for enemy protection. Bring a helmet for the first dive and choose somewhere with an easy route to the surface.
codex.quest.create_copper.backtank.title: Copper Backtank
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.0: A steam boiler converts heat and water into capacity for engines. Prepare the eight tanks and two engines requested, plus a pump, pipes and a heat source. The inventory set alone is not an operating boiler.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.1: Build a valid tank, provide heat underneath and mount engines on its walls. Supply continuous water, then create engine outputs by applying shafts. Keep the water pump on an independent drive for startup, or a stopped boiler may lose its own water supply.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.text.2: Use goggles to inspect three limits: size, water and heat. Increasing one parameter is useless when another is limiting output. Add load gradually; do not expect full output from two engines with any arbitrary eight-tank arrangement. Reliable generation begins with steady supplies and accessible burners.
codex.quest.create_copper.boiler.title: Steam Boiler
Copper casing is used in Create fluid machinery and other devices. Prepare four logs, an axe and four copper ingots. Smelt the copper first; copper sheets are not needed for this operation.

Place a log and strip its bark with the axe. Apply a copper ingot to the stripped wood, then collect the resulting casing. Repeat for the full stock. This is an item application to a world block, not plank pressing.

If no casing appears, check the stripped log and held material. Do not confuse casing with a fluid tank: it stores no water itself. The four casings support later equipment; divide remaining copper between pipes and sheets so water-service development does not stall.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.0: A copper diving helmet uses backtank air for underwater breathing, while diving boots help movement along the bottom. Craft both and fully charge the backtank before leaving. A helmet without an air supply does not grant unlimited diving time.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.1: Equip the set and test it beside a gently sloping shore. Enter the water, inspect remaining air time and try walking in the boots. Find an easy exit beforehand: heavy boots behave differently from ordinary swimming.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.text.2: During an expedition, reserve air for the return journey and watch for enemies. This equipment is for water and does not protect against lava. It helps explore submerged places, lay underwater pipes and operate a hose, but easy surface access remains part of preparation even with a full backtank.
codex.quest.create_copper.diving.title: Diving Gear
codex.quest.create_copper.guide_boiler_r: Manually stop and restore heating; with independent water supply, the boiler must power a machine again without carrying buckets

A verified restart is more useful than an impressive boiler that only works until its first shutdown. Choose a time without active production commitments, prepare fuel and keep the independent water supply running. Do not alter reservoir geometry during the trial.

Stop supplying fuel and wait for heat to fall while observing the boiler limit with goggles. Restore burner supplies and check that capacity recovers. Reconnect consumers gradually to distinguish insufficient heat from network overload.

Confirm manually when the boiler again powers the chosen machine without bucket-carrying or manually starting the pump line. If restart fails, record and correct the limiting parameter. Keep a modest maintenance fuel reserve nearby rather than directing the entire warehouse into continuously burning burners.
codex.quest.create_copper.guide_boiler_s: A boiler needs water before its engines can power consumers. If its only pump is powered by the same boiler, a shutdown can create a circular dependency. Prepare a water wheel and a separate pump for reliable startup.

Build a small water-powered drive and connect it only to the supply pump. Run a pipe to the boiler, then check direction and sufficient delivery using the water reading in goggles. Adjust pump speed through gearing without unnecessarily changing the whole engine room.

Stop the production branch and confirm that the pump keeps rotating. This objective checks components; the next trial verifies an actual restart. Continuous water does not replace burner fuel, so each boiler limitation needs separate attention.
codex.quest.create_copper.netherite_divi: Netherite diving equipment allows work in extreme heat, but lava protection requires a complete suitable set. The two requested items, helmet and backtank, are not the whole set: netherite leggings and netherite footwear are also required. The air supply must be charged.

Upgrade the copper equipment using the installed smithing recipes in JEI, then check all four armor slots. Prepare an independent safe exit from lava and backup fire resistance for the first trial. Do not begin by jumping into a deep lake.

The helmet consumes air to protect against fire and lava; watch the reserve and return early. Merely carrying the helmet and tank completes item objectives without establishing player protection. Once checked, the set supports work around lava sources where copper diving equipment cannot be used.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.0: A steam whistle provides an audible signal and adds character to an engine room or train. It does not increase boiler capacity. Craft a whistle and prepare an accessible fluid-tank wall with sufficient heat.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.1: Mount it on the tank and activate it to test the sound. Applying another whistle item extends the installed whistle and lowers its pitch, while the wrench switches octaves. Engineer’s goggles help identify its current pitch.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.text.2: If no sound plays, inspect mounting and heat before rebuilding the wiring. Begin with one brief signal, especially near a shared base. Then link it to a clear event such as equipment readiness. Several continuously sounding alarms stop being useful; retain a visible display for heat and water information.
codex.quest.create_copper.whistle.title: Steam Whistle
codex.quest.create_fluids.chocolate.text: Liquid foods need ingredients, containers and a free receiver at the same time. Prepare sugar, cocoa and milk for chocolate. In a heated basin, a mixer combines sugar, cocoa beans and 250 mB of milk into 250 mB of chocolate; a bucket takes several such batches.
Honey can be drained from bottles: each provides 250 mB of fluid and returns a glass bottle. Harvest from bees with safe hive access and account for their reaction to collection.

Keep chocolate and honey in separate tanks, then fill one bucket of each for the objective. If the drain stops, inspect empty-bottle storage and fluid output. Owning two buckets confirms the products; a continuous food line additionally needs container return and reliable ingredient supplies.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.0: A hose pulley draws fluid from a body of liquid or fills an area with it. Craft one with a pump and pipes, then choose a small safe pond for the first experiment. Build a stable platform above it, since draining removes the water surface you may rely on.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.1: Supply rotation, lower the hose end into the liquid and connect the pulley to the pumping route. Pump direction chooses draining or filling, while pulley rotation changes hose position. These are separate operations.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.text.2: Check that the pond shrinks and the receiving tank fills. Very large sources may count as bottomless under world settings, but thresholds and permitted fluids depend on configuration; read the pulley’s status. Never assume unlimited lava without checking, and fence the area before draining a dangerous lake.
codex.quest.create_fluids.hose.title: Hose Pulley
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.0: Fluid pipes connect a source, pump and consumer. Craft eight using copper according to JEI, and choose a short route between two accessible points. Pipes carry fluid but do not pump it themselves.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.1: Place connections in sequence and inspect junctions: a neighboring tank may accidentally join the network. The wrench changes supported pipe variants, and a viewing section helps reveal activity without dismantling the line.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.text.2: Fill the first route with water after installing a pump. If fluid does not move, trace the path from inlet to outlet and check the machine’s connection side. Smart pipes and valves handle separate filtering and isolation tasks; they need not replace every ordinary section. A short, understandable main line is easier to maintain and extend.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pipe.title: Fluid Pipes
codex.quest.create_fluids.portable_fluid: Portable interfaces connect storage on a moving contraption to a stationary network. Fluid interfaces serve tanks, while storage interfaces serve item inventories. The quest requests one of each, but a working connection of either type needs a pair: one moving and one stationary.

Place matching interfaces facing each other at a suitable distance and bring the contraption into docking position. Connect a pump to the stationary fluid interface and insertion or extraction equipment to the item interface.

Test docking with a small batch and watch both inventories. Merely placing blocks nearby without correct orientation does not transfer anything. Allow enough stopping time, particularly on a train. This arrangement unloads drills or freight trains without disassembling the contraption after every trip.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.0: A mechanical pump creates directed fluid movement through pipes. Prepare a pump, several pipes, a water source and an empty tank. Place the pump near both ends for the first trial; a very long main line complicates troubleshooting.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.1: Connect the source to the inlet side and the tank to the outlet, then supply rotation to the pump’s cogwheel. Check its direction arrow. Change direction through pump orientation or drive rotation; a redstone signal by itself is not a separate pump control input.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.text.2: Watch the receiving level. If it does not rise, check the source, rotation and direction, then pipe connections. More speed increases pumping but cannot correct a wrong route. A stable drive independent of frequently stopped production machinery is useful for later water service.
codex.quest.create_fluids.pump.title: Mechanical Pump
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.0: A spout applies fluid to items, while an item drain extracts fluid from suitable containers. Prepare both devices, pipes and a small water tank. The spout needs fluid supplied above and an item beneath its nozzle; the spout itself does not require rotation.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.1: For a simple test, fill a suitable empty container using a JEI recipe while it rests on a depot or belt. Then place the filled container on the drain and route the extracted liquid to a receiver. Check where the empty container exits.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.text.2: A stuck container often means insufficient fluid capacity or a blocked item output. Do not connect honey, lava and water to one setup immediately. After a successful trial, these devices support drinks, chocolate and sequenced assembly, where the correct fluid and processing order matter.
codex.quest.create_fluids.spout.title: Spout and Drain
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.0: A fluid tank stores a buffer between source and consumer. The four blocks in this objective let you build a small reservoir and observe adjacent parts combining. Choose a level site with wall access for a pipe and a visible window.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.1: Arrange the tanks in a compatible shape and connect a water pump. Not every arbitrary shape becomes one reservoir: keep a valid footprint when expanding and verify formation through goggles or its window.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.text.2: Watch it fill and check that water does not escape through an unintended side branch. One reservoir is not meant to store a mixture of water, honey and lava simultaneously. Separate labeled tanks are easier to service. They later smooth supply interruptions and, in a specially heated arrangement, become part of a steam boiler.
codex.quest.create_fluids.tank.title: Fluid Tank
codex.quest.create_fluids.water_service_: The next water-service component is a fluid valve. Despite this quest’s batch wording, its objective checks the valve rather than a volume of water. Craft one and prepare a pipe section between the buffer and a chosen consumer.

Install the valve and arrange rotation to change its position. In this version it is a mechanical valve; an ordinary redstone signal does not replace its drive. Use a hand crank or a transmission with a gearshift for convenient operation.

Fill the buffer before testing and choose a receiver with a visible level. Opening must permit flow and closing must isolate that branch. The valve neither creates pressure nor forces fluid against the pump. After obtaining the item, proceed to the separate installed-system trial and keep the control accessible.
Manually open and close the valve, check levels and pump direction, and confirm water delivery resumes when rotation restarts

Now test water service as a connected system. Prepare a partly filled tank and a consumer that can actually accept water. If both reservoirs are already full, changing the valve position will be hard to observe.

Open and close the valve while watching the tank level and consumer. Confirm that pump direction matches the intended flow and water returns after rotation restarts. Also check that an accidental side branch does not bypass the closed valve.

Confirm only after the in-world test; water service is not measured automatically here. If flow does not resume, begin with the pump drive, then inspect valve position and receiving space. A working arrangement should allow maintenance and return to service without moving pipes or carrying buckets.

A shared water service removes the need to carry buckets to every consumer. Prepare a pump, eight pipes, four tanks and an accessible water source. Place the buffer near the workshop with room around it for inspection and future branches.

Connect source, pump and reservoir with a short route. Check pump direction before startup and reserve an accessible section for a valve. The next quest supplies that valve, but planning its position now is easier.

Confirm that water reaches the tank independently of the production mixer or press. A separate drive simplifies maintenance and future boiler supply. This objective checks components, so watch the actual level rise after assembly: a stationary pump and a complete inventory of parts do not yet provide water service.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.chaindrive.t: Encased chain drives compactly connect several parallel shafts. Prepare four drives and mark out a row of machines requiring matching rotation. This is useful where several exposed cogwheels would occupy the entire walkway.

Place the drives beside one another in compatible orientations and connect one to the source. Run shafts to the consumers, first checking them without load. Correct a component with the wrench if neighboring drives have not formed a shared chain.

An ordinary chain drive relays rotation, while the adjustable version separately changes its speed ratio according to a signal. Do not assume every drive has that feature. Check total stress after attaching machines: a compact transmission does not reduce actual load. Leave room for a clutch to service one group of consumers.
A clutch stops one branch without shutting down the whole workshop. A gearshift continues transmitting power but reverses its output under a redstone signal. Prepare both blocks, a lever and a small load whose direction is easy to observe.

Insert the clutch into a shaft gap. It transmits rotation without a signal and disconnects when powered. Test the gearshift in another section: toggling the lever should reverse a belt or piston movement.

Do not confuse stopping with reversing. A sustained signal maintains its state; a short pulse does not turn the gearshift into an independent movement program. Automatic return needs your own logic or a sequenced gearshift. Place a manual switch beside a walkway so the mechanism can be serviced outside its moving area.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.clutch.title: Clutch and Gearshift
codex.quest.create_kinetics.display.text: A display link carries information from a supported source to a readable display. Prepare one link and two nixie tubes. Choose a simple value for the first test, such as sensor data or speed available in the source settings.

Select the target display with the link item, then install the link on a supported source as instructed by its hints. Open its settings and choose the content. Tubes offer limited space, so a larger board suits long messages better.

Change the monitored value and confirm that the display updates. If nothing appears, inspect target, source and output format instead of trying to power the link with rotation. Place the display beside a walkway with a label: an unexplained number can easily be mistaken for item stock when it represents speed.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.flywheel.tex: A steam engine extracts rotation from an operating boiler. In this Create version, a flywheel is a decorative rotating component: an engine does not require it, and it does not store spare energy. This quest asks for both items, but their purposes differ.

Mount the engine on a fluid tank belonging to an active boiler. Use a shaft on the engine to create its kinetic output, then connect a consumer. Before connecting, inspect boiler heat, water supply and size with engineer’s goggles.

You can place the flywheel on an operating transmission for decoration. Adding it will not fix a stopped engine: first investigate boiler limits and output connection. This check distinguishes actual generation from decorative components in the future engine room.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.gearbox.text: A gearbox changes the route of rotation when a straight shaft meets a wall or a machine stands to one side. Craft one and prepare several shafts. For the first experiment, make a horizontal turn between a source and an already tested consumer.

Feed a shaft into one side and take the output from another suitable side. Use the wrench to change orientation; a vertical arrangement carries rotation between levels. Check output direction before attaching a belt or pump.

A gearbox neither increases capacity nor replaces speed-changing gears. If nearby machines turn the wrong way, trace the gearbox route first. Avoid reconnecting two outputs into one network without checking compatibility: an innocent-looking branch can form a conflicting closed loop.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.0: Redstone links carry a redstone signal between parts of the workshop. Two blocks need the same pair of items in their frequency slots, including their order. Prepare a transmitter, receiver and linked controller as listed.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.1: Place one link beside a lever and another beside a test lamp, then select receiver mode according to its block hint. Choose an uncommon item pair to avoid operating another machine on the same frequency. Configure a controller button with that pair afterward.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.text.2: Test pressing and releasing the button from the operator’s actual location. Wireless control does not imply unlimited range or operation of every unloaded machine. If the lamp does not respond, check modes, frequencies and distance. Connect the clutch or drive after testing, while retaining a local maintenance switch.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.link.title: Wireless Link
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.0: Redstone lets a machine receive short commands and remember a state. A pulse repeater helps control signal timing, a powered latch retains its switched state, and an analog lever sets signal strength. Craft the three listed items and prepare an ordinary lamp for a test rig.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.1: Test each component separately before connecting a moving structure. Compare a brief button press with a continuous lever signal. Check the latch’s set and reset behavior against the connection sides shown in Ponder.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.text.2: Do not attach an unfamiliar combination directly to a lift or drill. First make the lamp show exactly the behavior expected by the clutch or gearshift. Then transfer the circuit to the machine and retain an accessible manual switch. A small understood circuit avoids accidental repeated starts.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.logic.title: Redstone Logic
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.0: A rotation speed controller sets shaft speed without a long staircase of gears. Crafting it requires a precision mechanism. Also prepare a large cogwheel and an instrument to observe the actual result.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.1: Place the large cogwheel above the controller in the arrangement shown by Ponder, then feed rotation into its shaft axis. Set the output speed on the side panel. The sign changes direction; begin with a modest value that is easy to observe.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.text.2: Check the output speedometer and total stress after attaching a machine. The controller does not create capacity from nothing: an excessively fast consumer will overload the source. A zero setting stops output, so inspect the panel if rotation unexpectedly disappears. It particularly suits an individual mixer or a frequently adjusted production line.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.rsc.title: Rotation Speed Controller
codex.quest.create_kinetics.sequenced.te: A sequenced gearshift executes a configured sequence of rotation. It suits doors, bridges or small platforms that need to move a defined distance. Prepare a precision mechanism for crafting, plus a power source and a clear safe travel area for testing.

Open its settings and create a short program: movement, pause, reverse movement. Choose step values appropriate to the operation and connected mechanism; angular rotation and linear travel are not interchangeable. Trigger the program with a control signal.

Begin with a short movement and watch the final position. The gearshift does not know where your walkway or valuable storage stands, so inspect obstacles beforehand. After the program works, add a manual way to stop the drive. This block controls movement without providing extra network capacity.
codex.quest.create_kinetics.stockpile.te: A stockpile sensor helps start production when supplies are low and stop it when storage fills. A content observer serves another purpose: detecting matching items on a supported section. Prepare both blocks and a small chest containing one material.
Attach the stockpile sensor to storage and set lower and upper thresholds. Add and remove items gradually while watching a lamp. Different thresholds prevent rapid switching around one value.

For the observer, choose the required item or filter and pass it through the monitored line. A signal is not automatic proof of finished production: the observer may be seeing raw input. After testing, connect the sensor to feeding controls or a clutch, and verify that high stock stops production while low stock restarts it.
codex.quest.create_packages.cardboard.te: Cardboard is used for package machinery and other newer Create items. It comes from pulp, not simply pressing paper. Prepare a mixer and basin, water, a press and suitable plant material such as bamboo, sugar cane or permitted saplings.
Mix four units from the accepted ingredient list with 250 mB of water. Press the resulting pulp to obtain cardboard. Repeat for eight pieces, arranging a separate route from the basin to the press.

If mixing does not begin, check plant compatibility in JEI and water delivery. Do not send the wet intermediate straight into packager crafting; it needs pressing first. Batch production fits beside an existing bread workshop, where basin use, water supply and depot processing are already familiar.
codex.quest.create_packages.chain_convey: A chain conveyor joins package-delivery nodes and transmits rotation between them. Prepare four nodes and ordinary chains for connections. Place the first two within clear view, leaving an unobstructed route and access to shafts above or below.

With chains held, select two conveyors to connect them, then supply rotation to the network. Connection length is limited: long routes use several spans rather than one endless chain. Attach frogports to suitable nodes.

Send one addressed box and follow it to the receiver. Reachable addresses matter at junctions, and a full port can delay delivery. Players can also travel on chains with a wrench, but check height and a safe exit first. Observing from the ground is sufficient for the freight trial.
codex.quest.create_packages.factory_gaug: A factory gauge monitors stock and can request replenishment. The two requested devices let you connect a simple output with an ingredient. Start with a real recipe in an already working workshop; the gauge neither builds a machine nor processes materials itself.

Bind gauges to the network, assign monitored items and connect dependencies through the interface. Set the output amount per batch and the address receiving ingredients. Finished products must return to linked storage or the network will not see replenishment.

Choose a small target stock and remove a few items. Verify the order, production and returning output. If stock appears permanently low, look for a wrong address or an output outside the network. A gauge on a packager can manage local inventory; its placement affects what it monitors.
codex.quest.create_packages.frogport.tex: A frogport sends and receives packages through a chain network. A first route needs two ports, two addresses and connected chain conveyors. Prepare both devices for now; they cannot move contents through empty space without transport.

Select a chain conveyor with the port item before placing the frogport nearby, then assign its address in the interface. A suitable inventory or packager can stand underneath. Repeat at the receiving end with a different address.

A package addressed elsewhere is sent onto the chain, while one matching the destination port is removed there. If a box spins in place, check for a reachable address and connected network. Begin with one shipment and a free receiver; accidental duplicate addresses make diagnosis harder.
codex.quest.create_packages.guide_addres: Manually verify the order reaches its specified address, unpacks and contains the ordered quantity

Before a factory orders resources automatically, verify one address from ticker to final chest. Put a small amount of inexpensive goods in linked storage and clear the receiving packager. Record the quantity you intend to receive.
Place one order with the frogport’s exact address. Follow box creation, chain travel, reception and unpacking. Compare the received quantity with the order without mixing the trial with older stock.

Confirm manually once the destination and complete contents match. If the box is stuck, locate it first; ordering again may only increase the queue. Check address spelling, chain connections and receiving space. A successful trial provides a clear diagnostic example for every new recipient added to the factory.
codex.quest.create_packages.guide_repack: An order supplied by several inventories may arrive in separate boxes. This is awkward for machines that need a complete ingredient set and predictable arrival order. A re-packager combines fragments of one logistics request before forwarding them.

Prepare a re-packager and a buffer inventory for incoming packages. Route fragments there, attach the device and power it with redstone. It waits for required parts and emits a combined package, so leave a clear output to the next recipient.

Test a small order whose ingredients come from two linked sources. Do not replace a missing fragment with an arbitrary box of similar contents; order membership matters. The item objective checks the device, while observing a real combination explains its role. Re-packaging helps before automatic crafters and is unnecessary for every simple single-source order.
codex.quest.create_packages.packager.tex: A packager takes items from an attached inventory and creates a package. When receiving a box, it can unpack contents back into storage. Prepare the device and a separate chest with a small inexpensive batch.

Attach the packager facing the chest and apply redstone for a simple shipment. A sign on the packager can supply an address; inspect the resulting package label before introducing it to transport. The box itself moves like an item.

Leave enough room in the destination inventory: a packager will not accept a box it cannot fully unpack. Test the first shipment on a familiar rig before enabling stock orders. An address does not automatically create a route; the next branch builds physical delivery between sender and receiver.
codex.quest.create_packages.postbox.text: A postbox transports packages using trains that stop at its linked station. It does not teleport a box to any other postbox. Prepare the red postbox and an existing route between two stops; a complete trial also needs a receiving postbox at the other end.

Select the station with the postbox item before placing it nearby, then assign an address. Packages addressed elsewhere wait for collection by a train, while those matching the receiving postbox are unloaded at its stop.

Send one inexpensive box and wait for the relevant service. Confirm that the train actually visits both stations and that the address matches exactly. Mail logistics can serve distant areas, but timing and capacity still depend on transport and free postbox space.
codex.quest.create_packages.requester.te: A redstone requester orders a configured set of items when signaled. It suits an installation that periodically needs the same ingredients. Prepare it after a successful manual ticker order, so delivery faults are not confused with control faults.

Bind the requester to the stock network and configure the order contents and destination address. For the first trial, select a small amount of inexpensive material and send one button pulse. Follow the complete route through unpacking.

Do not immediately connect a fast pulse generator: repeated commands can fill transport with unwanted boxes. Test sustained signals and missing stock before choosing a clear trigger from your machine. A requester does not automatically measure every production need; factory gauges provide the next approach to maintaining a target stock.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.0: A shop presents trading through the package network and is useful at a shared base. The red table cloth and desk bell requested are only part of the setup; working trade needs configured goods, exchange conditions and warehouse delivery. Start with an inexpensive test item.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.1: Connect stocked inventory to a packager and stock link, then bind a ticker in the shop. Place a mob or blaze burner in front as keeper. Interact with the keeper while holding the cloth to create an offer; after placing the cloth, set its price in the side slot. Put the bell somewhere accessible.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.text.2: Test a small purchase, including payment removal and package arrival. Avoid listing rare resources until conditions and destination are checked. Owning a bell does not create a store. After testing, the shop can provide standard consumable kits while you work elsewhere on the base.
codex.quest.create_packages.shop.title: Shop
codex.quest.create_packages.stock_link.t: A stock link makes a packager’s inventory available to a shared ordering network. It transmits information and requests, not the items themselves. Prepare a link and a tested packager attached to a chest from which a small batch can be safely shipped.

A newly placed link creates a network. To add another component to the same network, bind it by interacting with an existing link first, following the item hints. The link must serve the intended packager, or the ticker will show the wrong stock.

Verify chest visibility through a connected ticker once available. Stock-network communication spans distances freely, but every box still needs a delivery route. Redstone can change priority or suppress stock broadcasting; if goods disappear from the list, inspect that connection too.
A stock ticker displays available stock from linked inventories and lets you place orders. Prepare a ticker and shopping list, then bind the device to the intended network. Check the packager, destination address and physical box route before ordering. Place a seated mob or blaze burner in front of the ticker to serve as its stock keeper.

Interact with the stock keeper to open the goods list, choose a small quantity of a familiar material and enter the delivery address. Watch the source create a package and follow it to the receiving port. A shopping list helps with recurring component sets.

If an order fails to arrive, separate the checks: is stock visible, was a box created, did it find its address, and could it be unpacked? Avoid repeated large orders until the first is located. A ticker simplifies workshop supply but does not replace a clear output and sufficiently large receiver.
codex.quest.create_packages.ticker.title: Stock Ticker
A crafting blueprint provides convenient wall-mounted access to a chosen recipe. It helps make recurring components from your inventory, but is not an independent machine supplied by warehouse logistics. Prepare a blueprint and ingredients for one frequently used recipe.

Place the blueprint on an accessible surface and configure its recipe through the interface. Start with a simple part such as shafts, then interact with the configured entry and check material consumption from your inventory.

If crafting fails, compare inventory contents with the recipe and check available space. A blueprint does not bypass sequenced assembly, heating or oversized mechanical-crafter recipes. Group genuinely frequent ordinary crafts on the wall with labels; a few clear entries speed repairs more than a huge panel of unused recipes.
codex.quest.create_tools.blueprint.title: Crafting Blueprint
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.0: A schematicannon constructs a placed schematic using supplied materials. It needs the cannon, a prepared schematic, gunpowder and accessible chests of blocks. Choose a clear site and inspect the entire preview first.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.1: Load the schematic into the cannon, review the material list and fill nearby supply inventories. Check existing-block replacement settings, which determine what happens to an already built area. Start construction only afterward.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.text.2: If work stops, read the missing material or reason in its interface instead of blindly adding gunpowder. The cannon neither creates rare components nor proves that a copied machine works. After completion, inspect transmissions, filters and container contents, then run a small batch just as you did with the original installation.
codex.quest.create_tools.cannon.title: Schematicannon
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.0: The extendo grip increases the reach of items used in your main hand. Craft it, place it in the offhand and keep building blocks in the main hand. Choose a wall on safe level ground for the first test.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.1: Try placing and removing a block that was previously out of reach. Watch grip durability. A charged worn backtank can spend air instead of durability, so inspect its supply before a long building session.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.text.2: Do not treat two grips as a promise of doubling every interaction distance; follow the installed item’s actual hints. Extended reach does not prevent falls or make your footing secure. The tool is especially useful for ceiling transmissions and tall walls, allowing work from a platform without scaffolding every block.
codex.quest.create_tools.extendo.title: Extendo Grip
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.0: The potato cannon uses suitable plant items as ammunition. Craft it and bring ordinary potatoes for the first trial, keeping food reserves separate. Not every edible item necessarily works, and shot properties depend on the particular ammunition.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.1: Choose a safe target away from animals, villagers and other players. Load a compatible crop according to the hints and fire a few single shots. Watch ammunition use and weapon durability.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.text.2: A charged backtank can supply air for tool use, but does not create unlimited projectiles. Avoid turning your only travel food supply into ammunition. The cannon helps with ranged defense and crop experiments; test new projectile types at a separate range rather than beside a wooden workshop.
codex.quest.create_tools.potato.title: Potato Cannon
A schematic saves a selected structure for placement and reconstruction. Prepare a schematic and quill plus a schematic table. Begin with a small tested installation without valuable stored contents so its boundaries are easy to verify.

Use the quill to select two opposite corners and save the schematic under a clear name. At the table, load the chosen file into the appropriate schematic item. Place its preview in a clear area and inspect height, orientation and size.

A schematic does not replace building materials or guarantee transfer of every container’s contents. Avoid accidentally including the factory floor or a neighboring house, since extra layers complicate construction. A small press rig makes a good first copy that can be compared with the original before using a schematicannon.
codex.quest.create_tools.schematic.title: Schematics
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.0: The wand of symmetry mirrors block placement around a configured plane. It suits facades, towers and matching building wings. Prepare the wand and a stock of inexpensive blocks; additional Survival copies require building materials.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.1: Use the wand on a surface to place its mirror, and open settings by sneak-using it. Keep the item on the hotbar. Place one block and check where its reflection appears before building an entire wall.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.text.2: If the copy enters another structure or goes underground, stop and adjust the plane. Remove the active mirror through its intended action afterward so unrelated building is not accidentally duplicated. Symmetry helps geometry but does not verify machine orientation: a mirrored transmission may need separate rotational adjustments.
codex.quest.create_tools.symmetry.title: Wand of Symmetry
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.0: A toolbox carries several supply types and helps refill linked inventory slots nearby. This objective requires the brown variant, so check its color when crafting. Begin with shafts, cogwheels and building blocks.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.1: Place the toolbox beside the work area, divide items among compartments and link the required inventory slots through its intended controls. Start with one slot and confirm that it receives the chosen material.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.text.2: Refilling depends on toolbox availability rather than working from anywhere in the world. Before moving it, inspect contents and linked-slot behavior so your familiar tool arrangement is not disrupted. Avoid keeping your only expedition food there without checking access. A toolbox particularly suits long track or transmission projects that repeatedly need several component types.
codex.quest.create_tools.toolbox.title: Toolbox
codex.quest.create_tools.worldshaper.tas: Read: the worldshaper is a Creative-mode tool and is not required in Survival
codex.quest.create_tools.worldshaper.tex: The handheld worldshaper is a Creative-mode tool for changing terrain with large brushes. It has no ordinary Survival acquisition recipe, so this is an informational quest with a manual “Read” confirmation. You do not need to search for it as the next mandatory item.

If working separately in a Creative test world, the tool samples material from a targeted block and applies a configured brush. Begin in a small area away from builds: a large terrain edit can affect more space than the aiming point suggests.

In your main Survival world, prepare factory sites with ordinary tools or contraptions already learned. Confirm reading once you understand the distinction. This quest requires neither command-giving the item, changing game mode nor demonstrating actual worldshaper use.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.0: A display board makes station information visible without opening an interface. The four requested blocks form a small panel, but do not know the schedule by themselves. A display link to a supported railway data source is also needed.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.1: Place the board in a readable arrangement near the platform and connect the required source through a display link. Select available station or train information in its settings and check whether the text fits. Expand the panel if needed while keeping the walkway clear.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.text.2: Wait for an actual arrival and compare the display with events. If the board is blank, inspect source and link target rather than only panel size. Add a separate station-name label, which remains useful when data is temporarily absent. This helps once several routes share passenger platforms.
codex.quest.create_trains.board.title: Board
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.task.1: Manually: two bogeys stand on straight track within the station assembly area
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.0: A bogey supports a carriage on Create tracks and is created in station assembly mode. Prepare two railway casings and enter that mode. No separate bogey item is needed.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.1: Apply a casing to straight track inside the marked station area, then place the second bogey on the same straight. Leave room between them for the intended carriage and inspect both positions before gluing on its body. Interacting with the track can change the bogey variant when appropriate.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.text.2: Casing possession is checked through inventory, while placement must be confirmed manually only when two bogeys actually stand on straight track inside the assembly area. Two casings in a chest do not satisfy that observation. Next, add a connected carriage and controls so the station can assemble the train.
codex.quest.create_trains.bogey.title: Bogeys
This objective checks a freight schedule even though the quest title mentions a trial batch. Prepare one schedule item and two configured stations. Avoid loading a full wagon while stop conditions remain untested.

Add loading and unloading in journey order. Begin with understandable waits, then tune conditions to actual interface operation: the train must allow cargo transfer and be able to depart afterward. Check for a suitable conductor and controls facing both required directions.

Hold the completed schedule in your normal inventory for item credit, then give it to the operator. Inventory tracking does not validate the station list or prove transportation. Reserve a small clearly identified batch for the next trial, easily distinguished from previous stock in destination storage.
codex.quest.create_trains.freight_run.ta: Manually ship a small batch and wait for the return; check unloading, departure and an empty loading store
codex.quest.create_trains.freight_run.te: This freight trial confirms a completed transport cycle rather than simply owning a train. Prepare a small known batch, a free output chest and a way to observe both stations. Confirm that the operator has the schedule before departure.

Send the train with the small batch and wait for its return. Check unloading, departure conditions and behavior when the loading store is empty. The train must not lose cargo through poor docking or wait forever for an amount the store cannot provide.

Confirm manually after these in-world checks. The Codex does not automatically track the journey or station contents. If the train does not return, inspect schedule status first: waiting for cargo, an unreachable route and an occupied signal need different fixes. Increasing locomotive speed does not resolve them.
A freight route connects a material source to destination storage. Prepare the two stations and two portable storage interfaces listed, then choose a small train with attached storage. Serving several stops may require additional interfaces beyond the checked set.

Give stations clear names and align stationary interfaces with the onboard one at the stopping position. Connect loading at the source and extraction into a chest at the destination. Check each docking connection separately while the train is stationary.

Approximate placement along the platform is not enough: working faces must oppose one another at a valid distance. Allow transfer time and access to storage after disassembly. Items confirm equipment; schedule configuration and a real journey in the next quests will check whether cargo arrives.
codex.quest.create_trains.guide_passing_: Manually verify two opposing trains pass in sequence, never enter an occupied single-track section together, and continue their routes
Two opposing trains on one line need somewhere to pass. A signal cannot create that space itself. Prepare additional passing-loop track, signals and two small trains already tested individually.

Build a parallel section long enough for waiting and connect both ends. Divide occupancy with signals, checking displayed block boundaries and a free exit beyond junctions. Arrange directions so trains can wait without blocking each other’s exit.

Test an opposing journey slowly and confirm manually when both trains pass through in sequence without meeting on an occupied single-track section. If they wait for each other indefinitely, pause schedules and correct the signaling. Add freight after a successful trial while preserving enough waiting length for the complete train.
A Passing Loop for Two Trains
codex.quest.create_trains.guide_reverse_: A short railway branch often ends in terminals where trains must depart backward. Prepare two control blocks and check straight-track length at both stations. The second controls address direction; they do not replace a reachable route or correct schedule.

Disassemble the train at a station and install controls for both directions. Check that they join the connected structure, then reassemble. Configure the conductor and route so the chosen departure direction is available at each stop.

Travel to the second station manually and return first, then test the schedule. Two items in inventory do not prove an automatic return journey is possible. If the train will not leave, inspect direction availability and waiting conditions. This short branch is useful for a mine where a large turning loop is inconvenient.
A Route Without a Turning Loop
codex.quest.create_trains.railway_casing: Railway casing is used for stations and other train components, and becomes a bogey directly on track during assembly. Prepare four casings using sturdy sheets according to JEI. Reserve some material for controls and another station.

Craft the casings in the workshop first and take them into your normal inventory. Before making bogeys, choose a level track section: the station’s assembly area must fit the entire train, not just its cab.

Do not search chests for a separate bogey item; base Create makes bogeys by applying casing to track in assembly mode. A casing is not a finished locomotive either. Four provide a start on railway infrastructure, but later devices have their own recipes and may need additional materials.
A schedule defines stations and waiting conditions for an automatic train. Prepare a schedule and a route between two stops that you have already tested manually. Execution needs a suitable conductor at the controls; a schedule in your pocket does not start the train.

Open the schedule, add stations in visiting order and choose understandable departure conditions. A short timed wait suits the first trip; later use loading, unloading or signal conditions. Give the schedule to the conductor through its supported interaction.

Watch a full circuit and confirm the train can depart in the required direction. If a station is unreachable, check connected track, control orientation and its name. Avoid waiting for an impossible cargo quantity: the train will obediently wait forever even when scheduling works correctly.
codex.quest.create_trains.schedule.title: Schedule
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.0: Railway signals divide a network into sections and control automatic train traffic. A track observer detects passing trains and serves a different purpose. Prepare two signals and an observer, then choose a simple, clearly visible section.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.1: Select track with the signal item and place the device nearby. Check its direction and the displayed section boundaries; study normal versus chained modes in Ponder before handling junctions and passing loops. Connect the observer to a separate lamp to test a passing event.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.text.2: Test one train before adding a second. Signals do not create a passing loop on single track or fix a route where two trains cannot physically pass. Avoid full-speed opposing trials. If a train remains stopped, inspect section occupancy and a free exit instead of removing every signal.
codex.quest.create_trains.signals.title: Signals
A Steam ’n’ Rails conductor is a separate entity that can be created and used beside train controls. For the blue cap, prepare blue wool, a saw, a deployer, a precision mechanism and string. The objective specifically requires the blue variant.

Cut the wool workpiece, then apply the mechanism and string in the cap recipe’s sequence. Use the completed cap on an andesite casing to create a conductor. Also prepare the whistle and learn its available actions in a safe area.

Seat the conductor beside controls on an assembled train and provide a schedule. Test a short trip and return. Owning the cap and whistle does not verify the entity’s correct position aboard. If the train will not depart, inspect controls, station reachability and schedule conditions before creating another conductor.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_coupler.te: A Steam ’n’ Rails track coupler joins and separates suitable trains without fully disassembling them into blocks. The buffer in the second objective is end decoration and does not replace configured coupling machinery. Begin on a separate level track without regular traffic.

Select track with the coupler item and place it nearby. Use the wrench to choose coupling, decoupling or both, and scroll to set the distance between working pads. A station helps align the relevant train parts precisely.

Apply a signal only after correct alignment and stopping the test train. Check that the intended cars separated and that the remaining section has the required controls. Do not assume decorative buffers prevent every crash. This device suits a shunting yard after ordinary freight routing is reliable.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_handcar.te: A handcar serves short trips along the tracks and route inspection. Craft the Steam ’n’ Rails handcar and choose a clear straight away from automatic trains. The first trial is easier before regular traffic begins.
Place it on compatible track and use its available controls following the game’s hints. Travel a short distance, test stopping and return. Leave a place nearby where you can dismount safely.

Do not assume a small handcar is invisible to other trains, and never pull out in front of freight traffic. Clear the route temporarily for inspection or use a separate branch. A handcar helps reveal awkward platforms, gaps and abrupt route changes, but a freight schedule must still be tested with the train that will actually use it.
codex.quest.create_trains.snr_style.text: Locomotive styling helps distinguish trains and makes a cab more welcoming. The coalburner smokestack requested is a Steam ’n’ Rails decorative component; owning one is neither a movement requirement nor a substitute for train controls. Prepare it after checking the main route.

Disassemble the train at a station and mount the stack where intended. Check that it joins the connected structure, does not obstruct the driver’s view and leaves access to controls. Then assemble the train again.

Inspect its appearance on straights and curves while retaining access to freight interfaces. Avoid widening the body tightly against existing platforms, since a new projection can make boarding awkward. Add decoration gradually once actual station clearances and maintenance locations are known.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.0: A station defines a stopping point and provides the train assembly interface. Prepare two stations for the initial route and a straight track long enough for the planned train. Give them distinct names, for example based on their warehouse roles.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.1: Select a track section with the station item, then place the station nearby. Check approach direction and open assembly mode at the first stop. The game marks the area where bogeys and carriage structures can be built.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.text.2: Choose a valid area before building the entire train: an unexpected curve or short straight complicates assembly. Configure the second station as a destination and check for a connected route. Item objectives do not verify routing; test manually with one train before adding a schedule.
codex.quest.create_trains.station.title: Station
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.0: Sturdy sheets are used in railway equipment and come from sequenced processing of obsidian dust. First crush obsidian using its recipe, then prepare a lava-fed spout, a press and a safe workpiece route. Each sheet needs 500 mB of lava.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.1: Pass the dust through lava filling, then perform two pressing operations in order. Use two presses or send the workpiece through one press again; the important point is completing the second stroke.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.text.2: Separate finished sheets from unprocessed obsidian intermediates and collect eight. If processing stops, check spout lava and the item’s current stage. Keep lava in a closed pipe route and service it from a safe platform. This stock opens railway casings and the first trackside devices.
codex.quest.create_trains.sturdy.title: Sturdy Sheet
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.0: Create tracks serve large trains and differ from ordinary minecart rails. Prepare thirty-two pieces, building blocks and a level area near the base. Make an assembly straight first, then a short route toward a second station.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.1: Place endpoints and connect them using the shape preview. Curves and slopes have geometric limits, so leave enough distance for gradual bends. Inspect the preview before confirming construction.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.text.2: Track placement does not promise finished supports, a safe bridge or sufficient materials. Build a foundation where players will walk and fence dangerous edges. If a connection fails, simplify the bend and check endpoint orientation. A straight test line lets you learn train operation before investing in an expensive mountain route.
codex.quest.create_trains.track.title: Tracks
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.0: A first train needs bogeys, a body connected to them and train controls. An onboard boiler or electric motor is not a movement requirement for a normal Create train. Prepare controls and a small platform glued to the bogeys in the station area.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.1: Install controls facing the travel direction and assemble the train through the station interface. Interact with the controls afterward and move cautiously along a straight. For departures in the opposite direction, provide backward-facing controls or a turning route.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.text.2: Fuel in assembled chests or barrels increases speed, but stopping and returning matter more initially. Do not mistake a decorative firebox for a required engine. Completing the item objective only confirms controls; make the first trip manually before configuring a conductor and automatic schedule.
codex.quest.create_trains.train.title: First Train
codex.quest.create_world.arise.task.0: Manually find and inspect a Create structure in the world
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.0: Structures Arise adds varied builds using Create components: installed structures include fluid tanks, windmills, houses and a lost train station. These are diverse discoveries, not a promise of a working factory in every biome. Prepare food, lighting and a way to record coordinates.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.1: Explore new terrain normally and inspect a discovered structure from outside. Enter carefully, since rooms, enemies and loot vary. Trace at least one visible mechanism or railway feature instead of dismantling everything immediately.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.text.2: Confirm manually once you actually find a Create structure in the world. The Codex does not identify it automatically. Save the location for another visit and note something to reproduce at your base. A chest does not guarantee schematics, and installed machinery may need its drive restored.
codex.quest.create_world.arise.title: Create: Structures Arise
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.0: Copper shingles and metal girders help finish a workshop and distinguish its functional areas. Prepare one of each requested item using copper and other ingredients from JEI. Begin with a small wall or canopy sample.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.1: Place girders without blocking access to shafts and valves. Judge shingles in daylight; copper variants change appearance through oxidation, while suitable treatment preserves a chosen state.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.text.2: A decorative block does not automatically become an attached contraption member: moving components still need connections. Avoid hiding every fault-prone part behind attractive cladding. Retain walkways, inspection points and flow labels. Once the palette is chosen, finish the factory so appearance supports maintenance instead of requiring roof removal to reach a filter.
codex.quest.create_world.deco.title: Decorative Blocks
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.task.0: Manually find and inspect a rural Create structure
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.0: Rustic Structures adds rural builds with Create elements. The installed set includes a barn, smithy, well and windmill. Prepare for ordinary exploration rather than searching for one mandatory structure at guaranteed coordinates.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.1: Bring food, a boat if useful and materials for a safe overnight stop. On finding a suitable rural build, inspect its surroundings, entrances and machinery details. Do not assume all decoration is powered or that an inhabited village must be nearby.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.text.2: Confirm manually after an actual rural Create structure discovery. Record coordinates and choose a useful idea for your farm, such as barn access or windmill placement. Completion relies on your confirmation, so crafting a casing does not replace the expedition and inspection.
codex.quest.create_world.rustic.title: Create: Rustic Structures
codex.quest.create_world.stickywheels.te: Sticky Wheels adds a sticky tire for Offroad wheeled vehicles. The installed recipe uses an ordinary Offroad tire with four honey bottles around it. Prepare those materials; the underlying wheel and vehicle belong to a separate transport system rather than Create train bogeys.
Craft the sticky tire and check its role on a small wheeled build using the relevant add-on’s hints. Choose a level clear area and a modest slope for testing, with enough stopping space.

Do not interpret “sticky” as guaranteed travel up any vertical wall or safe braking on every surface. Behavior depends on the complete vehicle and wheel contact conditions. The item objective confirms tire crafting; test the capabilities of your actual vehicle gradually before attempting a dangerous slope.
Aether accessories use their corresponding equipment slots and provide different effects. Craft a Golden Ring from four Gold Ingots. Ice Pendants occur in dungeon loot, while Golden Feathers belong to silver rewards; one crafting recipe cannot replace all three acquisitions.

Let each item register, then equip and test it separately. The pendant freezes water and lava beneath you, and the feather slows falling. Test the feather from a low height over safe ground before trusting it near a cliff, checking the functional slot.

Do not generalise these effects to every similar ring or pendant. Obtain the three items gradually, retaining earlier detection. They complement protection and transport, while portal fences and secure bridges remain valuable; accessories cannot recover a lost homeward route.
codex.quest.dim_aether.accessories.title: Accessories
codex.quest.dim_aether.aether_portal.tas: Enter Aether through a water-activated Glowstone portal
codex.quest.dim_aether.aether_portal.tex: Build the Aether portal from Glowstone in a Nether-portal shape with a two-by-three interior. Activate it with a water bucket instead of flint and steel. Bring building blocks, food, and return supplies; supplement ordinary torches with local lighting later.

After crossing, fence the platform and record the portal position. Islands are separated by void and some creatures push players, so avoid unguarded edges. Prepare a parachute or another controlled-fall method before travelling far.

Falling out of Aether transfers you to the Overworld and may cause a dangerous landing, so it is no safe portal substitute. The objective records visiting the dimension. Test the return route, then collect nearby wood and establish a small supply cache.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.0: The Aether Altar enchants specific items and repairs suitable armour. Craft it by surrounding Zanite with Holystone and place it near Ambrosium storage. Put the input in its working slot and Ambrosium Shards in the fuel slot.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.1: The Freezer is a separate device powered by Icestone. Craft it from Holystone, Icestone, and Skyroot Planks. Test a simple freezing recipe rather than automatically feeding it the altar’s Ambrosium.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.text.2: The quest records both devices, but their roles and fuels differ. Enchant berries or Holystone for a first altar test before processing rare Gravitite. Separate raw materials from results to avoid confusing ordinary blocks with enchanted ones.
codex.quest.dim_aether.altar.title: Altar
codex.quest.dim_aether.bronze_dungeon.te: Recognise a Bronze Dungeon by its Carved Stone and the stone Slider’s chamber. Bring a durable pickaxe, armour, and healing; an ordinary sword cannot replace a mining tool against this boss. Beware of chest mimics in the corridors.

Start with a suitable pickaxe strike. The Slider charges along straight lines, so move sideways out of its path and strike between charges. Collect the Bronze Key after victory, let it register, and open the matching treasure.

The second objective’s Victory Medal comes separately from defeating a lesser Valkyrie in a Silver Dungeon. Bronze treasure does not substitute for it. Keep the first medal for the next trial; the Queen requires ten, linking preparation for two different dungeon types.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gold_dungeon.text: A Gold Dungeon houses the Sun Spirit in a Hellfire Stone chamber. Prepare healing, fire protection, and a reliable weapon. Interact through his warnings to issue the challenge; do not begin that conversation during an unprepared inspection.

Reflect one of his Ice Crystals back by striking it. A hit freezes the boss for roughly nine seconds, creating an opening for normal attacks. Avoid fire projectiles and spawned minions; ordinary snowballs do not replace this mechanic.

After victory, collect the Gold Key and open the treasury. The additional Hammer of Kingbdogz objective belongs to bronze rewards, so do not expect it from the Sun Spirit. Complete any missing bronze expedition separately and let important loot register before spending it.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.0: Gravitite is rare pink ore inside Aether islands. Mine it with Zanite or another suitable pick, checking overhead space first: an uncovered ore block can float upward. Prepare Ambrosium for processing before investing in distant mining.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.1: Put the ore into the Altar to obtain Enchanted Gravitite. Accumulate eight blocks in inventory, let them register, then use those same eight for the chestplate. Saved item detection means a duplicate batch is unnecessary.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.text.2: The high-jump ability belongs to a complete Gravitite armour set; a chestplate alone does not demonstrate it. Equip the piece and finish the set gradually. Test behaviour over a safe platform before relying on the armour to cross an island gap.
codex.quest.dim_aether.gravitite.title: Gravitite
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_altar_heali: Enchant Holystone in the Aether Altar to obtain a Healing Stone. Prepare Holystone and Ambrosium Shards, place them in the appropriate slots, and wait for processing. This is a useful first operation before spending rare Gravitite.

Collect the stone and save it for dungeon recovery. It grants regeneration when consumed, so use it during a safe opening instead of expecting an instant rescue from the next heavy hit. Carry food separately because healing does not replace hunger restoration.

Refuel the altar after testing and prepare a small travel reserve. The item objective records one completed stone, while repeating the operation confirms production. This recipe links common local material with combat preparation and reduces dependence on random healing loot.
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_first_parac: Cold Aerclouds around Aether islands provide material for a basic parachute. Collect them from a stable platform without removing your final foothold. Craft a Cold Parachute and keep it accessible before bridge building.
Test it during a short fall over a broad safe area. Confirm descent slows and learn its activation. The Cold Parachute is single-use, so craft another after the test for actual travel.

Owning the item records preparation, not timely deployment. Add bridge railings and do not expect a parachute to return you to an island after every knockback. Later silver rewards offer other slow-fall options; this consumable covers the dangerous early stage.
codex.quest.dim_aether.guide_medal_purse: Victory Medals come from duels with lesser Valkyries in Silver Dungeons. Collect ten together before challenging the Queen. Prepare armour and healing, inspect the space between pillars, and fight manageable individual duels.

Collect each medal and check weapon durability afterwards. A lance from bronze treasure helps with reach but does not replace collecting medals. Preserve a route to somewhere safe for recovery between fights.

Let ten medals register, then present that same stock to the Queen. The guide remembers the detected quantity, so a duplicate stack is unnecessary. A prepared batch makes summoning conditions clear and avoids repeatedly approaching the boss without the required proof.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.0: Begin with Skyroot wood, making planks, sticks, and a Skyroot Pickaxe. Mine Holystone and Ambrosium Ore with it. Skyroot tools can double suitable natural drops, so the wooden pick remains useful after upgrading.
codex.quest.dim_aether.holystone.text.1: Craft a Holystone Pickaxe and continue collecting Ambrosium. Holystone tools sometimes provide additional shards while working. Accumulate sixteen shards together and let both picks register; detected tools can then be used without spare copies.
