Build the new structure from the manual and form it with the hammer. Iron and coke enter above, steel leaves at the front and slag at the back. Provide separate receivers and begin with a small trial batch, without preheaters or large warehouse lines.

Wait for automatic delivery of both products and mark the manual objective. If metal leaves but slag has nowhere to go, the installation is not ready for extended operation. Preheaters come later and need FE; the furnace upgrade primarily provides supported service automation.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.0: The engineer’s hammer, wirecutter and screwdriver do different jobs. The hammer forms multiblocks and changes supported block settings; wirecutters handle wires and certain recipes; the screwdriver configures supported control modes. Prepare all three and leave accessible hotbar slots.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.1: Try the hammer on a safe block and observe orientation changes. A multiblock is activated at the point specified by the manual, not by hitting any casing at random. For a complex structure, compare layers before using the tool to search for a fault.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.text.2: Avoid accidentally cutting a working machine’s supply line with wirecutters. Disconnect sources before servicing wires and watch tool durability. The screwdriver often reverses redstone response, so check whether an applied signal means start or stop after changing the mode.
codex.quest.ie_start.hammer.title: Engineer's Hammer
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.0: The Engineer’s Manual is the main guide for assembling Immersive Engineering machines. Craft it at a crafting table using the available recipe and keep it near your hammer. Multiblock pages are particularly useful: a picture of the finished machine cannot show every hidden component.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.1: Open the coke oven section and inspect its layered layout. Check the material list and hammer activation point. Then find electrical connections: the manual distinguishes connectors, relays and transformers even though they look similar and often sit together.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.text.2: Some page values are inserted from world settings, so use your own book for current power figures. JEI conveniently shows component recipes, while the manual explains machine formation and ports. The two sources complement each other and should be consulted before preparing a large steel batch.
codex.quest.ie_start.manual.title: Engineer's Manual
codex.quest.ie_start.scaffold.text.0: Steel scaffolding serves both as machine framework and practical industrial flooring. Craft sixteen blocks of the standard variant for this objective. If components have consumed your steel, wait for another furnace batch instead of dismantling working equipment.
codex.quest.ie_start.scaffold.text.1: Lay out the future multiblock’s materials from the manual’s list. A visually similar grating of another type does not necessarily replace the specified structure block. Use spare scaffolding for access platforms and upper-connector servicing without obstructing wire or conveyor space.
codex.quest.ie_start.scaffold.text.2: Before working at height, add safe access and barriers wherever a fall is possible. Scaffolding alone neither transmits energy nor forms a machine without the other components and hammer activation. Keep a reserve with technical blocks to distinguish machine construction from workshop decoration.
codex.quest.ie_start.scaffold.title: Scaffolding and Stairs
codex.quest.ie_start.steel_service_batch: Prepare sixteen iron ingots and sufficient permitted blast-furnace fuel. Separate the intended batch from existing steel so actual production remains visible. Clear the furnace outputs and coke oven’s creosote tank before starting.

Run steel production and remove slag regularly. If the furnace stops, inspect both outputs and fuel before trying to supply FE. The crude furnace does not become faster when an electrical connector is placed on its wall.

Collect sixteen steel ingots in your ordinary inventory for detection. Possession does not prove automatic production and does not consume the metal. Keep the batch for your next industrial project; supply reliability is checked separately by deliberately interrupting and restoring the feed.
codex.quest.ie_start.steel_service_run.t: Manual: complete the coal-to-steel cycle and verify that accumulating creosote and slag does not block the next batch.

Run the complete coal-to-steel cycle on the prepared installation. Separate test iron and coal from old coke reserves and finished ingots. First produce fresh coke in the coke oven, then use it to turn iron into steel in the blast furnace.

During operation, remove creosote and extract slag. Verify that accumulation of either byproduct does not block the next batch: leave fluid capacity and space in the slag output. The crude furnace is serviced manually, while the improved version permits the corresponding automation.

After the first batch, start another in the same way and confirm continued production. Mark the manual objective only after the full coal-to-steel path and the creosote and slag checks. Codex does not measure this installation automatically; unrelated ingots from another store do not prove the trial.
codex.quest.ie_start.steel_service_setup: This node prepares servicing for the blast furnace you have already learned. The engineer’s hammer is needed for formation and structural checks, but one tool does not establish steel production. Place separate iron, fuel and product chests beside the furnace while preserving interface access.

Open the furnace and check permitted fuel, available iron and free steel and slag outputs. The coke oven must also keep removing creosote, otherwise coke supply can unexpectedly stop at a full fluid tank. Recognising the link between these two processes helps early.

The crude furnace is serviced manually; avoid surrounding it with unsupported decorative automation. Obtaining the hammer completes item preparation only. The next node checks a steel batch, while a separate manual objective checks supply and recovery after an ordinary interruption.
codex.quest.ie_start.treated.text.0: Treated wood connects coke production with engineering structures. It needs ordinary planks and creosote from the coke oven. Do not discard accumulated fluid merely to clear the oven: the early workshop needs many preserved wooden components.
codex.quest.ie_start.treated.text.1: Collect creosote in a suitable container and craft treated wood using its recipe. This objective requires thirty-two blocks of the horizontal variant; other decorative variants may not match the requested item. Obtain the required form before making stairs, fences and decoration.
codex.quest.ie_start.treated.text.2: Return the empty container to the oven and establish permanent fluid storage. If crafting rejects a container, check both the recipe and its actual creosote contents rather than relying on a similar fluid colour. Workbenches and early generating equipment need treated wood, so retain a small dedicated reserve.
codex.quest.ie_start.treated.title: Treated Wood
codex.quest.ie_start.workbench.text.0: The engineer’s workbench supports blueprint crafting and modifying compatible tools. It is a separate block crafted through an ordinary recipe. Prepare treated wood and the other components, place it with access to the work surface and open its interface.
codex.quest.ie_start.workbench.text.1: Blueprints contain different recipe groups. Check the category name: a random blueprint with the same item identifier does not necessarily contain press moulds or electronic components. Obtain the required category through the crafting or acquisition method shown by the manual and JEI.
codex.quest.ie_start.workbench.text.2: Insert the blueprint, choose an available output and prepare the exact materials. Manual work at this bench does not need an industrial electrical grid. Later it accepts drills, saws and weapons for component installation; do not confuse it with the large automated workbench, which does require power and item supply.
codex.quest.ie_start.workbench.title: Engineer's Workbench
codex.quest.life_furniture.comforts2.tex: A Comforts hammock provides another resting option alongside a home bed and travelling sleeping bag. It needs Rope and Nail attachments plus the hammock itself; attachments alone do not form a complete sleeping place.

Craft attachments from string and iron or an available rope recipe. One operation produces a pair. Carry them for the objective, then inspect the hammock recipe and prepare suitable supports with space to suspend it between them.

After placement, check access and the sleeping conditions shown by the game. Under default settings a hammock supports daytime rest, although configuration can change those rules. Keep a normal bed at the base as your permanent respawn point and use the hammock for your chosen resting routine.
Create’s copper shingles give a workshop a recognisable industrial appearance. They are decorative building material and need no rotational power for placement, but a large roof deserves an advance material count.

Inspect the Copper Shingles recipe in JEI and prepare its processed copper. Make a small batch and carry a block for the goal. Build a sample roof or cladding section to inspect its pattern beside your chosen wood, stone and windows.

Check how the material changes over time and inspect available treatment or coating recipes. Avoid accidentally mixing copper states when a uniform surface is intended. The sample makes it easier to estimate supplies and finish the workshop without rebuilding the whole roof.
codex.quest.life_furniture.domum.text.0: The Domum Ornamentum Architect’s Cutter creates building parts from selected materials. It is useful both in a colony and your own workshop, letting the same shape use different finishes without finding a separate fixed block for every combination.
codex.quest.life_furniture.domum.text.1: Craft the cutter and register the inventory goal. Place it, open the interface and choose a simple shape. Supply the required materials in their slots and inspect the preview before producing a large batch.
codex.quest.life_furniture.domum.text.2: Make one piece and place it beside the intended wall or roof. Check material compatibility and placement direction. Not every input suits every variation, so follow the interface’s accepted materials. A successful sample can then be repeated across the relevant building section.
codex.quest.life_furniture.domum.title: Domum Ornamentum
Eternal Tales decoration brings reminders of your travels into your home. A Soul Lava Lamp can become one such accent, but crafting it depends on materials from the appropriate stage of the mod. It need not be pursued on your first evening.

Open its JEI entry and trace the recipe to familiar ingredients. Follow the Eternal Tales branch for materials still beyond your reach; the relevant world’s description explains when to travel there. Craft the lamp and carry it for the item goal.

Place it in a test area and compare it with nearby lighting and materials. Verify the actual room instead of assuming a decorative object provides sufficient light. It works well as one distinctive detail alongside ordinary furnishings and collected trophies.
codex.quest.life_furniture.et_deco.title: Eternal Tales Decor
codex.quest.life_furniture.furnicraft.ta: Furnish and test a small resting corner
codex.quest.life_furniture.furnicraft.te: After learning individual furniture pieces, assemble a small resting corner. It gives the base a recognisable living space where you can pause between projects and find nearby supplies. Choose furnishings available in your world, such as Handcrafted pieces.

Place seating, a small surface and a light source. Match materials to the surrounding walls and leave a passage to the door and main workstations. Test the interaction of any functional furniture after placement.

Walk through the room, use the seating or chosen furniture and inspect the lighting before confirming the manual objective. Size is unimportant: a useful small arrangement teaches furnishing better than a room filled with every decorative item at once.
codex.quest.life_furniture.guide_furnish: Test the working route through a fully furnished room

A finished room should withstand an ordinary working day. Check that furniture, doors and decoration do not obstruct the route from entry to storage, rest and outdoors. Everyday use reveals the layout’s quality.

Walk the route carrying supplies, open the required containers, use the selected furniture and return items to storage. Inspect roof edges and the doorway, since pieces from different collections may need adjusted placement. Remove details that repeatedly block access.

Confirm the goal after fixing the obstacles. The room need not be large or expensive; its value lies in coherent materials and convenient use. You can now repeat successful choices in other spaces while preserving your base’s character.
A room that works every day
codex.quest.life_furniture.guide_materia: Build a room sample and choose its material combination

Before building at scale, view your materials together. Make a small sample of the wall, floor and ceiling edge using intended blocks. One successful corner explains more than separate inventory icons.

Place the main surfaces and add your chosen window or door. If using the Architect’s Cutter, make trial finishes and compare them in place. Inspect the sample from inside and outside under the room’s ordinary lighting.

Confirm the goal after choosing a combination to repeat. Record materials and part shapes so you do not have to guess between similar variants later. Expansion becomes easier once you know how neighbouring surfaces and their transitions fit together.
codex.quest.life_furniture.guide_room_li: Inspect lighting at entrances, workstations and room corners

Decorative lighting should help you navigate the room. Place it near entrances, workstations and passages, then inspect dark corners. A bright central accent does not guarantee adequate light behind cabinets or stairs.

Begin with ordinary lanterns or another familiar source, then add your chosen decorative fixture. Inspect the room without relying on sunlight through windows. Check access to switchable devices and power requirements where applicable.

Tick the goal after reviewing the entire room and fixing awkward dark areas. The Codex does not measure illumination automatically. Keep functional light alongside decoration so the interior remains convenient at night and after adjacent rooms expand.
codex.quest.life_furniture.handcrafted.t: Handcrafted makes a living space feel inhabited through seating, soft details and places to rest. Craft a bench and a blue cushion for your introduction. They are separate item goals and both need to enter your inventory.

Inspect their JEI recipes and prepare wood and cushion materials. Place the bench in a small test corner, then try the available cushion and seating interactions. Check that a chosen detail fits the particular furniture before furnishing the entire room.

Leave a clear passage and test nearby chests and doors. Decoration should not turn the workshop into an obstacle course. After the inventory goals register, use this trial arrangement as the basis for a resting place beside your base.
codex.quest.life_furniture.macaw.text.0: Macaw’s collections furnish the shell of a house through roofs, doors and windows. This introduction needs an oak roof, oak Japanese door and oak window. A combined sample reveals how their shapes connect before you begin a large facade.
codex.quest.life_furniture.macaw.text.1: Find each item in JEI and craft a small supply from its listed materials. Keep the three required items in your inventory, then build a short wall section with an opening and roof edge. Place pieces from different directions to understand orientation.
codex.quest.life_furniture.macaw.text.2: Open the door, inspect the window and walk beneath the eaves. Fix awkward joins in the sample now. You can then repeat the chosen design across the building with consistent openings and convenient access to its working rooms.
codex.quest.life_furniture.macaw.title: The Macaw's Series
codex.quest.life_furniture.refurbished.t: Refurbished Furniture combines furnishings and household devices. A computer and white bath introduce a workspace and domestic room fittings. Not everything uses an ordinary crafting table; some recipes require the mod’s own Workbench.

Open both JEI recipes and read their categories. The computer uses Workbench Constructing with iron, copper, glass, redstone and amethyst. Prepare that workstation, supply its required materials and create the items for both goals.

After completion, place the furniture in a test area and inspect available interactions. Check activation and connection requirements separately for functional devices; a finished-looking room does not guarantee every feature works. Begin with one convenient workspace that can expand later.
codex.quest.life_world.compass.text.0: Two similar-looking compasses answer different questions. Nature’s Compass searches for biomes, such as a particular forest or desert. Explorer’s Compass searches registered structures, including villages and dungeons. Neither is a universal locator for arbitrary blocks, creatures or chests.
codex.quest.life_world.compass.text.1: Craft both items using this pack’s recipes and open the appropriate compass interface. Select a biome or structure, start the search and wait for a result. Compare its direction with your map: the straight route may cross an ocean, mountain range or dangerous dungeon.
codex.quest.life_world.compass.text.2: A failed search does not prove the target is absent from the entire world. Check the dimension, selected name and search limits; moving your search origin can help. Save successful coordinates as a separate waypoint so that your next search does not erase an earlier landmark.
codex.quest.life_world.compass.title: Explorer's Compasses
codex.quest.life_world.dh.task.0: Read about distant rendering and its limitations
codex.quest.life_world.dh.text.0: A distant mountain ridge can be a useful landmark long before you reach it. Distant Horizons renders faraway terrain using simplified models. These extend the visible landscape beyond ordinary render distance, but they do not replace the actual blocks around your player.
codex.quest.life_world.dh.text.1: Visibility and world activity are different things. A distant image cannot confirm a chest’s contents, show every machine or prove that a farm is running. Buildings and entities outside normal loading may look different or be absent; interaction requires moving closer.
codex.quest.life_world.dh.text.2: If the horizon fills in gradually, allow time for data preparation. When performance suffers, reduce distant rendering or generation settings one at a time and compare the result. This is a reference quest: mark it after reading, then use silhouettes to plan routes and the map for precise coordinates.
codex.quest.life_world.dh.title: Distant Horizons
codex.quest.life_world.guide_alpine.text: Alpine surveying differs from a walk across a plain: the direction may be correct while no direct passage exists. Find Terralith’s Alpine Grove to practise approaching a biome with the terrain in mind.

Select the biome in Nature’s Compass and take food, torches and blocks for safe climbing. If the search finds nothing, move to another area and try again. The compass points towards a destination rather than plotting a convenient trail; walking around a cliff is often wiser than climbing its face.

Enter the biome itself for the visit goal to register. Mark a convenient approach and a resting place before exploring steep slopes. The useful result is a route a heavily laden traveller can repeat without risky jumps, rather than a new altitude record.
Compile an atlas of three biomes and check one route
Three discovered biomes become more useful when linked by a clear map. Turn your field notes into a small atlas: names, coordinates, approaches and reasons to return belong together rather than among unlabelled markers.

Review the entries for the Alpine Grove, Andesite Caves and Moonlight Grove. Give each a dimension, a safe entrance and an accessible route from home or an intermediate camp. Describe hazardous stretches directly; an attractive marker cannot replace a warning about a cliff.

Choose one location and reconstruct its route from the notes. Tick the manual goal after successfully checking it. This atlas will help place a settlement, mine or transport line using surveyed terrain rather than straight-line distance alone.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_atlas.title: An atlas of useful places
codex.quest.life_world.guide_cave_survey: A cave is a route with its own turns and changes in elevation. Locate Terralith’s Andesite Caves for this survey. Familiar stone is not enough to identify the biome: check its name, since isolated andesite blocks also occur elsewhere.

Bring light, food, a sound pickaxe and building blocks. Nature’s Compass can search for the biome, but arranging the descent remains your responsibility; never dig straight beneath yourself. Mark junctions consistently and leave a safe way up whenever you descend to another level.

The goal records entry into the named biome. Afterwards, find the exit without cutting a random tunnel and mark its surface entrance. A surveyed cave is much easier to turn into a working mine because you already know its access route, hazards and material transport direction.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_field_kit.t: A long journey starts with equipment that lets you survive a wrong turn. Light, food, spare blocks and working tools matter more than a random treasure. Prepare them before leaving, rather than discovering an empty food supply at the bottom of an unfamiliar cave.

Carry 32 torches and eight cooked steaks for this inventory goal. Add a pickaxe, a weapon, climbing blocks and room for discoveries. Other food remains useful for travelling, but this particular objective checks cooked beef. Your supplies are not consumed.

Mark home on the map and inspect equipment durability before departure. Leave unnecessary valuables behind: a spare rare machine component will not help you escape a ravine. You can now scout a short route and return while its landmarks are still familiar.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_moonlight.t: An expedition does not always begin with a missing ingot. Sometimes it is useful to locate an unusual biome, understand its surroundings and preserve the site for a future building. Terralith’s Moonlight Grove is the destination for this independent journey.

Find the biome with Nature’s Compass and prepare your usual travel supplies. Its name does not require a night visit: the objective checks the biome rather than the time of day. Daylight makes approaches, changes in elevation and nearby safe ground easier to assess.

After entering, save a marker and a few observations in your journal. Avoid dismantling the entire landscape for a casual sample; you may later want a home or a route stop here. The quest records your visit, while choosing and carefully surveying a site remains your field work.
A map stores coordinates, but does not explain why a place deserves another visit. Keep a field journal for locations with practical value: resource deposits, safe passages, interesting structures and encounters with unusual creatures.

Craft a book and quill and carry it for the inventory objective. Record the location’s name, dimension, coordinates and reason to return. Add a relevant obstacle, such as a cliff, flooded entrance or enemies. Leave the book unsigned while you still want to edit it.

The Codex checks for the book, rather than reading its pages. Try reconstructing the route from your notes later; if you have to guess, add a landmark. This habit becomes especially useful when a material search takes you back to a biome discovered many game days ago.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_notes.title: Field notes
codex.quest.life_world.guide_outpost.tas: Run an expedition through an equipped outpost
codex.quest.life_world.guide_outpost.tex: Once an area is surveyed and the route home is tested, a temporary camp can become an outpost. Its purpose is to support expeditions by storing supplies, receiving discoveries and providing a safe place to prepare the next trip.

Build shelter near your chosen route and light both its interior and approaches. Separate travel supplies from incoming materials; add a crafting table and the equipment you actually use in the field. Record the outpost’s purpose in your atlas and connect it to the nearest waystone.

Use the site for a real outing: take supplies, return with discoveries, unload and replenish what you used. Then confirm the objective. Your map now joins home, surveyed terrain and functioning travel infrastructure in a practical network.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_return_cach: Stock a route cache and locate it using the map

A field cache matters most when an expedition has gone badly. A small barrel of food, light and building blocks near a safe landmark lets you wait out the night, unload your inventory and prepare for the journey home.

Place storage in a protected location on your surveyed route. Leave food, torches and building blocks, light the approach and create a clearly named map marker. A chest alone is not a shelter: its surroundings must also give you room to avoid being surprised by enemies.

Leave the site and find it again using the map. Tick the goal after this check and after stocking the cache; crafting a barrel says nothing about its placement. Replenish used supplies on your next visit so the reserve does not become an empty decoration.
Complete a round trip and inspect both arrival areas

A useful network proves itself through a reliable return with supplies, rather than a single impressive departure. Travel to the remote stop and test the journey home without relying on a lucky reserve of experience.

Check the displayed travel cost before leaving and keep enough for the return if your configuration charges for it. At the destination, find home in the list and travel back. Ensure supplies and approaches at both stones are accessible from the player’s arrival side.

Tick the manual goal after completing the round trip. Fix an unclear name, awkward landing or missing supplies now. A working pair of stones supports further exploration, while the walking route and recorded coordinates remain useful if your plans change.
Scout a route and return using your own markers
Your first survey should end with a return, rather than lost equipment. Choose a nearby visible destination: a hill, a shore, a woodland edge or a valley entrance. This route teaches map use without demanding survival across several unfamiliar biomes at once.

Create a home marker, travel to the destination and mark at least one intermediate landmark. Avoid height changes that would require a dangerous jump on the return trip. If you cross water, decide where you will reach dry land before entering it.

Return home using your markers before ticking the manual objective. The map should explain the route without vague memories of somewhere beyond the trees. A successful short survey becomes the beginning of paths to mines, villages and future staging posts.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_route.title: A route you can retrace
codex.quest.life_world.guide_staging.tas: Prepare a safe arrival area and supplies beside a waystone
codex.quest.life_world.guide_staging.tex: A waystone shortens a journey, but does not pack equipment for the traveller. Before turning a chance discovery into a permanent stop, prepare storage and a safe approach to its arrival point.

Light the area around an activated stone, remove immediate obstacles and place storage for travel supplies. Keep the arrival space clear so a traveller does not appear at a dangerous drop. Name the stop after its purpose or surroundings; similar unnamed destinations are easy to confuse.

Inspect the site on foot and match the stone’s name to a map marker. Tick the goal after preparing the location; carrying a waystone item is not required. The next step is to test an actual connection between two stops and ensure the return is as convenient as departure.
codex.quest.life_world.guide_waystone_pa: Activate two waystones and travel between them
A permanent transport link starts with two recognisable addresses. Activate waystones near home and in a surveyed area; discovered stones are suitable if their locations fit your route.

Visit both sites and interact with each stone to add it to your available destinations. Give them distinct names and inspect the travel list. Costs and restrictions depend on Waystones settings, so read the displayed cost instead of assuming travel is free.

Travel from the first stop to the second and inspect the arrival point. Tick the objective after a successful transfer. This only tests one direction: you still need to check that you can afford the return and that the required stone is available in the destination list.
Read how Lootr personal loot works
In multiplayer, the first explorer does not necessarily take all the loot. Lootr gives supported containers personal contents, so the same chest can offer each player a separate selection. Ordinary chests you place yourself do not automatically become personal loot containers.

When surveying a structure, inspect the container’s appearance and block tooltip. If it belongs to Lootr, open it with your own character and take what you need. Another player should open the same container independently rather than expecting you to transfer your contents.

Do not break an exploration chest merely to test it, since that can remove a convenient access point for the next traveller. Personal loot also does not imply unlimited resource regeneration: refresh behaviour depends on settings and container type. Read this explanation now and apply it during your next expedition.
codex.quest.life_world.lootr_world.title: Personal Loot
codex.quest.life_world.mobs.task.0: Read the advice for encounters with unfamiliar creatures
codex.quest.life_world.mobs.text.0: This world contains more than familiar Minecraft creatures. Mods add animals with their own behaviour, unusual enemies and bosses that demand more than casual travelling equipment. Size, bright colours or a calm stance are not reliable indicators of safety.
codex.quest.life_world.mobs.text.1: When you meet an unfamiliar creature, identify its name using an available tooltip and inspect the surroundings. Keep a retreat route open, avoid cliff edges and resist testing everything with a sword strike. Consult the relevant mod’s guide for unusual animals, because feeding and taming methods differ.
codex.quest.life_world.mobs.text.2: Record the encounter location if the creature may be useful later. Leave bosses and specially summoned enemies until their dedicated quests explain preparation and combat conditions. This reference objective requires no fight: it teaches the difference between observation, ordinary hunting and a targeted trophy expedition.
codex.quest.life_world.mobs.title: The Pack's Mobs
codex.quest.life_world.structures.task.0: Find and mark a modded structure on your map
codex.quest.life_world.structures.text.0: An unfamiliar building may be a workshop, settlement or dangerous encounter. Additional mods expand the structure pool, so a familiar silhouette does not guarantee vanilla rules inside. Treat your first visit as reconnaissance rather than a compulsory assault.
codex.quest.life_world.structures.text.1: Find a modded structure while exploring or with Explorer’s Compass. Inspect the approaches from outside, mark the entrance and identify a retreat route. Before going underground, leave unnecessary valuables at home and bring lighting, food and spare blocks.
codex.quest.life_world.structures.text.2: This objective only asks you to find a structure and confirm it manually; defeating its boss is not required. Examine chests, suspicious altars and unusual blocks carefully, reading their hints. A separate waypoint lets you return prepared once other branches provide appropriate equipment.
codex.quest.life_world.structures.title: Structures
codex.quest.life_world.terralith.task.0: Find and identify a Terralith biome
codex.quest.life_world.terralith.text.0: This pack gives the familiar Overworld a new geography. Terralith adds biomes and distinctive terrain: a broad valley may border a sheer ravine, while a large cave hides beneath a gentle slope. The biome name matters more than your first impression of the scenery.
codex.quest.life_world.terralith.text.1: Take food, torches and building blocks on a short scouting trip. Find a Terralith area and check its biome name using the debug screen or an available map display. The search compass introduced nearby can locate a specific target if wandering takes too long.
codex.quest.life_world.terralith.text.2: Record the coordinates and mark a convenient approach. Do not descend into a deep fissure without a return route: scenery reveals neither fall distance nor enemies below. Tick the manual goal after confirming the biome, creating your first useful observation for a resource atlas.
codex.quest.life_world.terralith.title: Terralith
codex.quest.life_world.waystones2.text.0: Waystones shorten journeys between established locations. A regular waystone becomes a destination after activation. Sharestones use colour-based networks: blue ones connect with other blue ones. This objective specifically requires a blue sharestone rather than any colour.
codex.quest.life_world.waystones2.text.1: Prepare a regular waystone, a blue sharestone and warp dust. Dust is a crafting ingredient and does not itself replace a teleport scroll. Place a stone somewhere convenient, activate it and give the destination a name you will recognise later.
codex.quest.life_world.waystones2.text.2: Before a long expedition, check available destinations and travel costs: dimension restrictions, cooldowns and experience costs depend on pack configuration. A placed block alone is not proof of a working destination. This quest tracks the items; a separate test journey verifies the network itself.
codex.quest.life_world.waystones2.title: Waystone Network
codex.quest.life_world.xaero.text.0: A map turns a walk into a route you can repeat. The minimap supports local navigation, the full map shows explored surroundings, and waypoints preserve important locations. This is particularly useful when several valleys or cave passages look alike.
codex.quest.life_world.xaero.text.1: Find the full-map binding in Xaero’s controls and open it. Create a clearly named home waypoint. Use separate markers for your mine entrance and discovered dungeons: “Cave entrance” is more useful than another unnamed point.
codex.quest.life_world.xaero.text.2: The map stores landmarks but does not itself grant permission to teleport. If a waypoint seems missing after travelling between worlds, check the selected dimension and waypoint set. Complete the manual goal after opening the map; later assignments turn individual markers into a network of reliable routes.
codex.quest.life_world.xaero.title: Xaero's Maps
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.altar.text: The Infusion Altar makes most resource seeds. Craft one altar, eight pedestals, and a Prosperity Seed Base from wheat seeds and four Prosperity Shards. Ordinary Inferium Seeds do not require this structure.

Place the altar and follow its displayed pedestal positions. Put the central recipe item on the altar and the other eight ingredients on the pedestals. Activate a complete batch with a Mystical Agriculture wand or redstone signal.

If nothing starts, inspect every position and essence tier rather than adding random items. A large stack on one pedestal does not replace several correctly filled pedestals. Keep the structure near storage for iron, elemental, and other resource seeds.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.augments.t: The Tinkering Table installs augments on essence tools and armour. Craft the table and an Unattuned Augment, then choose a property for mining, survival, or movement. The empty base provides no useful effect by itself.

Check the selected augment recipe and equipment compatibility. Gear tier and available slots limit installation; an expensive module may not fit an early tool. Place the item and completed augment in the table and inspect the result.

After installation, read the equipment tooltip and test the property safely. Compare the same operation before and after the change. This quest records the table and augment base, so finish the actual configuration before relying on its benefits during an expedition.
Awakening uses a separate altar, four pedestals, and four Essence Vessels. Arrange them according to the markers shown after placing the Awakening Altar. The vessels hold elemental essence and cannot be replaced with ordinary chests.

For the first awakened block, put a Supremium Block in the centre and four Cognizant Dust on the pedestals. Load ten Air, Earth, Water, and Fire Essence into separate vessels. Activate with redstone and collect the awakened block.

Uncraft it into essence, then combine two awakened essences with a Prosperity Ingot for the requested ingot. A missing element stalls the entire recipe. This tier upgrades Supremium equipment and requires elemental crops prepared in advance, not merely a large Inferium farm.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.crystal.te: The Infusion Crystal combines four essences of one tier into one of the next. Its starter recipe uses a diamond, Prosperity Shards, and Inferium. Craft it and prepare thirty-two Inferium for the eight Prudentium required here.

Place the crystal and four essences in the crafting grid and collect the result. Repeat eight times or use batch crafting. The crystal returns after each operation, but the ordinary version has limited durability, so watch its remaining uses.

Upgrading reduces quantity rather than multiplying material. Keep some Inferium for seeds and farmland expansion. Prudentium leads onward to Tertium, Imperium, and Supremium through the same four-to-one progression.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.essence_se: Harvest thirty-two fresh Inferium Essence from the prepared patch. Store several cycles separately from existing reserves. If the field is small, wait for repeated maturity instead of filling the gap with mining supplies.

With machine harvesting, inspect fuel, output slots, and crop condition. Produce should reach an accessible chest while the crop remains planted. An overflowing Harvester may leave items on the ground, so watch the collection area rather than only the quest counter.

Process part of the batch through a clear recipe, such as upgrading Inferium into Prudentium with a crystal. Keep seeds for another harvest. This prepares the manual growth, collection, storage, and processing check that old essence cannot demonstrate.
Harvest repeatedly, preserve planting stock, and process fresh essence

Confirm the farm after a repeated operating cycle. Grow the crop, harvest fresh essence, deliver it to the selected storage, and process some into useful material or a higher tier. Then wait for another maturation on the same patch.

Check that seeds remain planted, farmland survives, and any collector has fuel and output space. If a Seed Reprocessor is involved, keep planting reserves outside its input. Fix any interruption before marking completion.

The criterion is repeatable harvest and working processing, not a one-time withdrawal from an old chest. Afterwards, expand the field or change crops. First make sure the current transport handles its output without dropping supplies on the ground.

Set aside an Inferium patch for testing sustained farming. Craft at least one seed from eight essence and wheat seeds, plant it, and provide light. Protect the field from trampling and identify storage for its future harvest.

Choose a clear collection method: manual harvesting that preserves the crop, or a serviced Harvester. A machine needs fuel and an empty output chest immediately. Accelerators are optional; maturity and successful replanting matter first.

The item objective checks seeds in inventory, so let it register before planting. Later quests require fresh essence from this patch rather than ore finds. Keep starting reserves separate so new harvests can be distinguished from existing supplies.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.farmland.t: Essence Farmland improves crop output, while accelerators affect plants above them. Make eight Inferium Farmland and four accelerators. Upgrade farmland by applying essence or craft the blocks separately, then plant your crops.

Place accelerators in vertical columns beneath farmland, keeping the plant within each block’s stated range. They accelerate the first suitable plant above them; placing them beside a large field does not boost the entire area.

Compare several harvests on improved and ordinary soil. Higher farmland increases Inferium yield, while extra seed chances depend on the crop and matching tier. A single unsuccessful bonus roll proves little. Leave access below for expanding the columns.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.first_seed: This objective asks for sixteen Iron Essence, meaning actual resource-crop harvests. Make Iron Seeds on the altar using a Prosperity Seed Base, iron, and the appropriate essence tier. Check the specific arrangement before activation; Inferium is not suitable for every seed.

Plant the seeds on prepared, illuminated farmland and wait for full maturity. Harvest while preserving the crop for its next cycle. Do not immediately turn all Iron Essence into ingots; accumulate the objective quantity first.

After detection, use the Iron Essence crafting recipe to produce useful metal. This is a separate craft, not an ingot automatically delivered by each plant. The first patch demonstrates renewable workshop supply from an initial iron investment.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.guide_elem: Awakening Supremium needs four elemental essences in addition to Inferium. Start a separate patch with Air Seeds, then add Earth, Water, and Fire. Make each resource seed on the altar using its own recipe and label the planting positions.

Store elemental harvests separately and preserve all four kinds. The first awakened block requires ten essence of each element. Avoid processing your last batches into other resources before filling the future vessels.

The item objective records only the initial Air Seeds, while the branch prepares awakening supplies. Verify repeatable harvests from every crop before building the advanced altar. This prevents an expensive recipe from stalling because one element was forgotten.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.guide_soul: Choose one useful mob crop and prepare a dedicated Soul Jar. Start with a creature you can obtain safely and whose seed recipe you understand. Check the required fill before fighting random enemies.

Collect souls with the appropriate dagger or process suitable drops in a fuelled extractor. Inspect the jar after the first operation; its soul type must match your intended crop. Preserve a separate breeding pair when using passive animals.

An empty jar satisfies the item objective, but the future recipe needs it filled. Label its storage and keep unfinished projects separate. A completed jar turns one creature’s loot into a permanent resource crop, reducing repeated hunting trips.
One jar for a chosen creature
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.inferium.t: Collect thirty-two Inferium Essence and sixteen Prosperity Shards. Look for their ores during underground expeditions; Inferium also appears in creature loot. Keep the green essence and shards separate because their crafting roles differ.

Turn some Inferium into starter seeds by surrounding wheat seeds with eight essence. Plant them on prepared farmland with light and protection against trampling. This establishes renewable supply instead of perpetual ore hunting.

Keep enough stock until both item objectives register. Prosperity Shards are needed for seed bases and the Infusion Crystal, so reserve an equipment batch. Your first harvest supports higher essence tiers and an altar for resource crops.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.insanium.t: Insanium from Mystical Agradditions extends essence progression beyond Supremium. Establish sustained high-tier production and a suitable crystal, then collect eight essence. Nether Star production also requires infrastructure that Inferium fields alone cannot provide.

The Nether Star Crux recipe uses Insanium, two Nether Stars, two Withering Souls, and a Diamond Block. This already requires Wither victories and its rare materials. Place the crux beneath the farmland for the corresponding seeds; carrying it nearby does not satisfy the growth condition.

Harvest the crop essence and process it into Nether Star Shards. The quest requests three shards rather than three complete stars. Preserve the starter seeds and foundation so the expensive preparation becomes repeatable supply.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.machines.t: The Harvester collects mature crops and replants them. The Seed Reprocessor turns surplus seeds into their corresponding essence. Craft both devices and machine frames, reserving planting stock outside the processing line.

These Mystical Agriculture machines run on solid fuel and have an internal energy buffer. Load fuel, position the Harvester by the field, and inspect its working area. Keep internal inventory space available and move output regularly into storage.

Redstone can disable the Harvester, and overflowing output is left near the plants. Observe a complete harvest before adding transport. Feed only surplus seeds into the reprocessor; losing the last rare seed forces you to pay its altar recipe again.
codex.quest.magic_agriculture.souls.text: Mob seeds require souls stored in Soul Jars. Find Soulium Ore within Soulstone veins in the Nether, then make the dagger, ingot, and extractor. Prepare a Soul Jar for your chosen creature.

Kill the appropriate mobs with the Soulium Dagger while carrying a jar to collect souls. Watch its fill level; an ordinary kill with another weapon does not replace this mechanic. Preserve a breeding pair before collecting souls from passive livestock.

The Soul Extractor provides another route by processing suitable mob drops into souls using solid fuel. This is convenient for surplus loot but usually less efficient than the dagger. Filled jars are ingredients for mob seeds; an empty container alone cannot unlock them.
Supremium comes from repeatedly upgrading essence through Inferium, Prudentium, Tertium, Imperium, and Supremium. One top-tier essence represents two hundred fifty-six Inferium. Sixteen is already a large batch, so expand the farm first.

Ingots are separate: combine a Prosperity Ingot with two Supremium Essence. First let the guide detect sixteen essence together, then spend them on ingots; the earlier mark remains. Also show four ingots before using them in further crafts. Armour follows an upgrade chain, so check its previous tier.

Do not spend everything on one piece or leave your field without seeds. Divide reserves between equipment, new crops, and awakening. A Supremium Helmet is only part of a set and does not automatically demonstrate all protective bonuses.
codex.quest.magic_ars.apparatus.text.0: The Enchanting Apparatus combines a central reagent with pedestal ingredients. Prepare an Arcane Core beside its base as well as the apparatus; the structure cannot work without the core. Place pedestals within three blocks and leave each accessible.
codex.quest.magic_ars.apparatus.text.1: Distribute one recipe across the pedestals, then use its central reagent on the apparatus. Recipes with a Source cost need a charged jar nearby. A Starbuncle Charm is suitable for the first four pedestals, with four gold ingots around its token.
codex.quest.magic_ars.apparatus.text.2: The quest requires only four pedestals, but some recipes use eight; expand as needed. If activation fails, inspect the core, range, reagents, and Source cost. Collect the result before loading another batch to distinguish successful crafting from merely placed materials.
codex.quest.magic_ars.apparatus.title: Enchanting Apparatus
codex.quest.magic_ars.archmage.task.1: Upgrade to an Archmage’s Spell Book
codex.quest.magic_ars.archmage.text.0: The Archmage’s Spell Book unlocks tier-three glyphs but requires an Apprentice’s Spell Book first. Upgrade the novice book using obsidian, three diamonds, two Quartz Blocks, and two Blaze Rods. Proper upgrade recipes transfer learned spells.
codex.quest.magic_ars.archmage.text.1: For the next upgrade, combine the apprentice book with three Ender Pearls, two emeralds, a Totem of Undying, a Nether Star, and Wilden Tribute. The tribute comes from defeating the chimera summoned by an augmented summoning ritual, requiring separate battle preparation.
codex.quest.magic_ars.archmage.text.2: After crafting, check your saved spells and learn the desired higher glyphs at the Scribe’s Table. The book expands your options without making lengthy spells free. Test personal mana consumption and recovery before challenging a serious boss.
codex.quest.magic_ars.archmage.title: Archmage Spell Book
codex.quest.magic_ars.book.text.0: The Novice’s Spell Book is crafted from a normal book and four iron tools: sword, pickaxe, axe, and shovel. Prepare spare tools so crafting does not remove your working kit. Place a Scribe’s Table nearby for learning more glyphs.
codex.quest.magic_ars.book.text.1: Open the spell interface with its configured key and compose a short sequence from an available casting method and effect. Save the slot, hold the book, and test against a safe target. Complicated combinations consume personal mana quickly.
codex.quest.magic_ars.book.text.2: The novice book supports tier-one glyphs; higher tiers require an upgraded book. Owning it does not mean every effect is learned. The Scribe’s Table expands your repertoire, while Source Jars supply devices separately from your personal spell reserve.
codex.quest.magic_ars.book.title: Spell Book
codex.quest.magic_ars.familiars.text.0: Starbuncles and Drygmys serve different workshop roles. Offer a wild forest Starbuncle a gold nugget; it collects it and leaves a token. Throw a Wilden Horn to a wild Drygmy. Turn their materials into the respective charms using the apparatus.
codex.quest.magic_ars.familiars.text.1: Use the Starbuncle Charm on the ground. Dominion Wand connections from creature to chest set destinations; the reverse order sets extraction. Use the Drygmy Charm on Mossy Cobblestone to create a home henge, then place a chest and Source Jar beside it.
codex.quest.magic_ars.familiars.text.2: A Drygmy produces loot from creatures within ten blocks of its home without killing them, with diversity affecting output. These workers differ from the personal familiar system. Confirm deliveries to the intended chest before expanding.
codex.quest.magic_ars.familiars.title: Helpers
codex.quest.magic_ars.gems.text.0: An Imbuement Chamber turns amethyst or lapis into Source Gems. Craft the chamber, place it somewhere accessible, and insert a suitable raw item. Early gems need no external jar because the chamber slowly accumulates the required energy itself.
codex.quest.magic_ars.gems.text.1: Wait for completion, collect the result, and repeat until you have sixteen gems. A Source Jar within two blocks speeds up later operation. More complex recipes use extra reagents on pedestals within one block, usually as retained catalysts.
codex.quest.magic_ars.gems.text.2: Do not confuse physical gems with the Source stored in a jar. If the chamber stalls, check the input and chosen recipe conditions. Your first batch supplies the Scribe’s Table, energy transport, and further equipment.
codex.quest.magic_ars.gems.title: Source Gems
codex.quest.magic_ars.glyphs.text.0: In the installed version, new glyphs are made at the Scribe’s Table from specified ingredients and experience. Use your book on the table, select Light, and confirm. Prepare a lantern, a torch, and twenty-seven experience points, not twenty-seven levels.
codex.quest.magic_ars.glyphs.text.1: Drop the displayed ingredients onto the table; it can also pull from nearby inventories. Collect the completed Light glyph for objective detection, then use it to learn the effect. Old blank glyphs are not required crafting blanks here.
codex.quest.magic_ars.glyphs.text.2: To inscribe parchment, place blank parchment on the table, select the desired spell in your book, and sneak-use the book on the table. Check the recorded sequence. A glyph unlocks one spell component, while parchment stores a completed combination for compatible devices.
codex.quest.magic_ars.glyphs.title: Glyphs
codex.quest.magic_ars.guide_directed_lin: The Dominion Wand sets directional links for Source and worker creatures. Craft it and start with two labelled jars, source and destination. Put a relay within thirty blocks of its linked points and charge the source jar.

Click the source jar and then the relay to set extraction. Click the relay and then the receiving jar to set delivery. Order matters; proximity does not replace a saved connection. Keep the relay free of redstone power.

Watch both reserves change. Sneak-use the wand on the relay to clear incorrect links and configure them again. This direction principle also helps workers: creature-to-chest sets unloading, while the reverse sequence sets an item source.
codex.quest.magic_ars.guide_growth_sourc: The Agronomic Sourcelink converts natural plant growth into Source. Place it beside farmland or Sourceberry Bushes. It detects growth within fifteen blocks and outputs to jars within five blocks.

Plant several crops, provide light, and leave a jar nearby. Bone meal does not generate Source this way, so observe ordinary maturation. Magical plants such as Sourceberries and Archwood provide bonus output and suit a permanent garden.

After the first charge, connect a small consumer and check recovery from subsequent growth. Do not remove every plant while expanding the workshop or the sourcelink loses its work. Later a Starbuncle can harvest ripe berries, making the garden part of ongoing device supply.
codex.quest.magic_ars.guide_wilden_trial: The Archmage upgrade’s Wilden Tribute comes from the chimera rather than ordinary forest Wilden. Make a Summon Wilden tablet and place a Ritual Brazier on a separate arena far from home; the augmented summon destroys surrounding blocks.

Apply the tablet, then add a Wilden Spike, Wilden Horn, and Wilden Wing before activation. All three augments change the ordinary monster summon into the chimera. Check armour, weapons, healing, and movement space, then activate with an empty hand.

Keep moving, avoid attacks, and retain space to recover. Collect the tribute after victory and reserve it for the book upgrade. Without the three augments, the ritual summons ordinary monsters instead, so check ingredients before consuming the tablet.
codex.quest.magic_ars.notebook.text.0: The Worn Notebook explains Ars Nouveau devices and creatures. Obtain it and find a Sourceberry Bush in a taiga or Archwood Forest. Bring a bush home and leave a lit patch for growth and regular harvesting.
codex.quest.magic_ars.notebook.text.1: The berries provide food and personal mana regeneration for spellcasting. They are not ready-made Source fluid for a jar. Later, natural bush growth can power an Agronomic Sourcelink, while a Starbuncle handles harvesting.
codex.quest.magic_ars.notebook.text.2: Open the getting-started section and distinguish personal mana from the future device reserve. Plant before eating all your berries; a permanent bush is more valuable than one serving. Next, an Imbuement Chamber transforms ordinary crystals into the workshop’s basic material.
codex.quest.magic_ars.notebook.title: Worn Notebook
codex.quest.magic_ars.rituals.task.1: Create a Warp Portal with a Sourcestone frame, Source, and a bound scroll
codex.quest.magic_ars.rituals.text.0: A Ritual Brazier uses ritual tablets: apply a tablet, add accepted augments, then click with an empty hand to activate. The tablet is consumed. If the ritual needs Source, keep a jar within six blocks; redstone disables a running ritual.
codex.quest.magic_ars.rituals.text.1: This quest also requires a portal, made differently. Build a rectangular frame from Sourcestone or its variants, put a full Source Jar nearby, and throw a Warp Scroll with a recorded destination into the opening. An ordinary scroll only travels within the current dimension.
codex.quest.magic_ars.rituals.text.2: Verify a safe arrival point and establish a separate return route because the portal is one-way. After creation it needs no Source per passage. Crafting a brazier alone cannot earn the portal advancement; complete both parts and test travel without valuable cargo.
codex.quest.magic_ars.rituals.title: Rituals
codex.quest.magic_ars.source.text.0: Source powers Ars Nouveau equipment independently of personal mana. Craft a jar, relay, and Volcanic Sourcelink. Build the sourcelink on a nonflammable site because generation also creates heat, converting nearby stone into magma and eventually lava.
codex.quest.magic_ars.source.text.1: Supply suitable fuel, such as Archwood logs, and place a jar nearby to receive Source. For a remote consumer, use the Dominion Wand on jar then relay to set extraction, and relay then another jar to set delivery.
codex.quest.magic_ars.source.text.2: A relay reaches up to thirty blocks, and redstone disables transmission. Check the destination jar after actually supplying fuel. Crafting the three blocks does not prove the network; successful transfer supports apparatuses, rituals, and helpers without carrying every jar manually.
codex.quest.magic_ars.source.title: Source and Relays
codex.quest.magic_ars.source_service_bat: Make sixteen fresh Source Gems in the Imbuement Chamber from amethyst or lapis. Inspect the nearby jar before starting. The chamber can slowly make gems without one, so output alone does not prove external supply.

Keep the jar within two blocks and observe Source consumption during the batch. Feed raw items gradually and collect finished gems in separate storage. Ensure redstone has not disabled the relay and generation continues.

After the batch, leave the network running and wait for reserve recovery. These sixteen items are material output, not sixteen units of Source inside the jar. The following manual confirmation requires both crafting and visible replenishment after consumption.
codex.quest.magic_ars.source_service_run: Observe consumer Source use and recovery in the same jar

This manual test confirms a Source network under load. Run the chosen consumer from a nearby charged jar, obtain a new result, and observe the level decrease. Then watch that same jar refill from an active sourcelink or relay.

Check the ranges independently: the consumer must reach its jar and the relay its linked destination. Dominion Wand click order sets flow direction. Remove blocking redstone and restore fuel or the conditions for natural generation.

Confirm after observing both consumption and recovery, rather than merely making Source Gems. The chamber can work independently, so its crystals alone prove no transport. If the jar fails to recover, reduce demand, repair supply, and repeat the complete cycle.
codex.quest.magic_ars.source_service_set: For the Source test, place a dedicated jar near a chosen consumer. An Imbuement Chamber is convenient and needs the jar within two blocks. Supply it directly from a sourcelink or through a correctly directed relay, keeping every part observable.

With a Volcanic Sourcelink, provide a safe heat area and fuel reserve. An Agronomic Sourcelink needs natural plant growth; applying bone meal does not provide equivalent generation. Choose one clear method and fill the jar first.

The item objective records the storage block, not its reserve or production rate. Confirm the Source level actually rises before continuing. Separate raw crystals from new output so the following check cannot be confused with old supplies.
codex.quest.magic_botania.apothecary.tex: The Petal Apothecary combines petals into working flowers. Place it near water and prepare a bucket, the required petals, and seeds; the seed finishes the recipe and belongs last.
Fill the bowl with water, throw in the ingredients for one recipe, then the accepted seeds. A Pure Daisy needs four white petals. Collect the flower and refill the bowl before another craft.

If you make a mistake, use an empty hand to remove the last ingredient. Do not mix several recipes or fill the apothecary with lava: lava makes it destroy items. Your first successful flower unlocks living wood and stone.
codex.quest.magic_botania.daisy.text.0: Plant a Pure Daisy and surround it with eight blocks at the same height. Ordinary logs become Livingwood Logs, while smelted Stone becomes Livingrock. Cobblestone must be smelted first.
codex.quest.magic_botania.daisy.text.1: In the installed version the conversion takes about eight seconds at normal game speed. Collect the transformed blocks and replace the batch. The flower remains and needs no pool, mana, or redstone.
codex.quest.magic_botania.daisy.text.2: The quest asks for all-bark Livingwood rather than the resulting logs. Craft four Livingwood Logs in a square to obtain three Livingwood. Prepare twenty-four logs to exceed the sixteen-block target, and make extra Livingrock for the pool and altar.
codex.quest.magic_botania.daisy.title: Pure Daisy
codex.quest.magic_botania.endoflame.task: Obtain a generating flower such as an Endoflame
codex.quest.magic_botania.endoflame.text: An Endoflame turns suitable furnace fuel into mana. Combine two brown petals, one red, and one light gray in a water-filled apothecary, then finish with seeds. Plant it near a spreader and check its binding with the wand.

Drop one coal or charcoal nearby. The flower takes the fuel, starts working, and supplies the spreader. Do not dump your entire stock: another portion is needed after the previous one burns, otherwise items remain on the ground.

Fuel that returns a container, such as lava buckets, is unsuitable. If coal disappears but the pool does not fill, inspect the whole transport chain. Limit automated feeding; controlled delivery is more useful than a continuous shower of items.
codex.quest.magic_botania.flowers.task.1: Pick up a Botania mystical flower
codex.quest.magic_botania.flowers.text.0: Look for Botania mystical flowers on the Overworld surface, rather than ordinary vanilla flowers. Collect several colours, particularly white, brown, red, and light gray, for the first working flowers.
codex.quest.magic_botania.flowers.text.1: Craft some finds into petals. Apply Floral Fertilizer to grass to grow more mystical flowers, keeping a patch clear of buildings. Save one flower of each colour as a reserve.
codex.quest.magic_botania.flowers.text.2: This quest specifically requests a white mystical flower and fertilizer, so keep the last white flower intact until detected. Next prepare the Lexica Botania and Petal Apothecary; decorative mystical flowers do not generate mana.
codex.quest.magic_botania.flowers.title: Mystical Flowers
codex.quest.magic_botania.guide_fuel_gat: An Open Crate drops incoming items straight down and helps service an Endoflame. Position it above the feeding point and supply a small coal reserve through a hopper. Leave a workable distance between the landing point and flower, testing one portion first.

Add a wooden pressure plate at the landing point and use its signal to lock the supply hopper. While an item remains on the plate, another portion should not arrive; feeding resumes after the flower takes it.

Watch several cycles and ensure fuel does not accumulate. Add a delay if necessary to match the flower. The crate is only part of the circuit; the useful result is controlled feeding that can remain enabled.
codex.quest.magic_botania.lexicon.task.1: Open and use the Lexica Botania
codex.quest.magic_botania.lexicon.text.0: The Lexica Botania explains flower recipes, binding, and projections of large structures. Craft it early and open its basics section; it remains useful through your first pool and preparations for Gaia.
codex.quest.magic_botania.lexicon.text.1: Read the relevant entry before making an unfamiliar device. Enable the projection for multiblock structures and build against it, especially where similar materials have different roles.
codex.quest.magic_botania.lexicon.text.2: The advancement requires using the book, rather than merely owning it. It cannot replace the Wand of the Forest or control mana. Later, send it through an active Alfheim portal to receive it back with elven knowledge.
codex.quest.magic_botania.lexicon.title: Lexica Botania
codex.quest.magic_botania.mana_service_b: Produce eight Manasteel Ingots on the installation being tested. Prepare eight iron ingots and at least twenty-four thousand mana. If reserves are low, keep feeding the Endoflame and watch the transfer.
Transform a small batch and collect every new ingot. Inspect the pool with the wand before and after; the consumption should come from this operation rather than an unrelated functional flower.

Old Manasteel may satisfy the inventory objective, but the following manual confirmation needs a fresh operating batch. Store it separately and let the pool recover. This reveals whether generation keeps pace with production before you move to more expensive runes and Terrasteel.
codex.quest.magic_botania.mana_service_r: Make fresh Manasteel and observe mana recovery after consumption

This manual mark confirms a full operating cycle. Make a fresh batch of Manasteel on the assembled line and observe the pool losing mana. Then keep generation running and watch reserves recover after that expenditure.

While waiting, check Endoflame fuel, its binding, spreader aim, and the clear burst path. With automatic feeding, confirm that another portion arrives and unwanted items do not accumulate around the flower.

Confirm only after observing both a successful conversion and subsequent pool replenishment. Previously stored mana and ingots from a chest do not prove this. If reserves keep falling, reduce demand or expand generation and repeat the experiment.
codex.quest.magic_botania.mana_service_s: Prepare a clear area for testing mana generation. Position the pool and spreader so both are visible from the working path. Plant an Endoflame nearby, prepare fuel, and keep the wand ready.

First check the flower-to-spreader binding, then the spreader aim at the pool. Remove obstructions and accidental redstone power. Supply one fuel item and confirm transport starts before adding automated feeding.

The item objectives record two blocks, not actual mana flow. Keep the installation assembled for the next Manasteel batch. The following test requires observing consumption and recovery, so accumulate a visible reserve in advance.
codex.quest.magic_botania.manasteel.text: Make the first mana materials directly in a pool. Drop iron ingots, ender pearls, and diamonds in small separate batches; sufficient mana transforms them into Manasteel, Mana Pearls, and Mana Diamonds.

One iron ingot costs three thousand mana, a pearl six thousand, and a diamond ten thousand. The eight ingots and the other two objectives require forty thousand in total. A starter generator needs time even after you have crafted the pool.

Collect the results and let reserves recover between batches. An ordinary item floating on the pool means conversion has not happened yet; check the recipe and reserve. These materials unlock portable storage, sparks, and rune production, so save some ingots.
codex.quest.magic_botania.pool.text.0: A Mana Pool stores energy for transforming metal, pearls, and diamonds. Make a normal pool from Livingrock and place it where a spreader can fire directly into it without a wall blocking the path.
codex.quest.magic_botania.pool.text.1: Its initial fill bar is barely visible because normal capacity is enormous compared with one flower. Inspect it with the Wand of the Forest and wait for several bursts before diagnosing a failure.
codex.quest.magic_botania.pool.text.2: Do not confuse the normal pool with the much smaller Diluted Mana Pool. Owning the block satisfies the item objective but proves no mana supply. The following steps provide a spreader and fuel generator so the pool can pay for recipes.
codex.quest.magic_botania.pool.title: Mana Pool
codex.quest.magic_botania.potato.text.0: The Tiny Potato is a small Botania workshop decoration. Take an ordinary potato and transform it in a mana pool; this is a quiet experiment after your first metal recipes and transport setup.
codex.quest.magic_botania.potato.text.1: Place it beside your work area without obstructing spreader bursts or access to the apothecary. A little shelf near the Lexicon leaves the important machines accessible for adjustment and replenishment.
codex.quest.magic_botania.potato.text.2: The potato does not replace a generating flower, mana receiver, or storage system. Obtaining the requested item completes the objective; decoration provides no hidden production bonus. After this optional pause, return to runes or a sustained-supply test for your pool.
codex.quest.magic_botania.potato.title: Tiny Potato
codex.quest.magic_botania.spark.text.0: Sparks move large amounts of mana between supported devices without spreader bursts. Place one on a pool and another on a compatible consumer, such as a Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate. The consumer requests mana when its recipe starts.
codex.quest.magic_botania.spark.text.1: Two ordinary sparks over neighbouring pools do not automatically transfer mana between them; that requires spark augments. Start with one pool-to-consumer pair and keep the devices close together.
codex.quest.magic_botania.spark.text.2: The Wand of the Forest displays connections; dyed sparks must share a colour channel. Crafting a spark earns the advancement, while actual network operation needs a separate consumption check. Sparks become particularly useful for Terrasteel and its large mana transfer.
codex.quest.magic_botania.spark.title: Sparks
A Mana Spreader receives mana from generating flowers and fires bursts into a pool. The first one uses Livingwood, copper, and a petal. It transports energy and produces nothing without a working flower.

Place it near your planned Endoflame and aim it at the pool with the Wand of the Forest. Inspect the trajectory: bursts must reach the pool instead of hitting a wall edge or losing mana over an excessive distance.

After supplying fuel, observe both the spreader reserve and pool. If the former fills while the latter remains empty, check aim and obstructions. A redstone signal stops a normal spreader from firing, so an accidental nearby lever can halt the line.
codex.quest.magic_botania.spreader.title: Mana Spreader
codex.quest.magic_botania.tablet.text.0: A Mana Tablet carries energy in your inventory and powers compatible tools and accessories. Craft the tablet and Mana Ring, remembering that an empty container cannot pay for equipment abilities.
codex.quest.magic_botania.tablet.text.1: Drop the tablet into a charged pool and inspect the transfer direction with the wand. The pool mode determines whether the portable item charges or returns mana. Wait for a visible charge, retrieve it, and test one compatible tool.
codex.quest.magic_botania.tablet.text.2: The ring fits an accessory slot and saves main inventory space. Keep part of the reserve during testing for your return trip and equipment needs. This brings magic outside the workshop while retaining the need for mana production at home.
codex.quest.magic_botania.tablet.title: Mana in Your Pocket
codex.quest.magic_botania.wand.text.0: The Wand of the Forest configures equipment and displays mana. Make Livingwood Twigs from Pure Daisy materials and add two petals. Their colours affect the wand appearance, not the power of your installation.
codex.quest.magic_botania.wand.text.1: In bind mode, sneak-right-click the connection source and then its destination. Bind a generating flower to a spreader and a mana-consuming functional flower to a pool. Sneak-right-click in the air to switch wand modes.
codex.quest.magic_botania.wand.text.2: Read a block tooltip with the wand before breaking equipment that appears idle. Check the spreader direction and each flower destination. This is the main diagnostic tool for your Botania network.
codex.quest.magic_botania.wand.title: Wand of the Forest
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.corporea.t: Corporea moves items between inventories using special sparks. Build a small network with ordinary sparks above chests and the index and one master node. The master cannot see its own inventory, so store useful supplies beneath ordinary sparks.

Neighbouring sparks connect over roughly eight blocks; extend longer networks in chains. All nodes must share a colour and exactly one master. Inspect connections with the wand, then put a test batch into a connected chest.

Approach the index and request an item by name or use the configured request key while hovering over an item in an interface. “10 of this” refers to your held item. Confirm delivery and reduced storage contents; sparks do not insert new items into chests.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.elven_gear: Elementium improves protection, while Dreamwood upgrades mana transport. Craft the Elementium Helmet and Elven Mana Spreader from your new trading resources. Divide supplies between equipment and future Gaia Pylons before crafting.

When replacing the old spreader, check its aim and flower bindings again. An improved block does not automatically fix network geometry; bursts must still hit the chosen receiver. Test the updated line with a small fuel batch.

Equip the helmet, assess overall protection, and provide portable mana for compatible items. This objective does not require a full elven set, but one armour piece is insufficient preparation for Gaia. Continue into Corporea storage or complete your battle equipment.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.gaia1.task: Defeat the normal Guardian of Gaia
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.gaia1.text: Prepare an active beacon with its base, four Gaia Pylons, and a Terrasteel Ingot to sacrifice. Arrange the pylons using the Lexicon ritual projection and clear the arena for movement.

Equip enchanted armour, a strong weapon, healing brews, food, and charged accessories. Start by sneak-right-clicking the beacon with the ingot, which is consumed. Beacon effects are suppressed during the fight, so do not rely on beacon regeneration.

Avoid purple hazardous areas, deal with spawned enemies, and retain room to retreat. Collect Gaia Spirits after victory and check the advancement. More participants increase ritual difficulty. Defeat the ordinary Guardian before attempting the stronger version and expensive upgrades.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.gaia2.task: Defeat the stronger Guardian of Gaia
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.gaia2.text: Summon the stronger Guardian on the same working arena using a different offering. Combine one Terrasteel Ingot with four Gaia Spirits from the ordinary fight to make a Gaia Spirit Ingot. Check equipment and supplies before spending your last spirits.

Repair armour, charge mana, and replenish healing. Sneak-use the new ingot on the active beacon with its four pylons. The offering is consumed; an ordinary Terrasteel Ingot summons the earlier version and cannot complete the hard-mode challenge.

Move carefully and control spawned enemies. Stay out of purple hazards and remember that beacon effects remain suppressed. After victory, collect rewards including a possible Dice of Fate, and verify the stronger-Guardian advancement before pursuing relics.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.guide_visi: The Corporea Crystal Cube displays a selected item’s network count. Craft it and add an ordinary Corporea Spark linked to your existing same-colour network, which must still have exactly one master.

Use a sample item, such as an iron ingot, on the cube. Compare the displayed count with connected chest contents. Punching requests one item and sneak-punching requests a stack; begin with a single request.

The displayed quantity should fall after delivery. If it is incorrect, inspect spark gaps and supplies stored beneath the master, which cannot see its own inventory. Keep the cube beside your workbench as a clear supply indicator instead of opening every chest.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.portal.tas: Open the Alfheim gateway with the Wand of the Forest
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.portal.tex: Prepare an Elven Gateway Core, eight Livingwood blocks, three Glimmering Livingwood, two pools, and two Natura Pylons. Build the frame against the Lexicon projection because normal and glimmering pieces occupy specific positions.

Place two charged pools nearby, each with a Natura Pylon directly above it, within the eleven-by-eleven-by-eleven area around the core. Click the core with the wand; an empty pool or incorrect frame cannot sustain the connection.

The portal transports items, not players. First send the Lexicon through and collect the expanded book, then begin trading. Watch both pools: energy is drawn evenly, and an exhausted participant closes the portal.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.rank_ss.ta: Infuse a Terra Shatterer to rank SS
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.rank_ss.te: The Terra Shatterer gains ranks by absorbing enormous amounts of mana. Craft the pick and drop it into a pool configured to charge items. The absorbed energy remains inside the tool and cannot be returned like a tablet reserve.

After rank B, each following threshold grows tenfold; SS requires one billion mana. This is a long-term network load, so establish continuous production and observe actual rank changes. One full pool cannot supply the final level.

Ranks increase the active mining area rather than simply mining speed. Toggle the ability by sneak-right-clicking in the air, and carry mana for durability. Test the wide excavation area away from your base and disable the ability when not mining.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.relics.tas: Obtain your own Ring of Odin relic
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.relics.tex: Dice of Fate come from the stronger Gaia ritual rewards. Defeat that Guardian and collect the loot, keeping a die in your inventory until the item objective registers. Then use it to obtain a relic; this consumes the die.

Relics bind to their owner, so another player’s reward is not equivalent to your own result. This quest also requires the Ring of Odin. Your first relic may be different, requiring further victories and rolls.

Once you obtain the ring, equip it in the appropriate slot and inspect its protection and extra health. An arbitrary relic does not satisfy Odin’s separate advancement. Keep the arena and sustained Terrasteel production ready for repeated prepared fights.
codex.quest.magic_botania_end.trade.text: Obtain elven materials by trading through active gates. Send two Manasteel Ingots for each Elementium Ingot, so prepare eight for the four-ingot objective. A Mana Pearl trades for Pixie Dust and a Mana Diamond for Dragonstone.
