Livingwood becomes the corresponding Dreamwood variant. This quest needs all-bark Dreamwood, so send all-bark Livingwood rather than logs; logs have a separate trade. Send small batches and collect each returned result.

Both portal pools must retain mana. If nothing returns, stop feeding items and check the connection and exact trade ingredients. These four materials supply improved equipment, spreaders, and later trial infrastructure. Do not send random valuables without a trade recipe.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.altar.te: Craft a Runic Altar from five Livingrock and a Mana Pearl; the installed recipe also accepts a Mana Diamond. Place it separately from the pool and aim a sufficiently supplied spreader at it.

Add the chosen rune ingredients by right-clicking or dropping them. Once the complete recipe is present, wait for mana charging to finish. Drop Livingrock onto the altar and click with the Wand of the Forest to complete the craft.

A forgotten finishing stone or final wand click often explains an apparent stall. Another cause is a spreader still aimed at the pool. Start with one simple rune to verify the entire sequence before using expensive components.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.belt.tex: The Sojourner’s Sash spends a little mana on movement speed, higher jumps, and easier terrain traversal. Craft it after learning runes and prepare a charged tablet or ring; its conveniences require available mana.
Equip it in the correct accessory slot and test a level path with a one-block ledge. Normal movement steps up the ledge automatically; sneaking changes that behaviour and helps with precise work.

Do not test your first acceleration beside a cliff or lava. Learn the jump distance and reserve consumption before an expedition. Obtaining the sash completes the quest, while a short walk confirms it is equipped and powered.
The Botanical Brewery makes multiple-dose brews using its own recipes. Prepare a Botania vial, ingredients for one brew, and a spreader aimed at the brewery. A vanilla brewing stand cannot replace it; mana acts as both solvent and energy.

Add the empty vial first, then all reagents for one recipe by clicking or dropping them. Once enough mana arrives, collect the finished brew. The advancement requires a filled vial, rather than merely crafting the block.

Choose useful effects before an expedition, such as healing, fire resistance, or regeneration. Check remaining doses; similar-looking vials are not unlimited. Partially used vials of the same brew can be combined in a crafting grid to consolidate supplies.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.elements: Make the four basic runes separately. Each uses Manasteel and Mana Powder, produced by treating a suitable ordinary powder in the pool. Water also needs bone meal, sugar cane, and a fishing rod; Air uses a carpet, feather, and string.

Earth needs Stone, a Coal Block, and a mushroom. Fire needs a Nether Brick item, gunpowder, and nether wart; check that you have the item rather than a brick block. Finish each recipe with mana, Livingrock, and a wand click.

Store completed runes separately. Rune catalysts return from later Runic Altar recipes, but that rule does not extend to the apothecary or crafting table. These four elements unlock seasonal runes and the Terrasteel plate.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.flowers2: Obtain a functional flower such as a Hopperhock

The Hopperhock collects dropped items and places them in nearby storage. Craft it in the apothecary and plant it beside the collection area with an accessible chest. As a functional flower, it binds to a pool when using mana, rather than to a spreader.
Drop one disposable item in its working area and confirm it reaches the intended chest. Item frames on inventories provide filters; verify a simple unfiltered setup before adding restrictions.

Keep it from stealing apothecary ingredients, altar components, or Endoflame fuel. Obtaining the flower completes the item objective; a test transfer proves useful operation. Filtering supports crop collection and safer servicing of other magical equipment.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.guide_re: A seasonal rune demonstrates the difference between consumed ingredients and catalysts. For Spring, prepare Water and Fire runes, three saplings, and wheat. Put everything on the Runic Altar and supply eight thousand mana.

Once ready, add Livingrock and finish with the wand. Collect the Rune of Spring alongside the returned input runes. Count your materials before another operation so a catalyst is not left outside storage.

This return applies to the Runic Altar operation; a petal recipe may consume its runes. Save Spring for the Terrasteel Helmet. Understanding these roles reduces unnecessary basic-rune production and pressure on your mana supply.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.halo.tex: The Assembly Halo is a portable crafting table with recipe memory. Craft and hold it to display its slots. Clicking the crafting-table image opens a grid for making items from your inventory.

Complete a simple recipe, then click an empty halo slot to save the last-used pattern. Selecting that saved recipe attempts to craft it from available materials. Torches or planks make clear first experiments.

The halo cannot create ingredients or retrieve them from arbitrary world chests. If repeating a craft fails, inspect your supplies and selected recipe. Sneak-punch a saved pattern to delete it. This is a useful travelling tool before expeditions for elven and runic resources.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.mana_run: The Rune of Mana complements the four elements and is used by more complex devices. Place five Manasteel Ingots and one Mana Pearl on the Runic Altar, with Livingrock ready for the finishing step.

The altar needs eight thousand mana in addition to the energy already spent making its ingredients. Aim a charged spreader at it, wait for readiness, add Livingrock, and use the wand. Putting the pearl back into a pool does not make a rune.

Check that you collected the rune rather than prematurely retrieving its ingredients. Save it for the agglomeration plate or another planned recipe. Bulk production is unnecessary until you know which runes your next device consumes and which act as returned catalysts.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terra_ge: The Terra Blade and Terrasteel Helmet are your first expensive uses for the alloy. The helmet needs an existing Manasteel Helmet, Livingwood components, and a Rune of Spring; it upgrades armour rather than following the ordinary five-ingot helmet pattern.

Craft both items and charge portable mana storage. The Terra Blade uses mana for its abilities, while Botania equipment can use mana to restore durability. Test the weapon against a safe target away from animals and decorative builds.

Check the crafted items and available charge before a serious battle. One helmet is not a full armour set, so equip suitable protection in the remaining slots. This gear supports Gaia preparations but does not replace enchantments, healing supplies, or an unobstructed arena.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terra_pl: The Terrestrial Agglomeration Plate transforms mana materials into Terrasteel. Its crafting ingredients include Lapis Blocks, a Manasteel Block, and five runes: the four elements plus Mana. It also needs a separate foundation in the world.

Build a three-by-three base with Livingrock in the centre and corners and Lapis Blocks at the four side centres. Put the plate above the central Livingrock. Check the Lexicon projection, then add sparks above the plate and a nearby pool.

Fill the pool at least halfway before starting and remove nearby item collectors. A crafted plate without its foundation cannot operate. Preparing the entire site lets the next expensive experiment finish without rebuilding midway through mana transfer.
codex.quest.magic_botania_runes.terraste: Collect a Terrasteel Ingot from the plate

One Terrasteel Ingot costs half a million mana, half a normal pool. Accumulate this reserve first and verify the plate foundation and spark connection. Prepare one Manasteel Ingot, one Mana Pearl, and one Mana Diamond.

Drop all three onto the plate and step back to avoid picking them up. Watch the transformation while maintaining supply. Retrieving an ingredient midway loses the mana already transferred to the plate, making a restarted attempt expensive.

Collect only the completed ingot and wait for the Terrasteel advancement. Decide how to spend it before crafting: portals, tools, and armour need further batches. This recipe tests home generation much more seriously than a few Manasteel Ingots.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.0: Arcane Essence supplies clothing and ingot recipes. Collect it in magical structures and from spellcasting enemies. Surround an iron, copper, or gold ingot with eight essence to make one Arcane Ingot; the four requested ingots need thirty-two essence.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.1: The Arcane Anvil has a separate recipe using a normal anvil, Amethyst Blocks, a diamond, and Polished Deepslate. Place it beside the Inscription Table. It upgrades scrolls, equipment, and books, while inscription remains the table’s job.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.text.2: Raise a scroll level using ink matching the next spell level’s rarity and inspect the preview. Do not assume two identical scrolls combine like vanilla enchanted books in this version. Save rare ink for a useful spell and check the displayed operation cost.
codex.quest.magic_irons.arcane.title: Arcane Metal
codex.quest.magic_irons.guide_ink_ladder: The Alchemist Cauldron upgrades ink rarity while reducing volume. Crafting it requires Cinder Essence, so prepare for Nether Ancient Knights first. Place the device beside bottle storage and label the intended input tier.

Four bottles of Common Ink plus a copper ingot produce one Uncommon Ink. Later upgrades use iron, gold, and amethyst. Each recipe takes one thousand millibuckets of the previous tier and yields two hundred fifty of the next. Load one selected type and bottle the result.

Check the new ink name before repeating. The chain consumes starting volume rapidly, so reserve ink for simple scrolls. This provides a route to Legendary Ink without making it free or removing your book’s rarity limits.
codex.quest.magic_irons.guide_scroll_for: The Scroll Forge creates spells from paper, ink, and a school focus. Craft it from Crying Obsidian and Polished Deepslate. Prepare ink of an available rarity and a school item, such as a Blaze Rod for Fire or Ender Pearl for Ender.

Open the forge and inspect available options before confirming. Ink limits rarity and level, while the focus selects the school. Choose a useful spell that fits your current book rather than merely the most expensive result.

Collect the scroll and inscribe it at the Inscription Table. Test mana cost, cooldown, and effect safely. The forge neither replaces inscription nor automatically teaches the character; it provides controlled spell acquisition instead of waiting for random loot.
A scroll from your chosen school
codex.quest.magic_irons.inscription.text: The Inscription Table uses a book, wooden slabs, and fences, making it available before dangerous magic expeditions. Prepare a Copper Spell Book and a suitable found scroll. The Ruined Book from the adjacent quest is unnecessary.

Open the table, insert the book and scroll, and choose an empty slot. Books have capacity and rarity limits; if the interface refuses inscription, check those rather than consuming the scroll directly.

Select the inscribed spell and test it with your book or a compatible casting implement. Repeated casts now use personal mana and respect cooldowns. You can retrieve the scroll, but doing so removes that spell from the book. This turns a disposable find into a permanent spell option.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.task.0: Obtain a bottle of Legendary Ink
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.0: Legendary Ink enables especially powerful scrolls. It appears in rare magical loot, and an Alchemist Cauldron provides a repeatable route. Prepare the cauldron, Epic Ink, amethyst, and an empty bottle while reserving supplies for existing spells.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.1: The installed recipe converts one thousand millibuckets of Epic Ink plus amethyst into two hundred fifty millibuckets of Legendary Ink. Four bottles of the previous tier become one of the next. Bottle the result to earn the Legendary Ink advancement.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.text.2: Rarity does not guarantee every spell’s maximum level. Some highest levels require further Arcane Anvil upgrades. Choose the desired school and spell in the Scroll Forge before spending expensive ink; a powerful random scroll may exceed your current book’s limits.
codex.quest.magic_irons.legendary.title: Legendary Ink
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.task.0: Assemble a complete four-piece magical armour set
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.0: This manual objective requires a complete magical outfit: headpiece, chestpiece, leggings, and boots from one chosen set. Wandering Magician armour, made from leather armour and Arcane Essence, is an accessible start; your first set need not wait for mithril.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.1: Craft all four pieces and equip them in normal armour slots. Check their names and remove any accidentally retained vanilla piece. Specialised school clothing needs Arcane Cloth and the relevant school runes, with materials budgeted for every part.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.text.2: Confirm after completing the full set, rather than one attractive robe. Assess protection, mana, and bonuses before combat. If using cosmetic slots, ensure the functional armour is equipped correctly; appearance alone proves neither an active set nor readiness for the catacombs.
codex.quest.magic_irons.robes.title: Mage Robes
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.0: Runestones specialise magical clothing and upgrades. Look for a blank stone in magical loot: it appears in mage-tower chests and drops from the Dead King. Completed runes hardly ever drop from mages — only the Archevoker drops an Evocation Rune — so the Fire Rune has to be crafted yourself. Enemies in their towers are dangerous, so prepare protection and an escape route.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.1: Surround a Blank Runestone with eight Blaze Rods to make a Fire Rune. Let the blank register first, then use it in the recipe: the guide remembers previously detected items, so the two objectives do not require a spare stone. The fire focus is a rod, not Blaze Powder.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.text.2: Save runes for your chosen school and inspect clothing or orb recipes. Owning a Fire Rune neither teaches a spell nor generates mana. Fire spells still require suitable scrolls and a book, while the rune is an equipment-upgrade component.
codex.quest.magic_irons.runes.title: School Runes
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.0: Early scrolls appear in loot and magical Overworld structures. Read the spell name, level, and rarity before use. Casting directly consumes a scroll, so save a useful copy for inscription into a spell book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.1: The second objective, Ruined Book, is found in deep Ancient Cities and belongs to later exploration. Prepare wool, food, and an escape route, and carefully avoid triggering sculk shriekers. Do not confuse it with an ordinary book or a completed spell book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.text.2: The Ruined Book is unnecessary for starting magic: make the table and Copper Spell Book while this card remains unfinished. Collect both requested items for full completion. Your saved scroll becomes a repeatable spell, while the rare book supports later recipes.
codex.quest.magic_irons.scroll.title: First Scroll
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.0: The Blood Staff is rare Dead King loot from Iron’s Spells catacombs. Prepare enchanted armour, healing, food, strong inscribed spells, and personal mana. Clear dangerous passages and remember the exit route before entering the boss chamber.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.1: Interacting with the resting king awakens him, so do not click during an unprepared inspection. Keep moving, avoid spell areas, and remove summoned enemies promptly to preserve room. Collect all loot after victory.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.text.2: The staff is not guaranteed: the loot table chooses between it and the Necronomicon after a chance check. Another reward means another attempt may be needed. The staff casts your selected spell and improves summoning; it has no general rule replacing mana costs with health.
codex.quest.magic_irons.staff.title: Staff
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.0: An Empty Upgrade Orb needs Arcane Ingots, Cinder Essence, and mithril material. Search below Y −38 in the Overworld; mithril ore does not generate exposed to air and requires a netherite pickaxe. This is late progression beyond the Copper Spell Book.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.1: Cinder Essence drops from Ancient Knights awakened by breaking armour piles in the Nether. Prepare for combat before disturbing them. Craft the empty orb and let it register, then convert it into the configured form; its saved mark does not require a second spare base.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.text.2: Surround a base with eight Recovery Runes for the Cooldown Upgrade Orb. Apply it to compatible equipment through the Arcane Anvil and inspect the preview and limits. It reduces cooldown rather than eliminating mana costs. Compare repeated casts of the same spell after installation.
codex.quest.magic_irons.upgrade.title: Upgrade Orbs
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.reward.0: A huge palette of building materials
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.0: The architect’s cutter creates Domum Ornamentum decorative products from selected base materials. Place it near building supplies and begin with available wood or stone. It needs no electrical network: product type and correct constituents are the central choices.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.1: Select a group and shape in the interface, then fill the required material slots. Inspect output before making a large batch: some shapes combine multiple materials, and swapping them changes appearance. Craft one sample and compare it with the builder’s request through its tooltip or goggles.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.text.2: If a request stays open, inspect composition rather than only the block’s general name. One registry ID can represent many designs with different data. After a successful sample, record the palette and produce the required batch instead of randomly trying similar panels during active construction.
codex.quest.mc_build.cutter.title: Architect's Cutter
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.task.1: Construct one blueprint decoration and inspect its available management
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.0: A decoration controller connects a decorative blueprint with colony construction and maintenance. Choose a small decoration through the build tool and place its plan inside the available colony. The controller belongs to blueprint handling; finding an ordinary item recipe is unnecessary.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.1: Inspect the plan’s interface, issue a construction order and supply materials. Choose an accessible decoration with a clear purpose, such as a small public area, while retaining civilian passages. A decorative plan does not become a residence or increase population simply through an attractive shape.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.text.2: After completion, open available decoration management and verify that it refers to the intended object. Confirm manually after actual construction, not merely a ghost preview. For later changes, use supported management and the correct blueprint so builders do not unexpectedly restore details you removed.
codex.quest.mc_build.decoration.title: Decoration Controller
codex.quest.mc_build.guide_palette_sampl: A Domum Ornamentum sample was crafted for a real request; the builder accepted its exact material and shape

Resolve complex decorative requests with one sample first. Open current builder requirements and select a Domum Ornamentum product whose ingredients you possess. Record shape, centre material and framing when that type includes it.

Reproduce these parameters in the architect’s cutter and make a small output. Compare its tooltip with the request, then deliver the sample through supported supply. Similar facade colour does not replace exact constituent matching; variants from one family may have closely related names.

Confirm when the builder accepts the sample and the request’s remaining amount decreases. Preserve the accepted palette details in your workshop before making the full batch. This prevents producing many nearly correct blocks that look attractive in a personal wall but cannot advance automatic construction of the selected blueprint.
codex.quest.mc_build.guide_upgrade_clear: The next building level’s preview was inspected; its bounds marked, neighbours’ entrances and the road kept clear

Upgrading a colony building may change its dimensions and approaches. Before issuing another order, select an operational hut and inspect the next-level preview in its chosen style. Do not judge only by first-level walls: stairs or roofs may extend beyond previous edges.

Measure uncertain gaps to neighbouring buildings with calipers and mark future boundaries using ordinary temporary blocks. Check roads, entrances, lighting and storage access. If the plan conflicts with infrastructure, first reroute a simple path or choose another available placement option.

Confirm after inspection and preservation of working passages without starting an expensive upgrade lacking supplies. This check helps before every major district reconstruction. Correcting approaches early prevents an attractive finished facade from blocking the courier’s only route and a delivery problem being mistakenly treated by adding another warehouse.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.0: The multipiston moves blocks between configurable directions and supports compact moving mechanisms. Craft it and reserve a clear test area with ordinary inexpensive blocks. Starting with an operating warehouse or another mod’s complex machine is inconvenient because direction errors affect their placement.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.1: Set distinct input and output directions and a short range. The interface reports that input and output cannot coincide. Apply a control signal and observe movement while leaving output space and a safe passage around the mechanism.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.text.2: After the first cycle, remove the signal and inspect expected return or subsequent movement. Moving one stone block does not prove compatibility with every container. For a practical design, repeat the trial using its real materials before connecting gate controls or other colony infrastructure.
codex.quest.mc_build.multipiston.title: Multi-Piston
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.0: The scan tool saves a selected region as a blueprint, calipers measure distances and the shape tool prepares geometric volumes. All three are obtainable in this pack: MineColonies supplies the shape-tool recipe using an emerald and two sticks. Distinguish scanning from placement.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.1: Measure a small model with calipers, select opposite scan corners and verify that the anchor lies inside the region. Save under a meaningful name. Begin the shape tool with a small cube, inspecting selected materials and mode before confirmation.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.text.2: Open the saved project through the build interface and verify dimensions. Scanning does not duplicate blocks for free in survival: later construction needs resources and an available placement method. Avoid scanning a large warehouse for your first attempt; a simple empty model is easier to inspect, rotate and reproduce safely.
codex.quest.mc_build.scepter.title: Structurize Tools
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.0: Placeholder blocks store special environmental handling rules in a blueprint instead of acting as ordinary walls. The regular and solid placeholders differ, so they should not be treated as interchangeable construction materials. Craft them and prepare a small test model away from housing.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.1: Place placeholders in selected parts, scan the model and compare its preview across different terrain. Their purpose concerns blueprint placement: they help reconcile a project with existing surroundings. Do not assume arbitrary stone fills every empty space without checking the relevant rule.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.text.2: Build a small test through available construction and inspect ground-level and interior results. Ordinary rooms usually need actual blocks; placeholders help authors create adaptable blueprints. Preserve the original model so an incorrect rule can be fixed without damaging a completed colony building.
codex.quest.mc_build.substitution.title: Substitution Blocks
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.0: A timberframe block combines visible framing and wall infill in one decorative product. Create it in the architect’s cutter under Timberframes. The dynamic_timberframe name identifies a family of variants rather than one predetermined wood-and-plaster combination.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.1: Prepare frame and centre materials, choose the brace pattern and craft a sample. Place several samples with different orientations to inspect joins and diagonal direction. An accidentally mirrored panel can disrupt a facade even when all ingredients match.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.text.2: For colony orders, compare tooltip materials and type with the exact requested panel. The Codex item objective introduces the block family without validating an entire facade palette. Keep a selected sample in the workshop and produce the required quantity while preserving wall access for repairs and future building levels.
codex.quest.mc_build.timberframe.title: Timber Frame
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.0: A builder turns plans into actual buildings, beginning with their own hut. Place it with the build tool, assign a free citizen and open Build Options, then Build Building. Without a construction order, the employee has nothing to erect even beside a chest of stone.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.1: Required Resources lists project materials; the worker’s own Open Requests shows missing tools and other immediate needs. Deliver items to supported inventory or fulfill requests directly. Bind a resource scroll to the builder so you can inspect requirements while visiting storage.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.text.2: First await completion of the builder’s hut and check further available orders. Builder level limits supported work, so workshop development cannot be postponed indefinitely. If the citizen stands idle, inspect food, time of day, routes, tools and open requests before cancelling the whole construction or relocating the colony.
codex.quest.mc_found.builder.title: Builder
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.0: Structurize’s build tool selects blueprints, rotates them and positions colony buildings precisely. Its golden appearance does not imply a gold cost: the installed recipe uses stone material and sticks. Builder goggles help interpret decorative-block requirements when supplying construction.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.1: Hold the appropriate hut, open blueprint selection with the tool and examine the preview from every side. Check future entrances, floor height and room for later building levels. Confirming placement defines a plan; it provides no free materials and does not instantly complete an order.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.text.2: Use goggles when handling complex Domum Ornamentum materials, distinguishing shape from its constituent materials. Similar textures do not always mean an item satisfies a request. Correct awkward placement before large deliveries: early inspection saves more time than relocating a nearly completed building.
codex.quest.mc_found.buildtool.title: Build Tool
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.0: Housing determines how many citizens can move in and where they shelter at night. Prepare two residence huts and one tavern, then order their construction. The installed tutorial gives the tavern four housing slots and a residence one slot per building level.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.1: A completed tavern also attracts visitors who can be recruited for their requested items when settlement conditions permit. Inspect a candidate’s attributes and available capacity first. Additional taverns are not an unlimited expansion method: a colony permits only one.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.text.2: Register the two residence blocks together for their numerical objective, then place them; inspect actual occupancy through management. A player bed beside a hut does not replace a colony housing slot. After recruitment, provide food and work, otherwise population growth increases unresolved requests rather than useful production.
codex.quest.mc_found.citizen.title: Citizen Housing
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.0: The farm grows crops, while the dining hall represented by blockhutcook serves hungry citizens. These are separate stages: a field without a menu does not provide finished meals. Construct the institutions, assign workers and place a field block on accessible irrigated ground near the farm.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.1: Choose a crop in the field interface, supply seeds and a suitable hoe, then verify assignment to the farmer. Configure the dining-hall menu and add permitted food with fuel for supported cooking. Raw food or an unsuitable meal tier may fail citizens even when players can eat it.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.text.2: Observe harvesting and a meal being supplied to one citizen. Higher-level residences increase dietary expectations; a separate chef’s kitchen and varied ingredients become useful later. For hungry citizens, inspect menus, warehouse reserves and deliveries before blindly expanding an already productive field.
codex.quest.mc_found.food.title: Food
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_housing_audit: The town hall shows free housing and filled jobs; a home and a job are chosen for the next citizen

Before another recruitment, check where the citizen will live and work. Open the town hall and compare population, available housing and population restrictions. Two placed huts do not necessarily provide two ready slots if construction is unfinished.

Choose a specific vacant profession and verify that its institution is built. If assignment is automatic, inspect hiring and housing settings so the newcomer does not take an unintended post. Also inspect food reserves: housing growth increases future dining-hall demand.

Confirm after selecting a home and job for the next citizen without necessarily recruiting immediately. This census distinguishes housing limits from research population caps. If a visitor cannot join, inspect those conditions and recruitment cost before building another prohibited tavern.
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_menu_trial.ta: An available menu was chosen in the dining hall, suitable food delivered and a citizen observed being served
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_menu_trial.te: A full food warehouse does not guarantee the dining hall permits serving its contents. Open the menu and select a dish suitable for current citizens and available from your farms. Prepare a small batch while retaining separate meals for the player and expedition workers.

Deliver finished food through the supply system and observe a hungry citizen being served. If refused, compare quality requirements, menu entries and raw versus prepared item variants. Players and colonists evaluate food differently; player edibility does not establish menu suitability.

Confirm after actual service. Then assess whether current crops can regularly support the dish. If not, adjust menus or ingredient production before upgrading many residences. This prevents attractive new homes from raising citizen expectations before the kitchen can meet them.
codex.quest.mc_found.guide_request_tools: A working citizen’s tool request was fulfilled through the colony system and the worker resumed work

Even timber-supplied construction stops when a worker lacks a suitable tool. Find an active builder or gathering-worker request and read permitted properties. A more expensive pickaxe may exceed the employee’s current allowance, so follow the actual request.

Prepare a qualifying item and place it in registered warehouse storage or fulfill the request through its interface. Observe status changes and delivery to the worker. Do not merely leave the item on the ground beside a door: colony systems must actually recognize the reserve.

Confirm after work resumes. Deliberately breaking a good tool is unnecessary; await a natural request or serve an existing one. Remember the supply route and keep reasonable simple-tool reserves. This resolves situations where the only toolmaker also needs a tool and the entire construction appears frozen.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.0: The hospital serves sick citizens, while the graveyard handles consequences of deaths and related research possibilities. Prepare both hut blocks, but do not treat them as automatic population protection. Effective help requires constructed buildings, assigned employees and the requested supplies.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.1: Provide a safe route from housing to the hospital. When illness occurs, inspect the medical worker’s requests and deliver the specified remedies; similar-looking food may not qualify. Following a citizen’s death, study the graveyard interface and current service conditions before expecting guaranteed revival of every casualty.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.text.2: Monitor supplies and capacity before a crisis. Historical possession of two huts completes the item portion, not treatment or resurrection. Lighting, defence and food still reduce pressure on these institutions; a hospital cannot compensate for a permanently open monster route into residential buildings.
codex.quest.mc_found.hospital.title: Hospital and Graveyard
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.0: A mystical site is a colony building supporting citizen happiness and a distinctive public space. In the installed mod, its happiness contribution depends on building level. It is not a portal, a magical resource generator or a replacement for an operational hospital.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.1: Check the required research and choose a blueprint with its large footprint and material cost in mind. Place the plan with the tool, then order construction after meeting essential settlement needs. A beautiful project should not indefinitely delay urgent housing, food or defence through shared shortages.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.text.2: After completion, inspect happiness at the town hall and preserve access to the site. The item objective records its hut block before construction; the practical effect belongs to an operational building. Develop it alongside the colony, comparing each upgrade with outstanding needs instead of expecting instant resolution of every citizen complaint.
codex.quest.mc_found.mystical.title: Mystical Site
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.0: A postbox lets players use the colony request system instead of searching every rack manually. Craft it after establishing a warehouse and courier. Place it somewhere accessible inside your colony, beside a regular work area where deliveries are convenient.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.1: Open its interface and request a modest amount of ordinary material already stored in the warehouse. Verify the exact item and a reasonable quantity. The courier needs a route, and the system needs available stock or trained production; the box does not create missing resources.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.text.2: Watch the request complete and collect delivery without leaving old orders clogging the receiver. If delivery stalls, inspect request status and courier workload. Stone or planks make a better first trial than a rare component requiring an unbuilt profession, allowing you to test the warehouse connection itself.
codex.quest.mc_found.postbox.title: Postbox
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.0: The supply camp deployer places a starter camp containing useful colony supplies. Craft it and choose open terrain where the entire preview fits. This is a sizeable placed structure, so a cramped room inside your house is unsuitable for the first attempt.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.1: Inspect orientation and height, then confirm placement after examining the boundaries. Collect starter tools and the town hall from the camp, reserving other materials for the builder. The game enforces deployment restrictions; do not plan unlimited supplies by repeatedly placing camps.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.text.2: The item objective records obtaining the deployer rather than founding a colony. Next, choose a permanent town-hall site with room for housing and production. The camp helps you begin, but does not replace citizens, construction orders or further material gathering for your selected architectural style.
codex.quest.mc_found.supply.title: Supply Chest
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.0: The town hall controls your colony: population, happiness, permissions and general settings are available here. Take it from starter supplies or craft it with an available recipe. Choose convenient approaches and sufficient space for future institutions rather than judging only the view.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.1: Place the block through the build tool with a selected blueprint, inspect boundaries and create the colony through the available interface. An installed block is not a completed building: the builder constructs the surrounding structure later. You can use management and organize initial jobs beforehand.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.text.2: Open colony information and verify that management belongs to your settlement. In multiplayer, assign participant permissions deliberately so helpers can build and service storage. The item mark records historical possession of the town hall; citizen arrival and completed construction must be observed separately in the world.
codex.quest.mc_found.townhall.title: Town Hall
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.0: The warehouse and courier connect professions into a shared supply system. Construct both institutions, assign a courier and prepare eight colony racks. Place the warehouse near major consumers: shorter walking routes often help more than another chest on the outskirts.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.1: Stock registered warehouse storage with simple tools and materials for an active building project. Couriers deliver against requests rather than guessing every future player intention. Check entrances, access to racks and free capacity for gathering workers’ output.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.text.2: Observe at least one delivery from storage to a citizen with a request. Item objectives verify crafted blocks, not employee assignment or operational logistics. Do not assume an ordinary chest outside automatically belongs to the warehouse: use its interface and registered storage, otherwise the courier may never see your neatly arranged reserve.
codex.quest.mc_found.warehouse.title: Warehouse and Courier
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.0: A rallying banner temporarily gathers selected guards and later returns them to regular duty. Craft it, check required military research and verify management permissions. The banner neither recruits fighters nor equips empty towers.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.1: Sneak-use it on the desired guard towers to add them to its list. Ordinary use opens management where bound posts can be inspected. Test rallying inside a safe colony area and verify that the intended defenders respond.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.text.2: After the trial, dismiss the group and observe their return to service. Guards have protection-range limits and will not escort players indefinitely far from their families. Avoid withdrawing all gate defenders during a real raid: select reserves and a clear rally point while maintaining protected civilian routes.
codex.quest.mc_military.banner.title: Rally Banner
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.0: Barracks support a larger military force together with barracks towers. Prepare the main block and tower block after studying available blueprints and research. A tower belongs to this system and should not be placed randomly as an entirely independent replacement for a normal post.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.1: Inspect the overall plan with the tool, reserve space for component structures and order construction in the intended sequence. Assign defenders as positions become available, supplying appropriate equipment individually. Avoid removing every supply worker at once: an army without food or repairs quickly becomes unreliable.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.text.2: Inspect actual occupied positions and available defence commands. The item objective records the two different blocks sequentially, so constructed institutions need no dismantling. Barracks development supports territorial growth but must accompany increased weapon and armour reserves and planned access to threatened areas.
codex.quest.mc_military.barracks.title: Barracks
A guard tower houses a defender and expands controlled colony territory. Prepare two hut blocks together for the numerical objective, then select approaches needing protection. A tower beside the town hall may not cover a distant mining district entrance.

Construct the towers, assign guards and supply equipment appropriate to role and available level. Melee fighters and archers need different conditions. Set a patrol or guard point and verify that routes avoid locked doors and dangerous excavations.

Check that defenders reach posts, receive food and have no outstanding equipment requests. Historical possession of two blocks does not establish active service. Tower placement should support the working colony rather than only expand borders: a lit route and quick reinforcement often matter more than map symmetry.
codex.quest.mc_military.guardtower.title: Guard Tower
codex.quest.mc_military.guide_patrol_rou: The assigned guard walked the whole route, gates remain passable and dangerous drops are fenced

A route on an interface map helps only when a defender can physically walk it. Choose an assigned guard and a short patrol around housing. Check stairs, gates, bridges and excavation edges with mechanisms in their normal state.

Observe passage through every marked point. If the fighter sticks beside an attractive facade, identify the actual entrance instead of repeatedly reassigning their profession. Light dark stretches and guard dangerous drops while retaining civilian and courier access to the same roads.

Confirm after a complete traversal without dangerous detours. No enemy must be summoned: the trial checks geometry and service accessibility. Revisit paths after building upgrades near changed entrances, since a new building level can occupy an old walkway or alter approach height.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.0: The Chief Sword is a rare MineColonies barbarian-chief trophy. Although the quest title refers to a repelled raid, its automatic item objective checks this sword specifically rather than any completed defence. The installed loot table has many alternatives, including no such trophy.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.1: Prepare defences, guard supplies and civilian shelter before combat. Monitor approaches during attacks without pulling every defender far beyond the settlement. Collect loot after victory once nearby threats are gone.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.text.2: If the sword does not drop, the defence still succeeded; the item node remains open until the trophy is obtained. Do not confuse ordinary-material swords with the Chief Sword. Preserve a found specimen for registration and display, while planning further defence around colony condition rather than expecting guaranteed rewards from another raid.
codex.quest.mc_military.raid.title: Raid Repelled
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.0: The combat academy trains future melee fighters, while the archery range trains future ranged defenders. Prepare both after required research and place them with safe student access. A training profession differs from active patrol duty: a trainee should not be counted as immediate gate protection.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.1: Assign suitable citizens and provide requested training equipment. Observe lessons beginning and compare attributes over time. Preserve functional blueprint elements: removing targets or work areas can halt exercises even beside a full weapon chest.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.text.2: Once prepared, transfer a trainee to an available military position and separately verify combat equipment. Obtaining two blocks does not make the army more experienced. Keep active guards at their posts during training so future recruitment does not temporarily leave an inhabited district undefended.
codex.quest.mc_military.training.title: Training
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.0: Walls direct enemy movement, while gates preserve controlled civilian access. Prepare a wooden gate and gatehouse, then choose an entrance around roads and visibility. An attractive closed wall without a working entrance obstructs your couriers as effectively as attackers.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.1: Inspect the gatehouse blueprint and designated defender positions. Construct the section, test gate opening and closing through available controls, then observe a citizen using the normal route. Avoid blocking essential supplies before providing a bypass or clear opening procedure.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.text.2: Check gate condition after attacks and preserve repair access. Historical item possession records materials, not an impassable border: height changes, water and neighbouring buildings may provide bypasses. Walk the exterior to inspect defence while retaining safe home access before any combat trial.
codex.quest.mc_military.walls.title: Walls and Gates
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.0: The shepherd, cowboy and beekeeper provide distinct renewable products: wool, milk and breeding outputs, and bee materials. Prepare huts and safe enclosures. Bring starter animals and hives before expecting results: a worker cannot create livestock in an empty pen.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.1: Inspect breeding settings, feed, tools and population limits. Shepherds also regulate flock size, so retain breeding stock in advance. Bind hives using the beekeeper’s tool; supported numbers depend on apiary development, and a nearby unrelated hive is not automatically serviced.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.text.2: Observe a collection of each desired product and its delivery. Avoid moving all animals into an attractive shared pasture if employees can no longer reach them. Separate storage for feed, containers and output helps distinguish consumable shortages from route or assignment errors.
codex.quest.mc_production.animals.title: Livestock
codex.quest.mc_production.blacksmith.tex: The blacksmith supplies tools and metal equipment, the mechanic handles complex devices and redstone, and the glassblower works with glass products. These workshops remove different manual duties. Prepare the blocks, check research and establish material delivery.

Begin teaching one necessary recipe per profession: an available tool, a simple mechanical component and a glass product. Verify exact output and current-level eligibility. Do not automatically assign another mod’s complex machine recipe to any workshop merely because it contains iron.

Create a small request and follow its completion. If the crafter needs a tool first, fulfill that request before expecting tool production, preventing a circular shortage. After testing, expand teaching around actual builder demand while reserving recipe capacity for your chosen architectural materials.
The concrete mixer produces concrete-related construction materials, while the alchemist handles potions, nether wart and mistletoe. These are independent advanced supply professions. Prepare their huts after relevant research and choose sites around actual ingredient flows rather than neighbouring names in the book.

Teach the concrete mixer the desired colour and product form, supplying sand, gravel and dye according to its recipe. Give the alchemist a supported task and necessary reagents. A brewing stand elsewhere in your base does not imply the citizen can access its contents through warehouse logistics.

Test one order each, separately following input consumption and output. Concrete colour and potion type matter for exact requests, so avoid similar substitutions without recipe checks. These workshops work best after basic logistics, otherwise expensive specialists wait for the same simple supplies as the first builder.
codex.quest.mc_production.concrete.title: Other Production
codex.quest.mc_production.fisherman.text: The fisherman gathers fish at accessible water and sometimes brings additional finds. Choose and construct a hut blueprint with a safe waterside approach, then assign a worker. A decorative drop of water behind a solid wall does not provide a usable workplace.

Supply a suitable fishing rod and inspect messages about available fishing positions. Watch the citizen approach the water and begin working without boats, fences or storage blocking the path. Treasure possibilities depend on fishing conditions and research; rare catches need not appear immediately.

Arrange fish deliveries to the dining hall or appropriate kitchen and leave room for incidental items. Raw fish still needs suitable menus and preparation for colony meals. If production stops, inspect the rod, working position and inventory capacity before enlarging the water body.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_chef_kit: The chef’s kitchen is built, a cook assigned and one available recipe completed

The chef’s kitchen prepares special MineColonies dishes for more demanding diets. It differs from the dining hall serving hungry citizens. Prepare its separate hut, check requirements and complete construction before expecting advanced meals.

Assign a chef and select an available recipe whose ingredients your farms can actually supply. New colony crops are obtained through suitable hoe use and cultivated by farmers with biome conditions in mind; an arbitrary player plot need not accept every crop. Fulfill the kitchen’s specific requests.

Await the first dish and confirm manually. Then arrange delivery and permission in the dining-hall menu. A kitchen does not remove other food-chain stages: ingredients, preparation, transport and serving must work together. Begin with one repeatable meal before offering a long menu reliant on scarce reserves.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_compost_: The composter’s allowed inputs are set, seed stock kept separately and the first output collected

A composter becomes useful once organic leftovers arrive regularly. Before enabling processing, separate seeds and products essential for the next planting. A labelled chest helps players, but actual storage and permission settings determine worker access.

Open permitted compost inputs and select one genuinely surplus resource. Supply a small batch, observe processing and inspect its product under the active recipe. Do not classify all crop output as waste merely because storage has filled for the first time.

Confirm after receiving output and rechecking the preserved planting reserve. Then compare consumption with farm renewal so composting continues to handle surplus. If kitchen ingredients disappear, revise allowed inputs and delivery routes: the problem concerns spending policy, not necessarily farmer speed.
codex.quest.mc_production.guide_sawmill_: The sawmill produced oak stairs from the taught recipe for a request

Oak stairs provide a simple sawmill-teaching test without rare materials. Prepare oak planks and an available recipe slot, then open teaching at the constructed institution. Select the oak output specifically: an identical shape in another wood cannot satisfy the request.

Save the recipe and create demand through a supported colony request or building project. Follow ingredient delivery, crafting and output transport. The numerical objective requires sixteen stairs together in the player inventory; it does not identify their producing workshop.

Confirm manually after observing sawmill operation. The saved recipe supports later orders, so avoid immediately deleting it merely to clear the interface. If production waits, inspect planks, courier service and an active request; lack of demand differs from an unknown recipe and needs a different fix.
codex.quest.mc_production.lumberjack.tex: The forester grows and cuts trees according to hut settings. Build the workplace near storage while separating its woodland from decorative trees and wooden buildings. Supply a suitable axe and saplings of the chosen species, then inspect permitted plants.

Use the forest tool to define a work volume between opposite corners, including future tree height. A low volume misses the canopy, while an excessively broad one can include a park. Observe the first felling and replanting before expanding.

Output should leave the worker’s storage to free capacity for another cycle. For stoppages, check tools, saplings, tree access and citizen messages. Obtaining the hut only introduces the profession to the Codex; reliable builder supplies begin after actual felling, delivery and renewed planting.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.0: The mine gathers stone and ores, the stonemason crafts products, the crusher converts loose materials and the sifter searches for useful inclusions. Prepare the four huts sequentially, but activate professions according to research and demand. Their roles are not interchangeable.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.1: The miner needs pickaxes and construction supplies to support the shaft, first digging downward and later expanding tunnels. Teach the stonemason a specific recipe. Check the crusher’s cobblestone–gravel–sand–clay transitions and current conditions; the sifter needs suitable input and an available mesh.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.text.2: Possessing four blocks does not establish an automatic ore-doubling line. Observe each profession’s products separately and free inventory through delivery. An active mine may intersect dangerous cavities, so preserve worker access and monitor requests rather than demanding deeper excavation at any cost.
codex.quest.mc_production.miner.title: Miner
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.0: The Nether worker obtains dangerous resources through a specialized colony institution. This is a separate profession with supply requirements and risks, not an ordinary miner pushed through your portal. Check required research and finish constructing the selected blueprint.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.1: Assign an employee and carefully fulfill equipment and consumable requests before expeditions begin. Provide reliable food and delivery. Do not send your last experienced citizen unprepared merely for one rare material: the installed profession description explicitly emphasizes its danger.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.text.2: Monitor the employee’s condition and actual incoming resources after outings. A hut block establishes access to the branch, not a successful expedition or guaranteed yield. Support a short working cycle before expanding supplies; investigate missing output through requests and worker status rather than assuming endless production.
codex.quest.mc_production.nether.title: Nether Worker
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.0: The plantation grows crops such as sugar cane, cactus and bamboo, the florist supplies flowers, and the composter processes organic leftovers. Also prepare a plantation field: an ordinary farmer field block is not a universal substitute for its specialized plot.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.1: Check research unlocks for the selected field type and assign it to the plantation. Supply the plant and suitable growing conditions. Select a supported florist crop and configure which leftovers the composter may consume. Do not classify every seed, meal or rare plant as waste without keeping reserves.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.text.2: Follow at least one cycle from consumable to product. If a plantation rejects a field, inspect the research restriction instead of repeatedly moving the block. This branch supplies paper, dyes and building consumables once the grain farm already covers citizens’ basic meals.
codex.quest.mc_production.plants.title: Horticulture
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.0: A medium quarry defines a large open excavation area. This version requires a constructed mine, a hired quarrier and assignment to a specific quarry. A quarry block alone does not automatically remove an entire column down to the world’s base.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.1: Choose terrain away from foundations, roads and underground services. Inspect blueprint dimensions with the tool and provide access, tools and supplies. Open excavation mainly yields common construction resources; its size does not guarantee a stream of rare ore.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.text.2: Observe initial digging and material delivery, then guard the edge against citizens and animals. Once finished, the worker needs another assignment, reported in their messages. Quarry development helps large construction projects, but requires advance planning for using or safely closing the remaining hole.
codex.quest.mc_production.quarry.title: Quarry
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.0: The sawmill crafts wooden products requested by the settlement. It complements the forester: a delivered log does not automatically become every stair, fence and door in your chosen style. Check required research, construct the institution and assign an available worker.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.1: Teach a specific simple recipe using available wood through its recipe interface. Use the material variant the builder actually needs, then create a small request. Recipe capacity and capabilities depend on building development; a newly assigned worker does not know every JEI entry.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.text.2: Follow incoming material and courier delivery of the finished order. If construction needs a different wood species, mentally recolouring planks does not alter the employee’s recipe. Compare exact ingredients and output before expanding the product list, preserving logs for your own building and further recipe teaching.
codex.quest.mc_production.sawmill.title: Sawmill
The smeltery handles ores and metals, while the stone smeltery handles fired construction materials and charcoal. Prepare both huts and separate their input streams beforehand. Their similar names do not mean a smooth-stone request automatically belongs to the metalworker.

Construct buildings, assign workers and provide fuel, ingredients and a supported available recipe. A smelter can break ore blocks into raw material and smelt it; actual processing determines output. Do not assign Mekanism enrichment multipliers without checking a specific recipe.

Request small batches of metal and a building product, following both outputs to storage. For idle workers, compare profession assignment, recipe and fuel. Coal shortages can halt several services together, so reserve fuel for meals and metallurgy before beginning a large decorative firing batch.
codex.quest.mc_production.smeltery.title: Smelteries
codex.quest.mc_production.timber_service: Gather thirty-two oak logs in one batch and let the Codex record them. Separate single pickups do not accumulate toward the required count if the stated batch was never held. The objective neither consumes timber nor identifies its source.

For a meaningful trial, use logs produced by your colony forester, then return them to accessible warehouse stock. Check replanting after felling and ensure the next cycle has not stopped for an axe. The batch must suit the builder’s upcoming request.

Avoid converting every log into planks before testing log delivery: that is a different item and request. If the chosen blueprint requires processed wood, teach the sawmill the appropriate recipe beforehand. The next quest examines the actual material route and stoppage causes that an ordinary item counter cannot see.
Create a timber construction request; follow worker → warehouse → builder and inspect tool supply and route

Create a construction timber request and follow material from worker through warehouse to builder. Choose a small clear order so dispatch and receipt are visible. Previously recording logs in the Codex does not prove this delivery.

Separately inspect tool shortages: open forester or builder requests and ensure you understand where the requested item is supplied. Then walk the courier route, checking doors, stairs, fences and storage access. Deliberately breaking good tools is unnecessary; inspect the active request mechanism and supply accessibility.

Confirm manually only after observing the complete chain and checking tools and routes. The Codex does not automatically measure citizen work. If timber sits in storage while construction waits, compare exact material type and order status: the issue may be a processed-product request rather than felling speed.

This branch tests builder timber supplies through colony services. Begin with the forester hut and warehouse, whether already registered or newly crafted. Once recorded, operational buildings can remain in place; this objective does not require dismantling them again.

Verify that the forester is assigned and has an axe, oak saplings and a suitable work volume. A courier must serve the warehouse with access to both institutions. Prepare an available builder project that actually requires oak timber so the later request has a clear recipient.

Equipment alone does not prove delivery. Before the trial batch, inspect free racks and unresolved requests blocking the forester. Preparation links production with a specific worker’s demand rather than placing two blocks together and expecting proximity to replace the request system.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.0: The enchanter’s tower produces enchanted books and magical scrolls through colony systems. Construct it, assign a specialist and configure workers they may observe to gather mana. Without observation targets, the mod explicitly reports that cause of inactivity.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.1: For teleport scrolls, provide three paper, a compass and a build tool: the installed enchanter recipe produces three scrolls. Supply ingredients through accessible logistics and await crafting. This is a citizen recipe, so a player enchanting table cannot replace the tower’s process.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.text.2: Obtain one scroll for the item objective, then study its binding and destination before using it on a distant outing. Avoid consuming your last return method in a casual trial. Enchanted books separately depend on tomes and institution level; an available scroll does not mean the tower already supplies every desired enchantment.
codex.quest.mc_research.enchanter.title: Enchanter
codex.quest.mc_research.guide_first_rese: An available research was chosen, paid for and completed; its effect checked in the relevant building

Choose your first research around the active colony’s needs. Find an available discovery unlocking a waiting profession or improving a clear service. Read its price and prerequisites, then prepare materials without taking workers’ last food or tools.

Start research at the university and verify that it appears among active projects. Await completion with an assigned researcher and maintained building. Paying through a button does not immediately provide the effect: research time is part of the process.

Open the associated institution or setting and locate the promised change. Confirm only afterward. If the expected function is absent, compare the completed research and its actual effect instead of a similarly named neighbouring branch. This trial makes later spending deliberate and helps plan university upgrades.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.0: The library gives adult citizens somewhere to study and develop intelligence. It does not run university research or automatically improve everyone merely because its block exists. Check its unlock, select a suitable blueprint and complete construction.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.1: Assign an adult student who benefits from further preparation and provide requested study materials. Compare attributes before and after a period of work. Intelligence helps learning other skills, so choose students with their future profession in mind rather than simply selecting the nearest free citizen.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.text.2: Ensure the move to education does not remove the colony’s only builder or courier. If study fails to begin, inspect assignment, building condition and requests. The item objective accepts the crafted hut; meaningful attribute changes require actual citizen work and time, which books in a player’s chest cannot replace.
codex.quest.mc_research.library.title: Library
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.task.1: Complete an available citizen request and find it in the log’s finished quests
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.0: The quest log records available citizen requests, active stages and completed stories. Craft it and open it near your colony. Some requests appear only after particular buildings, professions or earlier conversations; an empty page does not necessarily indicate a malfunction.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.1: Choose an available request, speak to the designated citizen and read the required action. For deliveries, distinguish handing items to the character from storing them nearby: the dialogue objective must actually advance. Finish the story and receive its intended response or reward.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.text.2: Confirm manually once the completed request appears in the log. The internal Monster Encounter token is unnecessary: it represents combat in expedition simulations rather than ordinary player reward currency. This task checks actual citizen interaction, helping you understand colony requests and further tutorial chains.
codex.quest.mc_research.quests.title: Colony Quests
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.0: The school educates colony children and prepares future workers. Obtain its hut after required research, construct the blueprint and provide a teacher. An empty school does not create citizens: population growth still depends on housing and colony conditions.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.1: Assign children and inspect requests for educational materials. Preserve study places included in the blueprint: the installed mod reports missing seating if school elements are damaged. Do not remove the interior as useless decoration before checking its functional role.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.text.2: Inspect attendance and pupil development through the interface rather than simply seeing a building on the map. School assignment also contributes to children’s happiness. Plan available jobs and housing before adulthood so a trained citizen enters active production instead of waiting for another hut and construction-material queue.
codex.quest.mc_research.school.title: School
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.0: Ancient tomes appear among MineColonies raider trophies and support colony enchanting. The installed barbarian-chief loot table includes one as a random option, so victory does not guarantee a book. Do not plan an exact tome count per raid.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.1: Collect a found tome after safely ending combat and register it before further processing. Store it separately with rare trophies. An ordinary Minecraft book or another mod’s similar grimoire is not the same ingredient.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.text.2: An enchanter processes tomes through recipes depending on tower level, producing enchanted books from the corresponding result tables. Read each research’s requirements independently: tomes are not universal payment for science. For your first specimen, reliable defence and loot preservation matter more than provoking another dangerous raid to accelerate collecting.
codex.quest.mc_research.tome.title: Ancient Tome
The university unlocks research permitting professions, improving supply and expanding colony capabilities. Construct it and assign a researcher; possessing its hut does not start study. Begin with a discovery addressing a specific current settlement problem.

Open the tree and read predecessor research, building requirements, level and cost. Materials can be funded from available university inventory. Starting confirms the chosen work, while completion takes time; several visible branches do not imply unlimited parallel projects.

Track progress and the completion message, then inspect the new capability in its associated profession. University upgrades increase available options and researcher capacity. An inactive button is not necessarily a bug: it often correctly identifies an unmet condition requiring construction, supplies or a preceding discovery.
codex.quest.mc_research.university.title: University
codex.quest.mek_gear.atomic_disassembler: The atomic disassembler combines several mining functions in one electric tool. Prepare the expensive alloys in its recipe and a charging location; an uncharged item does not demonstrate its capabilities. Keep an ordinary pickaxe as backup for the first outings.

Charge the tool, inspect its available modes and begin at normal speed on a safe stone patch. Changing mode alters behaviour and energy consumption. Check the pack’s control settings rather than assuming keys from someone else’s configuration.

Test bulk-mining modes away from base floors, cables and decorative structures. Before entering a mine, assess charge and room for dropped blocks. The disassembler is a convenient general tool, but does not replace a modular Meka-Tool’s specialised functions or guarantee a particular harvesting enchantment.
codex.quest.mek_gear.guide_charge_stop.t: A chargepad provides a fixed preparation point for electric equipment. Place it near the base exit and connect it to storage through an enabled side. Avoid hazardous conveyor routes or exposed laser paths.

Equip a partly discharged set and stand on the pad. Watch equipment energy rise and the supplying cube’s reserve fall. If an item does not charge, inspect compatibility, source reserves and connections before changing the entire power system.

Robit’s home pad must also remain accessible; with an active assistant, a separate player charging spot is convenient. Crafting the pad completes the item objective, while the trial reveals actual service speed. Before a long expedition, check every piece: a full bodyarmour battery does not mean the tool or boots are full.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.0: A Mekanism laser emits a dangerous directed beam using electricity. The amplifier stores energy for a controlled pulse, while the tractor beam helps collect the results of breaking blocks. This objective needs all three devices, but begin with one short enclosed beam.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.1: Place the emitter so its path avoids walkways, chests and other players’ structures. Connect power only after checking direction. Study amplifier thresholds and redstone control: stored energy may discharge later when a player has entered the area.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.text.2: Before servicing, disconnect power and account for energy remaining in the amplifier. Fusion startup directs the beam into a dedicated laser focus matrix, not an arbitrary reactor wall. The laser area needs controlled activation and a safe endpoint even during ordinary experiments.
codex.quest.mek_gear.laser.title: Lasers
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.0: MekaSuit is a four-piece set of electric armour. Crafting it requires late Mekanism materials, including polonium components in the current recipes. Establish dependable material production and charging before spending your reserve on a random single piece.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.1: Craft the helmet, bodyarmor, pants and boots; the Codex can record different pieces sequentially. Then charge them and equip the complete set. Inspect internal reserves: the armor itself uses energy for protection, while modules add separate functions. A piece equipped after registration need not be returned for its item objective.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.text.2: Do not assume an unmodified set provides flight or complete radiation protection. Those require the appropriate installed modules and verified operating conditions. Test the armour in a safe setting and retain an ordinary set; the following modification station lets you develop the suit around actual needs.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekasuit.title: MekaSuit Set
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.0: The Meka-Tool is a configurable electric tool whose abilities expand through modules. Craft the tool, an excavation escalation unit and a vein mining unit. These are three separate item objectives; after they register, install the upgrades through the modification station.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.1: Charge the tool and select moderate speed for its first trial. Test vein mining on a small natural deposit far from important structures. Additional modes such as Silk Touch or Fortune require their own compatible modules and settings, rather than arriving automatically with vein mining.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.text.2: Watch energy consumption and dropped-item volume: a fast tool easily overwhelms an ordinary inventory. Keep a clearly understood safe mode for workshop work. If the affected area is too large, stop and change settings before continuing instead of trying to repair a dismantled structure afterwards.
codex.quest.mek_gear.mekatool.title: Meka-Tool
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.0: The modification station installs and removes modules in compatible equipment. A module base is an ingredient for functional modules, so the four bases requested here do not increase capacity or speed by themselves. Prepare station power and the item you want to improve.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.1: First craft one useful functional module, open the station and insert a compatible suit piece or tool. Check which modules it accepts and their quantity limits. Some upgrades allow several installed units, while others only need one.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.text.2: After installation, open the equipment’s own settings and confirm that the feature is enabled appropriately. Keep removed modules: extraction lets you change equipment roles without crafting a new armour set. Avoid making every upgrade before checking compatibility and the energy demand of the chosen operating mode.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modification.title: Modification Station
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.0: The energy unit increases compatible equipment’s energy reserve; it does not create charge. Electrolytic breathing and inhalation purification perform separate helmet functions. Prepare a charging system first so you can actually test the new capabilities.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.1: Install the modules into permitted suit pieces through the station. For breathing, check helmet settings and energy reserve, then enter shallow water beside an exit. Inhalation purification handles its supported effects and is not universal protection against every hazard.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.text.2: Observe consumption with the features enabled and disable unnecessary ones before travelling far. Extra capacity helps an expedition but also means more energy is needed to recharge later. Do not confuse these modules with radiation shielding: a nuclear site requires appropriate protection across all pieces, not simply improved breathing.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_core.title: Core Modules
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.0: Movement modules change suit controls and can substantially affect energy consumption. The gravitational modulating unit provides controlled flight and needs late-game resources; hydraulic propulsion changes jumping, while locomotive boosting increases movement speed. The three are not interchangeable.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.1: Install each in a supported suit piece through the station and open equipment settings. Begin with moderate values: high jumps and fast running can be awkward in a cramped workshop. Test flight above a level area after charging fully.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.text.2: Before an expedition, practise enabling and disabling features, landing and low-energy behaviour without risking a fall. Extra energy units help if flight drains the suit quickly. A module carried in your pocket grants no effect: it must be installed, enabled and sufficiently powered in the relevant piece.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_move.title: Movement
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.0: These utility modules cover three jobs: enhanced vision, item attraction and radiation shielding. Begin by checking compatibility for each suit piece in the modification station. Crafting one radiation-shielding module does not mean the whole set is protected.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.1: Install vision and magnetic attraction in supported pieces, enable them and test in a safe dark area with a few ordinary items. Choose a magnet setting that avoids unwanted clutter while building or organising storage.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.text.2: For nuclear work, provide shielding in every required piece and inspect the set before entering the site. A radiation meter does not replace protection, and clear vision does not protect against mobs. Keep feature controls accessible: disabling an unnecessary effect is often more convenient than running every module continuously.
codex.quest.mek_gear.modules_util.title: Utility
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.0: Robit is a mobile assistant with storage and useful work interfaces. It needs a chargepad for placement and returning home, so prepare one separately. Supply the pad with power and leave space around it for the assistant to appear.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.1: Place Robit on the pad, open its interface and inspect following and item-collection modes. Start with one dropped cobblestone to see where cargo goes. Check charge and settings before taking it on a long mining trip.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.text.2: Do not treat Robit as an autonomous factory: smelting, storage and other functions have their own interface limits. Before a dangerous crossing, make sure you understand the return action and know where its home pad is. The assistant is particularly useful for carrying finds once the route home is protected.
codex.quest.mek_gear.robit.title: Robit
