codex.quest.more_explore.atlas_done.text: A filled map is a physical result of atlas exploration but does not automatically contain every discovered biome. Craft an empty map and use it in the desired Overworld region to create a filled item. Choose scale for a specific district rather than expecting the entire world on one sheet.

Travel around the activation area to reveal its image while preserving a home route. A cartography table helps manage scale, copies and locking. Label the region clearly to distinguish nearly identical items in shared storage.

The item objective checks one filled map; geographic visits were recorded by separate nodes. Display the result or keep it in travelling equipment after registration. For multiple areas, prepare separate sheets and coordinate notes: finishing a multiworld chapter does not turn the map into an interdimensional navigator.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.0: Mirage Isles belong to Terralith in the Overworld. The quest’s technical name survives from another theme, but the actual target is mirage_isles; visiting the End is unnecessary. Prepare a boat or another familiar water-crossing method and food.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.1: Search using Nature’s Compass in the correct dimension, then approach the island area. Its styling includes large and small mushrooms with trees, but a similar mushroom island of another type cannot replace the identifier. Land safely and inspect the biome.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.text.2: Mark the return shore and examine possible dock sites. Mushrooms do not guarantee vanilla mushroom-fields monster rules: this is another biome with its own data. Visiting is sufficient, so avoid leaving transport far offshore to circle the entire island before the first registration.
codex.quest.more_explore.endbop.title: Mirage Isles
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.0: Geobstractsite is associated with a special Eternal Tales area and a useful material of the same name. The objective checks geobstractsite_biome, so an ordinary amethyst geode is insufficient. Prepare underground exploration equipment: lighting, a pickaxe, passage blocks and a marked exit.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.1: Search for the biome through available tools in the appropriate world, accounting for vertical position. If the direction leads above or below you, inspect elevation instead of endlessly walking the surface. On finding an unusual formation, check the area’s name before choosing samples.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.text.2: Await the biome mark and preserve the return route. The material has Eternal Tales uses, including mechanics involving comet creatures, but obtaining it cannot replace visiting. Avoid removing the entire formation before studying applications: a preserved section and coordinates are more useful than an arbitrary pile of unknown items.
codex.quest.more_explore.geob.title: Geobstractsite
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.0: A glacial chasm is a cold area with complicated elevation changes and slippery surfaces. Bring food, building blocks and a safe descent method. The objective needs glacial_chasm, so an ordinary snowy plain or frozen ocean cannot replace the destination.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.1: Approach the located chasm and inspect footing before descending. Ice can carry you past an edge, while snow may conceal awkward drops. Choose a stopping place with a usable return route and check the actual biome on arrival.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.text.2: Save coordinates for an accessible entrance rather than an unreachable cliff point. For future development, identify where stairs or a bridge fit without obstructing an existing route. Visiting does not require standing inside a dangerous cold block: the task teaches terrain and navigation rather than damage endurance.
codex.quest.more_explore.glacial.title: Glacial Chasm
codex.quest.more_explore.guide_cartograp: A named banner is marked on the map and shown with its label

A cartography table expands maps, copies them and locks them against changes. Craft it from two sheets of paper and four planks, make an empty map from eight sheets of paper and a compass and open it outdoors to get a filled map. Two different filled maps in the inventory satisfy the item objective; the second may be a copy or a neighbouring area.

To mark a place, name a banner on the anvil before placing it, set it down and click it with the map in hand. An icon in the banner’s colour with that label appears on the map. If the banner is removed, the marker disappears the next time you visit the area: the map remembers only what it has seen.

Expand the map on the table by adding paper until the scale covers your route; make a copy with an empty map in the lower slot. A map locked with a glass pane can no longer be drawn on, which is handy for an expedition archive. Tick the manual objective when the banner label is visible on the map itself, not only in the world.
codex.quest.more_explore.guide_desert.te: Terralith redraws deserts: among the familiar dunes you find oases with water and greenery and desert spires, tall stone pillars. Both biomes are visible from afar, yet finding them at random takes long. Take a Nature’s Compass from the conveniences map or food and water for a long day’s march and leave while it is light.

Search hot, dry regions: neighbouring Terralith biomes of the same temperature hint at the direction. Descending into an oasis, check the area name on the debug screen or in the compass: the objective counts precisely desert_oasis and desert_spires, not any picturesque corner of desert. At night the desert fills with husks, so keep a shelter or return before sunset.

The marks arrive on first entry to each biome. Record the coordinates: the oasis provides water, sugar cane and shade for a farm, while the spires suit an observation post and a waystone. Collected block samples help with building, but owning them does not replace the visit itself.
codex.quest.more_explore.hotsprings.text: Terralith’s moonlight grove is in the Overworld and requires no Ad Astra rocket. Its styling includes blue flower groups, unusual ground details and amethyst features. Search for moonlight_grove rather than following the node’s historical hot-springs identifier.

Locate it with Nature’s Compass and enter its boundaries. Inspect details by daylight or with adequate lighting: attractive night colours do not remove ordinary threats. Mark the entrance so palette research can continue later without another distant search.

Check the visit mark and choose combinations for a home garden. Water there does not automatically gain healing properties, and the grove’s name does not imply an Eternal Tales lunar event. The task requires the actual biome and helps distinguish themes across mods without mixing their mechanics.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.0: The lavender card requires two distinct biomes: valley and forest. They share floral and tree styling but have separate identifiers, so one attractive meadow cannot satisfy both. Prepare Nature’s Compass and record which destination is already visited.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.1: First find lavender_valley, enter its boundaries and check progress. Then switch to lavender_forest and visit it separately. Follow biome names instead of expecting an obligatory “lavender” item: Terralith composes landscapes from existing blocks.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.text.2: Save two differently labelled atlas points. This helps return to the desired vegetation density when choosing a home or flower plot. If the second objective fails beside the first location, continue searching for the forest variant specifically; another walk through the valley cannot change its actual identifier.
codex.quest.more_explore.lavender.title: Lavender Valley
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.0: Mucunfectio Abyss is a specific infection-themed Eternal Tales biome. The objective specifies mucunfectio_abyss, so Mucunfectio Beach or another infected area does not automatically qualify. Prepare healing, protection and a safe descent to the located region.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.1: Use biome search with dimension and height in mind, advancing through small inspected sections. If mutated creatures appear, preserve retreat space instead of combining reconnaissance with optional combat. First establish the geographic destination rather than collecting any infection trophy.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.text.2: Once progress appears, record a safe entrance. Bring infection-related materials home only after learning their behaviour: certain specialized forms can spread. Visiting does not require making an infected garden beside the colony; samples and a separate research site let you study the branch while preserving normal base access.
codex.quest.more_explore.mucun.title: Mucunfectio
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.0: Terralith’s emerald peaks are a mountain biome with cold elevated areas and sparse surface vegetation. The objective needs emerald_peaks; its name does not promise a mountain made entirely of emerald ore. Bring supplies and tools, prioritizing a safe route.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.1: Locate it with Nature’s Compass and climb accessible ledges. Inspect slopes before transitions while preserving a descent without jumping from the summit. Infested stone features occur within these mountains, so unnecessary wall mining can add unexpected enemies to ordinary height hazards.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.text.2: Await the visit mark and save coordinates of an actual stopping platform. Inspect the natural palette and neighbouring-valley views for future construction. Collecting emeralds cannot replace entering the biome, and reaching its highest awkward point is unnecessary for completion.
codex.quest.more_explore.mystic.title: Emerald Peaks
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.0: Terralith’s volcanic crater has the distinct volcanic_crater identifier and differs from the earlier caldera route. Bring bridging blocks, food and available fire protection if inspecting hot areas closely. Visiting does not require entering lava.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.1: Follow the outer rim using stable footing and inspect the interior terrain. Do not rely solely on dark rock colours: check the biome name locally. An accessible part of the correct area suffices, leaving a risky descent into its centre for a separately prepared expedition.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.text.2: Record safe approaches and possible future road bypasses. A volcanic theme does not imply automatic electricity generation or unlimited stocks of a particular fuel. When collecting building stone, first check mining safety and preserve the only route capable of carrying a full inventory home.
codex.quest.more_explore.ominous.title: Volcanic Crater
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.0: This map’s cloud forest is Terralith cloud_forest, not necessarily a grove of giant redwoods. Its design uses its own trees and pale floral groups. Prepare Nature’s Compass and spare luggage space for small palette samples if collecting materials.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.1: Approach the located forest and inspect the biome underfoot. Dense vegetation reduces visibility, so mark the entrance instead of circling among similar trees. Preserve lit footing and safe transitions over elevation changes.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.text.2: After progress registers, study foliage, flower and stone combinations without removing the whole landmark for a few blocks. No special Redwood item is required. Old route names may remain in technical book identifiers, but the actual destination follows the displayed title and the specific Cloud Forest biome.
codex.quest.more_explore.redwood.title: Cloud Forest
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.0: Terralith’s sakura grove combines flowering trees with its own vegetation composition, including birch and bamboo. The objective needs sakura_grove rather than any vanilla cherry grove. Prepare Nature’s Compass, food and a tool for clearing a small passage.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.1: Choose the exact search name and follow the result while avoiding ravines and water obstacles. Enter the grove itself on arrival and inspect the displayed biome. Nearby pink leaves may belong to another area, so colour alone is insufficient.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.text.2: Record a safe stopping point and inspect wood-and-stone combinations for future building. The biome objective requires neither clearing the grove nor collecting a particular tree. If taking saplings, retain replanting stock and restore the route-side area so it remains a useful landmark on later expeditions.
codex.quest.more_explore.sakura.title: Sakura Grove
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.0: Terralith’s spring skylands use elevated terrain with waterfalls, small lakes and flowering vegetation. This is an Overworld biome rather than a separate dimension needing another portal. Prepare a controlled ascent method and supplies for descending again.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.1: Locate skylands_spring and assess target height relative to your route. With elytra, reserve landing space and check durability before flight. On foot, build supported stairs; a visible waterfall does not necessarily provide a convenient descent everywhere.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.text.2: Enter the required area and inspect biome progress. Save coordinates of a place where you can safely stop with luggage rather than an attractive point in midair. A future sky base separately needs logistics and railings: visiting alone creates no bridges, lifts or fall protection.
codex.quest.more_explore.skylands.title: Skylands
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.0: Terralith’s caldera is a distinct mountain landscape and must not be confused with the separate Volcanic Crater objective. Its data includes vegetation and ordinary surface features; the name does not guarantee a lava lake at every site. Prepare mountain-travel equipment.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.1: Choose caldera in Nature’s Compass and approach along an accessible slope, inspecting interior terrain before descending. Check the biome name inside the area. A crater-shaped formation without progress may belong to another similarly shaped landscape.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.text.2: Mark the approach, viewpoint and home route. Visiting is sufficient: destroying the rim or collecting a special volcanic item is unnecessary. If later building a base there, assess height changes and inner-slope lighting first so an attractive natural amphitheatre does not complicate every material delivery.
codex.quest.more_explore.volcano.title: Caldera
Terralith’s painted mountains offer coloured layers and pronounced slopes for studying building palettes. The objective specifies painted_mountains rather than any wasteland or vanilla plateau. Bring climbing blocks, food and space for a sample if needed.

Locate the biome with a compass and travel along sufficiently wide ledges. Goats occur on exposed heights, so avoid stopping on narrow edges. When mining, account for infested stone instead of assuming every mountain block is harmless decoration.

Check progress and record an accessible viewpoint. Compare colours in ordinary lighting before applying the palette at home: distance and shadows affect appearance. Visiting completes the task, so a large scar in an attractive slope is unnecessary and merely complicates the return journey with materials.
codex.quest.more_explore.wasteland.title: Painted Mountains
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.0: A bedroom and bathroom begin with available pack items: a red bed, two blue Handcrafted cushions and a white Refurbished Furniture bath. Craft them using installed recipes and register different types sequentially. No unloaded furniture datapack is required.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.1: Place the bed with a clear waking position and doorway access. Arrange cushions in a resting area and the bath where use does not block movement. Decorative proximity does not automatically make the bath part of another mod’s plumbing system.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.text.2: Verify access and safe bed use in the appropriate dimension. Beds are not safe sleeping devices in the Nether or End, so begin this bedroom at home. The item objective does not measure interior beauty; its practical outcome is a clear room for recovering and preparing luggage.
codex.quest.more_home.bed.title: Bedroom and bathroom
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.0: This garden combines three independent growing methods: Farmer’s Delight rich soil, Eternal Tales gardener’s pot and Immersive Engineering cloche. Prepare sixteen soil blocks and one of each device. Proximity does not imply shared water, fertilizer or electricity systems.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.1: Rich soil forms when organic compost matures under suitable conditions; freshly crafted compost is not yet rich_soil. The Eternal Tales pot uses its own water and fertilizer with supported plants. The cloche requires FE, water, valid soil and seeds under a specific recipe.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.text.2: Verify growth or production separately at each plot, retaining output room. Item objectives introduce three approaches without proving every system operates. Do not spend rare saplings on randomly incompatible machinery: test one sample first and keep planting reserves to restore the garden.
codex.quest.more_home.garden.title: Garden
The dining room continues the kitchen: a table, chairs, tableware and light above them. Handcrafted makes furniture from ordinary planks: a table is three planks above two sticks, a chair is a slab, two planks and two sticks; each recipe yields two items. A wooden plate is three wooden slabs in a row, giving three.

The copper chandelier from Macaw’s Lights is crafted by the recipe in JEI and hung under the ceiling. Arrange the chairs so that each can be reached and keep the table close to the kitchen. Plates go on the table as decoration, and food can be placed on them so the table looks set.

The item objectives count the listed quantities: two tables, four chairs, four plates and one chandelier. Holding them together is not required, and placed furniture need not be taken apart. Check the room’s lighting: a chandelier is pretty, but dark corners of a dining room still give mobs a place to spawn.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_dining.title: Dining Room
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.task.3: The yard and the path to the door are lit so that no mob spawned near the house overnight
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.0: The yard is the first thing a guest sees and the first place where mobs appear at night. The classic street lamp and garden light from Macaw’s Lights are crafted from iron and glowing materials: the garden light from iron nuggets, an ingot and glowstone dust, low and suited to paths; the street lamp is tall and lights a whole corner of the yard.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.1: The Refurbished Furniture mail box is made on that mod’s workbench from eight oak planks; through it other players can leave you items. Put the box by the gate, street lamps at the yard’s corners and by the door, garden lights along the path to the entrance and towards the workshop or colony.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.text.2: Walk the yard at night: mobs spawn where the light level is zero, so there must be no dark patches between lamps. Check that the lights do not block the passage or obstruct doors. Tick the manual objective after a quiet night without a single mob inside the lit yard.
codex.quest.more_home.guide_yard.title: The Yard
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.0: The trophy hall collects a Twilight Forest pedestal, Handcrafted bear trophy and Naga trophy. These have different origins: a decorative head cannot replace an actual boss reward. Prepare an accessible lit display without blocking functional containers.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.1: Obtain the Naga trophy through its Twilight Forest encounter, collect it and register before display. Acquire the pedestal through the mod’s available source, accounting for its special progression role. Craft or obtain the bear decoration through Handcrafted’s actual route, checking its exact name.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.text.2: Place exhibits after registration and inspect them from normal walking height. No repeat boss fight is needed if the trophy was already recorded. Label future specimens by source to distinguish decorative products from important trophies that may serve other adventure mechanics.
codex.quest.more_home.hall.title: Hall
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.task.0: Assemble an accessible Refurbished Furniture kitchen and test its furniture
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.0: Build this kitchen from the installed Refurbished Furniture mod’s own items. Choose counters, accessible storage and a useful appliance while leaving room in front of doors. The manual objective checks an arranged kitchen rather than a random pile of similar furniture.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.1: Begin with a small area near ingredient supplies. If the selected appliance needs power, use Refurbished Furniture’s electricity system and supported connections, checking its screen. An industrial FE cable should not be assumed a substitute for this furniture’s generator and electrical rules.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.text.2: Open containers, inspect passageways and perform an available appliance action before confirming the kitchen. Decorative cabinets need not cook meals themselves. Separate raw ingredient reserves from prepared dishes and arrange household items so eating does not require dismantling walls or moving primary storage.
codex.quest.more_home.kitchen.title: Kitchen
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.0: The architect’s cutter and Create schematic table serve different construction-preparation systems. The cutter makes decorative blocks from selected materials; the table handles Create schematics. Craft both and place them beside organized samples, paper and ordinary building supplies.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.1: Test a small decorative element in the cutter, comparing its composition with your palette. At the schematic table, prepare a saved Create schematic without confusing it with a Structurize file. These formats belong to different systems and do not become interchangeable merely through adjacent tables.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.text.2: Keep labelled samples and clear interface access. Obtaining both blocks establishes equipment rather than an automatically blueprint-built house. Actual reproduction needs the appropriate tool or construction mechanism, material costs and a site; the workshop organizes these stages instead of removing them.
codex.quest.more_home.workshop.title: Workshop
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.0: Sandwiches use ordinary crafting with bread, cooked meat and vegetables. Prepare eight bacon sandwiches and eight chicken sandwiches; both batches are consumed on submission. Do not expect to continue travelling on the same food afterward.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.1: The bacon variant needs bread, cooked bacon, leafy greens and tomato. The chicken version uses bread, cooked chicken, greens and carrot. Raw meat cuts still need cooking, and replacing tomato with carrot changes the recipe rather than filling a universal vegetable slot.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.text.2: Make one sample each before expanding to eight and submitting the complete set. Reliable production needs separate bread, greens and meat supplies; a full wheat chest does not replace missing filling. This step connects conveniently with an existing farm and cutting board.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.bread.title: Sandwiches
codex.quest.more_kitchen.colony_food.tex: The colony meal requires two MineColonies cheese pizzas and four portions of borscht. This is a Consume submission: prepared dishes leave your inventory. Preserve a separate dining-hall reserve instead of taking citizens’ last suitable meals for a completion mark.

Craft cheese pizza through its available recipe, and order borscht from the chef’s kitchen: the installed entry belongs to crafterrecipes/chef. A Farmer’s Delight cooking pot cannot replace the citizen merely because the dish is soup. Check ingredients and recipe availability at the colony’s current stage.

Await finished items, collect the full set and confirm delivery. If the kitchen waits, inspect chef assignment and requests, then supplies of required crops. Raw vegetables in storage are not finished borscht; this batch connects colony development to real specialty-food production and separate expendable stock accounting.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.0: These three Eternal Tales advancements check different actions despite sharing a food theme. Blueberries and crabsburgers require obtaining the corresponding item, while mutatongue chowder must actually be eaten. Showing all three foods alone cannot complete the card.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.1: Find blueberries through their plants and available Overworld sources. Crabsburgers belong to the Mucunfectio crab-product branch; prepare ingredients using the available recipe while preserving trophies separately. For chowder, craft the finished dish and ensure it can be consumed if current fullness prevents ordinary eating.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.text.2: Check each mark after its appropriate action. Eating consumes a portion, so register rare food before eating it when relevant. This card does not require sampling arbitrary dangerous mod foods: its named advancements teach the distinction between obtaining food and using its effects.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.et_food.title: Food of Other Worlds
codex.quest.more_kitchen.feast_hall.text: The feast contribution accepts two honey-glazed hams, two whole roast chickens and one stuffed pumpkin. Every item is consumed. Submit complete dishes rather than individual servings already taken from a plated feast.

Prepare glazed ham using its available recipe and assemble roast chicken with cooked meat and accompaniments. Stuffed pumpkin cooks from rice, onion, brown mushroom, potato, berries and a suitable vegetable, using a pumpkin as container. Provide heat and the correct container before beginning.

Keep everything as inventory items and verify counts before confirming. Serving friends is a separate use: dishes donated to the Codex do not automatically appear in the hall. For a real feast afterward, prepare another batch and place it separately while preserving walkways and convenient table access.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.guide_three_cou: A dinner of salad, fried rice and pasta with meatballs demonstrates three ways of cooking in Farmer’s Delight. Mixed salad is assembled directly in the crafting grid: a bowl, any leafy green, a tomato and a beetroot. Fried rice and pasta need a cooking pot above a heat source, a furnace, campfire or stove, with bowls in its lower slot.

For fried rice put rice, an egg, a carrot and an onion into the pot. For pasta first prepare minced beef by cutting raw beef with a knife on the cutting board, cook tomato sauce from tomatoes and make raw pasta, then combine everything in the pot. JEI shows exact ingredients and portion counts for each dish.

Each dish must be held at least once as two portions at a time; gathering all three together is not required, and eating them after they were counted subtracts nothing. Hearty meals give long saturation and extra effects: read the item tooltip and take such a dinner on a long trip instead of a pile of bread.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.0: This objective needs whole pies: two apple and two chocolate. Consume removes all four, so avoid cutting them into portions before submission. Prepare pie crusts and separate fillings, optionally keeping another sample for your own table.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.1: Apple pie uses three wheat, three apples, two sugar and a crust. Ordinary chocolate pie combines cocoa, milk, sugar and crust; the installed Create integration also fills a crust with five hundred millibuckets of chocolate. Choose an available method and inspect exact output.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.text.2: Retain whole items until delivery. The cutting board turns each pie into four slices, but slices cannot replace whole pies here. If crafting fails, distinguish crust from finished pastry; for the fluid route, verify chocolate type and sufficient volume in the filling system.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.pies.title: Pies
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.0: Submission requires four each of Farmer’s Delight beef stew, chicken soup and fish stew. All three objectives Consume: finished portions are removed on delivery. Prepare a heated cooking pot and bowls for extraction, plus separate food for yourself.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.1: Beef stew combines raw beef, carrot and potato. Chicken soup uses raw chicken, carrot, leafy greens and a suitable vegetable; fish stew needs safe raw fish, tomato sauce and onion. Load ingredients for each recipe separately and await cooking.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.text.2: Collect portions in bowls and retain all three submission batches until confirmation. A similar vanilla soup cannot replace the specified dish. For stoppages, inspect heat and containers; output space matters alongside ingredients because food in the pot must still become transferable items.
codex.quest.more_kitchen.stew.title: Three Soups
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.0: Autocannons use assembled cartridges and supported ammunition containers rather than big-cannon powder bags. Prepare one hundred twenty-eight autocannon_cartridge items and two containers. Cartridges are consumed on submission; containers are recorded without consumption and remain equipment.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.1: Follow the finished-cartridge assembly chain using a suitable projectile and casing, verifying its result. An empty intermediate component is not the final item. Begin with a small series and confirm your operational autocannon accepts the chosen ammunition before manufacturing large service reserves.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.text.2: Submit a separate batch of one hundred twenty-eight, preserving a loaded working container only when needed for further tests. Container possession does not prove filling or weapon connection. On the range, check feed orientation and cease-fire behaviour; sustained bursts consume stock quickly and require a clear area in front of the barrel.
codex.quest.more_munitions.belt.title: Belt
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.0: Fuzes define shell triggering by impact, flight time or proximity to a block. Prepare eight each of impact, timed and proximity fuzes for Consume submission. All three checked recipes yield four per craft, so craft counts differ from item counts.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.1: Timed fuzes are configured through their interface before use. Proximity fuzes react to blocks within the selected range rather than universally detecting enemies. Impact fuzes have a triggering chance and need not detonate on grazes or ricochets.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.text.2: Submission requires no test explosion. For separate trials, respect mounting positions: impact and proximity fuzes belong on the front and cannot serve as base fuzes. Label operational settings so delay and distance are not confused later, producing unexpected effects over your own battery.
codex.quest.more_munitions.fuzes.title: Fuzes
codex.quest.more_munitions.guide_range.t: A test shot at a target was fired from the carriage away from buildings; nobody was behind the target or on the firing line

A firing range separates cannon trials from residential buildings. The carriage is crafted from planks, a shaft and a pair of cannon wheels and lets you move a small cannon, while a target block made of four hay bales and redstone dust signals a hit and shows where the shot landed. Set four targets at different distances.

Choose a firing direction towards empty land: no buildings, colony citizens or animals behind the targets and no people on the firing line. Make the first shots with few powder charges and solid shot: high-explosive and shrapnel shells on a close range tear up the ground and damage everything nearby.

Fire a test shot and find the impact by the target and the crater. Tick the manual objective once the firing line is verified and nobody was hit. Repeat shots while changing angle and charge to learn the range of a specific barrel, and write the results down: before combat firing a table beats guesswork.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.0: CBC machine-gun rounds are cheaper autocannon ammunition oriented toward entities. This objective consumes sixty-four finished rounds. Do not confuse it with a requirement to build another mod’s similarly named weapon.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.1: The checked recipe uses a copper nugget, accepted gunpowder and an empty machine-gun round. Assemble components and verify the finished machine_gun_round result. The empty casing serves another purpose and cannot satisfy the finished-ammunition count.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.text.2: Before submission, separate operational rounds if testing a compatible autocannon. A bulk batch does not require firing at colonists or pets: this check is item-based. For subsequent range testing, use a safe in-game target, compatible feed and an accessible stop control while retaining control over the whole burst.
codex.quest.more_munitions.mg.title: Machine Gun
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.0: CBC powder charges provide propellant for compatible big cannons. Prepare sixty-four for a Consume contribution; this batch disappears instead of automatically entering an artillery warehouse. Keep firing charges separately.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.1: The installed recipe combines packed gunpowder with an empty powder-charge casing. Make components first, then assemble finished powder_charge items without confusing them with ordinary gunpowder or empty bags. Check each ingredient reserve before mass production.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.text.2: Count finished charges before submitting. The quest quantity is not an allowable load for one barrel: actual limits depend on cannon and material. At a range, use only supported projectile-and-propellant configurations, treating bulk stock as supplies for many operations rather than an invitation to load everything together.
codex.quest.more_munitions.powder.title: Powder Magazine
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.0: The arsenal accepts eight shrapnel, eight smoke and four fluid shells. All batches are consumed. Prepare different casing materials: shrapnel and fluid versions use Create mechanical crafting, while smoke shells have an ordinary shaped recipe.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.1: Make one sample of each and verify output names before expanding production. Shrapnel provides its damaging effect, smoke creates concealment and fluid shells deliver contents. An empty fluid shell satisfies the item objective but is not an already filled useful round.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.text.2: For a separate operational shell, fill through the fuze-mounting face before installing the fuze, which blocks filling. Supported examples include water, lava and liquid potions; an unknown fluid may have no effect. Avoid testing contents near your machinery: the submitted batch establishes supply rather than firing readiness.
codex.quest.more_munitions.shells.title: Shell Rack
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.0: Battery supply links Create requests with physical ammunition delivery. Prepare a redstone requester, two cannon loaders and two Frogports. Their roles differ: requests specify batches, ports move packages and loaders operate compatible cannon mechanisms.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.1: First configure a small order of an ordinary harmless material and a correct package address to test logistics. Connect ports to an operating package network, and test loader travel length and direction separately. Possessing every block does not imply a direct Frogport-to-breech connection.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.text.2: Once the route works, introduce controlled ammunition stock and a clear reorder condition. Avoid endless requests into an occupied receiver: overflow complicates servicing. Firing and supply must have separately accessible stopping controls so delays can be investigated without an unintended shot.
codex.quest.more_munitions.supply.title: Battery Supply
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.0: Nature’s Compass searches biomes, while Explorer’s Compass searches structures. Craft both and choose a target actually belonging to the current dimension. Search does not teleport you or guarantee a safe route across mountains, oceans or underground cavities.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.1: Open the appropriate interface, choose the exact name and start searching. Read distance, direction and available coordinates. If nothing appears, inspect dimension and search limits: no nearby result does not prove the mod or entire structure type is absent.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.text.2: Follow the route with ordinary supplies and record your return separately. For biomes, account for height; for structures, find an actual entrance, which may differ from central coordinates. The item objective records tools, but successful reconnaissance requires personally reaching the destination and verifying its name or contents.
codex.quest.more_qol2.compasses.title: Compasses
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.task.0: Hover an enchanted item and read its enchantment description while holding Shift
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.0: Enchantment descriptions explain effects before expensive equipment upgrades. Take an enchanted item or book, open inventory and hover its enchantment listing. Hold Shift as indicated to read the available effect explanation.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.1: Compare the description with your intended equipment. Combat, mining and defensive enchantments solve different problems, while compatibility still follows game and mod rules. Displaying explanatory text does not allow every enchantment on every tool without a suitable application method.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.text.2: The manual objective confirms reading the Shift description. No book must be spent at an anvil and no levels paid merely for this check. Afterward choose a useful upgrade deliberately and inspect application cost separately; explanatory tooltips inform decisions without removing experience costs or combination restrictions.
codex.quest.more_qol2.enchdesc.title: Enchantment Descriptions
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.0: Building Gadgets 2 provides separate building, exchanging and copy-paste devices. The template manager handles saved projects. Craft the set, charge it through a supported method and prepare materials; copying geometry does not generate free survival blocks.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.1: Select a simple block and small placement mode with the building gadget. Test the exchanger on one sample wall after inspecting selection. For copying, define a small area without valuable containers, save its template and inspect preview orientation before pasting.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.text.2: Learn undo on the same example and keep affected chunks loaded: the installed mod reports undo failure when too far from the operation. The item objective records tools rather than proficiency. Before large projects, separately check materials, energy and selected mode so an accidental exchange does not affect a neighbouring workshop.
codex.quest.more_qol2.gadgets.title: Building Gadgets 2
The destruction gadget’s area is configured and verified by removing a test wall on an empty plot

The Destruction Gadget from Building Gadgets 2 removes a whole volume of blocks in one use, the opposite of the building gadget. Recipe: iron in the corners and centre, redstone dust on top, ender pearls at the sides, lapis at the bottom. Before using it open the settings: they define the size of the removal area from the aimed point.

Set the width, height and depth of the area and aim the gadget at a surface: the preview shows exactly what will disappear. Before clicking, move chests, machines and valuable blocks out of the area: the setup is tested on an empty plot, not on the wall of your own warehouse.

Start with a small volume on waste ground: remove a test wall and make sure the preview matched the result. Tick the manual objective after that check. In town use the gadget with a reduced area and only after inspecting the preview; one wrong click erases a wall together with the neighbouring house.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.0: The Just Hammers iron hammer mines several neighbouring blocks at once. Craft it and choose an ordinary stone wall for the first trial. Expanded mining helps tunnels but can remove more than intended beside complex machinery.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.1: Inspect the affected area and strike its centre while preserving durability and drop capacity. Surface orientation affects tunnel convenience, so test walls and floors separately before a large excavation. The hammer does not bypass tool-material requirements for harder ores.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.text.2: Check collected blocks and the opening’s shape before using it in the main mine. Avoid digging blindly downward: a larger area does not reveal lava, voids or another structure beforehand. Keep an ordinary pickaxe for precise base work and use the hammer where excavation dimensions have already been inspected.
codex.quest.more_qol2.hammers.title: Just Hammers
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.task.1: Open a Lootr chest, barrel and loot minecart
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.0: Lootr makes supported naturally generated container loot personal to each player. The first advancement requires opening a Lootr chest. Social does not require inviting a friend: its installed JSON combines opening a chest, barrel and loot minecart from the mod.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.1: Explore appropriate structures and inspect container identification before opening. Take your loot while leaving the object for other explorers. A player-crafted and placed chest does not automatically become a Lootr container because of similar appearance or contents.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.text.2: After the first chest, find the required barrel and minecart, opening each personally. Check individual marks if the combined objective remains incomplete. Avoid breaking every container for testing: the system preserves access to independent loot, and its advancement concerns opening rather than destruction or trading items with another player.
codex.quest.more_qol2.lootr2.title: Lootr
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.0: Macaw’s adds construction details with their own placement rules. Prepare oak roofing, a roofing hammer and a window base. Begin with a small facade model: one roof sample tests slope and joins before spending large amounts of timber.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.1: Place roofing on a clear slope and use the hammer for supported shape adjustment. Inspect neighbours and roof edges, then prepare the window section from its chosen base through the available recipe. Nearby ordinary glass does not necessarily change window type without proper crafting.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.text.2: Check appearance outside and circulation inside while preserving light and maintenance access. Item objectives do not require roofing an entire house. Determine palette and connections before manufacturing the full batch: mixed slopes or materials can create gaps and an awkward eave above the main entrance.
codex.quest.more_qol2.macaw.title: The Macaw's Series
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.task.0: Choose an installed additional style while preparing a colony building
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.0: Style Colonies expands MineColonies blueprint packs. Exploring it requires a build tool and access to pack selection rather than another machine or electricity. Hold a hut and open blueprint previews to compare an additional style with your current one.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.1: Select an installed additional style and inspect a suitable building on clear terrain. Check dimensions, entrances and material palette across several levels. A pack name does not guarantee that all required wood and decoration already exist in storage.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.text.2: Confirm after choosing a new style while preparing colony construction. Rebuilding every house immediately is unnecessary: one inspected project helps assess supplies. Preserve a coherent choice for a future district and obtain materials first so attractive expansion does not delay urgent housing, kitchen or defence orders.
codex.quest.more_qol2.styles.title: Style Colonies
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.task.1: Obtain an item, fluid or energy trash can; the item version here qualifies
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.0: An item trash can deletes accepted items to free space in automation. Craft it and first test it away from primary storage. The advancement triggers on obtaining an eligible trash can; destroying rare items or filling its interface is unnecessary.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.1: Filter for one unwanted material and feed a few ordinary blocks. Verify that only the selected material disappears and a valuable sample is rejected. Do not attach unrestricted shared-storage output before testing: deleted items cannot be recovered merely by reopening the interface.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.text.2: After success, use the can for an explicitly surplus stream. Fluid and energy versions serve different purposes with their own conditions; this objective requires no expansion. If useful products disappear, stop input and inspect filter mode rather than increasing production to compensate for accidental deletion.
codex.quest.more_qol2.trash.title: Trash Cans
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.0: A track coupler joins and separates trains without fully disassembling them at a station. This quest consumes four devices, so keep a separate operational one for testing. Prepare a level shunting section with room for two aligned train portions.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.1: Select a track and place the coupler nearby. A wrench changes coupling or decoupling mode, while scrolling adjusts pad spacing. Bogey centres must align with marked points and carriages must face compatible directions; a station helps stop accurately.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.text.2: Apply a signal after alignment and inspect the expected connection. The four submitted blocks do not automatically appear on track. For errors, compare bogey positions and carriage orientation before increasing signal strength or dismantling the whole train: the coupler depends on correct geometry rather than merely nearby bodies.
codex.quest.more_rails.couplers.title: Couplers
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.task.2: Manually: test train passage and pedestrian access with the section stopped
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.0: A crossing must reconcile railway movement with pedestrian access. Prepare eight track pieces and two signals, select a straight visible section and provide a waiting area outside train clearance. Signals do not automatically protect someone stepping in front of a train.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.1: Divide the section according to signalling rules and inspect each signal’s direction. Run a train through while observing occupancy and clearance. Then halt traffic through controlled operation and test pedestrian passage across the stopped section, never in front of a moving locomotive.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.text.2: Confirm after both trials: train passage and crossing with traffic stopped. Provide clear waiting markers and preserve sightlines. If schedules operate the line, account for the next train: one completed passage does not leave the crossing permanently clear or remove management needs.
codex.quest.more_rails.crossing.title: Crossing
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.0: Three schedules help organize different services, while four blue conductor caps form the depot contribution. Only caps are marked Consume and disappear; schedules remain recorded items. Keep separate equipment for conductors already serving the line.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.1: Assign existing clearly named stations and waiting conditions to each schedule. Test a short route before complex loops. Steam ’n’ Rails conductors use an andesite casing and cap following their Ponder scene; a stack of hats alone assigns no drivers.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.text.2: Test one trip and return for servicing, then expand schedules. Ensure duplicate station names do not send trains along unintended routes. Submitting accessories completes the contribution but does not validate every schedule: unloading delays, fuelling and track occupancy require observation on the operating railway.
codex.quest.more_rails.depot.title: Depot
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.0: Steam ’n’ Rails fuel tanks participate in an assembled train’s liquid-fuel supply. Prepare two tanks and a diesel smokestack for appearance. The stack does not turn the train into an FE generator or prove fuel is already aboard.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.1: Include tanks in the train structure and fill them with accepted fuel, checking the particular fluid’s support. The installed conventional-fuel entry uses the c:fuel tag rather than every similarly named “diesel.” For route replenishment, use an appropriate fuel interface and aligned stop.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.text.2: Check actual stock and usage on a short trip. Unfuelled train behaviour depends on realism settings, so identical stopping or speed cannot be promised across worlds. The item objective also accepts empty tanks; operational readiness depends on filling, inclusion in the train and a working resupply route.
codex.quest.more_rails.fuel.title: Diesel
codex.quest.more_rails.guide_timetable.t: The scheduled train travelled between two stations and returned to the origin without manual control

A schedule turns a train into an automatic route between stations. Place two stations on straight sections and give them clear names; each is crafted from a railway casing and a compass, and the recipe yields two. The assembled locomotive must stand at a station to accept the schedule and depart.

Open the schedule with a right click and add instructions: “Travel to” with the first station’s name, a wait condition such as a delay, then the trip to the second. Hand the sheet to a conductor: a Blaze Burner on the train or a creature seated on a seat. Without a conductor the train stays put even with a correct schedule.

Watch a full cycle: departure, the stop at the named station and the return. If the train cannot find a station, check the spelling and a track without gaps or opposing signals. Tick the manual objective after an unattended round trip; schedules stay in the inventory and count without being handed in.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.0: A coal-burning smokestack, four Locometal boiler blocks and a smokebox decorate a steam-locomotive body. These parts are not an independent steam engine requiring a water feed. Prepare them for an understood Create train design with bogeys and controls.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.1: Install decoration on the connected structure while retaining cab access and luggage space. Smokestack variants use the block-cycle menu; its tooltip identifies the Open Cycle Menu key. Inspect the body through a curve so projecting parts do not create awkward platform clearances.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.text.2: The item objective verifies decoration stock, while an actual train must be assembled at a station and tested separately. Check that required parts joined the train, then make a short run and stop. An attractive boiler cannot fix missing bogeys, disconnected track or incorrect controls, so inspect those before cosmetics.
codex.quest.more_rails.locomotive.title: Steam Locomotive
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.0: A semaphore displays a train signal’s state through a visible mechanical arm. Prepare four and mount them on poles above Train Signals. A semaphore itself neither divides track into occupied sections nor replaces basic Create signalling.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.1: First test one pole: the underlying signal should control the visible arm as a section becomes occupied and clears. Pole materials may vary. For a brass signal with several exits, two semaphores convey different information: the lower closes when any path is blocked, the upper when all are.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.text.2: Inspect indications from an approaching driver’s viewpoint and preserve visibility around curves. Above an ordinary non-brass signal, both semaphores close together, so duplication does not always add information. The item objective cannot verify placement: the system must clearly represent the section the train is about to enter.
codex.quest.more_rails.semaphore.title: Semaphores
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.0: A beacon applies an area effect when supported by a suitable mineral pyramid with an unobstructed beam. Obtain a Nether star by defeating the Wither and craft the beacon. The nine iron blocks in this quest form only the initial three-by-three base layer.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.1: Place the beacon centrally above the layer and provide an upward beam path. Open its interface, choose an available effect and insert accepted payment. Pyramid blocks are structural material rather than fuel needing constant replenishment.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.text.2: Check the selected effect while standing nearby. A single layer does not unlock every maximum-pyramid option and cannot immediately promise Haste II. If the beam is absent, inspect the base and overhead obstruction; if the effect is absent, check selection, payment and distance from the active beacon.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.beacon.title: Beacon
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.0: Sixteen diamonds provide reserves for enchanting, tools and later upgrades. Search deep Overworld layers for diamond ore using an appropriate pickaxe. Stone tools do not yield the required drops; verify suitability and durability before mining a vein.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.1: Inspect adjacent blocks for lava and provide lighting and an exit. Fortune can increase diamond yield, while Silk Touch preserves ore blocks for later processing. This objective needs diamonds themselves, so collected ore is not yet a finished batch.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.text.2: Hold sixteen together and register the reserve before allocating it. Separate finds immediately spent individually do not accumulate for this check. Avoid converting everything into armour before making an enchanting table and retaining material for necessary tools.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.diamonds.title: Diamonds
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.0: Elytra enable gliding and firework acceleration but need open space and adequate durability. Their ordinary source is an End city ship. Prepare expedition equipment and preserve a safe return method after reaching the outer islands.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.1: Craft sixty-four rockets without firework stars for propulsion. Stars add explosive effects unnecessary for ordinary flight and potentially harmful. Equip elytra in the appropriate slot, begin gliding and test a short boost over a familiar open area.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.text.2: Check landing, rocket consumption and durability before a long route. The item objective does not establish handling skill, and losing height beside a wall remains dangerous even with ample boosters. Keep food and repair supplies accessible; another stack of fuel does not restore elytra durability.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.elytra2.title: Elytra and Rockets
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.0: An enchanting table uses player experience and lapis, while bookshelves unlock higher offers. Prepare the table and fifteen ordinary shelves. Its recipe needs a book, two diamonds and four obsidian; another mod’s decorative furniture does not necessarily replace functional shelves.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.1: Arrange shelves around the table with the required open gap and no obstructing blocks between them. Open the interface with an eligible item and inspect the high-level offer. The highest ordinary tier requires experience level thirty, although the operation itself consumes fewer levels.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.text.2: Add lapis and choose after reading the offer. Historical possession of fifteen shelves does not verify placement. If offers remain low, inspect distances and obstacles, including gap decorations, before checking experience and whether the selected item can be enchanted.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.enchant.title: Enchanting Table
codex.quest.more_vanilla.guide_conduit.t: The conduit is activated under water inside a prismarine frame and grants Conduit Power

A conduit is the beacon’s underwater relative: it grants Conduit Power, which lets you breathe, see and mine quickly under water, and with a full frame it also strikes hostile sea creatures. The heart of the sea lies only in buried treasure; treasure maps come from shipwreck and ocean ruin chests. Nautilus shells drop from drowned carrying them and occasionally come from fishing.

Craft the conduit from the heart of the sea and eight shells, then build the frame: at least sixteen blocks of prismarine, prismarine bricks, dark prismarine or sea lanterns arranged in rings one block away from the conduit. Prismarine is mined in ocean monuments guarded by guardians, so stock potions of water breathing and night vision.

A working conduit opens its “eye” and surrounds itself with particles. The effect radius grows with the number of frame blocks up to a full frame of forty-two. If there is no effect, check that the conduit is surrounded by water on all sides and the frame follows the required shape. Tick the manual objective only after you have seen the Conduit Power icon.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.guide_pyramid.t: The beacon stands on a two-layer pyramid (9 + 25 blocks) with Resistance or Jump Boost selected

A beacon’s first layer unlocks only Speed and Haste. The second layer of twenty-five blocks adds Resistance and Jump Boost and extends the range to thirty blocks. The quest counts thirty-four iron blocks seen at once, the mass of both layers together; an already assembled pyramid need not be dismantled, showing the stock once is enough.

Any mineral block works: iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite, and they may be mixed within a layer. Build the pyramid squarely: a five-by-five square, a three-by-three square on top, the beacon centred on the upper one. Nothing opaque may stand above the beacon up to the sky, otherwise the beam will not emerge and no effect activates.

After building, open the beacon interface: available effects light up, and payment is accepted as an iron, gold or netherite ingot, an emerald or a diamond. Choose Resistance or Jump Boost and check the effect icon near the beacon. The third and fourth layers are needed for Strength and boosted effects, but that is the next construction.
Netherite ingots combine scraps smelted from Nether ancient debris with gold. One ingot requires four netherite scraps and four gold ingots. Prepare sufficient stock for four ingots without confusing mined debris blocks with finished components.

Mine with a suitable pickaxe while checking lava pockets and return routes. Smelt and craft, then register four ingots together. If using explosive mining methods, choose an isolated site away from infrastructure with prepared shelter rather than testing inside your portal base.

Upgrading diamond equipment in this version additionally requires a netherite upgrade template and smithing table. An ingot cannot directly convert an iron tool to netherite. Preserve or duplicate the required template with its available recipe before assigning metal to priority equipment and future mod components.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.netherite.title: Netherite
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.task.1: Apply a smithing trim to any armour item
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.0: Armour trims change equipment appearance rather than automatically increasing protection. Prepare a smithing table, a found trim template, eligible armour and a colour material. A netherite upgrade template performs another operation and cannot substitute for a decorative pattern.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.1: Open the table, insert template, armour and colouring material, then inspect the preview. If satisfied, take the finished item. The template and material are consumed, so consider preserving a rare design through its available duplication recipe first.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.text.2: The manual objective requires applying a trim to any armour; merely owning the table does not complete it. Equip or inspect the result before confirming. For a coordinated set, budget templates separately for each piece instead of expecting one decorated chestplate to automatically decorate helmet and boots.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.trims.title: Armor Trims
Trading converts renewable resources into emeralds and useful purchases. Prepare thirty-two emeralds together and an Easy Villagers Trader block. This block serves an inserted villager; an empty trading housing does not generate offers itself.

Transfer a villager using the mod’s supported method, supply a suitable workstation and inspect trades before the first purchase. Trading locks profession and offers, so select the desired specialization beforehand. Monitor stock and offer restocking instead of expecting unlimited sales from one batch.

The Codex does not consume your emerald reserve. Divide it between planned purchases and trading reserves while storing sale inputs separately. If the Trader shows an unexpected profession, inspect the villager and previous deals; changing a workstation does not erase an established trading history.
codex.quest.more_vanilla.villagers.title: Trade
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.0: Rock cutting wheels on a borehead bearing break blocks around themselves and collect drops in attached storage. Prepare the bearing, a cutting wheel and a container; one cutting item without storage is not an operating drill.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.1: Assemble the head in front of the bearing according to Ponder and supply rotation. Wheels follow their own attachment rules; the bearing reverses direction and runs at one quarter of input speed. Begin with a small patch of ordinary stone away from the base.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.text.2: Breaking more blocks simultaneously slows operation. Full storage stops excavation; items can be extracted through the bearing, so provide output beforehand. Fence the working area and retain a safe tunnel retreat. Item checks prove neither excavation depth nor available vehicle storage.
codex.quest.offroad.borehead.title: Borehead
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.0: A tire is installed by interacting with a suitable wheel mount, and its size affects vehicle geometry. Prepare four ordinary and four sticky tires. The installed add-on makes a sticky tire from an ordinary one and four honey bottles.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.1: Equip the frame with one matching set first and inspect steering clearance. After a short trial, switch to the other set while keeping mass, speed and surface unchanged. This makes behavior changes attributable to the tires.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.text.2: Sticky wheels are not permission to drive any slope without brakes. Grip depends on contact and the whole vehicle. The objective checks inventory items, so register the ordinary set before converting it into sticky tires. Supplies for both variants help repairs and route comparisons.
codex.quest.offroad.tires.title: Tires
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.0: A first wheeled vehicle combines a physical frame, mounted tires, rotation source and understandable controls. The directional gearshift requested selects drive direction but does not replace the whole car. Prepare all components on clear level ground.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.1: Its command sides are separate: one transmits rotation and the other reverses it; no signals or both signals stop output. Test this on a shaft before connecting wheels. Configure mount steering and braking separately, then assemble the hull with the physics assembler.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.text.2: Make a brief acceleration, turn and stop without cargo. If the vehicle will not move, inspect engine, gearshift commands and wheel brakes in sequence. Avoid heading straight into mountains: inertia, wheel clearance and mass distribution need a simple route with safe dismounting.
codex.quest.offroad.vehicle.title: First Vehicle
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.0: A wheel mount attaches a wheel to a physical ground vehicle and accepts braking and steering control. Four mounts begin a four-wheel frame, but without tires, drive and physical assembly it is not a car. Prepare a light rectangular platform.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.1: Place mounts consistently on both sides and leave tire clearance. Power from above applies braking; power from a side steers toward that side. Test these responses on one mount before wiring all four.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.text.2: Avoid sending arbitrary shared wiring into top and side inputs. Steering and braking are different actions, and a stationary vehicle may simply have its brakes continuously powered. Check access to every mount before installing tires. Low speed and level ground are safest for the first rig.
codex.quest.offroad.wheel_mount.title: Wheel Mount
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.0: Yaw and pitch controllers rotate a gun toward a selected network target. A fire controller emits redstone when the linked mount is aligned; it does not check propellant or gun integrity for you. Prepare all three devices and a completely unloaded gun.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.1: Place the yaw controller under the mount and connect data links, then configure pitch control according to Ponder. Select a known safe point on the monitor. Route fire-controller output to a lamp first, observing readiness without firing.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.text.2: Test both directions and response to a target change. Correct reversed motion through orientation and settings before loading ammunition. Readiness indicates alignment rather than an empty range. Keep an independent manual firing inhibit that does not depend on the data network.
codex.quest.radar.controllers.title: Targeting Controllers
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.0: A data link connects radar components and a monitor. It differs from power cable and Create wireless redstone links. Prepare the link device, monitor and assembled radar while keeping weapons disconnected.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.1: Place the monitor conveniently and link it to the radar according to Data Link hints. Open the installed link’s settings and check selected endpoints. A broader network uses a separate Network Controller for filters and additional components.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.text.2: Find a known track on the monitor and compare it with the object’s world position. If the screen is empty, inspect assembly, linkage and filters in sequence. Red weapon-network links and blue radar-network links have different roles. Owning both items does not confirm correct data exchange or safe target selection.
codex.quest.radar.datalink.title: Data Link
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.0: A guided fuze belongs to specialized guided ammunition and requires compatibility with your radar system. Prepare it along with the warning receiver and identification transponder. These three inventory items do not assemble a guided shell by themselves.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.1: Establish a stable target track and verify identification on an unloaded rig first. Check the selected ammunition’s recipe and hints for permitted fuze mounting and required network linkage. A normal projectile is not guided merely because a radar stands nearby.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.text.2: Use one shot at a remote training target with an inspected flight area for the first trial. Observe track loss and system behavior before repeating. A warning receiver only reports detection, and a transponder relies on filters; neither guarantees protection from incorrectly configured weapons.
codex.quest.radar.guidance.title: Shell Guidance
codex.quest.radar.guide_fire_inhibit.tas: Manually verify the switch blocks the final firing signal while aiming continues, using a lamp and no ammunition
codex.quest.radar.guide_fire_inhibit.tex: Automatic aiming is easier to service when firing can be inhibited independently of target selection. Prepare a separate switch and a lamp in place of the mount’s firing input. Do not begin with a loaded gun.

Separate aiming from the final firing permission. With permission disabled, change the training target: axes should keep tracking while the firing-input signal remains blocked. Test readiness with permission enabled using only the lamp.

Confirm manually once firing can be stopped without dismantling the network or losing observation. Label the switch and place it outside the gun’s sector. Repeat a brief trial after wiring repairs, since an accidental bypass signal can make the familiar lever ineffective even when it looks operational.
Manually exclude your own code from automatic targeting while confirming selection of a permitted training target without ammunition

A transponder does not prevent friendly selection unless its code is excluded. Prepare a friendly physical construct and a separate training object. Keep every linked gun unloaded and temporarily route firing output to a lamp.

Assign a known transponder code and configure its identification filter in the Network Controller. Verify that your own object is excluded from automatic selection while the permitted training target remains available. Do not confuse category exclusion with a specific identification code.

Confirm manually after observing both results. Change a training copy’s code to understand the resulting behavior, then restore the safe configuration. This experiment belongs before automatic fire: an accidentally invisible object and a correctly identified friendly object can look identical during a superficial check.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.0: An identification transponder assigns a physical construct a name and code. Exclusion from automatic targeting occurs only when the code matches a configured identification filter in the network controller. Prepare the transponder and warning receiver while keeping ammunition separate.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.1: Install the transponder on a Sable physics construct: it does nothing on an ordinary machine block. Set its code and enter that code in your radar network’s filter. Check the object’s track and exclusion from automatic selection. A matching name without the correct code is insufficient.
codex.quest.radar.iff.text.2: The warning receiver sounds when within radar coverage and when locked onto, but does not prevent lock-on. Test both sounds with a friendly observer and no firing. Do not assume protection from another network that has not excluded your code. Verify filtering before connecting automatic weapons.
codex.quest.radar.iff.title: Friend or Foe
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.0: Binoculars let you manually designate a point for guns linked to a network controller. They are useful for aiming tests without automatic track selection. Prepare binoculars, an operating Network Controller and a completely unloaded mount.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.1: Sneak-interact with the controller using the binoculars to pair them. Zoom in and hold the left button while pointing at a safe location. Connected guns should follow the selected direction according to network settings.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.text.2: Test several range points and releasing control. Avoid pointing the training network through base walkways even when firing is not intended: another connected gun might still contain ammunition. Verify every linked gun is unloaded first. If a gun does not respond, inspect the paired controller, weapon links and axis operation rather than binocular magnification.
codex.quest.radar.misc_radar.title: Manual targeting
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.0: Radar plates form part of an antenna structure and expand detection capability. Prepare eight plates and a clear area above a roof or beside the workshop. Plates in a chest have no effect; they must belong to the assembled antenna.
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.1: Arrange them on a connected frame that will later mount on a radar bearing with its receiver. Dishes and plates can substitute for each other in the antenna; check the chosen geometry against Ponder. Leave rotational clearance.
codex.quest.radar.plate.text.2: Do not expect a fixed range solely from the number eight: configuration and network parameters determine actual results. After startup, compare detection of a known object with and without added plates. This expands coverage deliberately while retaining maintenance access and avoiding an obstructing wall.
codex.quest.radar.plate.title: Radar Plates
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.0: A radar receiver on its dedicated bearing forms an operating detection node. Prepare both requested devices, an antenna and rotational power. This is not an ordinary windmill bearing, so a similar-looking component cannot replace it.
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.1: Place the radar bearing, receiver and connected plates or dishes as shown in Ponder. Supply rotation and verify assembly. The next step adds a monitor where detection results become visible.
codex.quest.radar.radar.text.2: Begin observation without connected weapons and choose a known object for testing. A missing track can depend on target type, position, configuration or linkage, not merely antenna area. Do not assume every moving block is a supported target. Record one working radar configuration before adding several stations to a shared network.
codex.quest.radar.radar.title: Radar
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.autocrafter.tex: An autocrafter stores patterns and exposes them for requests. Ordinary crafting needs the network and ingredients; processing patterns send ingredients into an external inventory. Prepare the device and one encoded simple pattern.

Connect the autocrafter and insert the pattern. Request a small output batch through the grid, inspect material planning and start the task. Confirm the product appears before adding dozens of recipes.

For processing, the autocrafter’s output face must point into a suitable machine input or buffer. Return machine output through an importer or another verified route. If ingredients leave but the task remains waiting, do not blindly add a second pattern. Locate the expected product physically and check its exact quantity.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.big_project.tex: An advanced processor needs a chain of raw-processor crafting and smelting. For eight products, prepare diamonds, silicon, redstone and bindings, or working patterns for missing intermediates. One ordinary crafting pattern for the finished processor is insufficient.

Encode the raw recipe and a separate furnace-processing pattern. Configure insertion into the correct furnace input, fuel supply and output return. Request eight processors through the grid and watch both stages.

Compare completion in the monitor with network stock. If eight processors were registered earlier, they need not be held again solely for the item check; the new trial verifies the chain. Historical credit is not evidence of working return logistics: the actual furnace must deliver requested products without hand-carrying.
A subrecipe lets you request processors from basic supplies without manually preparing bindings each time. Gather string, slime and a blank pattern. Verify the ordinary recipe first: two strings and one slime produce eight bindings, so encoded output quantity matters.

Encode the craft and place it in an accessible autocrafter. Request sixteen bindings and compare planning with input stock. A correct pattern needs two recipe batches rather than sixteen separate slime balls.

Obtain sixteen identical bindings together for tracking if that maximum has not already been registered. Separate small holdings do not accumulate toward that quantity. Use the bindings in processors afterward rather than creating an unnecessary spare stock. This subrecipe supports longer chains in which the network calculates intermediate materials.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.guide_return_fa: Manually locate the monitor’s expected product while return is stopped, restore import and finish the same task

A task can remain waiting despite a working furnace if its product does not return. Choose inexpensive processing with a known result and a controllable importer. Avoid a recipe simultaneously serving an important shared request.

Temporarily stop output return, process a small batch and open the monitor. Identify the expected product and verify that it physically occupies the machine’s output. Restore import and wait for the same task to finish without placing another request.

Confirm manually after finding the cause and observing automatic completion. Do not cancel first, since that may conceal that the network was waiting for an already made item. If the product returns but waiting continues, compare expected type, data and quantity. This distinguishes routing faults from recipe-planning errors.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.guide_stock_lim: Manually verify export stops at the configured limit and resumes after consumption to restore the same stock

An autocrafting exporter may keep filling its destination while ingredients remain. A regulator limits the selected resource quantity in the target inventory. Prepare the upgrade and a small chest holding one consumable the network can craft.

Configure the regulator’s item and modest limit, then install it in a supported exporter with autocrafting. Wait for stock to fill and verify that insertion stops. Remove some and check replenishment to the same level.

Confirm manually after stopping and refilling are observed. If production continues, check whether the actual destination stock is regulated and filters match. A huge capacity is not a sensible stock target by itself. This arrangement can supply repair parts while preserving network materials for other requests.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.task.0: Manually request crafting from JEI through the grid and verify the result appears in the network
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.0: JEI integration helps bring a known recipe into network crafting and reveal missing ingredients. It does not turn every displayed recipe into an already encoded pattern. Prepare a working grid and a simple resource the network can actually craft.
