codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.1: Open the JEI recipe from the grid interface and use the available transfer or request action. Inspect planning before starting: a missing ingredient may need its own pattern or replenished stock. Observe completion and the product appearing in storage.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.text.2: Confirm the manual “Order crafting from JEI through the grid” objective after an actual request, not merely viewing a recipe. If unavailable, check grid type, integration and encoded pattern. Avoid endless repeated requests; first determine whether the original is waiting for external processing.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.jei_rs.title: JEI Integration
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.0: An autocrafter manager presents patterns in one interface and helps service a distributed workshop. Prepare it after the first successful autocraft. It neither speeds recipes up nor replaces the devices physically holding patterns.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.1: Connect it and find a familiar recipe by output, input or autocrafter name. Give devices understandable names, especially when several serve identical furnaces. If one is absent, check its manager-visibility setting.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.text.2: For duplicate recipes, compare priorities: the network favors the pattern in the higher-priority autocrafter. Avoid deleting working patterns randomly during an active request. Finish or deliberately cancel the task first, then correct one entry and repeat a small trial. This keeps a growing recipe collection manageable.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.manager.title: Pattern Manager
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.monitor_craft.t: An autocrafting monitor shows task state and distinguishes ingredient waiting from waiting for machine output. Prepare it on the same network as a working simple pattern. Use a small inexpensive request for learning.

Start a recipe and open the monitor while it runs. Inspect required and expected resources, then locate the corresponding machine state. Raw material missing from network stock may already be in an external buffer.

Canceling a task does not automatically retrieve every item from outside inventories. Inspect furnace, input and output before ordering again so you do not duplicate an unwanted batch. If output fails to return, fix physical routing or the expected-output pattern. The monitor supports diagnosis rather than automatically unblocking every machine.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.pattern_grid.te: A pattern grid encodes a recipe onto a pattern item for an autocrafter. Prepare the device and eight blank patterns, then connect it to a powered network. Choose a simple first recipe with an unambiguous result, such as ordinary planks from a suitable log.

In crafting mode, define ingredients and output, then encode the pattern. A furnace or external machine needs processing mode: inputs specify resources sent out, and outputs specify the exact expected return. The grid does not perform processing itself.

Do not declare a probabilistic result guaranteed without additional handling. Check output quantities and permitted substitutions, especially for items with special data. Place the pattern in an autocrafter next. Execute complex recipes manually first to verify the installed pack’s actual result.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.processor_line_: The trial batch checks several processors moving through one line. Reserve materials for eight advanced processors and inspect the request preview. Replenish the specifically missing ingredient instead of changing every pattern at once.

Start the request through the grid and watch raw crafting, furnace processing and return. Ensure the importer extracts finished processors rather than pulling raw inputs. Output stock should increase by the requested quantity after completion.

The item objective requires having shown eight identical processors together in a tracked inventory once; separate small batches do not add up to that holding. No repeat showing is needed if already registered. The Codex does not consume them. Observation proves this line works; a checkbox may have come from previously produced processors.
Manually request eight processors, check missing materials, replenish supplies and receive all eight outputs back into the network

Acceptance should include missing materials and correct completion after replenishment. Prepare the network interface, monitor and room for finished processors. Keep a missing ingredient outside the network for a controlled check.

Request eight processors through the interface. Compare the missing-material list; after replenishment, the order must finish and return all eight. If the interface prevents starting with shortages, inspect the preview first, supply materials and then confirm the request.

Confirm manually after the in-world check; the Codex does not automatically measure operation. Follow the external furnace too: completion must not depend on manually extracting output. If waiting persists, inspect fuel, importer side and exact expected product, preserving intermediates instead of repeatedly restarting without diagnosis.

A processor line connects an autocrafter, furnace and return path. This objective asks for an autocrafter and importer; previously registered devices can be reused without removing them for tracking. Prepare a furnace, cable and separate fuel supply.

Install raw advanced-processor and smelting patterns in the autocrafter. Direct raw items toward a suitable furnace input and the importer toward finished-output extraction. Do not send fuel into the same slot as raw ingredients.

Test one processor from diamond, silicon, redstone and binding. If raw crafting works but smelting does not, inspect fuel and input. If smelting finishes but the task waits, locate output. Prepared components do not prove the whole cycle; a batch and separate trial establish reliability.
codex.quest.rs_autocraft.upgrade_craft.t: An autocrafting upgrade lets a compatible device request a missing resource through a pattern. It suits an exporter, interface or constructor needing a steady material supply. Prepare it only after that resource has been requested successfully by hand.

Install it in a supported device and set the desired filtered item. Start with a small receiving chest, limiting stock through a suitable regulator or controlled capacity. Remove some material and observe the resulting task.

The upgrade does not invent missing recipes or know a desired stock ceiling without other settings. Continuous export into a huge chest can consume all network ingredients. Check that production stops at the target and resumes after consumption. Diagnose waiting tasks through the monitor: materials, power, machine access and output return.
A wireless autocrafting monitor lets you inspect and cancel tasks without returning to a fixed screen. It uses network coverage and its own energy. Prepare and charge the item, then bind it to the intended network.

Start a small task near the base, open the handheld monitor and compare it with the stationary one. Move to your normal working distance and test connectivity. Coverage depends on transmitters and upgrades rather than pattern count.

Cancel only with an understanding of external-machine consequences: dispatched ingredients may remain in a furnace or buffer. A discharged monitor does not mean the network stopped. Keep a stationary monitor and accessible charging source. This is useful in long factories where a visible fault and its autocrafter are far apart.
codex.quest.rs_network.blocks_storage.te: A storage block combines capacity and network connection in one installed device without a disk drive. Prepare the 1k variant and space along the cable route. It suits a small network where a separate drive is inconvenient.

Connect the block and insert a small known batch through the grid. Watch usage change, then retrieve the same items. If other storage exists, account for priorities: insertion may have gone elsewhere.

Before moving it, check content-preservation behavior and preferably empty the training block. Closing a grid window does not make storage empty. Block and disk forms solve similar problems but differ in expansion and handling. After testing, choose based on placement convenience while preserving free capacity for incoming production.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.0: Cable connects devices into a network, while a relay controls an entire branch. Prepare sixteen cables and one relay. Use a short visible route between controller and future grid instead of immediately hiding everything under the floor.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.1: Place the relay at a branch boundary and inspect direction and mode. Simple pass-through shares the whole network; advanced settings selectively expose storage, energy, security and patterns. Avoid adding filtering without a concrete need.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.text.2: Test disconnecting and restoring one branch while retaining main-network access. An empty but powered grid may indicate that the relay is not passing storage. Distinguish missing energy from missing resource access. Cable stores nothing itself, so the next quest adds disk capacity.
codex.quest.rs_network.cable.title: Cables and Relay
A constructor places selected blocks from the network into the world, while a destructor breaks suitable blocks in front and returns drops. Prepare both and a small dirt or stone supply. Keep the test area away from important machinery.

Connect the constructor, select material and check its working face against empty space. Test the destructor separately on one prepared block. Configure filtering where necessary and provide storage space for drops.

Do not point a destructor at an expensive machine without understanding its drops; the harvested result may differ from the installed block. Adjacent constructors and destructors can repeatedly recycle one position while using energy. Add an understandable enable control and inspect the result before automating a farm or rebuilding wall.
codex.quest.rs_network.constructor.title: Constructor and Destructor
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.0: A controller supplies electrical energy to Refined Storage devices. Prepare one and a steady FE source; placing the block alone does not activate grids or storage. One controller is enough initially, but version 2 permits several, so the old one-controller-per-network rule is incorrect here.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.1: Connect power, then add a short cable and initial devices. Open controller status and compare stored energy with demand. Consumption changes as the network grows, especially with upgrades and disks.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.text.2: If everything goes dark, inspect energy and source connection first. A nearby chest of materials does not replace electrical delivery. Keep the controller accessible and avoid moving the whole warehouse before testing insertion and extraction. This leaves restoration parts available outside an unpowered network.
codex.quest.rs_network.controller.title: Controller
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.0: A disk drive holds storage disks, while the disks themselves hold the data. Craft and register a housing first, then use it for a 1k disk; no spare housing is needed solely for tracking. Prepare a drive too. An empty housing combines with a storage part when crafting a disk but stores no items alone.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.1: Connect the drive to a powered network and insert the disk. Once a grid is available, insert a few inexpensive items and inspect usage. A drive without disks provides no storage capacity.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.text.2: Removing a disk makes its contents unavailable through the network, so label and protect transported media. The supported action disassembles a disk into components when it is empty; evacuate contents and verify zero usage first. The objective checks three items rather than recording data. Use a small countable trial before migrating a warehouse.
codex.quest.rs_network.drive.title: Disk Drive and Disks
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.0: External storage exposes a connected chest, tank or compatible inventory to the network. Items remain in their original container rather than necessarily moving onto a disk. Prepare the adapter and a small chest with known contents.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.1: Point the device into the container, connect cable and inspect the grid listing. Configure permitted resources, mode and priority where needed. Avoid exposing the same container through several independent paths without a clear reason.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.text.2: The disk interface in the second objective does something different: transferring resources between inserted disks and the network in a selected direction. Test with a separate inexpensive sample disk and enough free space. Do not confuse external-chest access with disk migration; verify both through actual stock changes.
codex.quest.rs_network.external.title: External Storage
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.0: A grid shows available network resources and lets you insert and extract items. A crafting grid adds an ordinary crafting matrix. Prepare both devices; register the basic grid before using it in an upgrade recipe.
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.1: Connect a grid to a powered network with a disk or external storage. Insert a small stack of stone, find it through search and remove some. Then try a simple recipe in the crafting grid using available materials.
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.text.2: An empty list may indicate missing storage, display filtering, a disabled relay or permissions rather than loss of every item. Check these before rebuilding. A crafting grid assists manual crafting; patterns and autocrafters provide automation in the next chapter. Retain an ordinary emergency chest for power-restoration components.
codex.quest.rs_network.grid.title: Grid
codex.quest.rs_network.guide_disk_migrat: Manually transfer a known batch from disk to network, verify the source disk is empty and quantities match

A disk interface empties media before disassembly or storage changes. Prepare a separate training disk containing a known inexpensive batch and a network with sufficient free capacity. Keep the transfer source clear so identical resources are not confused.

Insert the disk into the interface and choose transfer from disk to network. Check filter and direction before starting. Wait for completion, then compare the empty source state and destination quantities.

Confirm manually after both checks. If contents remain, inspect capacity and blocking filters instead of disassembling the disk in the hope of finishing transfer. Only an empty disk should undergo its supported disassembly action. Perform this trial before migrating rare items and enchanted equipment, where mistakes are more costly.
codex.quest.rs_network.guide_power_recov: Manually restore power using supplies outside the network and verify the original sample quantity after the outage

A power outage temporarily removes grid access, so restoration parts should not exist only inside the network. Prepare an ordinary external chest with cable, generator fuel and required tools. Put a small precisely known batch into the network for testing.

Stop energy delivery to the training section and wait for access to switch off if controller reserves remain. Restore power using externally accessible supplies, reopen the grid and count the sample. Avoid unnecessary disk removal during the trial.

Confirm manually once access returns and quantities match. A dark screen does not mean destroyed data, but you need a clear way to restart generation. This reserve matters after adding autocrafting, since devices increase demand. Keep actual repair essentials rather than duplicating the whole digital warehouse.
codex.quest.rs_network.io.text.0: An importer pulls resources from an external inventory into the network, while an exporter sends selected resources out. Prepare both, an interface, and speed and stack upgrades. Use two small chests so transfer direction is visible.
codex.quest.rs_network.io.text.1: Attach the importer to the input chest and the exporter to the output, configuring the exporter’s filter. An interface has intermediate slots for both directions; neighboring machinery must insert and extract through suitable logistics. It is not two universal contactless pipes.
codex.quest.rs_network.io.text.2: Test one stack before adding acceleration. Upgrades work only in supported devices and increase energy use. If items loop endlessly, check whether the same supply is being exported and immediately imported. A production machine separately needs correct raw-material insertion and finished-output return.
codex.quest.rs_network.io.title: Import and Export
codex.quest.rs_network.monitor.text.0: A storage monitor displays the quantity of a selected resource, while a detector emits redstone under a quantity condition. Prepare both and an item whose stock is easy to change. This is useful for generator fuel or iron before a large build.
codex.quest.rs_network.monitor.text.1: Connect the monitor and assign its displayed item. Set the same resource and a threshold in the detector, then add and remove it through the grid. Watch the number and a lamp attached to the detector.
codex.quest.rs_network.monitor.text.2: Check comparison direction: signaling shortage differs from signaling surplus. A monitor does not create infinite stock, and a detector does not create a replenishment recipe. After testing, connect the signal to an external production line with a stop control. Internal manufacturing requires the separate pattern and autocrafting branch.
codex.quest.rs_network.monitor.title: Monitor and Detector
Quartz-enriched iron is needed for casings, cables and other basic network parts. Prepare ordinary iron ingots and quartz. Do not smelt all quartz into silicon; some is needed as the original crystal.

The installed recipe combines three iron ingots and one quartz into four quartz-enriched iron. Repeat four times to obtain sixteen. Check the square ingredient pattern in JEI if manual crafting produces no result.

This is a separate material rather than an upgrade applied to existing cable. Divide supplies between controller, connections and disk housings, retaining a few ingots for repairs. A shortage of one cheap material can delay a network longer than a rare processor, so this small repeatable batch belongs among the workshop’s frequent crafts.
codex.quest.rs_network.quartz_iron.title: Quartz Enriched Iron
codex.quest.rs_network.security.text.0: A security manager controls player actions in a shared network. In this version, an active manager blocks operations by default until cards grant permissions. Prepare the device and a card, planning owner access first.
codex.quest.rs_network.security.text.1: Configure a personal card with required rights: opening devices, insertion, extraction, autocrafting and network modification are distinct. Test your own access on a training setup before connecting the main warehouse. A separate fallback card defines rights for players without individual cards.
codex.quest.rs_network.security.text.2: An inactive manager does not protect the network, so check accidental redstone control. On a shared server, test an allowed and denied action with an agreed participant. Do not place the only recovery method beyond your own access. The item objective confirms components; tested cards and manager state establish the actual policy.
codex.quest.rs_network.security.title: Security
codex.quest.rs_network.silicon.text.0: Silicon and processors are used in most Refined Storage devices. The installed silicon recipe smelts quartz in an ordinary furnace. Prepare quartz, iron, redstone, string, slime and fuel; register eight silicon together first, then use them in processors.
codex.quest.rs_network.silicon.text.1: Two strings with slime produce eight processor bindings. Combine a binding, silicon, redstone and an iron ingot into a raw basic processor, then smelt it. Gold and diamond serve other tiers rather than replacing iron in this objective.
codex.quest.rs_network.silicon.text.2: After silicon, register four finished basic processors; different item objectives can be shown sequentially. A raw processor does not count as finished. Later automation must repeat two distinct steps, crafting the raw processor and smelting it, with output returning to the network. A small manual batch reveals the complete route first.
codex.quest.rs_network.silicon.title: Silicon and Processors
codex.quest.rs_network.wireless.text.0: A wireless grid accesses the network within transmitter coverage and needs its own charge. Network transmitters and receivers connect remote network segments and serve a different purpose. Prepare the four listed devices plus a network card for segment linking.
codex.quest.rs_network.wireless.text.1: Charge and bind the wireless grid using its supported method, then test beside an operating transmitter. For a remote segment, sneak-use the card on the receiver and insert the bound card into the network transmitter.
codex.quest.rs_network.wireless.text.2: Ordinary wireless coverage is not unlimited access from anywhere. Check range, energy, loading of both endpoints and required upgrades for the intended route. Insert and extract an inexpensive item before traveling. Keep a normal grid at the base so an empty handheld battery does not block access to charging materials.
codex.quest.rs_network.wireless.title: Wireless Access
codex.quest.space_glacio.colony.reward.0: A second homeland, built with your own hands
codex.quest.space_glacio.colony.text.0: This node accepts an equipment set as a contribution to an off-world colony. Every listed item objective is marked Consume: submitting it removes the device from your inventory. This neither automatically places machines on Glacio nor checks an existing habitable room.
codex.quest.space_glacio.colony.text.1: Prepare a separate batch: an oxygen distributor, water pump, gravity normalizer, four solar panels, two airlocks and an energizer. Do not dismantle the outpost’s last working devices for submission. First ensure remaining base equipment and transport support safe continued play and returning home.
codex.quest.space_glacio.colony.text.2: Before confirming, count the expendable stock and read the objectives. Glacio’s surface has oxygen, but this donated set represents a general colony project that may serve other environments. Submission completes the contribution; actual sealing, power and operation require separate equipment you retain.
codex.quest.space_glacio.colony.title: A Colony Off Earth
codex.quest.space_glacio.glacio_life.tex: Glacio provides local fur and further ice-shard supplies. Find Glacian rams and bring shears for fur: the animals support shearing, so killing the entire group is unnecessary. Record their location to return after their coats recover.

Obtain four fur and separately mine thirty-two ice shards from suitable ore. Ordinary ice blocks cannot substitute for shards in the item objective. Keep fur for local decoration and supported recipes, and shards for fuel reserves.

Explore gradually while preserving the route back to landing. Atmospheric oxygen helps on the surface but does not make neighbouring dimensions safe without a suit. Before returning, check cargo and fuel separately from the collected fur; resource gathering does not replace spacecraft preparation.
codex.quest.space_glacio.guide_glacio_ai: Oxygen, temperature and gravity were checked on the surface of Glacio Ti-69; a separate oxygen reserve prepared for orbit

Glacio does not repeat lunar conditions: the installed planet data gives its surface oxygen, a temperature of minus twenty degrees and gravity different from Earth. Bring a Ti-69 and inspect these properties after landing before redesigning the colony kit around familiar assumptions.

Compare readings with your outing plan and keep protective equipment accessible. Surface atmosphere does not automatically extend to orbit: Glacio’s orbital dimension has no oxygen. Prepare a separate filled reserve for the next orbital transfer and inspect it before launching.

The manual objective confirms measurement of all three properties and a ready orbital oxygen reserve. It does not require exposing your character to cold without protection. This survey helps select infrastructure for actual local conditions instead of building an identical lunar room on every new planet merely because its name is alien.
codex.quest.space_glacio.guide_ram_shear: A live Glacian Ram was sheared; the wool collected and the animal left in a safe pen

Glacian fur does not require killing the animal: the installed mod supports shearing Glacian Rams with shears. Bring a serviceable tool, locate a ram on Glacio and prepare a small nearby pen. Leave enough room to approach and collect output without forcing the animal outside.

Use shears on the living ram and collect the dropped fur. Preserve access to suitable local ground: its behaviour includes eating permafrost. Do not expect wool from every repeated click or replace observation of regrowth with another attack.

The manual objective completes after shearing and placing the living animal in a safe pen. This begins renewable colony supplies rather than a kill task. Mark the herd’s coordinates and keep spare shears: finding animals again on an unfamiliar planet usually takes longer than carefully maintaining a small enclosure.
codex.quest.space_glacio.interstellar.te: Glacio is this branch’s first accessible destination in another star system. Travel with a tier-four rocket, return fuel, a pad and a complete expedition kit. Keep space equipment ready even though the planet has oxygen: the route and orbit have different conditions.

After landing, recover transport from the lander and record coordinates. Check conditions with the Ti-69: the installed planet data specifies oxygen, a temperature of minus twenty and lower-than-Earth gravity. It is not an airless copy of the Moon, though movement still takes adjustment.

Interstellar and the dimension objective trigger on entering Glacio. Completing them does not require building a huge colony immediately. Begin with protected storage and a short survey while preserving the return reserve; local animals and icy resources form the next separate task.
Manual: the rocket cargo inventory contains a second launch pad and three fuel buckets for the return flight.
Before launch, place a second launch pad and three ordinary fuel buckets for returning in the rocket inventory. This is separate cargo in addition to fuel already loaded into the rocket. Open the cargo interface and count the reserve instead of relying on memory of the last crafting session.

Wear the complete filled suit and bring full oxygen tanks, food, weapons, tools and glowstone or soul torches. Ordinary torches are unsuitable in airless conditions, while Moon water freezes rather than behaving like an Earth farm’s water.

Mark the manual objective after actually packing the pad and return fuel in the rocket. Codex does not automatically inspect cargo contents. Replenish missing supplies on Earth; the possibility of finding a trader on the Moon should not be your only return plan.
codex.quest.space_ground.checklist.title: Pre-flight Check
codex.quest.space_ground.compressor.text: The Ad Astra compressor makes metal plates from ingots or blocks using FE. It is not a PneumaticCraft air compressor and needs no pressure tubes. Craft the machine, connect electricity and prepare eight iron ingots for the first batch.

Feed iron into the processing input and wait for plates. The installed recipe gives one plate per ingot or nine per iron block; compression does not double metal quantity. Keep eight plates in your inventory before crafting them into the next machine’s components.

The advancement detects obtaining the compressor itself, while plates have a separate objective. If processing does not start, inspect energy, input type and output space. A small permanent plate stock supports oxygen equipment, rocket parts and later construction, so give it a dedicated chest.
codex.quest.space_ground.furnace.text.0: The etrionic blast furnace uses electricity and has two modes: blasting and alloying. Space-program steel requires alloying specifically. Prepare FE, iron and coal rather than expecting ordinary smelting of an iron ingot to turn it into steel.
codex.quest.space_ground.furnace.text.1: Open the interface, select the appropriate process and supply the steel recipe ingredients. Blasting serves another purpose and supports several working positions; switching modes changes input meaning. Begin with a small easily verified batch.
codex.quest.space_ground.furnace.text.2: The advancement is awarded on obtaining the furnace, so demonstrate startup separately with an actual steel ingot. If the machine waits despite full energy, inspect mode and output space. Reliable electric steel production feeds the large rocket batch; keep an ordinary furnace available for simple materials while configuring the new process.
codex.quest.space_ground.furnace.title: Etrionic Blast Furnace
The coal generator supplies FE for Ad Astra’s first machines by burning accepted fuel such as coal or wood. Craft it and place it near the future compressor while preserving interface access. Its name does not exclude other supported combustible items.

Load a small fuel amount and check energy accumulation. Connect the correct output to the consumer input with available compatible energy transport. One machine is enough for the first test so fuel shortages are not confused with simultaneous workshop demand.

This node’s advancement is awarded for obtaining the generator, not generating a particular amount of FE. Separately confirm that the compressor actually receives power. If the generator is full and stops burning fuel, inspect energy reception; that may be normal no-load behaviour.
codex.quest.space_ground.generator.title: Coal Generator
codex.quest.space_ground.guide_fuel_rese: Ordinary fuel must cover two flights: three buckets for departure and three more for returning. Produce six in a fuel refinery supplied with oil and electricity. This is a round-trip reserve, not six buckets that necessarily belong inside the rocket simultaneously.

Split the batch before fuelling: use the departure portion on Earth and pack the return portion with a verified launch pad. Do not make returning depend on finding local oil. Unlocking a planet does not mean a fuel workshop already exists there.

The item objective checks possession of the batch, not where you subsequently store the reserve. Count the luggage again before launch. Cryofuel later reduces the required bucket count, but until its production is established, use the ordinary-fuel calculation and keep those two consumption rates distinct.
codex.quest.space_ground.guide_oxygen_re: Two portable oxygen tanks are filled; refilling the space suit was tested

An oxygen loader is useful at home, but a field reserve must travel with you. Prepare two portable gas tanks and fill them with oxygen from a working loader. Owning a gas tank does not prove it contains breathable material: this container supports different fluids.

Inspect the contents name and fill level of both tanks. Test the mod’s supported suit-refilling method in your Earth workshop, where mistakes do not require an emergency return. Keep oxygen separate from rocket fuel and mark spare containers in your luggage.

Confirm the manual objective after successful refilling and inspection of both filled reserves. They cover a travel delay rather than replace a base’s stationary system. Refill used reserves after returning and before the next flight: identical-looking full and empty tanks are easy to confuse.
codex.quest.space_ground.launch_service_: Thirty-two iron ingots form a repair and production reserve for the launch site. Set aside a separate batch after major rocket components without taking the last iron from ongoing production. This stock supports simple parts, extra containers and ground servicing.

Obtain the ingots through ordinary smelting or an established ore-processing line and collect them in inventory. The check does not consume metal or require a particular production machine. Do not confuse iron with finished steel or plates needed by other recipes.

After detection, decide what stays at the launch site and what travels as backup. Iron cannot replace return fuel, a launch pad or oxygen. Check mandatory equipment separately before departure; an additional resource reserve is useful only once safe return conditions are satisfied.
Manual: check suit oxygen, rocket fuel and landing preparation; the return flight requires no resources still to be obtained.

The launch complex is ready for testing when the rocket is fuelled and the player can actually breathe after landing. Check the complete equipped suit, its oxygen reserve and spare tanks. Open the rocket and distinguish loaded fuel from buckets carried as cargo.

Check the selected destination, landing preparation and return-flight kit. Return pad and fuel must already travel with you rather than depending on unmined desh, lunar trading or a future base. Bring tools to recover the lander’s contents.

Mark the manual objective after these in-world checks. Codex does not automatically measure launch readiness or whether return fuel remains available. Fly only after verified preparation; repeat oxygen and cargo checks if you changed armour or reorganised inventory before departure.

This node prepares a separate launch-site check after rocket crafting. Choose level ground with open sky, easy access and space for expedition cargo storage. A rocket in inventory completes equipment only, not ground infrastructure operation.

Place the launch pad and install the rocket according to Ad Astra rules. Open both fuel and cargo interfaces to confirm access. Remove accidental redstone control beside the pad: a signal can launch a fuelled rocket, so the first departure should be deliberate.

Prepare nearby equipment charging and oxygen replenishment. Do not pack your last loader before filling the suit and spare tanks. The next iron batch serves as supply reserve, while a separate manual check confirms a return flight without lunar materials you have not yet mined.
codex.quest.space_ground.oil.task.1: Fill a bucket with oil from a source
codex.quest.space_ground.oil.text.0: Ad Astra oil appears in spouts above the ocean and is refined into rocket fuel. Prepare a boat, several empty buckets and a safe route back to shore. The advancement requires actually filling a bucket with oil; retrieving an already filled bucket from a chest does not trigger the bucket-filling event.
codex.quest.space_ground.oil.text.1: Bring oil to a fuel refinery and supply FE. The installed recipe converts equal amounts of oil and fuel. Obtain three fuel buckets for the item objective, but prepare another three for the return flight: six ordinary fuel buckets total.
codex.quest.space_ground.oil.text.2: Oil and fuel are different fluids, so fill the rocket with accepted fuel. Store the return reserve separately and avoid spending it on trial launches. If refining stops, inspect input fluid, energy and output space before setting out to find more oil.
codex.quest.space_ground.oil.title: Oil
codex.quest.space_ground.oxygen.text.0: The oxygen loader extracts oxygen from water using electricity. Prepare water, FE and a gas tank; the requested oxygen gear is an equipment component rather than proof of a filled spacesuit. An actual reserve in wearable equipment is required before flight.
codex.quest.space_ground.oxygen.text.1: Supply water to the loader and wait for oxygen. Fill the tank and a compatible suit piece through the intended slots. Gas tanks can hold fluids, so inspect the content name rather than relying only on a filled bar.
codex.quest.space_ground.oxygen.text.2: Test oxygen transfer from tank to equipment on Earth and prepare spare filled tanks. Food or ordinary torches cannot replace an empty oxygen supply on the Moon. If the loader stops, inspect water, power and oxygen capacity; obtaining the block does not establish ready life support.
codex.quest.space_ground.oxygen.title: Oxygen
codex.quest.space_ground.rocket.reward.0: A second pad — so you have something to come back on
codex.quest.space_ground.rocket.text.0: The tier-one rocket is assembled at the NASA workbench and opens the Moon and orbital destinations. Prepare a nose cone, four fins, two steel tanks, a steel engine and six steel body blocks according to the installed recipe. Listed component objectives do not cover every crafting cost.
codex.quest.space_ground.rocket.text.1: Let individual component objectives register, then assemble the rocket and take it into inventory. Place a launch pad on flat open ground and put the rocket at its centre. Allow room for the body and avoid launching beneath the workshop roof.
codex.quest.space_ground.rocket.text.2: Fuel is loaded through the rocket interface; an ordinary flight needs three fuel buckets. The advancement confirms obtaining the rocket, not a successful launch. Prepare the suit, return pad and separate fuel before starting; an otherwise complete vehicle leaves an unprepared expedition dependent on chance assistance.
codex.quest.space_ground.rocket.title: Tier One Rocket
codex.quest.space_ground.steel.text.0: A rocket program needs substantial steel in several forms. Prepare sixty-four Ad Astra steel ingots and thirty-two plates for this objective. Do not turn all steel into plates: each inventory objective needs its own stock, and the rocket additionally requires steel blocks.
codex.quest.space_ground.steel.text.1: Make steel from iron and coal in the etrionic furnace’s alloying mode, then compress the allocated portion. The installed plate recipe uses one ingot per plate. Other mods’ steel compatibility follows recipe tags, but this objective names the specific Ad Astra item.
codex.quest.space_ground.steel.text.2: Separate ingot, plate and future block storage. This avoids completing an expensive engine only to find too little ordinary metal for the rocket body. The requested batch is preparation stock, not the exact full cost of an expedition including oxygen equipment, launch pads and return reserves.
codex.quest.space_ground.steel.title: Steel
codex.quest.space_ground.suit.task.4: Have all four ordinary spacesuit pieces together for the advancement
codex.quest.space_ground.suit.text.0: The Moon requires the complete ordinary Ad Astra spacesuit: helmet, chest piece, pants and boots. Craft all four and keep them together for advancement and objective detection. A partial set leaves protection incomplete even if one piece displays oxygen.
codex.quest.space_ground.suit.text.1: Fill the appropriate suit component through the oxygen loader, equip everything and inspect the displayed reserve. Also bring filled gas tanks, food and lighting that works without oxygen. Check filling before leaving the safe Earth workshop.
codex.quest.space_ground.suit.text.2: Astronaut reacts to obtaining the four inventory items rather than filling or correctly wearing them. Do not confuse the ordinary spacesuit with the heat-resistant netherite version needed on hot planets. Recheck every equipment slot before each launch after repairs, enchanting or changing everyday armour.
codex.quest.space_ground.suit.title: Space Suit
The NASA workbench assembles rockets from major components using separate layouts. Craft it and place it in a spacious workshop area near metal storage. An ordinary crafting table cannot replace this interface even with every rocket part already in your inventory.

Open the tier-one rocket recipe and inspect every position: nose cone, body materials, fins, tanks and engine. List missing parts before assembly. The same bench later handles higher tiers, but tank and engine materials must match the selected rocket.

Rocket Science detects obtaining the workbench rather than flying into space. This is not the end of ground preparation: fuel, oxygen and the suit are made separately. Leave output space and let the finished rocket register in your inventory before placing it on a launch pad.
codex.quest.space_ground.workbench.title: NASA Workbench
codex.quest.space_hot.calorite.text.0: Calorite is used in the tier-four rocket and jet suit. Search for its ore on a hot planet with a suitable tool and complete environmental protection. Register the raw form before smelting your haul; advanced components require several processing stages.
codex.quest.space_hot.calorite.text.1: Register sixteen raw material in one batch, smelt them and show sixteen ingots, then make eight plates. The Codex remembers these forms sequentially; extra metal solely to hold them together is unnecessary. Ad Astra machines use FE for smelting and pressing. At remote bases, leave adequate power for oxygen equipment.
codex.quest.space_hot.calorite.text.2: Allocate finished metal between transport and equipment according to current recipes. A calorite item in inventory provides neither flight nor heat resistance. After detection, store reserves safely and mine again only for missing components while retaining return oxygen and fuel.
codex.quest.space_hot.calorite.title: Calorite
codex.quest.space_hot.guide_jet_trial.ta: The full jet suit is filled with oxygen and charged; both flight modes tested with a safe landing
codex.quest.space_hot.guide_jet_trial.te: A jet suit combines protection and movement, but an expedition needs two independent reserves: oxygen and electrical charge. Prepare the complete set, service its oxygen with a loader and its energy with an energizer. Owning four pieces does not establish flight readiness.

Choose a spacious safe area and locate controls in the game settings. Test normal and boosted modes with small movements, then land calmly. Watch energy consumption and avoid a first trial over lava, a crater or far from backup transport.

Confirm the objective after both trials with oxygen still in reserve. Boosting helps local exploration, but the suit does not replace a rocket for travel between planets. Back at the charging stop, restore both resources separately and pack enough reserve to cover a delay during the next outing.
codex.quest.space_hot.jet.task.4: Have all four jet-suit pieces together for the advancement
codex.quest.space_hot.jet.text.0: The jet suit combines stronger space protection with electric flight. Prepare calorite and previous components according to all four piece recipes. Flight depends on energy and breathing on oxygen; one full gauge does not replace the other.
codex.quest.space_hot.jet.text.1: Craft the set, register it in inventory, fill oxygen and charge the flight component with an energizer. Equip everything and check the flight toggle. Test ordinary ascent above a level safe area first; learn boosted flight separately with enough stopping space.
codex.quest.space_hot.jet.text.2: The advancement checks obtaining the complete set rather than performing a dangerous manoeuvre. Watch energy in flight and retain a backup landing method. The jet suit does not replace a rocket for choosing another planet: it provides local mobility, while interplanetary travel still needs suitable spacecraft.
codex.quest.space_hot.jet.title: Jet Suit
codex.quest.space_hot.mercury.text.0: Mercury is another hot-tier destination accessible with a suitable rocket. Recheck the complete heat-resistant suit, oxygen, food and return kit before travelling. A successful Venus landing does not mean those resources remain sufficient for another trip.
codex.quest.space_hot.mercury.text.1: After arrival, recover lander contents and choose a safe return-launch location. Inspect surroundings and Ti-69 readings while keeping protective equipment on. A short survey with a clear route back is enough for a first expedition.
codex.quest.space_hot.mercury.text.2: The dimension objective and advancement require visiting Mercury itself, not extended residence or a special kill. Do not leave the return kit in someone else’s unloaded base. For a local power outpost, measure actual solar generation and establish life-support backup before expanding the room and mining operation.
codex.quest.space_hot.mercury.title: Mercury
codex.quest.space_hot.tier4.text.0: The tier-four rocket uses calorite and opens travel to the Proxima Centauri system. Prepare two calorite tanks, an engine and the remaining NASA workbench ingredients. Avoid spending every ingot on a jet suit if a distant expedition is your next priority.
codex.quest.space_hot.tier4.text.1: Assemble the vehicle after intermediate objectives register and inspect available destinations. Place it on a prepared pad, fuel it and separately pack the return kit. A higher tier creates no fuel and does not remove tools, food or oxygen requirements for transitional stages.
codex.quest.space_hot.tier4.text.2: The advancement triggers on obtaining the rocket; the interstellar objective requires visiting Glacio separately. Record home coordinates and ensure you can return without mining on the new planet. Make the first trip a survey, leaving large-scale relocation until local conditions are verified.
codex.quest.space_hot.tier4.title: Tier Four Rocket
codex.quest.space_hot.venus.text.0: Venus is accessible with a tier-three rocket and has a hot hazardous environment without ordinary breathing. Equip the complete netherite spacesuit, fill oxygen and pack a return pad and fuel before departure. Do not test whether ordinary armour works only after leaving the lander.
codex.quest.space_hot.venus.text.1: After landing, inspect a safe nearby area, recover transport and record return coordinates. Prepare shelter and lighting before searching for calorite. The hostile environment requires monitoring oxygen even while placing the first wall.
codex.quest.space_hot.venus.text.2: The advancement and dimension objective trigger on entering Venus, not on establishing a successful base. Return with reserves if equipment is damaged or supplies become uncertain. The planet provides specific materials; a modest collected batch with reliable return is more useful than equipment lost beside a random mine.
codex.quest.space_hot.venus.title: Planet of Storms
codex.quest.space_mars.cryo.text.0: The cryo freezer turns icy materials into more efficient rocket fuel using FE. Prepare the machine, electricity and collected ice shards. One shard produces twenty-five fluid units in the installed recipe, so one bucket requires forty shards.
codex.quest.space_mars.cryo.text.1: Feed the material and collect fluid in separate containers. Ordinary, packed and blue ice also have recipes, but their yields differ; do not treat them as equivalent to a shard. The manual recommends one bucket of cryo fuel for each flight, including the return.
codex.quest.space_mars.cryo.text.2: Obtaining the machine and bucket awards their advancements, but prepare return stock separately. Avoid placing cryo fuel in living areas: contact damages entities and it freezes nearby water. Before launch, confirm the rocket accepted the fluid and a separate reserve remains in cargo.
codex.quest.space_mars.cryo.title: Cryo Fuel
codex.quest.space_mars.energizer.text.0: The Ad Astra energizer stores energy and transfers it to compatible items. An etrionic capacitor carries FE for expedition equipment. Supply the energizer from a working source first; two empty new batteries cannot charge one another.
codex.quest.space_mars.energizer.text.1: Connect the device and wait for an internal reserve. Use a supported item on it to transfer energy, then inspect that item’s own gauge. The capacitor can distribute charge through inventory and supports sequential or round-robin distribution selected through its controls.
codex.quest.space_mars.energizer.text.2: The advancement checks obtaining the energizer rather than a full capacitor. Distinguish oxygen and electricity before flight: a charged energy item does not allow breathing without a suit. If charge fails to transfer, inspect compatibility and receiving mode before power; portable storage is useful backup, not continuous base generation.
codex.quest.space_mars.energizer.title: Energizer
codex.quest.space_mars.guide_charge_stop: A powered Energizer at the base charged an item; the base’s energy reserve was restored afterwards

A Mars base makes a useful intermediate charging stop before the hot planets. Connect an energizer to a power source and place it somewhere accessible near luggage. Charging equipment consumes electricity, so a small generator may struggle to supply all machines simultaneously.

Insert a supported rechargeable item and watch its energy indicator rise. If it remains still, check the charger’s power and item compatibility instead of adding oxygen to an electrical system. Equipment oxygen and charge use different service devices and require separate checks.

Finish the trial, allow the base’s energy reserve to recover and only then confirm the objective. This establishes that the stop actually services expeditions rather than merely containing a decorative block. As the base expands, preserve adequate power for essential consumers while charging: an empty equipment battery should not shut down the oxygen distributor.
Cryofuel supports one flight per bucket, so two buckets form a separate round-trip reserve. Produce them in the cryofreezer with electricity and suitable cold ingredients. Ice shards yield twenty-five millibuckets each; forty provide one full bucket.

Collect fuel in a closed system and label the return container. Do not pour it beside a walkway: the fluid damages entities and freezes nearby water. A cryofreezer produces fuel, but does not automatically pack expedition luggage.

Once the batch registers, divide the two buckets between departure fuelling and the return reserve. Do not apply the three-bucket ordinary-fuel rate to cryofuel or assume fuel remaining in the home machine is available on another planet. Checking stock before every departure remains necessary regardless of fuel efficiency.
codex.quest.space_mars.landing_mars.text: Travel to Mars with at least a tier-two rocket, a complete suit and oxygen reserve. Before selecting the planet, recheck return fuel, launch pad and space for mined cargo. A visible Martian sky does not imply breathable air.

After landing, recover transport and the return kit from the lander, mark the site and inspect the nearby safe area. Only then begin searching for ostrum. Prepare outpost power and oxygen independently of the first ore you discover.

The dimension objective and advancement confirm arrival rather than colony construction. Watch oxygen during exploration and return with allowance for unexpected delays. For a longer stay, establish a sealed room and water-and-power supply first, keeping the suit ready for an emergency exit.
codex.quest.space_mars.netherite_suit.ta: Have all four netherite spacesuit pieces together for the advancement
codex.quest.space_mars.netherite_suit.te: The netherite spacesuit is needed for hot planets and improves protection over the ordinary set. Prepare ostrum, netherite materials and every recipe’s other ingredients. One upgraded chest piece is not a replacement for all four required items.

Craft helmet, chest piece, pants and boots, register them together in inventory and fill the supported piece with oxygen. Equip the set and check every slot after changing armour. Keep spare tanks and the ordinary suit safely at base.

The combat-named advancement checks obtaining the complete netherite spacesuit, not killing a particular enemy. Venus and Mercury require actual protection as you leave the rocket. Recheck oxygen before interplanetary travel: heat resistance creates no breathable atmosphere and does not remove the need for return fuel.
codex.quest.space_mars.ostrum.text.0: Ostrum is the Martian metal used for stronger machines, heat-resistant suits and tier-three rockets. Search underground with a suitable pickaxe while retaining the route back to landing. Avoid spending all oxygen on one deep mine without an established base.
codex.quest.space_mars.ostrum.text.1: The quest requires sixteen raw material, sixteen ingots and eight plates. Show the Codex the raw stock, smelt it, register the ingots and only then send eight to the compressor. Different forms count sequentially; each numerical objective needs the stated batch of one item, not a sum of individual pickups.
codex.quest.space_mars.ostrum.text.2: Reserve material for protection before Venus and Mercury before spending it on optional machines. Possessing ostrum does not make an ordinary suit heat-resistant. After detection, compare future recipes and plan another excursion around missing metal rather than filling every free inventory slot.
codex.quest.space_mars.ostrum.title: Ostrum
codex.quest.space_mars.tier3.text.0: The tier-three rocket uses ostrum and opens hot planets. Prepare two ostrum tanks, an engine and the remaining body materials from the NASA workbench recipe. Register intermediate components before consuming them in the completed vehicle.
codex.quest.space_mars.tier3.text.1: After crafting, take the rocket into inventory for its advancement, place it on a tested pad and fill it. Suitable fuel and a separate return reserve remain necessary at every tier. A higher-tier rocket neither refills oxygen nor improves worn armour.
codex.quest.space_mars.tier3.text.2: Before heading to Venus or Mercury, prepare the complete netherite spacesuit and inspect its oxygen. If heat-resistant equipment is unfinished, leave the new rocket safely on Earth or Mars. Obtaining the transport tier and preparing the player for the destination are independent checks.
codex.quest.space_mars.tier3.title: Tier Three Rocket
codex.quest.space_moon.cheese.text.0: Moon cheese is an unusual Ad Astra food obtained from its lunar ore. Look for cheese ore during ordinary underground surveying rather than spending your final oxygen on an optional find. Bring a suitable tool and preserve a clear exit route.
codex.quest.space_moon.cheese.text.1: Obtain cheese through a supported method; a preserved cheese ore block can be smelted using the installed recipe. Let one cheese enter your ordinary inventory for objective and advancement detection before eating it or placing it in remote storage.
codex.quest.space_moon.cheese.text.2: The advancement checks obtaining cheese, not eating it or visiting a special village. It is a pleasant expedition extra rather than a dependable substitute for food prepared on Earth. If the find is far from a safe route, refill oxygen and return for a separate short trip.
codex.quest.space_moon.cheese.title: Cheese
codex.quest.space_moon.desh.text.0: Desh is the Moon tier’s main new metal, used in improved machines, an orbital station and the next rocket. Search underground on the Moon with a suitable pickaxe and oxygen reserve. Ice shards come from a separate ore, not arbitrary snow.
codex.quest.space_moon.desh.text.1: First register sixteen raw desh in one batch, then smelt them and show sixteen ingots. The Codex retains different item objectives sequentially, so extra mining solely to hold both forms together is unnecessary. Store shards separately for future cryofuel.
codex.quest.space_moon.desh.text.2: Smelt at a prepared safe outpost or after returning to Earth. Do not dismantle the only oxygen system to power a new furnace. Even a small desh batch is useful; secure the return route before deciding whether reserves support a longer lunar mining trip.
codex.quest.space_moon.desh.title: Desh
An oxygen distributor makes a sealed room habitable while supplied with water and FE. Build a closed room and safe entrance first. Place a pump over a prepared water source and beside the distributor as shown in the guide; both devices need power.

Seal every opening, including cable passages, and enable the distributor’s area display. Highlighting confirms the served space. Internal walls and closed doors can block oxygen spread; vents connect rooms while preserving the outer enclosure.

Keep the suit on until supply stability and room condition are checked. Breaking the sealed shell causes dangerous decompression and rapid resource use, so keep repair blocks ready. The advancement detects obtaining a distributor, not room airtightness; an installed water pump alone does not prove sufficient oxygen.
codex.quest.space_moon.distributor.title: Oxygen Distributor
codex.quest.space_moon.gadgets.task.3: Use a Zip Gun to produce an oxygen impulse
codex.quest.space_moon.gadgets.text.0: The Ti-69 reports local oxygen, temperature and gravity so you can verify conditions rather than judge a room by appearance. The zip gun spends oxygen on movement and is particularly useful in zero gravity. Prepare both devices and a separate breathing reserve that will not be used for propulsion.
codex.quest.space_moon.gadgets.text.1: Open the Ti-69 in a safe area and compare readings inside and outside base without removing the suit. Fill the zip gun with its required resource and use a short burst where stopping is safe. In orbit, momentum persists, so a long burst can carry you away from the station.
codex.quest.space_moon.gadgets.text.2: The Ti-69 advancement checks obtaining the device; the zip-gun advancement checks using it. Merely carrying the latter is insufficient. Learn short bursts near support before distant construction; convenient mobility cannot compensate for a lost station and empty oxygen tank.
codex.quest.space_moon.gadgets.title: Instruments
codex.quest.space_moon.gravity.text.0: The gravity normalizer changes movement inside a sealed area. It helps in orbital workshops or lunar rooms where unusual jumps hinder precise work. It produces no oxygen: sealing, breathing and gravity are separate conditions requiring separate checks.
codex.quest.space_moon.gravity.text.1: Install it, supply sufficient power and select a moderate gravity setting. The manual allows zero to twice Earth gravity. Begin at a familiar level and test a short jump on level flooring while keeping oxygen equipment on.
codex.quest.space_moon.gravity.text.2: Compare its consumption with generation under load: the normalizer must not deprive the oxygen distributor of power. The advancement confirms only obtaining the block. If the effect is absent, inspect the sealed served area and settings instead of increasing the value without understanding its coverage.
codex.quest.space_moon.gravity.title: Gravity Normalizer
codex.quest.space_moon.guide_airlock.tas: The airlock was tested: doors open one at a time and the living space keeps its oxygen
codex.quest.space_moon.guide_airlock.tex: A sealed room remains useful only if people can enter safely. Prepare two airlocks and connect the exterior to living space through a small intermediate chamber. A permanently open door turns a working distributor into an attempt to oxygenate the surrounding vacuum.

Place doors with room between them to stop, close the first and only then open the second. Test the route while wearing a filled spacesuit. Observe distributor readings when leaving and returning; keep protection on until the room’s behaviour is verified.

Confirm the manual objective after travelling both ways while maintaining oxygen in the living area. Possessing two items does not verify sealing. If resource consumption spikes, look for an open door or hole; a ventilation passage to the exterior also defeats the isolated room.
codex.quest.space_moon.guide_sealed_serv: The cable and fluid line pass through sealed conduits and the room keeps its oxygen

An ordinary pipe or cable inside a wall opening does not replace a solid sealing block. Cable and fluid ducts carry services through a lunar home’s shell. Prepare four cable ducts and two fluid ducts, then choose an accessible wall section for maintenance.

Move power and water passages to the appropriate ducts while keeping connections continuous on both sides. Cable ducts serve electrical lines; fluid ducts serve fluids. Keep your spacesuit on while changing the wall and allow for possible depressurization.

After closing the shell, verify that the consumer receives power, fluid actually arrives and the oxygenated zone recovers and remains stable. Only then confirm the check. A running machine alongside disappearing air can indicate a wall problem rather than a generator fault; the distributor’s area display helps distinguish them.
codex.quest.space_moon.guide_station_wal: A railed path from the arrival point was laid on the orbital station; short Zip Gun bursts were tested

Orbit lacks ordinary braking: a poor impulse can carry you away from the station. Prepare railings for a work path, oxygen reserves and an oxygen-filled Zip Gun. First identify the arrival point and a safe area for movement tests.

Build a short guarded route to luggage storage. Try small impulses close to the station and learn to cancel velocity by thrusting in the opposite direction. Do not test maximum range over the void without a return reserve; the propulsion tool consumes its oxygen supply.

The manual objective confirms an accessible path and completed handling trial. Bars help orientation and limit accidental departures, but do not form a sealed living volume. Keep your suit on and check oxygen separately: safe station geometry and a breathable atmosphere are different tasks.
codex.quest.space_moon.landing.text.0: After selecting the Moon, complete landing and remain in the fully filled spacesuit. The surface is cold and lacks breathable oxygen. Lower gravity changes jumping, so inspect the area around the lander before a long excursion.
codex.quest.space_moon.landing.text.1: Open the lander cargo through its supported interaction and recover rocket, return pad and fuel. Record landing coordinates and prepare a small shelter with suitable lighting. Ordinary torches and exposed water do not behave as they do on Earth.
codex.quest.space_moon.landing.text.2: The dimension objective and advancement trigger on entering the Moon; they do not confirm equipment safety or return readiness. Check oxygen after unloading and separate reserves from mined cargo. Desh is the next useful resource, but searching for it should not exhaust the first landing’s breathing supply.
codex.quest.space_moon.landing.title: One Small Step
codex.quest.space_moon.orbit.text.0: Earth orbit is a separate dimension accessed through the planet screen and a created space station. Its recipe requires sixty-four iron plates, thirty-two steel ingots, thirty-two desh ingots and thirty-two desh plates. Creating the station consumes these materials.
codex.quest.space_moon.orbit.text.1: Bring a complete suit, oxygen, return fuel and movement tools. Create the station through the available planet-menu recipe and select it as your destination. A rocket rising into the sky is not the same as entering the required orbital dimension.
codex.quest.space_moon.orbit.text.2: Orbit lacks familiar gravity and friction: a push preserves motion, so stay near the structure instead of accelerating into empty space. The objective confirms entering Earth orbit, not furnishing a habitable module. Prepare sealing, oxygen and a safe return route separately before expanding the station.
codex.quest.space_moon.orbit.title: Orbit
codex.quest.space_moon.rover.text.0: The rover speeds up surface travel and carries cargo but does not replace the driver’s oxygenated spacesuit. Prepare the vehicle and radio, which is also used in vehicle-related recipes. Let both items register before final installation and driving.
codex.quest.space_moon.rover.text.1: Place the rover in an open area and fill it with accepted fuel through its interface. Test boarding, movement and cargo access on a short loop near base. A second passenger seat is available, but that rider also needs environmental protection.
codex.quest.space_moon.rover.text.2: The radio plays internet streams when their source is available; silence does not indicate engine failure. These advancements check obtaining a radio and rover rather than listening or driving distance. Watch fuel and stay within an oxygen reserve that permits walking home after an unexpected breakdown.
codex.quest.space_moon.rover.title: Rover
codex.quest.space_moon.solar.text.0: Ad Astra solar output depends on world conditions, lighting and planetary position. Craft the panel, steel cables and solid cable ducts. A lunar outpost needs storage or backup generation for periods of insufficient output.
codex.quest.space_moon.solar.text.1: Place the panel in the open and connect storage, then inspect current generation in its interface. Steel cable carries FE but does not seal a wall opening. Use a solid cable duct at the oxygen-room boundary while maintaining electrical continuity.
codex.quest.space_moon.solar.text.2: The advancement is awarded for obtaining the panel, not reliably powering an entire base. Compare generation with life-support consumption under real load. Do not remove the suit simply because the sun is visible: the room must be sealed and its distributor supplied with water and energy beyond one favourable daytime reading.
codex.quest.space_moon.solar.title: Solar Panel
codex.quest.space_moon.tier2.text.0: The tier-two rocket uses desh and opens the route to Mars. Prepare desh tanks, an engine and the remaining body materials from the NASA workbench recipe. The two tanks and engine are separate intermediate objectives best registered before final assembly.
codex.quest.space_moon.tier2.text.1: Verify the tier-two recipe, craft the vehicle and take it into inventory. Fuel and the launch pad are separate preparations. The tested launch complex can be reused when the new rocket’s placement conditions are satisfied.
codex.quest.space_moon.tier2.text.2: The advancement confirms obtaining the vehicle rather than reaching Mars. Refill oxygen and retain separate return fuel instead of treating the new planet as an established filling station. Keeping the first rocket or a clear fallback route is useful until the new transport passes its own preflight check.
codex.quest.space_moon.tier2.title: Tier Two Rocket
codex.quest.start_first_day.backpack.tex: A Sophisticated Backpack adds portable storage and later accepts upgrades. Its initial job is simple: carry food, tools and discoveries without filling every slot in your main inventory.

The basic backpack uses a wooden chest, leather and string; check the arrangement in JEI. Craft it, open it through its interaction or assigned key and place a few items inside. Keep the backpack itself in the tracked inventory for this item objective.

Separate travel essentials from incidental loot so important supplies remain easy to find. A backpack does not make travel risk-free or replace reserves at home. Leave excess valuables at the base before dangerous expeditions and add upgrades when you have a specific use for them.
codex.quest.start_first_day.backpack_upg: Upgrades turn a backpack into an assistant for gathering supplies. A Pickup Upgrade routes collected items into it, while a Magnet Upgrade attracts suitable nearby dropped items. These are different stages, and filters are best configured before a large expedition.

Craft an upgrade base and pickup module first. Keep the pickup module in your inventory until its counter updates, then use it to craft the magnet. The objectives are remembered separately, so a second pickup module is unnecessary. The recipes also require redstone and the other materials shown in JEI.

After the objective registers, install the intended module in an upgrade slot and test its filter with inexpensive blocks. Useful items should enter without unwanted material filling the pack. Owning the modules is detected automatically; their configuration and operation need your own check.
codex.quest.start_first_day.base.task.0: Choose and prepare a lit base site
codex.quest.start_first_day.base.text.0: A good base site saves more effort than an extra chest of loot. Look for water, accessible wood and room to expand. Reserve space for storage, workshops and future machines with inputs, outputs and maintenance access.
codex.quest.start_first_day.base.text.1: Mark the first work area, light it and provide a protected entrance. Arrange the crafting table, furnaces, storage and resting place with clear passages. A large house is unnecessary at this stage; a useful small workshop beats empty walls surrounding cramped chests.
codex.quest.start_first_day.base.text.2: Walk from the entrance to each workstation and confirm you know where new supplies belong. Tick the manual goal after choosing and preparing the site. You can then develop mechanical, industrial or exploration branches while keeping shared reserves and a clear route home.
codex.quest.start_first_day.base.title: A Place for a Base
codex.quest.start_first_day.carry.task.0: Move a chest with Carry On and inspect its contents
codex.quest.start_first_day.carry.text.0: Carry On can move a supported container with its contents intact. It is useful when rearranging chests, avoiding the need to spill and collect every item. Not every block in the pack permits this kind of carrying.
codex.quest.start_first_day.carry.text.1: Test a plain chest containing a few inexpensive items first. Empty both hands and use the Carry action shown in your controls, normally associated with sneaking and interacting. If nothing happens, inspect its binding, your offhand and the block’s restrictions.
codex.quest.start_first_day.carry.text.2: Place the chest in a clear spot, reopen it and compare the contents before ticking the goal. Stop complex machinery and learn its dismantling rules before attempting to move it: convenient carrying does not promise to preserve every external connection.
codex.quest.start_first_day.carry.title: Carrying Things by Hand
codex.quest.start_first_day.crafting.tex: A crafting table opens recipes that do not fit the small inventory grid. Make one from planks, craft a wooden pickaxe and mine stone for a more durable tool. The goal requires both the table and a stone pickaxe.

Keep the crafted table in your inventory until its counter updates, then place it and make the pickaxe. Different item objectives are remembered separately, so an already recorded table does not need to be picked up again. Arrange storage before discarding equipment in a dangerous location merely to clear a slot.

The stone pickaxe lets you progress to iron ore. Prepare torches and food before going underground and light your work area. These first tools establish a calm workshop for learning unfamiliar recipes, rather than forcing a race into the depths.
codex.quest.start_first_day.death.task.0: Read how to recover equipment after death
codex.quest.start_first_day.death.text.0: Corpse leaves a body containing your equipment after death. It helps recover your supplies, but the return route may still contain the danger that killed you. Prepare for the recovery instead of leaving empty-handed.
codex.quest.start_first_day.death.text.1: Remember the dimension and location, using the map’s death marker where available. Take food, light, a spare tool and building blocks. At the body, open its storage and transfer the equipment, checking that your inventory has room.
codex.quest.start_first_day.death.text.2: This reference goal does not ask you to die deliberately. Read the recovery steps and keep a small spare kit at home. Corpse behaviour and persistence may depend on settings, so avoid treating a death location as permanent storage or delaying recovery unnecessarily.
codex.quest.start_first_day.death.title: Death Is Not Loss
codex.quest.start_first_day.guide_charco: You can light a workshop even without visible coal ore nearby. Smelting logs in a furnace produces charcoal, which works as fuel and a torch ingredient. Trees planted at home make the supply renewable.

Put logs in the upper furnace slot and suitable fuel below. Collect charcoal specifically; smelting planks will not produce it. Carry sixteen pieces for the objective while keeping some wood for tools and buildings.

After it registers, divide the batch between torches and the next smelting job. Plant saplings while the furnace runs. This simple cycle supplies your first light and fuel independently of whether you have found a convenient mine.
codex.quest.start_first_day.guide_labels: Label storage and check the locations of three materials

Your first store does not need to be large, but it should be understandable. Group supplies by purpose: building materials, ore and metal, food, and tools. This helps reveal shortages before you start assembling a recipe.

Place several containers with clear access, label them with signs or another available method and sort materials into your chosen groups. Keep rare components separate from bulk mining stone so they remain easy to find and are less likely to move accidentally in a bulk transfer.

Take three different items and check that you can immediately name their storage locations before ticking the goal. A storage network can replace these containers later, but distinguishing incoming materials from finished components stays useful at every scale.
codex.quest.start_first_day.guide_pack_f: Configure a backpack filter and test two materials

Automatic pickup is useful with a clear filter. Without one, a backpack quickly fills with incidental stone and leaves no space for discoveries. Test its module in a calm setting before entering a mine.

Open the installed pickup or magnet upgrade’s settings. Choose an allow or exclude mode and add two familiar materials. Test with small amounts of inexpensive items nearby, observing what enters the backpack and what stays outside.

Change one rule and repeat the test, then confirm the goal once behaviour matches the selected mode. Collect the test items from the ground. Review filters when switching tasks, such as moving from bulk mining to trophy hunting, because yesterday’s helpful rule can obstruct today’s expedition.
A backpack that collects what you need
codex.quest.start_first_day.guide_reserv: Prepare a separate reserve of food, light and tools
Working supplies disappear quietly when every new idea uses the last planks, food and fuel. Set aside a small reserve for ordinary life: mining, lighting and returning from short trips.

Place food, torches, wood and a spare tool in a separate labelled container. Establish a clear replenishment habit, such as restoring used essentials after every mining trip. Choose quantities that suit your routes instead of trying to fill a barrel for appearance alone.

Check that you can assemble a simple travel kit without dismantling the current project or emptying the furnace, then confirm the manual goal. A reserve does not forbid spending supplies; it identifies what must be restored before another expensive construction begins.
A water bucket supports crops, simple water sources and initial fluid processes. Pumps are unnecessary yet; first learn to collect a source block and choose a place where flowing water will not wash away torches or dropped supplies.
Craft a bucket from three iron ingots and fill it at a source. Carry the full bucket for the objective. Prepare a small recessed area near the workshop and inspect where water will flow when placed.

For a renewable supply, make a level two-by-two pool and place water in opposite corners. Check that a collected source restores itself. The next optional assignment uses accessible water for a small crop plot and an initial dependable food supply.
Found food gets you through the first night, but regular work needs a reserve. A small wheat plot supplies bread ingredients and seeds to continue the cycle. Place it near a lit base and accessible water.

Till soil near the source, plant wheat seeds and provide light. Wait for mature crops, harvest them and replant the emptied spaces. Avoid jumping on farmland and leave an access path so collection does not damage the plot.

The objective requires sixteen wheat items in your inventory. It does not inspect the farm, so check that the next crop is already growing. Make bread with some of the harvest and keep the rest for animals or later food recipes.
codex.quest.start_first_day.guide_worksh: Prepare supplies and an action sequence for your next project

The first conveniences matter when they work together. Before entering a major branch, run a small workshop check: recipes should be easy to find, ingredients accessible and ordinary reserves still available.

Choose the first item in your next direction and trace its recipe. Place familiar ingredients in a separate container, record missing ones and leave room for the output. If unfamiliar processes are required, open their introductory quests and make a short sequence of actions.

Confirm the goal after preparing that plan and workspace. You do not need to finish a complicated machine for this manual objective. Your next project now begins with a clear action while the base retains dependable light, food, storage and reserves.
A workshop ready for the next step
codex.quest.start_first_day.iron.text.0: Iron connects your first tools to a workshop capable of further progress. Buckets, equipment, storage and many modded components need it. Gather thirty-two ingots without spending the entire reserve on the first interesting recipe.
codex.quest.start_first_day.iron.text.1: Mine iron ore with a suitable pickaxe and smelt raw iron in a fuelled furnace. Maintain light and a way back from the mine. The objective needs all ingots in your inventory together; iron blocks and unsmelted ore do not substitute for them.
codex.quest.start_first_day.iron.text.2: Once it registers, divide the supply between tools, fluid handling and initial machinery. Industrial processing can improve metal yields later. For now, a simple repeatable mining and smelting cycle is more useful than waiting for an ideal factory without working tools.
codex.quest.start_first_day.iron.title: Iron Age
codex.quest.start_first_day.jade.task.0: Identify a block and its mod using Jade
codex.quest.start_first_day.jade.text.0: Jade displays information about the block or creature under your crosshair. Its name and source mod identify what you are looking at, while extra lines often reveal machine state, contents or stored energy.
codex.quest.start_first_day.jade.text.1: Point at a plain chest and then a familiar machine, comparing their tooltips. If the display is hidden, find Jade’s settings or key binding. Some details only exist for supported blocks; a missing line does not prove a feature is absent.
codex.quest.start_first_day.jade.text.2: Tick the manual goal once you can identify at least one block and its mod. Use Jade for an initial inspection when something fails, then open the machine and examine its power, inputs and outputs. The tooltip assists diagnosis without replacing a guide.
codex.quest.start_first_day.jade.title: What Is This Block
codex.quest.start_first_day.map.task.0: Mark home on the map and return using the waypoint
codex.quest.start_first_day.map.text.0: Xaero’s map records explored terrain and helps you return to useful places. Start with one important marker: home. A correct waypoint saves you from guessing which of several similar hills hides your storage.
