codex.quest.start_first_day.map.text.1: Find the full-map action in Xaero’s control settings and open it. Create a waypoint at your base, check its coordinates and dimension and give it a recognisable name. Rebind a conflicting key instead of relying on whichever mod happens to open first.
codex.quest.start_first_day.map.text.2: Walk a short distance away and return using the marker before confirming the manual goal. The map shows known terrain rather than guaranteeing a safe passage. A direct heading may cross a ravine, water or a dangerous structure, so also mark convenient approaches.
codex.quest.start_first_day.map.title: World Map
codex.quest.start_first_day.night.text.0: A Comforts sleeping bag lets you rest on a journey while preserving the respawn point at your home bed. It is useful for exploration, but does not protect you from nearby enemies or replace a safe resting spot.
codex.quest.start_first_day.night.text.1: Craft the red sleeping bag from three red wool blocks using its JEI recipe. This goal specifically checks the red variant. Other colours work in the game but do not advance this counter. Carry the crafted item in your inventory.
codex.quest.start_first_day.night.text.2: Choose a flat, protected site and try the bag when sleeping is allowed. If sleep is unavailable, check your surroundings and the server’s rules. Keep a normal bed at home as well: portable rest and a permanent place to respawn serve different purposes.
codex.quest.start_first_day.night.title: Surviving the Night
codex.quest.start_first_day.waystone.tex: A Waystones waystone establishes a permanent fast-travel destination. At home it becomes especially useful once you activate a second stop. Discovered stones can be used without crafting your own, but this inventory objective requires a waystone item.

The recipe uses stone bricks, obsidian and a Warp Stone. The latter needs amethyst shards, ender pearls and an emerald; gather them and inspect the arrangement in JEI. It is reasonable to postpone this step until you have made a few prepared expeditions.

After it registers, place the stone safely, activate it and give it a clear name. Visit another stone to add a travel destination. Read displayed costs and restrictions before using the connection, since settings may require experience. A home marker on the map remains useful.
codex.quest.start_first_day.wood.text.0: Wood is your first supply for tools, light and storage. Find an oak tree and gather sixteen oak logs. This objective checks oak specifically, so unusual modded wood will not replace it in the counter even when ordinary recipes accept that wood.
codex.quest.start_first_day.wood.text.1: Keep the logs in your inventory until the objective registers. Turning all of them into planks immediately removes the required stock. Later, use some for a crafting table and sticks, while reserving some for charcoal and further recipes.
codex.quest.start_first_day.wood.text.2: Collect fallen saplings and plant several near your future base with room to grow. The next wood supply will then be close to your workshop. This step’s reward helps with initial provisions, but you will still need a dependable food source.
codex.quest.start_first_day.wood.title: The First Tree
codex.quest.start_qol.almanac.task.0: Choose your next gameplay branch and inspect its first recipe
codex.quest.start_qol.almanac.text.0: The installed mod list is longer than the list of independent activities in the world. Some components support other systems: Almanac is a library, while Sable supports moving structures’ physics. You do not need a separate crafting chain for every listed name.
codex.quest.start_qol.almanac.text.1: Choose your next step by its gameplay result: process ore, build transport or organise storage. Find the corresponding Codex branch and read its beginning. Then inspect the recipe for the first required item and compare it with your available resources.
codex.quest.start_qol.almanac.text.2: Tick the goal once you have chosen a clear direction. Supporting components work alongside gameplay mods and need not be changed merely to shorten the mod list. Understanding a tool and its purpose is more useful than turning every installed entry into a mandatory progression stage.
codex.quest.start_qol.almanac.title: Choosing your next path
A chunk loader keeps selected areas active while you are far away. It supports machinery that needs to continue processing and receiving supplies. It does not itself provide energy, ingredients or output space.

Craft a Basic Chunk Loader from its recipe, then place it near a small working installation after the inventory goal registers. Inspect its chunk selection interface and enable the required areas. Include the machine’s power source, input reserves and output storage.

Leave the ordinary simulation area, wait a reasonable time and return to inspect production. Avoid loading the entire base immediately, since active areas use server resources. Limits and behaviour while players are offline depend on settings; simply owning the block cannot promise indefinite unattended operation.
codex.quest.start_qol.chunkloaders.title: Chunk Loaders
codex.quest.start_qol.easyvillagers.text: The Easy Villagers Trader provides a compact place to trade with a villager. An empty block does not contain a merchant: you need a suitable villager and the workstation associated with the desired profession.

Craft the Trader using JEI. Find Easy Villagers’ Pick Up action in your controls and use it to carry a suitable villager. Place the trading block and insert the villager and workstation through its interface. For your first trial, choose an adult whose profession has not been locked through trading.

Inspect the offers before making a first trade. Trading locks the profession and offers under normal villager rules. This inventory goal checks the Trader item, so complete it before placement and then verify the trading station’s operation separately.
codex.quest.start_qol.gadgets.text.0: The Building Gadget from Building Gadgets 2 repeats construction shapes such as rows, walls and surfaces. It is useful when you already understand your building’s form and want to place repeated blocks faster.
codex.quest.start_qol.gadgets.text.1: Craft it using the recipe with iron, redstone, diamonds and lapis. Charge it with compatible FE power and prepare building materials. Use the assigned Switch Modes action to choose a simple mode with a small range, then inspect the placement preview.
codex.quest.start_qol.gadgets.text.2: Test on a clear site with inexpensive blocks. Verify direction and material before confirming a large operation. The item goal records ownership of the gadget rather than a completed building. Undo is useful, but a careful small trial is still the best first step.
codex.quest.start_qol.gadgets.title: Building Gadgets 2
codex.quest.start_qol.guide_recipe_batch: Calculate and craft a small recipe batch
After tracing a recipe, test your calculation with a small batch. Choose a simple component you actually intend to use several times. Accurate accounting matters here more than production scale.

Inspect output per operation and calculate materials for two or three operations. Set those supplies aside, craft the batch and compare the result with your prediction. Account for returned containers and tools when the selected recipe uses them.

Tick the manual objective once the calculation matches the result. If something was missing, identify the overlooked stage instead of bringing another stack of everything. The same skill later helps plan ingredient supply and explain why one machine keeps waiting for another.
codex.quest.start_qol.guide_recipe_chain: Trace one recipe chain back to familiar raw materials

A complicated item often needs components that must also be crafted. Looking only at the final recipe can hide a required machine, processed material or intermediate fluid. Trace one modest production chain beforehand.

Choose an accessible item from a branch that interests you and open its JEI recipe. Inspect each unfamiliar ingredient’s recipe until you reach materials you know how to obtain. Record intermediate stages and equipment, distinguishing table crafting from machine processing.

Confirm the goal once you can explain the route from raw material to result. Watch recipe output counts: one operation may produce several components, so ingredients need not be multiplied separately for each. This helps plan machinery without collecting unrelated supplies.
Trace a recipe to its ingredients
Test sorting or transferring matching items
Inventory QoL adds shortcuts for sorting and transferring contents. You can move everything or only matching items, which is especially useful once home storage is organised by purpose and contains sample materials.

Find Inventory QoL in the controls and inspect the bindings for Take Matching, Deposit Matching and Smart Sort. Test your chosen action with two kinds of inexpensive blocks in a chest. Check both the slot arrangement and the stacks transferred between containers.

Confirm the goal once the result is clear. Bulk transfers can include more supplies than intended, so keep materials for your current recipe separate when necessary. Sorting orders items without deciding which storage chest should contain each resource.
codex.quest.start_qol.inventoryqol.title: Inventory QoL
codex.quest.start_qol.jei.task.0: Open a JEI recipe and identify its required equipment
codex.quest.start_qol.jei.text.0: JEI is an item and recipe reference beside your inventory. It explains both how an item is made and where it is used. This matters for unfamiliar components, which may require a machine rather than a crafting table.
codex.quest.start_qol.jei.text.1: Open your inventory, search for an item and inspect its recipe. Read the processing category, ingredients and output, then view the uses of one ingredient. If there are multiple pages or alternatives, inspect them before choosing a production route.
codex.quest.start_qol.jei.text.2: Confirm the goal once you can name the equipment the recipe needs. Viewing it does not create the item or power the machine. Item icons in the Codex also open recipes with a left click and uses with a right click.
codex.quest.start_qol.jei.title: JEI
codex.quest.start_qol.keyconflict.task.0: Inspect and configure one conflicting key binding
codex.quest.start_qol.keyconflict.text.0: A large pack often assigns multiple actions to the same key. A screen may then fail to open as expected or another action may trigger with it. Learn your controls before handling complicated machinery or entering a dangerous fight.
codex.quest.start_qol.keyconflict.text.1: Open key settings and find frequent actions for the Codex, map, backpack and tool menus. Key Conflict Wheel helps choose between conflicting bindings where supported. A dedicated free key is still convenient for an action you use every day.
codex.quest.start_qol.keyconflict.text.2: Change one conflicting binding and test it in the appropriate gameplay context before ticking the objective. Guides often quote default keys; after rebinding them, follow the action’s name in your own settings instead of relying on the printed letter.
codex.quest.start_qol.keyconflict.title: Key Conflict Wheel
codex.quest.start_qol.lootr.task.0: Read how Lootr’s personal loot works
codex.quest.start_qol.lootr.text.0: Lootr containers provide loot tracked separately for each player. In multiplayer, a chest opened by a friend does not necessarily mean your reward has been taken. Ordinary storage chests at home remain shared containers.
codex.quest.start_qol.lootr.text.1: When exploring a structure, secure the approach, identify the container through its tooltip and open it. Collect your loot with enough inventory space available. Avoid breaking the container as a test, since other players may still need access to their own contents.
codex.quest.start_qol.lootr.text.2: You may mark this reference after reading; it does not require a dangerous expedition. Distinguish personal loot from shared storage when you encounter Lootr later. Do not assume supplies refresh indefinitely, since refresh behaviour depends on pack or server rules.
codex.quest.start_qol.lootr.title: Lootr
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.task.0: Test mouse gestures for moving items in a plain chest
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.text.0: Mouse Tweaks speeds up movement between inventory slots. Dragging and the scroll wheel can replace many individual clicks in supported interfaces. First learn what a gesture actually does in the container you are using.
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.text.1: Place inexpensive blocks in an ordinary chest. Try dragging transfers and distributing items between slots, then inspect how the wheel acts over a stack. Enabled gestures depend on the mod’s settings, and unusual machine screens may handle the mouse differently.
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.text.2: Compare the chest and inventory before confirming the manual objective. A learned gesture should make supplies easier to manage rather than leave you guessing where a stack went. Inspect the result especially carefully in filters, upgrade slots and automated installations.
codex.quest.start_qol.mousetweaks.title: Mouse Tweaks
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.task.0: Identify slowdown conditions and test one setting
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.0: Smooth gameplay depends on more than one setting. A long render distance increases rendering work, active machinery needs computation and exploring new terrain adds chunk generation. First identify which activity produces the slowdown.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.1: Compare standing at your base with travelling into unexplored terrain. Change one setting at a time, such as distance, expensive effects or distant landscape options. Compare similar conditions so a coincidentally quiet moment does not look like a successful fix.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.text.2: Mark the goal after reading and performing one deliberate check. Avoid disabling unfamiliar mods during a playthrough as an experiment, since some support gameplay systems. For a factory-specific slowdown, inspect accumulated dropped items, stalled transport and the size of constantly loaded areas first.
codex.quest.start_qol.performance.title: Performance
Check that working supplies are stored in containers
Smart Item Deleter monitors dropped items and cleans them up according to the pack’s rules. The floor is therefore not reliable storage: even a neatly gathered pile remains a collection of item entities outside a container.

Move supplies into chests, barrels or other storage after gathering them. Give automated lines an output destination and spare capacity so an overflowing exit does not continually spill items onto the ground. If a pile grows beside a machine, fix transport and storage rather than merely collecting the overflow.

Mark this reference after reading and inspecting your work area. Do not test cleanup by dropping valuables and waiting for deletion. Exact timing and exceptions depend on settings; the useful rule is to place supplies in their intended storage.
codex.quest.start_qol.smartdeleter.title: Smart Item Deleter
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.task.0: Test tree felling and inspect the active TreeChop mode
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.0: TreeChop changes woodcutting: repeated chops can prepare an entire tree to fall. The work required depends on the tree and settings, so do not expect every enormous trunk to disappear after one swing.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.1: Find an ordinary tree away from buildings and prepare an axe. Inspect TreeChop’s chopping, felling and sneak behaviour settings. Start chopping while watching its indicator and tool durability; switch modes when you need to break an individual block normally.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.text.2: Collect the wood and inspect what remains before ticking the objective. Understanding the active mode matters especially near wooden buildings: convenient felling does not replace careful block selection. Replant saplings so your next supply grows nearby.
codex.quest.start_qol.treechop2.title: TreeChop
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.task.0: Inspect voice chat settings and microphone muting
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.0: Simple Voice Chat supports spoken conversation when configured and available on the server. It is useful during shared construction: a partner can explain a block placement while you look at the structure instead of typing into chat.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.1: Find the voice menu in your controls, select input and output devices and inspect volume. Configure push-to-talk or your chosen transmission mode. A client mod alone does not guarantee the server’s voice service is running when the connection is unavailable.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.text.2: This reference goal only asks you to inspect the menu and learn how to mute your microphone. Another player and actual voice transmission are unnecessary. Before a shared session, test audibility and the selected channel with the participants.
codex.quest.start_qol.voicechat.title: Voice Chat
Backpack modules perform specific operations within portable storage. Automatic smelting processes suitable items with fuel, a crafting module provides a workbench, and compacting converts resources into supported compressed forms. Prepare the three upgrades and a backpack with free module slots.

Install them one at a time and test small supplies. Configure smelting input and fuel, then inspect the product. For compacting, review supported recipe sizes and filters so materials needed as individual units are not transformed.

A crafting module does not mean universal automatic crafting across the backpack. Each upgrade has distinct compatibility and behavior. Close and reopen the pack after configuring it to verify stock and modes. Carry fuel and leave output space on long expeditions, or portable processing will stop when storage fills.
codex.quest.storage_local.backpack_filte: A filter upgrade controls items piped into or out of a backpack. A void module deletes selected items, while a deposit upgrade unloads into a targeted inventory. Prepare all three, but initially install only filtering and deposit.
Test permitted inputs and outputs with an inexpensive mixture. To deposit, sneak-interact with the chosen chest and compare both inventories. Avoid sending working tools out with ore.

Configure voiding last and only for a narrowly selected unwanted material. Remove valuables from the test backpack before activation because deletion is irreversible. A logistics filter does not necessarily replace automatic-pickup settings in other modules. Check each route separately, particularly before connecting the backpack to pipes or machine storage.
codex.quest.storage_local.backpack_tiers: A backpack tier upgrade adds room for items and upgrade modules. This objective needs iron and gold variants, which can be registered sequentially: obtain and register iron first, then use the same backpack in the next upgrade recipe.

Inspect contents and installed modules before crafting. The intended upgrade recipe preserves backpack data, but test first with a small inexpensive load and compare afterward. Upgrading an existing backpack is different from crafting another empty one.

Check available slots and active-module settings afterward. More capacity does not remove pickup filters or individual upgrade limits. You need not carry two separate backpacks solely for these objectives; the registered iron tier remains recorded. Choose the final tier according to normal expedition cargo and material costs.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.0: A Mekanism bin stores a large quantity of one item type. It suits cobblestone, timber or other bulk materials that overflow ordinary chests. Prepare a basic bin and a small uniform batch for configuration.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.1: Place it, insert the chosen material and test manual extraction. Configure retention of its assigned type if an empty bin should not accept an accidental different item. Check its interface and hints for the exact locking action and capacity.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.text.2: Do not treat one bin as mixed storage for every ore; its benefit comes from one resource type. Filter automatic input and plan behavior when full. Tier upgrades change capacity without replacing resource assignment. Connect it to external networks only after testing, retaining a visible label and extraction access.
codex.quest.storage_local.bins.title: Mekanism Bins
codex.quest.storage_local.everlasting.te: An everlasting upgrade protects the backpack item against destruction and disappearance, including ordinary despawning and void loss under the module’s rules. Prepare the upgrade and a suitable backpack with a free slot. It does not make the wearer invulnerable.

Install the module and verify its active presence in the backpack interface. Compare the tooltip with the expected protection. Do not begin by deliberately throwing your only valuable backpack into lava or the void; recovering it remains a separate practical problem.

The upgrade does not grant access to a loss location or automatically send the pack into a safe chest. Death coordinates, spare equipment and room for recovered cargo remain useful. The item objective confirms crafting; protection applies to the equipped backpack module, not every nearby container.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_bin_assi: Manually verify an emptied configured bin rejects another resource and accepts its assigned material again

An empty buffer can accidentally accept another resource and disrupt an established feed. Prepare a bin assigned to a bulk material and a small supply of a different item. Use the storage’s available assignment-retention setting.
Fill with the first resource, lock its assignment and empty it. Try inserting the second resource, then the first again. Confirm that the assignment survives emptying and correct input resumes.

Confirm manually after both trials. If the other resource enters, fix locking or add a precise external filter before connecting the shared line. Achieve the actual result in the installed version rather than merely seeing a lock icon. This prevents accidental reassignment beside cobblestone generation and autocrafting material stores.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_bulk_net: Manually verify grid insertion fills the chosen external buffer, extraction returns resources, and full-buffer behavior is tested

Bulk resources can stay in a dedicated buffer while disks serve mixed loot. Prepare an assigned bin or Create vault, a Refined Storage external-storage device and a small known resource batch. Do not migrate the whole warehouse immediately.

Connect the buffer and set its intended priority and precise filter. Insert material through the grid and check that the external buffer grows rather than another disk. Extract some and compare the remainder.

Confirm manually after verifying both directions. Decide beforehand whether a full external buffer should overflow into other storage or stop input, then test those settings cheaply. This connection combines local storage benefits with shared search, but needs understandable priorities rather than merely neighboring blocks.
Keep Bulk Stock in External Storage
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_deposit_: Manually verify selected loot deposits, the tool stays, and a full chest causes no item loss

Returning from a mine is easier when the backpack unloads loot while retaining the next trip’s equipment. Prepare a deposit upgrade, empty chest and training set of stone, ore and one cheap tool. Disable any void module during testing.

Configure the deposit filter for resources permitted to leave, then sneak-interact with the chest. Compare both sides: loot should reach the receiver while the tool remains available. Repeat with a full receiver and verify that items are retained.

Confirm manually after correct selection and a safe stop. If the tool leaves, fix the deposit filter rather than relying on another upgrade’s settings. This route separates personal equipment from shared stock and reduces the chance of beginning the next expedition without a pickaxe.
codex.quest.storage_local.guide_void_fil: Manually delete only the selected cheap material, retain the control and verify deletion stops when disabled

A void upgrade is useful only when the unwanted resource is precisely known. Empty valuables from a training backpack and insert two different cheap materials. Designate one as trash and keep the other as a control.

Create a narrow deletion filter for the first material only and enable the module. Verify selected items disappear while controls remain. Disable it and confirm that newly added stock of the selected material is no longer deleted.

Confirm manually after both states. Deleted items do not return when disabled, so the trial must contain nothing valuable. Avoid broad rules such as an entire mod when only one stone type is unwanted. Retest after adding modules, since automatic pickup may introduce items previously absent from the backpack.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.0: MineColonies racks serve storage and colony warehouse operations. Prepare one and learn its local-container behavior first. An external network adapter is not automatically a replacement for couriers and colonist supply requirements.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.1: Place the rack and test inserting and removing a small batch. If part of an active colony warehouse, preserve worker access and follow that building’s rules. For Refined Storage integration, separately check whether the installed rack exposes a compatible inventory.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.text.2: Test reading and extraction with inexpensive materials rather than draining all resident supplies. Seeing an item in a grid does not mean the colony no longer needs it. Separate personal resources from working stocks with clear containers. The objective checks a rack item, not successful integration of both supply systems.
codex.quest.storage_local.rack.title: Colony Racks
codex.quest.storage_local.vault_create.t: A Create item vault provides a large production buffer before a digital network exists. Prepare eight blocks and funnels or another insertion and extraction method. Its contents cannot be opened like an ordinary chest, so provide output immediately.

Build a valid shape, verify formation and insert a small known batch through logistics. Extract it into an accessible chest afterward. An arbitrary group of touching blocks does not necessarily form one inventory.

Later, Refined Storage external storage can expose the compatible vault to the network. Items remain in the original buffer. Watch filters and priority so unintended mixed stock does not occupy all capacity. Verify retention and return of the sample before automation; eight crafted blocks alone do not prove a working warehouse.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.task.0: Grow the colony population to 50 citizens
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.0: Fifty citizens require stronger supply than a few additional houses. Prepare a mystical site and grow population with housing, research and current colony limits in mind. This structure belongs to the town project but does not create fifty citizens by itself or remove other growth conditions.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.1: Expand residences as food, workplaces and deliveries become ready. Inspect unemployment, unresolved requests and distances between districts. If population hits a cap, find its relevant development requirement in colony interfaces instead of ordering endless identical houses in hopes of bypassing it.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.text.2: Wait for your personal 50-population advancement and register the mystical-site block before construction. The ordinary item objective does not consume it. Afterwards, assess food reserves for the next building cycle: the final town hall takes time and materials while existing citizens continue consuming supplies daily.
codex.quest.story_colony.fifty.title: Fifty
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.0: The first colony section connects a town hall, builder and residence into a working order. Prepare these three MineColonies hut blocks and the building tool. A hut item designates a workplace but does not replace the completed structure, which an assigned builder must construct from requested materials.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.1: Place the town hall and establish territory, then choose builder and residence schematics that suit the terrain. Request construction, supply tools and watch requests. Do not place neighbouring projects tightly without previewing their full dimensions: future buildings can overlap even when hut blocks are well apart.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.text.2: The book remembers each block shown before installation, so demolishing an emerging settlement is unnecessary. Finish initial requests and check worker assignments. The old card title is not an exact population counter: its actual objective is the building kit from which a managed colony begins.
codex.quest.story_colony.found.title: Establish a Settlement
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.task.1: Form a colony army of eight soldiers
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.0: The garrison turns initial guard posts into an organised military force. Prepare a barracks and develop military workplaces until eight soldiers are assigned. The advancement counts army size; neither a raid nor defeating a particular enemy is required.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.1: Place the barracks with room for associated military structures in the chosen schematic, request construction and arrange assignments. Check weapons, armour, food and road access for every unit. Citizens working other jobs do not become soldiers because an attractive military building appears nearby.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.text.2: Install the barracks after its item registers. Wait for your personal MineColonies eight-soldier advancement, then inspect routes to vulnerable settlement entrances. The book evaluates neither tactics nor guaranteed raid defence: the numerical milestone is a reason to inspect functioning protection.
codex.quest.story_colony.garrison.title: Garrison
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.0: The first defenders should cover real approaches to the colony. Prepare two guard towers and a guard rally banner. Choose positions from which assigned soldiers can reach roads and homes rather than becoming trapped behind their own wall without stairs.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.1: Request tower construction, assign guards and provide suitable weapons, armour and food through available supply. Inspect movement routes on an ordinary day. The banner controls guard gathering, but merely carrying it does not create an army or fill empty workplaces.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.text.2: Show both tower blocks together before placing them; the banner may register later. Nothing is submitted. Check both posts are ready before night or a raid, then expand defence according to settlement size: two working towers cannot guarantee protection for every distant warehouse or farm.
codex.quest.story_colony.guard.title: First Night Under Guard
codex.quest.story_colony.guide_food_chai: The dining hall cooks from colony produce and the warehouse keeps a food reserve

The book took the bread from the previous quest, yet citizens keep eating every day. As long as you carry the food, the colony depends on your trips. Three buildings settle the matter: the farm grows wheat and vegetables, the fisher's hut brings fish, and the bakery bakes bread from the farm's grain. All three huts are made as ordinary colony blocks through the build tool and need no research.

The farm needs fields that you place nearby and assign to the farmer; the fisher needs water close to the hut. The baker takes wheat from the warehouse, so the chain starts working only after the courier begins carrying the harvest. The cook in the dining hall prepares raw produce and hands meals to hungry citizens.

The huts can be placed right after registration. The objective is the moment the cook works with what the colony grew while the warehouse holds a reserve rather than the last loaf. If citizens complain of hunger with a full warehouse, check that the dining hall is built and has a worker assigned.
A guard trained at a training ground has been assigned to a post

Barracks give numbers, not skill. The archery range and the combat academy teach citizens shooting and melee so that posts are taken by more than recruits. Both buildings are locked behind research: in the university's combat branch, after Tactic Training come Improved Bows for the archery and Improved Swords for the academy. Each requires a level-three barracks and six iron blocks.

Order the research early: the university works slowly, and the barracks must reach level three in time. Then place both buildings through the build tool and assign trainees. Training runs during working hours, and a trained citizen is afterwards moved to guard duty on a tower or in the barracks.

The huts can be placed right after the book registers them. The objective is a trained guard standing at a post. If a building does not appear in the list, check that the research is finished, not merely paid for.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.0: The industrial district adds a smeltery, blacksmith and mechanic workshop. Prepare their hut blocks, then decide which actual colony requests each will serve. Three neighbouring buildings do not automatically form a chain: every worker needs inputs, tools and suitable recipes.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.1: Build and start the sections sequentially. Supply smeltery processes with appropriate materials, teach the blacksmith required item recipes and give the mechanic orders valid for that profession. Inspect each building’s interface because a colony worker cannot perform every other mod’s recipe merely because of a job title.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.text.2: Install huts immediately after inventory registration. For your own check, follow one request from its creation to finished-item delivery through the warehouse. If work stalls, identify the missing resource or recipe: a second identical workshop does not fix knowledge missing from the first.
codex.quest.story_colony.industry.title: Smithy and Mechanic
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.0: Shared access to warehouse supplies is useful when it does not disrupt colony couriers. Prepare two Refined Storage external storages and a grid; a controller, power and connections are additional requirements. Connecting to an accessible inventory does not guarantee visibility of the entire warehouse at once.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.1: Connect one suitable warehouse inventory first and verify several known items in the grid. Configure external-storage modes and priorities to avoid endlessly returning items between import and export. Add the second connection after testing the first, avoiding duplicate access to the same contents.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.text.2: Show both external storages together; the grid may register separately before placement. The book does not verify warehouse integration. Follow a real courier delivery afterwards: searchable materials are useful only if the colony still receives its own building supplies and food.
codex.quest.story_colony.network.title: Warehouse on the Network
codex.quest.story_colony.population.task: Grow the colony population to 25 citizens
codex.quest.story_colony.population.text: The twenty-five-citizen milestone checks actual MineColonies growth rather than stored residence blocks. Increase housing capacity while maintaining food and conditions for further settlement. Also prepare a hospital so population expansion includes treatment capacity rather than only new work orders.

Request upgrades gradually and watch colony limits, research and citizen requests. Construct the hospital and support its operation according to current staff requirements. A hospital hut in inventory satisfies the item point but does not treat illness or shorten a queue for a missing doctor.

Your character must register the advancement for at least 25 citizens. Install the hospital block after registration without a spare copy. Once both points are complete, assess warehouse and food demand: population growth opens education and industry while also increasing everyday consumption.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.0: The education district separates learning and research between a library, school and university. Prepare all three hut types. They are not interchangeable decorations: the university unlocks research, while educational workplaces develop citizens under their own rules and available assignments.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.1: Construct the buildings, inspect their interfaces and provide requested supplies. At the university, choose research that addresses a current colony constraint, checking building-level and resource requirements first. Connect school and library operation to actual training needs instead of expecting every skill to appear when a block is placed.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.text.2: The book tracks each item separately, so construction can proceed in stages. This objective does not measure completed research. Check the first available research process and educational worker assignments; these establish a clear foundation for town growth and a more demanding industrial district.
codex.quest.story_colony.science.title: University
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.0: The supply chain lets builders and other workers receive materials without constant personal deliveries. Prepare warehouse, courier and restaurant huts, plus 64 bread for a separate delivery. A restaurant block cannot feed citizens until its building is constructed and its kitchen supplied.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.1: Request the buildings, assign workers and load available materials into the warehouse. Inspect actual courier and cook requests, including tools, ingredients and accessible routes. Follow one delivery to a construction site and one available meal before treating settlement-wide supply as established.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.text.2: Huts may be installed after book registration. The entire bread stack, however, must be in inventory at submission and is consumed by the book rather than sent to the restaurant. Keep colony meals separate: the reward does not replace everyday food or current building materials.
codex.quest.story_colony.supply.title: Warehouse and Bread
codex.quest.story_colony.technopolis.tas: Complete construction of a level-five town hall
codex.quest.story_colony.technopolis.tex: Technopolis completes the urban route with a level-five town hall and a delivery of eight Mekanism ultimate control circuits. These verify different developments: completed MineColonies construction and advanced-electronics reserves. A town-hall block in a bag does not replace its finished upgrade.

Request available town-hall upgrades in order, supplying the builder with tools and the complete material list. Ensure couriers do not drain food production’s final operating resources for construction. Prepare electronics from a steady factory surplus rather than dismantling controls from active installations.

Once construction finishes, your personal level-five town-hall advancement should appear. All eight circuits must be present now at submission and are consumed. The final mark does not end city needs: inspect food, defence and storage after the large build so the technopolis continues its ordinary working cycle.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.0: Wood and stone give the colony its own construction-material foundation. Prepare forester, sawmill, miner and stonemason huts. These are four distinct jobs: gathering citizens supply raw materials, while producers process them through learned recipes and actual requests rather than creating resources from nothing.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.1: Construct accessible workplaces and give each assigned citizen tools appropriate to their level. Foresters need trees, miners need room to develop a mine, and processors need inputs and known recipes. Follow warehouse delivery before opening many building requests simultaneously.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.text.2: Register and place each hut separately; spare huts are unnecessary for the book. Owning four blocks does not prove production of planks or stone products. Follow at least one builder request through to a finished material: this connection matters more than a row of decorative industrial buildings.
codex.quest.story_colony.wood.title: Forest and Stone
codex.quest.story_current.alternator.tex: The Create Crafts & Additions alternator lets existing mechanical power supply electrical machines. Prepare two alternators and a rolling mill. This is another generation branch after steel: IE dynamos are not a prerequisite, but a working Create rotation source is.

Connect the first alternator to a shaft and inspect source stress capacity before adding the second. Route electrical output through suitable connections into storage or a consumer. The rolling mill produces wire and other addon parts; include its rotational demand in the shared load.

Show both alternators together, then install them; the mill may register separately. The book does not measure energy production, so check that power reaches the recipient. If rotation stops, fix source overload; if shafts rotate without energy transfer, inspect electrical connections and side modes.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.0: Coke connects your first blast furnace to a steady fuel supply. Set aside 64 Immersive Engineering coal coke to begin the electrical story. This delivery concerns finished fuel reserves; it does not prove continuous coke-oven operation or a correctly built nearby blast furnace.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.1: Load coal into an assembled coke oven and follow both outputs: solid coke and liquid creosote. Empty its internal tank so fluid accumulation does not stop another batch. Reserve fuel for your own steelmaking first, then collect a separate stack for the book.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.text.2: All 64 pieces must be in inventory at submission and are consumed. Minecraft coal does not replace coke even if other devices accept it as fuel. Afterwards, check remaining coal and creosote capacity: the next stage uses two independent metallurgical chains.
codex.quest.story_current.coke.title: Smoke Over the Coke Oven
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.task.7: Form the diesel generator and verify energy transfer into storage
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.0: The diesel branch supports the grid with stockpiled liquid fuel. An IE generator is built from multiblock materials: there is no ordinary survival item representing the complete machine. Prepare the listed components and separately sixteen biodiesel buckets without draining the base’s only operating reserve.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.1: Build the generator from the Engineer’s Manual and form it with a hammer. Squeezer oil and fermenter ethanol become biodiesel in a refinery using saltpeter catalyst. Supply fuel and connect electrical output to storage with spare capacity; merely having a tank does not establish consumption.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.text.2: Show construction materials before building, but all sixteen filled buckets must be present together at submission and are consumed, containers included. Confirm manually after actual generation increases the recipient’s energy reserve. If the engine remains idle, check fuel, output and control before rebuilding its structure.
codex.quest.story_current.diesel.title: Diesel
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.0: An Immersive Engineering kinetic dynamo converts rotation from that mod’s water wheel or windmill into electrical energy. Prepare a dynamo, LV capacitor and four LV connectors. A Create wheel is not automatically a compatible drive merely because it looks similar.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.1: Build the chosen IE drive on the dynamo’s working side and check its rotation conditions. Feed energy through suitable LV connections into the capacitor, configuring its input and output faces with the engineer’s hammer. Connect one clear consumer initially so energy direction is easy to observe.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.text.2: Install components after registration and show the four connectors together. Verify the capacitor’s stored energy rises: a dynamo checkmark is not a generation measurement. Route wires away from walkways and safely insulate accessible sections before extending the grid across the yard.
codex.quest.story_current.dynamo.title: First Current
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.0: A fission reactor needs complete cooling and waste systems before the first fuel load. A logic adapter, four turbine rotors and four spare fuel assemblies are only part of the project. These items do not let the book verify reactor structure, turbine efficiency or safe burn rate.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.1: First assemble and check the reactor, cooling circuit, steam route and coolant return, then arrange radioactive-waste removal. Configure emergency shutdown and start at a minimal safe rate. Watch temperature and damage; complete protection is needed for radioactive work, and occupied pipes or containers must not be dismantled casually.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.text.2: The adapter and rotors may be installed after registration. Four spare fuel assemblies must remain in inventory for submission and are consumed: do not remove them from an operating reactor. If anything becomes unstable, stop burning while preserving cooling instead of raising output to finish the trial.
codex.quest.story_current.fission.title: Heart of the Base
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.0: A shared grid moves energy between generation and consumers, but IE connectors retain their wire classes. An ordinary transformer links low- and medium-voltage lines. This kit therefore uses medium-voltage electrum wire rather than high-voltage steel wire.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.1: Prepare a transformer, four electrum wire coils and a basic Mekanism energy cube. Build the transition with suitable connectors and configure cube faces for input and output. Connect the cube through supported energy interfaces rather than attaching IE wire directly to an arbitrary face.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.text.2: Components can register and be installed separately; show four coils of the same type together. First verify the chosen source charges the cube and runs one consumer. Then expand while retaining shutdown access and keeping high-voltage wire away from the ordinary transformer.
codex.quest.story_current.grid.title: One Grid
codex.quest.story_current.guide_backup_h: With the main source stopped, the storage still receives energy from the backup generator

A dynamo stops with its water wheel, and a diesel generator with its last bucket of fuel. For such moments you need a reserve that depends on neither rotation nor biodiesel. The Mekanism heat generator draws energy from lava and burnable items: lava can be poured into its tank, and lava blocks adjacent to the casing add heat to the output. In the Nether it yields noticeably more.

Place the generator next to the basic energy cube and join them with four universal cables, which carry energy between Mekanism machines and other mods' equipment. Show the four lava buckets together; the book does not consume them, but they go into the tank. One heat generator will not replace diesel, so its job is to keep the storage charged and power what matters most: lighting, pumps and defences.

For the objective, stop the main source and watch the cube's charge grow from the reserve. The generator and cables can be installed right after registration. Decide in advance which consumers stay on the reserve and separate them from the rest of the workshop with a breaker.
The breaker de-energised the section: consumers stopped and the storage behind it stopped charging

One grid is fine until it needs repairs. A breaker switch joins two wires of the same class and passes current only when switched on; it cannot be installed on a high-voltage line. A current transformer sits in any line and counts the energy that passed through it, while the engineer's multimeter shows how much charge is stored in the storage block or machine you click.

Put the breaker between generation and a hungry workshop, and the current transformer on the same line. Clicking the transformer reports average throughput; a comparator at its base gives a signal from zero to fifteen according to wire load. A switched-on breaker also emits a redstone signal, and the engineer's screwdriver inverts that behaviour. High voltage calls for the redstone breaker: an applied signal opens it, and it cannot be toggled by hand.

For the objective, switch the breaker off and confirm that the machines behind it stopped while the multimeter shows their storage no longer charging. The instruments can be placed after the book registers them. Such a cut-off point spares you from tearing down wires every time the workshop is rebuilt.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.0: Mekanism chemical processing extracts more output from suitable ore inputs, but the “fivefold” name does not promise identical yields for every form of iron. Prepare a dissolution chamber and crystallizer, then follow your chosen input’s entire recipe through to iron crystals.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.1: The dissolution chamber uses sulfuric acid and produces dirty slurry; a chemical washer cleans it with water before the crystallizer makes crystals. These stages need suitable chemical connections, power and free outputs. Skipping the washer cannot be fixed by connecting the two listed machines directly.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.text.2: Equipment registers before installation, but 64 iron crystals must be submitted together and are consumed. Test a small batch and verify the yield of your actual recipe. Turning remaining crystals into ingots requires Mekanism’s subsequent standard purification and processing chain.
codex.quest.story_current.ore5.title: Fivefold Ore
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.0: Two steels introduce different ways to obtain similar industrial material. This task needs 32 Immersive Engineering steel ingots and 32 Mekanism steel ingots. Some recipes accept both through shared tags, but this delivery distinguishes exact items and requires both variants.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.1: In IE, run iron and suitable fuel through a blast furnace while clearing steel and slag. In Mekanism, carbon-infuse iron into enriched iron and steel dust, then smelt the ingots. Give each chain its own output chest so product origin remains clear.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.text.2: Bring both batches together: submission consumes all 64 ingots rather than remembering halves shown earlier. Keep materials for your own machine casings. Then choose generation through an IE kinetic dynamo or an alternator driven by Create rotation.
codex.quest.story_current.steel.title: Steel of Two Houses
Obtain the Royal Banner after defeating Xaxxas XIX
The Kingdom of Amber continues the story through local events towards Xaxxas XIX. It is more than a mining stop for rare ingots: the map requires a world visit and its ruler’s trophy milestone. Prepare story access and replenish supplies after Volcanech before crossing.

Follow kingdom dialogue and required areas while maintaining a route through explored rooms. If progress stops, revisit the current assignment instead of seeking a random fight to replace its story condition. Reserve space for the Royal Banner and ensure sufficient equipment durability before the final encounter.

After victory, acquire the banner in your own inventory: this item triggers the installed Xaxxas XIX advancement. The book does not take the trophy, so display it at home after registration. Check your character’s condition and gather necessary story items before the final crossing to Unahzaal.
codex.quest.story_expedition.amber.title: Amber
codex.quest.story_expedition.comets.task: Obtain the Comet Banner after defeating Terrible Tree
codex.quest.story_expedition.comets.text: Comets opens the long Eternal Tales route after two independent journeys. First prepare access using its dedicated chapter and local advancements: Aether or Twilight Forest portals do not lead there automatically. Bring durability reserves and leave room for story loot.

Explore the nearest safe area and locate Terrible Tree’s stage in local progression. Before the major encounter, mark the portal route and keep essential items out of random chests. Victory should end with trophy collection, so inspect the battlefield before opening book rewards.

This task requires visiting Comets and the advancement that the installed version awards for a Comet Banner in inventory. Collect it personally before displaying it or giving it to a teammate. It is not consumed; the registered trophy completes this route segment and opens preparation for Purgatory.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.0: The Twilight Forest teaches ordered boss progression. Prepare its portal: a small pool surrounded by natural decorations following the mod’s rules, activated by throwing in a diamond. After crossing, mark the exit and bring enough food for several encounters rather than a short walk.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.1: Find the Naga courtyard and obtain its progression stage first, then travel to the Lich Tower. Protection in the next area may depend on the previous advancement. During the Lich’s initial phase, reflect suitable projectiles into the real boss to remove shields while avoiding its copies.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.text.2: The book requires visiting the forest and both Naga and Lich trophies. Show them separately if convenient, then display them at home without an extra pair. If the tower remains protected, inspect local advancements rather than only this route map’s marks: item objectives do not replace dimension rules.
codex.quest.story_expedition.dusk.title: Twilight
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.task.1: Complete the quest to free the Altar of the Sun from Eternal Dawn
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.0: Eden differs from the previous trophy stops: it needs a completed story assignment rather than merely a banner in your bag. Visit the Gardens of Eden and locate D’Kudja’s Altar of the Sun quest line. Read the local dialogue before travelling to the encounter so you know whom to report to.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.1: The assignment concerns freeing the Altar of the Sun from Eternal Dawn. Prepare for the event and follow its quest sequence, including the intended subsequent conversation. Victory alone may not grant the mark before story interaction finishes, because Eternal Tales quest logic awards it.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.text.2: Check the Drink of the Sun advancement after completing the assignment. The book records the dimension visit separately without substituting it for the story requirement or demanding the drink itself. The route now splits towards Rayana and Karvat, each requiring an independent expedition.
codex.quest.story_expedition.eden.title: Eden
codex.quest.story_expedition.guide_magic: The filled magic map shows at least three different forest landmarks

The Twilight Forest hides towers, labyrinths and boss courtyards among identical trees, and scouting on foot eats evenings. The magic map solves this: it paints biomes and marks landmark icons within its radius. The focus needs a raven feather, torchberries from the forest caves and glowstone dust; the map itself is made from the focus and eight sheets of paper.

The map works only inside the forest; in another world the magic falters, and the mod says so plainly. Unfold it, walk a little so the area fills in, and compare icons with what you see: the Naga courtyard, the Lich tower, the labyrinth. This way you choose the boss order in advance and do not run into a protected area without the required stage.

An important accounting detail: the objective asks for a blank magic map, and after first use the item turns into a filled map with a different identifier. Show the book the blank map before unfolding it. The focus can be registered separately. The objective is three different landmarks on the filled map.
codex.quest.story_expedition.guide_wayst: Three named waystones stand in different places and travel between them has been tested

A single home waystone brings you back from a trip, but it does not shorten the road to the mine, the portal or the colony. A network of several stones turns the map into a list of stops. A waystone is crafted from three stone bricks, three obsidian and a warp stone in the centre, and the warp stone from four amethyst shards, four ender pearls and an emerald. A warp scroll takes an ink sac, an ender pearl, four gold nuggets and three paper, three scrolls at once.

Place stones where you go most often, activate each with a click and give it a clear name. The stone's menu lists every activated point; a trip may cost experience, and a warp scroll carries you to any known stone and vanishes after use. The return scroll from the expedition kit leads to the nearest stone, so put stones near distant exits too.

Show the three stones together in your inventory, then place them. For the objective, walk a chain of trips between all three and make sure the names in the list are distinguishable. An unactivated stone never appears in the list, however long it has been standing.
codex.quest.story_expedition.karvat.text: Karvat contains three recorded stages: Enicrih, Arla and Ikkorh. Prepare for an extended expedition with repair returns instead of expecting one unchanged supply kit to cover every encounter. Follow Eternal Tales’ local route for access order and story conditions.

Visit the Lands of Karvat and progress through required events while preserving loot from each completed section. After each victory, collect its corresponding banner: the three advancements have different item criteria. One acquired trophy does not replace the other two, even if encounters seemed similar within the same dimension.

Check all three separate marks and the registered Karvat visit in the book. Banners may be acquired sequentially and then left at home because none are submitted. Once Karvat and Rayana are complete, the shared route continues to Volcanech; gather story materials from both branches before crossing.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.0: A travel kit should provide a way home, not merely a quick departure. Prepare a Waystones waystone, two return scrolls and a red Comforts sleeping bag. The bag colour is exact here; another colour may work in play but does not match the item objective.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.1: Activate the home waystone and verify the scroll’s actual destination before a dangerous crossing. Keep food and repair supplies near the return point. A sleeping bag helps with overnight travel under suitable conditions but does not make every dimension safe or replace checking your normal respawn point.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.text.2: You keep every item: show both scrolls together, while other objectives may register separately. Read the selected travel method’s tooltip and consider the current world’s restrictions. If return travel is untested, make a short nearby trip first and retain the second scroll for the expedition itself.
codex.quest.story_expedition.kit.title: Kit
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.task.1: Obtain the Purgatory Banner after defeating Nyetet
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.0: Purgatory continues the Eternal Tales story and needs separate crossing preparations. Before leaving Comets, repair equipment and preserve acquired story materials. This map orders the reading route, while the mod’s own mechanics determine actual access to Purgatory.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.1: After entering, establish a safe return landmark and follow local progression towards Nyetet, the Fallen Guardian. Scout the approach before combat: unknown terrain and no escape route are more dangerous than spending a few extra minutes exploring. Agree on trophy collection during a shared expedition.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.text.2: Completion requires visiting Purgatory and acquiring its banner, which registers Nyetet’s advancement. The item must enter your inventory; someone else’s wall collection is not your acquisition. You keep the banner after registration, and the next route section leads to Eden’s story assignment.
codex.quest.story_expedition.purg.title: Purgatorium
codex.quest.story_expedition.rayana.task: Obtain the Rayana Banner after defeating Pterion
codex.quest.story_expedition.rayana.text: Rayana is one of the two branches after Eden. Prepare its own crossing and exploration supplies; unlocking the card does not build a portal. Avoid spending all Eden loot before checking later recipes and story requirements.

After arrival, mark the exit and locate Pterion’s stage in Rayana progression. Choose positions with visible passages and known terrain, particularly while following the opponent. Before combat, reserve space for the specific Rayana Banner needed to register the local victory.

Completion requires visiting Rayana and the advancement for acquiring its banner. Pick it up into personal inventory before automatically sending it home; the book does not consume it. The next shared crossing also requires Karvat, so replenish supplies and finish that neighbouring branch instead of trying to skip it with one checkmark.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.0: The first sky stage leads to the Aether and a bronze dungeon. Prepare an Aether glowstone portal activated with water, then bring blocks and protection against falling. Islands do not form continuous ground, so choose travel directions carefully.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.1: After crossing, secure a return platform and locate a bronze dungeon. Its Slider boss requires a tool suitable for the stone opponent; relying only on a sword may fail. Preserve dodging space and avoid leaving essential loot in an inaccessible part of the structure.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.text.2: The task checks visiting the Aether and obtaining a bronze dungeon key. Put the key in inventory before using it on the reward chest: the book remembers this ordinary item and requires no spare key. Next, compare this encounter with the Twilight Forest’s local boss sequence.
codex.quest.story_expedition.sky.title: Sky
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.re: The expedition is over. Another game begins
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.ta: Defeat Unahzaal and earn the Eternal Tales finale advancement
codex.quest.story_expedition.unahzaal.te: The final crossing leads to Unahzaal’s Multiverse and completes Eternal Tales’ main route. Finding a decorative dimension block or bringing a similar trophy is insufficient. The map separately checks the dimension visit and the final victory advancement awarded by the mod’s event logic.

Before entering, inspect equipment, recovery supplies and reserves for another attempt. Keep everything needed for continued access in a safe place and understand how to return after failure. Do not begin the last stage on food scraps and nearly broken weapons after the previous long expedition.

Complete the Unahzaal encounter and let its intended events finish, then check your personal advancement. This card does not require the special Eternal Darkness mode. No loot is consumed, so claim the reward once safely out of danger and back with your preserved expedition collection.
codex.quest.story_expedition.volcanech.t: Volcanech combines preparation from Rayana and Karvat and leads towards Arahulum. Check both book branches are complete, then prepare the actual Eternal Tales crossing. Store previous worlds’ story rewards separately from raw materials automatically sent into production.

After entering Volcanech, secure a return method and understand the nearby part of local progression. Repair armour and weapons before the decisive fight and check suitable protection for the environment you encountered. Do not replace scouting with assumptions based on the dimension’s name: terrain and opponents determine actual hazards.

This card requires visiting the world and Arahulum’s advancement, awarded for its banner in inventory. Collect the trophy personally after victory and let the mark update. The banner remains yours, while the next section opens preparation for the Kingdom of Amber with previous story results preserved.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.0: The steam section provides rotation for larger processing, but several conditions limit its output simultaneously. Prepare four steam engines, sixteen tanks and four occupied blaze burners. These quantities form a component kit, not a promise of any particular boiler level.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.1: Join tanks into a valid structure, provide continuous water and heat from below. Install engines with correctly arranged rotational outputs and inspect boiler indicators. Another burner cannot fix missing water, just as a larger tank cannot fix insufficient heat.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.text.2: Show each required batch before installation; different component types may register separately. Then check stable loaded operation, including pump power during startup. If the boiler powers its own water supply, arrange an initial start method or an empty installation cannot provide its first flow.
codex.quest.story_forge.boiler.title: Steam Power Section
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_belt_sorti: Two different items from one belt each end up in their own chest

As soon as ingots and slag travel the belt mixed, you need sorting. A brass funnel is crafted from a brass ingot, an electron tube and dried kelp; a brass tunnel from two ingots, a tube and two kelp. A filter is made from two iron nuggets and wool and stores a list of allowed items.

Place two chests with brass funnels at the end of the belt and give each funnel its own filter: the slot accepts a prepared filter with a list or simply the item itself. A brass tunnel above the belt splits the flow between neighbouring belts and also accepts a filter on each side, so a single junction can send two kinds of cargo in different directions without extra funnels.

The test is simple: send two different items along the belt and make sure each landed in its own chest and nothing jammed at the entrance. Every part can be placed right after the book registers it. If a funnel takes everything, open its filter slot: an empty slot means no restriction at all.
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_signal_blo: A train stopped before an occupied block and proceeded once it cleared

A second train on the line already calls for signals. A signal is crafted from a railway casing and an electron tube, four at a time; the first line rewarded you with exactly such a set. A track observer is made from a casing and a wooden pressure plate and emits a redstone signal while a train passes over it.

Signals are placed in pairs on both sides of the track and divide it into blocks: a train will not enter a block occupied by another train but waits for it to leave. Put two signals before the loading station and check that a carriage left on the block really stops an approaching train. The observer is useful for nearby automation: it can open gates or start a belt while the train rolls past.

The objective calls for observation, not just parts: a train must stop at the signal before an occupied block and move on once it clears. Signals and the observer can be placed as soon as they are registered. If a train ignores the signal, check that both signals stand on the same stretch and face the right way.
codex.quest.story_forge.guide_stress_aud: The stressometer shows spare capacity with every machine of the smelting row connected

The millstone, crushing wheels and fans of the smelting row usually share one shaft, and every new machine takes a share of its capacity. You have owned a stressometer since the start of the road; a speedometer is crafted from a compass and an andesite casing and shows the rotation speed of the chosen section. Together they show the free stress headroom and the speed at the farthest machine.

Place the stressometer on the shaft next to the source and the speedometer at the last consumer. Connect machines one at a time and watch the needle: an overstressed network does not slow down, it stops completely. Stress grows with speed, so speeding up through cogwheels makes every machine hungrier. Two gearboxes made from a casing and four cogwheels carry rotation around a corner without a long chain of cogs.

The objective is complete when, with the last machine connected, the stressometer shows headroom rather than the red zone. Instruments and gearboxes can be placed as soon as the book registers them. If there is no headroom, add a second source to the same shaft or move some machines to a separate shaft with its own drive.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.0: A hand crank teaches the relationship between rotation and machinery before a permanent power system is built. Prepare a crank, mechanical press and iron ingots for ten sheets. A clear space above a depot is enough for the first station; no tower or large workshop is needed.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.1: Connect crank rotation to the press, place an ingot on the depot beneath its head and turn the handle. Watch the press complete its stroke and confirm that the output becomes an iron sheet. Repeat, keeping finished output separate from raw ingots.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.text.2: Install the crank and press as soon as inventory registration occurs; dismantling them again is unnecessary. Show ten sheets together because the quantity of one item is measured simultaneously, not added across separate acquisitions. Next, choose wind or water to replace manual effort.
codex.quest.story_forge.hand.title: Hand on the Crank
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.0: Milling offers a simple finished product from your established rotation source. The order needs 32 units of Create wheat flour. Farmed wheat becomes an intermediate useful for a later food line, although this particular batch goes to the book.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.1: Install a millstone, supply rotation and load a little wheat. Verify flour production and extraction before feeding an entire harvest. Keep seeds for replanting and some grain for ordinary bread while the next food-processing stage is still unbuilt.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.text.2: All 32 flour must be together in inventory at submission and will be consumed. The millstone itself is not submitted. This is a full alternative to crushing wheels on the route to fan processing, letting you postpone expensive brass assembly until it is actually needed.
codex.quest.story_forge.mill.title: Mill: a batch of flour
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.0: Precision mechanisms connect your available power to a controlled production line. You need eight completed Create precision mechanisms. Allow extra golden sheets and consumables because sequenced assembly sometimes yields by-products instead of the desired result.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.1: One cycle adds a small cogwheel, a large cogwheel and an iron nugget using deployers; the initial golden sheet passes through that entire sequence five times. Arrange return routing for incomplete mechanisms and extraction for finished ones. Five mechanical crafters are unnecessary here: operation order and repetition count matter.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.text.2: Submit eight completed mechanisms together from inventory; the batch is consumed. The book cannot infer automation from the output, so personally observe one full pass without carrying the workpiece by hand. This skill supports later freight and control equipment.
codex.quest.story_forge.precision.title: Precision Line
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.0: The railway branch starts with a route rather than locomotive decoration. Prepare 64 Create tracks and two stations for the base and mining site. This reserve may not cover every chosen distance, so survey the terrain and estimate actual route length first.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.1: Lay continuous track between the two sites, leaving convenient station and loading areas. Form curves with track placement controls and inspect each segment’s connection. Give stations distinct names: schedules refer to stops, and accidental duplicate names complicate route diagnosis.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.text.2: Show the full track stack and both stations before installing them; registered items may be used immediately. Owning the kit does not verify a traversable route. Walk it end to end and decide how the train returns, using a loop or controls that support reverse travel.
codex.quest.story_forge.rails.title: First Line
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.task.2: View the encased fan Ponder scene and airflow-processing methods
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.0: Fan processing turns airflow into a Create production tool. Prepare two encased fans and eight belt connectors, then open their Ponder scene. For blasting, air must pass through lava and reach items; lava merely beside the machine does not establish the correct mode.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.1: Choose airflow direction, put the processing source in its path and run an item belt through the working area. Begin with a material that has a bulk-blasting recipe. Protect lava from accidental contact and verify that finished output reaches the destination chest.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.text.2: The book counts components and viewing the reference, not smelting speed. Install registered fans immediately and show the eight connectors as one batch. Before expanding, give the test item enough time in the airflow: an overly fast belt may carry it away before processing finishes.
codex.quest.story_forge.smelt.title: Smelting Row
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.0: A stressometer turns a visibly rotating windmill into an understandable power reserve. Craft the gauge and connect it to the same mechanical shaft that drives the press. An unrelated rotating shaft reports a different network and cannot assess your workshop load.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.1: Read the gauge with processing idle, then operate the press and compare. Engineer’s goggles help read Create parameters in place. If the network is overstressed, temporarily disconnect some consumers and identify which machine or speed increase caused the stop.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.text.2: The item objective remembers the stressometer from inventory; an installed gauge need not be collected again. Its checkmark does not mean enough capacity remains. After testing, choose milling or crushing: both lead to further processing, with the water confirmation remaining an alternative entrance.
codex.quest.story_forge.source.title: Source Found
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.0: After installing water wheels, check stress capacity as well as visible rotation. One stressometer on the shared shaft shows the effect of connected machinery. Reuse an existing gauge if available: the item objective does not require a separate copy for each branch.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.1: Connect the gauge where the wheel and future processing equipment genuinely share one mechanical network. Start the first consumer and observe the load change. If rotation stops, check water flow and connected drive directions before investigating excessive speed or machine count.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.text.2: This optional card confirms the water entrance into processing; the wind branch is not required to reach milling. The gauge may remain installed after registration. Keep some capacity for transport: a running press is useless if adding its belt stops the entire network.
codex.quest.story_forge.source_w.title: Source Found
codex.quest.story_forge.train.reward.0: The first achievement that moves by itself
codex.quest.story_forge.train.task.4: Manually: the train completed a round trip and transferred cargo through the interfaces
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.0: The freight train completes the mechanic’s path only after a real round trip. Prepare controls, a schedule, a blue conductor cap and two portable storage interfaces. A cap alone does not become a driver: assign an appropriate operator according to Create and the installed railway addon.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.1: Assemble the train at a station, provide travel in both directions and schedule the two stops. Align storage interfaces at loading sites so the stopped train exchanges items with the base. Send a small cheap cargo first, with free space in receiving storage.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.text.2: Item objectives may register sequentially before components are used. Confirm the manual objective only after a complete trip that loads and unloads through interfaces. If the train arrives empty, inspect its stop, interface alignment and waiting conditions rather than treating movement itself as completed freight service.
codex.quest.story_forge.train.title: A Train That Doesn't Wait
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.0: The water branch offers another continuous drive for the first workshop. Prepare two large Create water wheels and a site for directed flowing water. Water merely sitting nearby is insufficient: its flow must affect the wheel in a suitable position.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.1: Install one wheel first and arrange water until it rotates steadily. Add the second and connect shafts while checking compatible directions. Remove spills from walkways and retain access to the connection point so future gears need not be installed blindly through water.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.text.2: Show both wheels together in inventory before installation; no second pair is needed after registration. Verify the flow visually and through a connected mechanism’s rotation. This branch reaches processing without a windmill, while another source can be added later to increase available stress capacity.
codex.quest.story_forge.water.title: The Way of Water
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.0: The crushing branch suits players who already have Create brass machinery and mechanical crafters. Prepare two crushing wheels and inputs for 128 crushed raw iron. Milling remains an alternative entrance, so this complex line need not precede your actual technology level.
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.1: Craft the wheels through mechanical crafting, install them as a pair and arrange inward rotation towards the processing gap. Test a small amount of compatible iron input first. Fence off the crushing area and check collection below so output is not lost among ground items.
codex.quest.story_forge.wheels.text.2: Wheels use ordinary item tracking: show the pair, then put it to work. The full 128 crushed raw iron, however, must be present now at submission and is consumed.
